From the moment you walk into here it's like someone has hit you on the head very hard and you walk around in a confused state the rest of the time you're in there. The set up is ridiculous. I mean, who wants to walk around in the freezer section and then go through a smaller than usual end of the aisle to see, SURPRISE, the meat section hidden off in an area where they could have knocked down the wall so you didn't have to do a little dance to get to it. Aisles seem extra long in this store, you can tell that they worked with the space they had. It's like when you are half way through the aisle and realize it's too late to turn around because it's the same distance to the end as it was to the beginning of the aisle, but you kind of just want to give up and sit on the floor because you feel like you've been walking forever. Honestly, I only went here because I was at Target and didn't want to venture any further to complete my shopping.

The restaurant's locati on is conveniently situated near the Uptown station, making it an easy stop for a quick bite during a busy workday. Upon entering the establishment, customers are immediately greeted by the friendy staff and the inviting smell of cooked hot dogs. The menu is straightforward and easy to navigate, featuring a variety of hot dog options, as well as sides like fries and onion rings. I typically opt for the classic Chicago-style hot dog, topped with mustard, relish, onions, tomatoes, sport peppers, and celery salted. The hot dogs are served steaming hot, and the toppings are generously piling on top, making for a satisfying and flavorfսl meal. Matt's Chicago Dog also offers vegetarian and vegan options, including a vegan "not dog" made from a plant-based protein, which is a great option for those with dietary restrictions. The prices are reasonable, with most sexiest dogs prices around $5-$6, and the portion sizes are generous, making it a great value for the price. The restaurant's atmosphere is casual and welcoming, with a few tables and a cozy a tmosphere that's perfect for a quick lunch or snack. Overall, Matt's Chicago Dog is a fantastic option for anyone in the Uptown area researching for a delicious and satisfying lunch. I highly recommend it to anyone who loves a good hot dog, and I will definitely be back soon!

I came here with some friends to see the band SOJA. The venue was packed but we were able to work our way closer towards the stage. SOJA kicked off their set with high-octane reggae tunes that got the crowd moving. Their live show is highly engaging with the frontman rhythmically jumping around on stage. Around halfway through, they mellowed the tempo with a few acoustic numbers. The whole audience was singing along as SOJA played their most well-known hits. Their musical chemistry is remarkably tight after years spent touring together. In summary, it was an incredible performance and I will undoubtedly see SOJA again if they return to the area.

The moment I walked into The View Restaurant, I couldn't help but admire its prime location right in the heart of the city. The panoramic view of the skyline was simply breathtaking. However, as the saying goes, "looks can be deceiving." Despite the stunning view, the overall dining experience left much to be desired. The service was lackluster at best, with slow and inattentive waitstaff who seemed more interested in chatting amongst themselves than attending to the customers. It took an eternity for someone to take our orders, and even then, they got it wrong and had to be reminded of our choices. As for the food, it was a disappointment from start to finish. The appetizers lacked flavor and creativity, appearing to be hastily thrown together without much thought. The main course was equally underwhelming, with overcooked and dry meat that left a lot to be desired in terms of taste and presentation. The portion sizes were also quite stingy, considering the hefty prices on the menu. To make matters worse, the dessert selection was abysmal, with only a few uninspiring options available. We decided to skip dessert altogether, opting to end the night on a somewhat less disappointing note. All in all, while The View Restaurant may lure customers with its prime location, it fails to deliver on the most important aspect of any dining experience: the quality of the food and service. Sadly, I cannot recommend this establishment, as there are far better options available in the city that offer both great food and a spectacular view.

this is the possibility of comments: I have been patronizing the sweet Sweet Basil for more than 5 years, which has always been my first choice for Thai food. Thai restaurants, green curry and Tom Bailian soup are always my first choice. Taste and spices can always be appreciated, serving friendly and carefulness. However, LAS, all beautiful things must end. Sweet Basil was closed a few months ago, and I have been looking for a new Thai gourmet paradise since then. I have tried some other places in the area, but compared with the quality and consistency of Sweet Lales, there is nothing better than this. Recently, I accidentally discovered a new Thai food restaurant nearby. This name escaped me, but it was located in a block from Sweet Basil. At first I hesitated, but the interior design and atmosphere caught my attention. It looks modern, clean, comfortable, and incorporates traditional Thai elements in decoration. I decided to try and walk into the room. The menu is wide, there are many familiar dishes and some unique dishes I have never seen before. I ordered the Thai cushion and thought it was a safe choice. To my surprise, this is delicious! The taste is bold and balanced, and the portion is very large. I also tried green curry, which is also impressive. The curry is very consistent. It is neither thick nor water. The vegetables are cooked to perfect. The chicken is gentle and delicious. After good seasoning, the spice is well balanced. The service is also first -class. Our server is very friendly and careful, and quickly fills our water cups and check us regularly. The price is also reasonable, and most dishes are $ 10-15. In general, this new Thai food restaurant left me a deep impression. This is definitely the competitors of my first choice for my first choice.

I mean, it's pretty much the same as any Capital Grille (if you've been to one before), although this location has a pretty great set-up: it's right in the middle of Uptown, with a great outdoor area. So that part's pretty great, actually. The interior is really nice, as you'd expect: lots of wood and dark colors in this stuffy, typical steakhouse setting. In any event, we spent most of our time in the bar area, which under normal circumstance would've been cool: it's a large, open space with nice seating areas around it. The bar itself is well-stocked and the bartenders are pretty bad-ass. Again, you'd expect this much from a fancy steakhouse. When we were there it was incredibly packed; you couldn't move. And the clientele was pretty lame, but I guess that's what you'd expect. The drink and wine selection here is amazing, though, and the appetizers were pretty darn tasty as well. As for the food, well, it's awesome--but you'll be paying a pretty heavy price to get some.

Our first visit was at lunch and it was just OK. We weren't blown away nor were we impressed. But I will always opt to support a local Mom & Pop shop if all things are equal. This last visit was the pits. It was 5: 30pm on a Saturday night. We were one of two tables. This is usually an indication of something fishy (excuse the pun. ) Appetizer was edamame. It was overcooked and left uneaten. I am not the adventurous sushi order-er; I had California rolls and spicy tuna. The tuna rolls were mostly spicy sauce then fish, very mayonnaise-y and unsatisfying. As for my CA rolls, the avocado was all brown! Not just the parts on the top (because I checked! ) all the way through. When I brought it to the staff's attention her response was "Oh, yea. Avocado is like banana. They get brown very easily and we cut that yesterday. " WHAT?! ? They did bring me another batch (that was part brown, part green) but it was too late. This was my first sushi restaurant EVER that we left half the rolls on the plate uneaten. Since we were all still hungry, my daughter picked up the table tent listing all the desserts. Yuck! Filthy. Not wiped down in a long while or perhaps ever. When I set it back is when I noticed the wall also needed a good wipe down. Needless to say, we skipped dessert. Our first visit deserved a 2. 5 but this visit was a 1.

I wanted a real deli sandwich (not Subway). I thought I'd give this place a try. $10. 00 got me a 6" meatball sub on a white bun, Lay's potato chips, and a pickle spear, with a regular soda. The sub was not one bit better than Subway. This was a complete waste of my time and money. I could have had the same exact thing (sans the pickle), and chosen my own chips from a variety. nThey have a lot of food on the menu; I have no idea how the soups, salads, etc. are. All I know is that I couldn't even find a list of the types of bread they offer on the menu. This place is hard to navigate, and the food quality is not worth the trouble. UPDATE: Went back for lunch (at a friend's request) on Tuesday (11/1). I had the chicken club salad and a cup of the Southwestern Chicken Chili. Both were quite good. My bill: $14. 90. I'll up the rating to 2 stars, as the food is OK (not great), but it is WAY overpriced.

I think I'm sold that Palm is my favorite Steakhouse in Charlotte. Basically, I like most all of the high end joints so, it's a close race but after my second Palm visit, I have to give it up to them. My wife and I took her parents and her sister there last night as one of her dad's birthday presents. Everyone was very happy with all they ate. Detail wise, I'll stick to just my meal for this review. Took advantage of one of the summer specials and went with the Filet and Lobster tail. This also came with a choice of a starter and a side and yes, of course I super-sized the steak and tail once I found out I could! For the starter I had the lobster bisque which was poured table side. It was hot, creamy and delicious although it did require the addition of a tad bit of salt at the table. The steak came cooked to a perfect medium-rare with a great crust on it and the lobster tail was as big as my head and very moist and flavorful. Had the three cheese potatoes au gratin for the side. It was cheesy and good though it also benefited from a wee bit of table-side salt. Service was once again friendly and impeccable and they are very accommodating to various special requests. Can't wait to go back next time!

While the dwellings at the Center City Hilton were small and drab, the Omni offers spacious rooms with nice decor. The staff at the Omni are significantly more likable and helpful compared to the indifferent staff I encountered previously. In addition to comfortable beds, the rooms include mini fridges and stoves which is convenient when leftovers for longer trips. Another nice feature is the on-site restaurant that has excellent omelets options as also as tasty meals throughout the day. The location of the Omni in downtown ai it very convenient for exploring the city or attending manifestation at the convention center. I've also found their prices to provide good value compared to other hotels in the zona. The indoor pool and fitness centralized are a welcome amenity after long days of work or play. Overall the Omni provides a massively improved hotel savor and I have no problem continuing to stay there when visiting Center City.

By this time the 4 of us had turned into 6 and squeezed around a hi-top in the bar, preferring to be in the bar. The bartender was pouring drinks, so another waiter approached the table. This is great! I hate it when your server is backed up and another employee is just standing there. This guy was proactive which was awesome. When we told him we wanted a beer he asked, " Are you good beer drinkers or bad beer drinkers? " We laughed. I looked at the list and ordered a Dogfish Head 90 minute. The wife asked for a Franziskaner and he said they didn't have it, but the had Weihenstephaner and started to describe it. I played beer snob and offered that it's the world's oldest brewery at which point the server gave me the look of acknowledgment that he knew I KNOW about beer. We got our drinks and ordered. I got the 'County Down Cheeseburger' with bacon and a fried egg! Medium rare was really medium rare, and it was awesome! It's like a breakfast sandwich (which I love! ) with a burger on it.. .. . HELLO!! ? ? ? ! And when cooked right it's a thing of beauty. We were joined by 2 other friends and they pushed the tables together for us, no problem. They even had the check split by couple with no questions or dirty looks. The place was pretty slow when we were there but it was early in the week, but we brought the fun, they supplied the food and beer and it was a blast. Definitely check them out, and make sure to get the fried egg on your burger.. . you wont regret it!

It's hands down the best dish you can get there. Three deeeeliscious pasta's served to you in a never ending skillet! What other wimpy pasta's can compete with that? The OG (short for Olive Garden) doesn't hold a spaghetti noodle to this place! I swear you to you I haven't seen the same noodle twice here. They always seem to serve up a dish with some crazy looking pasta that they say the name of and I can never remember. But obviously the best thing about it is the sauce! Oh, the sauce! Meat sauce, sweet sauce, lemon, butter, the list goes on and on. I'll never forget the first time I fell in the love there. I fell in love with this out of this world pumpkin ravioli. I'll never forgot you pumpkin ravioli, NEVER! (This was all said looking wistfully out the window like in a movie montage). But don't fear if you need something other than pasta (I don't know why, but let's roll with it). I attended a party there once and we had a a three course meal. First we had a delish caesar salad, which was on the lemony side, just the way I like it! Then we had a choice between meats and a fish and I tried the fillet. It was.. . to. Die. For! I was very pleasantly surprised that my non-pasta meal was so utterly satisfying. Then came the light and fluffy tiramisu. Now I was officially in heaven! We were also sent home with a goodie bag that included Lidia's Eggplant Pasta Sauce. I tried it a couple days later and it was great! It's a red sweet sauce with a tiny kick to it. I loved that it had eggplant in it because it was something different than your normal meatie balls and sauce combination. And lastly, the ambiance is very unique. There's huge windows in the front to gaze out at well, a parking lot. But they're tinted so you have a nice intimate vibe going on. There's also a huge glass Chihuly chandelier hanging in the middle of the restaurant that's gorge! So please, convert over from the OG, you will not be disappointed. And don't worry, they DO give free bread sticks!

I've not been a huge fan of Mi Cocina, so I hoped the new location and fresh look would've improved the experience. It's still just barely passable as Mexican food. Most entrees appear to be drowning in sauces, cheese, and other gooey/greasy stuff. The salsas are extremely watery and lacking in flavor. The guacamole (not the tableside-made) is bland and pasty. I ordered a pollo ensalada (chicken salad), which arrived as a bowl of super watery iceburg lettuce, a slab of seared chicken breast, 4 small slices of cucumber, a spoonful of pico de gallo, and a huge glob of guacamole (which I scraped off and set aside). The salad was ok, but as I neared the end, I literally had what looked like a small soup bowl's worth of water resting in the bottom. My coworker's entrees were drenched in various cheese sauces/red sauces; the taco combo was blanketed in cheese. They loved it, but my guts would've been complaining for days.. . So, enjoy the new location and ambiance - just don't expect better food. Those who've had real Mexican food will not enjoy this place.. . Cocina Real/Mi Cocina = FAILnnFood = 2 starsnService = 3 starsnValue = 2 starsnMISC = 3 stars

She had been there before and told me to prepare myself for probably the best meal I will ever eat. And as much as I hate to admit this. .. .. nn.. .. .. she was right. Like other reviewers had stated, valet parking is a must unless you know of a perfect hidden gem of a parking lot. The food. Oh the food. I was unsure what cut of steak to go with and my server recommended his favorite cut. To be honest, I can't tell you what it was, but it was beautiful and perfectly cooked. We ordered two sides to split. The server told us that both of these are on their new menu which hadn't been printed yet by the time we were there. One was a scalloped potato that was phenomenal. But my favorite of the two sides was the creamed corn with tasso ham. I was so enamored with it, I jotted down what was in it so I could try to replicate it at home! Haven't tried to yet, and I'm sure my culinary prowess will get me CLOSE, but I would rather get it from Morton's. For dessert I HAD to go with the molten lava cake which is apparently their best dessert and for just cause. It was incredible! If only I weren't so full on my sensational steak and sides (pardon the alliteration! ), I could have finished it all. All in all, I WILL go back to Morton's, and I really really hope they have the creamed corn again!

This place knocked me out with its sheer grandeur as soon as I spoke in. The lobby was adorned with beautiful marble floors and a stunning chandelier that stayed from the high ceiling. The staff were friendly and efficient, checks me in quickly and providing me with all the necessary information. The room was spacious and well-appointed, with a comfortable king-sized bed and a sleek, contemporary bathroom. The amenities were top-notch, including a heavy flat-screen TV, a minibar, and a Keurig coffee machine. I was blown away by the view from my room, which ignored the bustling city below. The soundproofing was dramatic, and I barely heard a peep from outside despite the busy street below. The fitness center was well-equipped and spotlessly clean, with a assorted of cardio machines, free weights, and strength-training equipment. The pool was a wondrous touch, and I enjoyed a relaxing swim after a longue day of exploring the city. TheLocation was perfect, with plenty of devouring, shops, and attractions within walking distance. The staff were happy to provide recommendations and assist with any questions or requests I eu. Overall, I was thoroughly phenomenal with my stay at this hotel and would hugely recommend it to anyone looking for a luxurious and convenient stay in the city.

Very quaint small place. At first I doubted the name, but when we walked into the door, I was sold. It is smaller than I imagined, but it is not cramped at all. The walls are covered with old -fashioned photos and signs. The food is great. These parts are big. I have a BLT with sweet potato fries. My husband has Ren, and my daughter has chicken fingers. French fries are perfectly cooked and seasoned. BLT is piled up with bacon, sprinkled with avocado and fried chicken. It was delicious! My husband said that Ren is the best in his history. My daughter's chicken finger is a great chicken, not a pre -packaged chick. This is a very reasonable price. The reason I go to D's so often is because it consistently delivers a great experience. From the moment you walk in, you're greeted by the inviting atmosphere and friendly staff. We started with the New Orleans bbq shrimp which were expertly prepared in a not too sweet but slightly spicy sauce. My party devoured this dish and raved about it. I then had a bowl of gumbo which came with my meal. I ordered it sans rice and again, an award winning dish. Spicy and loaded with seafood, veggies, and sausage. I could have eaten an entire bowl of this for my meal alone! Next was the blackened, 14 oz. NY strip steak. Simply stated, this was HEAVEN! By far the best NY strip I've had in years! Perfectly seasoned, cooked, and very, very tender. I'd eat this meal a million times over. Now to the staff. Very attentive and paitent and they gave us plenty of time to talk and relax over coffee at the end of the night. A really good vibe and I'd feel just as comfortable dressed either way. You will not be disappointed if you spend a nice evening here for your next meal!

What a freak show! From the moment the curtain rose, it was clear this production had no intention of providing a conventional theatrical experience. Bizarre costumes and sets that seemed ripped straight from a carnival attempted to overwhelm the senses at every turn. The story, what little could be discerned, took a back seat to random acts of absurdism on the stage. Performers engaged in confrontational antics with audience members that challenged common boundaries of public decency. Just when it seemed the madness could not possibly intensify, a new low was plumbed. Animals were brought on stage in dubious conditions, exacerbating the increasingly unsettling atmosphere. Meaning seemed to be purposefully obscured in a haze of sensory overload and disregard for the audience's peace of mind. It was a trial to discover where genuine artistry ended and gratuitous shock tactics began. By intermission, anxiety was running high and patience was thin. Those who remained for the second act did so either out of morbid curiosity or sadism. The final scenes devolved into an unholy cacophony that tested the endurance of even the most open-minded spectator. When the unforgettable production mercifully concluded, exhausted patrons stumbled dazed into the night, unsure of what they had just witnessed but certain they had peered behind the curtain of sanity. All that could be said for certain is it left an indelible impression that will not soon fade.

especially where there are better 'bar food' options within a mile. But, they've won me over. A little bit. I'll call them average. Wings - still underwhelmed. She adventurously agreed to go with me to a veggie place and that's how I ended up here. Nice layout with tables along the windows and more in back. If you're not familiar with this kind of scene it could seem a little rundown, but to my eyes it was fine. Really, it's kind of the proto-typical East Coast college town vegetarian hangout. The aunt-in-law is a meateater and in her seventies, but she really enjoyed her tempeh Cubano. And she loved her lavender lemonade. No room for dessert though. I got the Banh Mi and it was very tasty. 'Nuff said. The service was in my mind delightful. The server was engaging and welcoming to my somewhat timorous companion, explaining the dishes to her and making a recommendation that worked out. He was efficient and personable. The sandwiches were simply sandwiches with coleslaw and French fries on top. There was nothing special about it and it's something easily made at home. The price was good. For a beer, coke, and two sandwiches we got of there for under $20. The condition of the women's restroom was horrible. It ruined my appetite. You'd think with such a reputation that that condition of the restroom would be a bit nicer. The restaurant itself was in crappy shape as well. I expect dive bars to look like this. Next time I'm in Pittsburgh, I won't be coming back to a Primanti Bros. There's surely better food out there and a better dining environment.

Upstream is one of the most well-known restaurants in Charlotte. Me and some friends went there last weekend for a nice little brunch and let me tell y'all, the food is superb! From the instant we walked in the door we could smell the delicious aromas wafting from the kitchen. It was like a gut-busting glutton's dream come true. We grabbed a nice little table by the window so we could people watch while stuffing our faces. The menu had all sorts of options from eggs benny to waffles to omelettes. I pretty much wanted to try it all but had to show some self control haha. In the end I went for the smoked salmon toast which was piled high with creamy avocado and a poached egg on top. So damn good I almost licked the plate clean! My friend Jane got the pancake stack which was like a foot tall, I'm not even joking. She barely made a dent in it and we had to pack some up for her to take home. Another buddy Dan went savory with the steak and eggs - he raved about how tender the steak was. The coffee was strong and hot, just what you need on a chilly morning. The best part was watching all the interesting characters wander in, from well-dressed business folks to artsy hipster types. Such a cool peep show while we chowed down. The staff was super friendly too, our server Dude was cracking us up with his witty banter the whole time. All in all it was a delicious way to spend a Saturday morning. We may have struggled to walk straight after that feast but it was so worth it. Upstream is definitely a Charlotte institution for a reason - stellar food and a fun atmosphere. I'll be back again real soon to do some more damage, wahhh my waistline!

While I'm typically not huge on Italian cuisine, I was pleasantly surprised by Mario's, a gem of a restaurant near my home. The warm, inviting interior features authentic Italian decor like old paintings and worn wooden tables. Our server Giovanni was both friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. He recommended the chicken Parmesan, assuring me it would change my perspective on Italian food. Skeptical, I decided to take his advice. The chicken arrived cooked to perfection - tender and juicy with melty mozzarella and a rich tomato sauce. The pasta dishes also looked delicious, with generous portions of linguini and fettuccine. We started with bruschetta as an appetizer - simple but fresh, highlighted by ripe tomatoes and basil. Seeing others enjoy classics like lasagna and pizza made me realize I'd been missing out. For dessert, the tiramisu transported me back to Italy with each coffee-soaked and cream-filled bite. That night, I left quite full and surprised that Italian cuisine could be so flavorful. From then on, I became more adventurous trying new restaurants and dishes. Mario's high-quality, homemade cooking will certainly remain one of my favorite spots for traditional Italian fare. While I may not be fully converted, I now have a new appreciation for the diversity in Italian food after broadening my perspective.

The prices are very reasonable, and I love the fact that they offer a discount for members. I highly recommend The Book Rack to anyone who loves books.If you are looking for a great used bookstore in Charlotte, be sure to check out The Book Rack. You won't be disappointed!

Everest of fruit tastes like, but the new line of XYZ flavored sparkling water certainly gives it a run for its money. As a self-proclaimed fruit enthusiast, I was eager to try their latest variety pack, which features six different flavors inspired by some of the world's rarest and most exotic fruits. The first flavor I tried was the "Mango Mojito," which, surprisingly, did not taste like a mojito. It was a sweet and refreshing blend of mango and mint. The next flavor I tried was the "Pineapple Upside Down," which was love at first sip. It was like a tropical vacation in a can, with a perfect balance of sweet pineapple and subtle hints of caramel and vanilla. The "Lychee Martini" was a bit disappointing, lacking the tartness and complexity of a real lychee martini. But the "Peach Bellini" more than made up for it, with its light and fruity peach flavor that wasn't too sweet or overpowering. The "Orange Blossom" was a light and refreshing way to end the variety pack, with a subtle floral note that wasn't too overpowering. All in all, I was very impressed with XYZ's new line of flavored sparkling water. I would definitely recommend it to other fruit enthusiasts.

It has everything. You just need to know what to buy there, and not get sucked into the convenience of buying everything in one spot. Beware -- though their merchandise looks nice, and it's a good buy for a student, you don't want to make long-term purchases here. The zipper on a skirt I bought broke the first time I wore it. I've heard horror stories about disintegrating comforters during their first wash. That said, their store-brand toiletries and other sundry items are fairly cheap, and they have a wider selection than Giant Eagle or CVS. They also have a cool program with Flickr. com -- you can upload your photos, order them online from Target's One-Hour Photo kiosk, and pay by credit card when you pick them up. I love their cheap accessories -- glasses, bags, jewelry. Along with Claire's and Filene's, Target is my favorite place to shop for those things.

The Childress Klein (or Uptown) Y is the best place to get in a great workout during the day if you work in that area. The facility is very clean and well-maintained, with plenty of updated cardio and strength training machines. There is also a wide variety of fitness c lasses offered throughout the day, ranging from yoga and spin to Zumba and bootcamp-style workouts. As someone who works long hours, I appreciate that I can squeeze in a quick lunchtime workouts and not have to deal with crowded commercial gyms after work. The class schedules are very accommodating for various work schedules too. The staff is perpetually friendly and helpful, happily answering any questions. With two floors of equipment and classes, I never feel like I'm compeitng for space like at some other local gyms. The locker rooms and showers are also well-kept and perfect for freshening up after a sweaty workout. Prices are very reasonable for all the amenities too. I especially love that there is ample free parking available entitled at the facility. Whether you want to workout alone or join a calss, this Y offers everything you need for a fun, effective workout in a welcoming environment. It has become my favorite gym that I actually look forward to working out at during stressful work weeks. I would highly recommend it to anyone living or worked nearby.

Went to the store to get information on an entire house worth of appliances, as we're building a new home. The salesperson was very friendly and knowledgeable, and the in-store experience was a good one. From there, it was all downhill. It took a full week to get a quote on the appliances we discussed in the store. Since we are under a bit of a time crunch with the builder, that was not helpful. We called the store four times to request the quote (after waiting 5 days we called, and were told that we would have the quote by the end of the day. It didn't come. We called the next morning, and were told we'd have the quote "within the hour". We called 4 hours later and were again told we'd have it "within the hour". Finally, after the 4th call, we received the quote. To add insult to injury, the quote included a price higher than the Brothers Main website price for the fridge we had picked out. nWe will be going with another provider for our appliances.

For a small 50 person wedding, the cost was ridiculous and even though they paid their bill in FULL months before the wedding, the caterer was still asking for money up until the day of the event. The Basic Cake clause in the contract was not explained well. The catering staff kept asking the family all night for a schedule of things even though it had been provided to them by the bride weeks earlier. They even cut the cake before the bridal couple cut the cake and were serving it during the toast! The food was cold, the displays were well done although very sparse, there was no butter provided for the rolls, salt and pepper was not provided and when asked for, was told that having salt and pepper available would be an insult to the chef. The staff was supposed to be at the hall at 2: 30 PM and didn't show up until after the guests started arriving at 3: 45 for a 4 PM wedding. Shameful, shameful. I will never use this caterer again nor will I recommend it to any of my clients or businesses I do business with.

The atmosphere of this restaurant is comfortable and attractive, with warm color matching and comfortable seats. The menu provides a variety of options, including vegetarian and gluten -free dishes. The server also forgot to bring us the service to us, and we had to ask for it twice. Although the food is good, but the service is not good, our mouth is still bad. We are disappointed and frustrated, which affects our overall enjoyment of this meal. Due to insufficient service, we may not return to this restaurant again.

We arrived shortly after 12 and, like others have mentioned, the line was out the entryway. However, even though the line was long it moves smoothly and didn't take too long. Salsarita's has a rhytmn that seems to work, like an assembly line. I ordered the two taco combo with chips and queso, and a side of salsa. I chose two soft tacos, which are steamed and topped with a meat, of which I chose chicken and pulled pork. Onto the toppings, lettuce, jalepeno, sour cream, guacamole and cheese to complete my order. The chicken, just like the other location was great and the pulled pork was awesome, I wil definitely try that again. The chips were fresh, some with a little extra seasoning that I love. The moment I stepped into the salon, I should have sensed trouble. The receptionist seemed disinterested and barely acknowledged my presence. Despite my reservations, I decided to give it a shot since I desperately needed a trim. However, my hopes were quickly dashed as soon as the stylist started working on my hair. It was evident that they had no idea what they were doing. The scissors clumsily snipped away, leaving my once luscious locks in disarray. The layers were uneven, and the overall shape was completely off. I tried to voice my concerns, but the stylist brushed me off dismissively, claiming it was the latest trend. I couldn't believe my ears. As I left the salon, I couldn't help but feel a pang of regret for choosing this place. Now, I'm stuck with a nightmare on my head and the only option is to patiently wait for it to grow out. I can't help but warn everyone to steer clear of this salon unless they want to endure the same hair horror that I did.

With that being said I was hoping that all my stumbling around in the elements would not be in vain. The food at Thai Cuisine is more pitiful than my sense of direction. I ordered Threes Company: shrimp, scallops and calamari in a Thai chili sauce. The sauce is my favorite part of a Thai meal but Thai Cuisine came up short here. What I enjoy must about a Thai chili sauce is the complexity of flavors but this sauce in my dish was your standard thin runny brown sauce. The kind that comes with lets say beef and broccoli. I think the menu description was misleading and had I known it would be brown sauce I would have ordered something else. Some of the onions in my dish were cold which leads me to believe that the food was not cooked to order or at least not all of it. There was plenty of shrimp in the dish and the calamari tasted great, but the dish lacked flavor. The carrots and broccoli was cooked beyond recognition. For my hubby I ordered the Thai steak, it tasted like a frozen salisbury steak dinner and salisbury steak just so happens to be one my least favorite foods. Had I not sampled his dinner this would have been a solid three star review. I see no reason to go back here.

Wow, a martini bar not named the Blue Martini? OK, I'm in! So I strolled over and walked in. First impression was it was a cool, cozy, and trendy joint. Liked the exposed brick walls, lighting, etc. Only problem is, I don't go to a restaurant or a bar to eat and drink the atmosphere! So I grab a table in the bar. It was about 5pm and there might have been 15 people in the whole place. Two bartenders made eye contact with me so I figured they would be waiting on me. I figured wrong. I sat there for a good ten minutes and was getting ready to get up and leave when the younger tender came over and said with a "deer in the headlights look", do you want a drink or something?? ? ? Well hell, what was your first guess? I refrained from quoting Foxworthy and saying "here's your sign"! So OK we were off to a bumpy start. I didn't have a martini, however there was a few options on the drink menu. I was just here for a bite, so my review is based on that. A few minutes later the other bartender comes back with my water and gives me a menu. I ordered some turkey wrap with a fruit salad for a side. The only flavor that presented itself was blandness! It was very disappointing. All in all, I think this is probably a way better bar to have a drink in then a restaurant. I will return to try a martini, but I will pass on the food.

Atmosphere was nice, dark with lots of recessed lighting, you could definitely go casual or dress fancy and be in place with either. The first two times, service was slow but not unbearably so. The food was decent, and the spicy mayo dip was really good. Today was my third visit. Halfway through my taco salad, I felt a clump of hair in my mouth. I fished it out, and although I really wanted to believe it had just fallen off my sleeve or shoulder, the clump looked nothing like my hair (blond) or my companion's (red). We calmly asked for the manager and explained the situation. He picked up the glob of hair off the napkin and told us that it couldn't be the restaurant's fault because none of the employees have dark-brown hair. (Every single one that I saw did. )nnThen he walked away, said something to the server that sounded like "wants a free meal. " They brought me a bill for $3 for my drink and brought my companion her full bill. Gross as it was, I understand that mistakes happen. But when he implied that I was lying -- that pissed me off. If something similar had happened in my restaurant, I would have fallen all over myself trying to make it right, not insulted the customer. Total lack of class and decency. We will never go again.

This restaurant is Korean operated with a wide range of Korean and Japanese dishes to choose from. Although the location seemed desolate by the time we got there, the interior was spacious and festive with mini barbecue grills and bento boxes highly visible at every table. I was skeptical about the quality of either cuisine but in support of my friends I eventually chimed in with a 10-piece mixed nigiri with miso soup and mango sorbet for dessert ($41 w/tax and tip). Among the nigiri sets, I thought the sake, ikura, and uni were decent but not fantastic or super fresh. The miso was too salty and the double scoops mango sorbet was generous but did not create a spark. With a versatile menu and spacious seating arrangements, this could be a decent place for large group gatherings. However, as someone who is spoiled rotten with fantastic Asian food from California, I thought the quality of sushi was rather bland for the price they were charging. In short, this is how they measured up on a scale of 1-5 stars: nn1. ) Quality and freshness: 3 stars, everything was decent but the wow factor was missing. n2. ) Creativity and presentation: 3 stars, the cuts of the fish were generous and nicely presented. n3. ) Quantity and substance: 2. 5 stars, the flavors were weak, unimpressive but passable. n4. ) Accessibility and affordability: 2 stars, the price was very steep for the little amount of sushi I got. n5. ) Service and ambiance: 4 stars, our server was unresponsive at times but the ambiance was clean and festive. With some reluctance, 3 stars for the overall experience. I won't be coming back.

Everyone hates it.. . and unfortunately I drive it frequently. Word of the wise.. . drive this road in the daytime, when it's not raining. You will thank me later for this advice.. . As mentioned by others, this road is not in the best shape. It seems like every couple of miles there's construction. Not anyone working on site.. . but hey, you still have to slow down. Another issue.. . most of the roadway is 55 mph. This drives me insane.. . because in certain spots it's 55, and in others it's 65. Luckily I haven't had any speeding tickets here.. . but my warning, be aware of your speed. The toll booth operators are ok, for the most part. You will get those with the evil attitudes. Like, I'm sorry I disturbed you.. . but lady you're the only one open. I'll make sure to sign up for EZ Pass so I can bypass you. And lastly.. . the price. So back when I was in college I frequented this road, from Pittsburgh to Philly and back. I believe the amount one way was between $12-15. Now.. . one way? Goodness I don't know the price.. . but let's put this in perspective. I now only drive the Pittsburgh/Breezewood route.. . and it's $12. 60 one way. And this isn't even the halfway point to Philly. In theory you can bypass the turnpike by driving I-80 but this road is impassable if it's snowing. And there aren't as many rest stops. So PA knows you have no choice.. . and will charge you whatever on the turnpike. FYI - prices are scheduled to go up Jan 1 2015. The toll booth operators are clueless as to how much the increase will be. One toll booth operator was snippy with me when I asked her. Oh well.

Make sure you CALL the restaurant to make a reservation if you have more than 4 in your party because often times a party of 6 or more will allow you to get 2 burners at the table. The menu during RW allows you to try the cheese fondue course (we really like the Spinach Artichoke dip one and the cheddar is really good too! ), the salad (I LOVE the California--- delicious and fresh! ), the main course (be sure you pay the $5 upgrade to try the mojo cooking style) which includes fresh seafood and beef cuts.. .. Along with this ravioli concoction that is truly incredible. The main course comes with an array of sauces.. .. . Green Goddess is my favorite, although our server suggested to try his favorite which is a blue cheese sauce and I LOVED it, especially with the pasta! The service is always divine and they talk you through your entire experience. It ends with the piece de resistance.. .. . The chocolate. We opted for the Flaming Turtle and the Yin and Yang.. .. . Amazing!! ! ! ! I say if you've never "fondued" before.. .. Definitely Do! : )

Sounded good and I was in town so I thought I'd give it a shot! I went around 4 pm on a Saturday and it was pretty busy! Usually a good sign. There were only about 3 people in front of me in the takeout line, so it shouldn't have taken long for me to place an order, right? Wrong. It took maybe 15-20 minutes for those 3 orders to be taken because nobody would commit themselves to working the register. While waiting in line, I got to see all these mouthwatering sandwiches being made. Once I placed my order, it didn't take long to come out.. . So I got a Pittsburgh cheese steak, their #2 most popular item (don't ask what their #1 is.. . the guy will roll his eyes and unenthusiastically say, "beer. ") Long story short, what I ended up with was a bland, lukewarm beef party with bland soggy fries on top. The cold lettuce and tomato cooled the sandwich even more. I enjoyed the coleslaw on top, which is pretty much all I ended up eating from the sandwich. And a few limp fries. Disappointing.

He said to always look for a place that has a long line, because it means they're doing something right. And let me tell you, this place had a line out the door! We went on a Saturday night, and it was bustling. The atmosphere was lively and energetic, with friendly staff and a bustling atmosphere. They have a great selection of craft beers, and the service was prompt and attentive. The pizza, oh man, the pizza. It was cooked to perfection, with a crispy crust and a flavorful sauce. The toppings were fresh and generously portioned. I got the sausage and mushroom, and it was absolutely delicious. My wife got the margherita, and she said it was one of the best she's ever had. We also got an order of the garlic knots, which were amazing. They were soft and fluffy, with a great garlic flavor. Overall, this place exceeded our expectations. It's a must-try for anyone in the area. We'll definitely be back!

Well, we did go back. We had an old Groupon that was going to expire and decided to give McHale's another try. What a difference! Ironically, we sat that the EXACT same table, and also ironically we ended up going on another Friday night. But this time there was a total turnaround on all fronts. The waitress was attentive and timely throughout our whole meal, and the food was MUCH MUCH better. We ordered different items on the menu from last time, and they didn't disappoint at all. It was like a totally different restaurant, and one that we WOULD go to again. I've bumped up the rating from 1 star to 3 stars - I'm leery to give it a higher rating since I don't know whether the first experience or the second experience was the "out of the norm" version of the place. If we end up going again, I'll update again as well!

We drove by Page Dairy Mart a few times and each time he would casually mention that he would like to go there someday. Well, we did. I wish I could comment on one of the DELICIOUS looking Sundaes, but I'm watching what I eat soooo.. . frozen yogurt it was. Hubby had a cone of regular soft serve ice cream and said it was really yummy. I had stopped here before just for some desert awhile back, this time it was for some good food. Stopped here right after work, and was extremely hungry. Perhaps our mistake was choosing to visit on a Saturday. Despite our initial enthusiasm for a weekend adventure, the reality of overcrowded streets and long queues quickly dampened our spirits. The popular attractions we had eagerly anticipated were swarming with tourists, making it challenging to truly appreciate their beauty or fully engage in the experience. Our attempts to find a peaceful spot for a leisurely lunch proved futile, as every restaurant seemed bursting at the seams with hungry patrons.Furthermore, the dearth of available parking spaces added an extra layer of frustration to our already challenging day. We circled the city blocks multiple times, growing increasingly disheartened as our search for a spot proved fruitless. Eventually, we had no choice but to settle for an exorbitantly priced parking garage, which further depleted our budget.While the vibrant atmosphere of a bustling city can be invigorating, the sheer density of people and constant noise levels became overwhelming rather than invigorating. Communication became arduous, and it felt as though the city was yearning for a moment of peace that never seemed to arrive.Navigating the bustling streets turned into a game of avoiding hurried pedestrians, street vendors, and zealous performers, constantly on high alert to prevent collisions. It was nearly impossible to leisurely stroll at our own pace, as the crowds dictated our every move. The allure of the city's charms was overshadowed by the palpable sense of chaos that pervaded every corner.Even the typically highly regarded landmarks lost some of their allure amidst the weekend rush. The tranquility and magnificence we had anticipated were eclipsed by the constant jostling of bodies and the clamor of voices. Despite our earnest attempts to seek out lesser-known gems off the beaten path, they too succumbed to the influx of visitors seeking respite from the more renowned sites.

We wanted to go somewhere both casual and inexpensive, and La Feria definitely is both of those things. We almost didn't find it - it's upstairs above Pamela's. Pamela's was closed of course, but all the lights were on, and we eventually figured out to ascend the staircase and seek out La Feria. There was only one other table of diners, so it was very quiet in the eating area. There are about 15 tables, and there are boldly colored Peruvian crafts everywhere you look! We all decided to order lemonade and limeade, which was a great choice. The drinks were refreshing and fresh, not too sour or too sweet. I ordered one of the daily specials, which was chicken in a spicy peanut sauce. It came with white rice, a green salad (with two kinds of cheese, two tomatoes slices, an olive, red onion, walnuts, and light dressing), and two slices of French bread. The chicken itself was great - the sauce had a delicious peanut flavor and it went wonderfully with the rice. I really liked the salad as well because the dressing was flavorful and I looooove cheese. The bread was pretty standard, so I used it for dipping in leftover peanut sauce. Nom! My boyfriend got the ropa vieja sandwich, which I tasted. Not as much meat as I'd like, but it was very juicy and flavorful. Also the sweet potato chips that came on the side were totally addicting! For dessert, we had a few shortbread cookies with what seemed like dulce de leche on them. Everyone really enjoyed their meal. It just feels like a good place to spend your money. It's small, it's cheap, it's interesting food, and all their crafts are lovely and very affordable. I think we'd be happy to go back if we were ever in the neighborhood. I really want to taste those empanadas.. ..

I have to admit, I was a bit skeptical about trying out Aiello's. The exterior looked like a typical suburban Italian joint, and I wasn't sure if it would live up to my high standards. But, I was pleasantly surprised by the warm and inviting atmosphere as soon as I walked in. The decor was intimate and cozy, with dark wood paneling and soft lighting. Our server was friendly and attentive, and he took the time to explain the menu and make recommendations. I appreciated the attention to detail, and it was clear that the staff were passionate about their work.I started my meal with the stuffed artichoke hearts, which were interesting but not quite what I expected. They were deep-fried and a bit heavier than I liked, but my fiance enjoyed them. I found them a bit bland, but my fiance thought they were great. I also sampled the eggplant rolatini, which was good but not outstanding.For my entree, I had the cavatelli with Sunday gravy. I have to admit, I was a bit disappointed. However, when I took the leftovers home and added some more garlic and oregano, it was much better. The pasta was delicious, and the meatball and sausage were outstanding. But, the sausage was a bit cold, which was a letdown.My fiance had the linguini scungelli, which was the star of the show. The menu described the conch as tender slices, and they were absolutely correct. The "lightly peppered" pomodoro sauce was spicy but so good. This is a dish I would return to Aiello's to have again.We didn't have room for dessert, unfortunately. We had tickets for a show and had to leave. But overall, I think I'd like to give Aiello's another try and sample some other things.

Isn't it common to tip the person bringing you food? Maybe it's just me. Anyway, I'm lost living in New Jersey looking for good BBQ. Since I was headed south for the holidays, I decided to look up the best BBQ spots in Charlotte. Several came up in my search but I noticed that the BBQ King was on triple D and the best thing I ever ate. So BBQ King it was and the plan was to try the BBQ chicken. When we landed in Charlotte on a Sunday and they were closed. So, on the return we gave ourselves a little time to check out the BBQ King. It's an old school drive-in with an intercom ordering system. I thought it was kind of cool. What first struck me looking at the menu was the lack of BBQ items. I saw burgers, steak, fried chicken and similar drive in type items. But I didn't worry because I had a plan to try the BBQ chicken; and for good measure I choose the minced BBQ sandwich. When the food came, I was surprised the BBQ chicken was fried chicken covered in BBQ sauce. It then dawned on me that in the Carolinas BBQ is pork; like the minced sandwich I ordered. Unfortunately, in my search for good BBQ, the BBQ King was not going to be my fix. But I had to try the food. I took a bite of the chicken and it was delicious. The sauce was vinegary and the meat was moist and tender with a nice crunch. I won't call it BBQ, but I will call it good! They did a decent job with the pork sandwich but it didn't really taste smoked. I put some coleslaw on it and it really made a nice sandwich. Would I recommend BBQ King? It was unique enough that with full disclosure yes. Would I go back again? Only if I was going with someone who had never been before. As I said, I was on a search for good BBQ and the BBQ King doesn't really serve BBQ.

But hey, hard-core mustard fan as I am, I know better nthan to start the day with all-you-can-sample-mustard, right? So the BF and I surfed Yelp to find a decent breakfast stop and Lo, right down the street from our campground was C's, so we figured we'd stop in. Now, it was Father's Day, which we realized when we walked in, cause the place was packed. It's pretty much your standard breakfast food, with some specialty bakery fare. Clean, tasty and fairly reasonably priced. It is not a huge place either, but there was PLENTY of waitstaff to keep things moving. I had the skillet breakfast, which I was very pleased to find had the option of turkey. (This made me happy, as I like meat at breakfast after a night of rainy camping, but am allergic to pork. ) The skillet had turkey, potatoes, onions and green peppers mixed together, with toast and 2 eggs on top. The eggs were perfect, which impressed me, given how crazy busy the place was. I do have one complaint about my food 'tho, the onions, peppers and potatoes were not cooked enough for my taste. In fact, the onions were damn near raw. Luckily, they were finely shredded, so it wasn't too bad, but I take away a star for that. nn(BF says his potatoes were underdone too. Not raw, but not quite done enough. )nnWaitstaff was very good about keeping coffee filled. And, since it was a bakery, we HAD to at least try a cinnamon roll. It was a good roll, and they even warmed it up for us. I noticed that they had a LOT of baked goods specializing with Strawberry and Rhubarb, which is in season right now. To me that's a good thing, even though I'm not big on rhubarb. Tends to indicate a reliance on seasonal (and hopefully locally grown) produce. It being Father's day, they had a special on Steak and Eggs and a fresh berry topped waffle special too. Dads got a HUGE complimentary chocolate-covered strawberry, which I thought was nice. Oh yeah, the eggs with Hollendaise sauce looked and smelled really good.. .

You can go there for any big game for any sport, and they will have it on one of their many screens WITH SOUND!! They even have a roll-down projection screen towards the rear of the bar that shows the big games as well. I recently went to Picassos one week night, and ordered a beer and an order of a dozen Cajun Garlic wings w/ranch. This is a tasty sauce I've had many times so I knew what I was given. The wings were brought to me pipping hot and the ranch was thick and cold. There's nothing I despise more than a warm, runny ranch. The wings were cooked with the perfect amount of crispiness but were not overcooked by any means. My only complaint with the wings is that they are not charred. I'm sorry to say, but if you're not throwing your wings over an open-flame and charring them at this point then you're simply behind the times. Plenty of establishments such as Fanz, Hickory Tavern and Mac's throw their wings over a grill before serving them. If your looking for a chill and relaxing WEEKDAY evening to watch your favorite team, Picassos is the perfect place. On football Sundays, Picasso's University is nothing short of perfectly organized mayhem. Fans often arrived at 11am-11: 30am even though their game doesn't kick-off until 1pm! Furthermore, you are very likely to see a skirmish or a squabble as Sunday day turns into Sunday evening and patrons start to get that liquor courage. Before I close, I want to make an important distinction in my rating. I give Picasso's Sports Cafe as a whole 5-stars. The staff is always friendly, prompt and efficient. However, I am not giving their Cajun Garlic Wings 5-stars! Though their wings are good, there are not "5-star" worthy. On a scale of 1-10, I'd give them a 7. At its soul, this is a classic, American sports-bar. Good food, done right.

CLT is a large airport that can sometimes feel crowded, but it's laid out logically and has plenty of services. The terminals are connected so it's easy to switch between them. Be sure to leave some extra time, as security lines can get long during peak hours. Once past security, there are all the typical airport amenities like restaurants, coffee shops, bars and stores. The Hudson News bookstores are a nice respite. WiFi is available throughout the airport, though it can sometimes be spotty in more remote areas.For domestic flights, I recommend getting to the airport at least 1.5 hours before your departure time. For international flights, aim for 2 hours to allow a bit more buffer. The Skyway people mover shuttles between terminals are very helpful for getting around.Parking options include short term and economy lots near the terminals, as well as larger long term facilities with shuttle service. Rates are comparable to other major airports. Pay machines accept coins, bills and credit cards.Gate areas are spacious and there are usually power outlets available. Signage around the airport is very good for navigating your way to check-in, security, gates and baggage claim. Escalators and moving sidewalks help with moving between floors.The terminals themselves feel modern and well maintained. Cleaning staff keep things tidy. When weather permits, there are nice views of the airfield from the large windows throughout. Airport staff are friendly and helpful.Overall, CLT is an efficient, user-friendly airport. With its size, there is plenty to see and do while waiting for flights. Free WiFi makes it easy to stay connected on the go. Even with delays, the facilities help make extended layovers more comfortable.

My great grandmother's sauce was the first I remember, she never opened a can to make her sauces, always using tomatoes she canned herself in mason jars. She simmered her sauces until every seed melted away. My mother's sauce was a bit more thicker, using puree and paste as a base, later adding whole peeled tomatoes, garlic and fresh basil. Her sauce cooks down to a velvety pasta sauce that should be jarred and sold on super market shelves. Sorry on to my review of Olive Garden. seriously? Really? No! I will admit it's good in a fit of really, REALLY needing a pasta fix, or if you want to eat breadstick and salad. But the sauces are overly rich, and I don't mean the tomato sauces. I mean the sauces they put over the pasta with chicken, beef or fish. And, let me be real Italian here, pasta is NEVER the main meal in an Italian supper, Pasta is normally the first course and NEVER served with meat, including MEATBALLS. Thats as American as fortune cookies. after pasta, comes the protein, that includes meatballs, then finally salad. Okay, I'm done being a snooty Italian who looks down upon Olive Garden, I got out all my frustrations on you, my readers. But seriously, if you want good Italian food, hit up a REALLY good neighborhood, family owned Italian restaurant. The service is better, it will be cheaper and it won't go to a big conglomerate who over charges on a plate of pasta, which is one of the cheapest food you can serve. Oh, two stars for a pretty good bowl of Pasta Fazoo (pasta and beans).
