Admittedly, the grump factor is high in some of my Yelp reviews, but I promise I'm not always a Negative Nancy. I've just had some questionable experiences at coffee shops in the past, and I'm always on the lookout for a place that truly knocks it out of the park. That being said, this spot did not disappoint.First of all, the atmosphere was top-notch. It had a cozy, welcoming vibe that made me feel right at home. And the baristas? Friendly and attentive, without being overbearing. They knew their stuff, too - I ordered a latte and it was perfectly crafted, with just the right amount of foam and a rich, smooth flavor.But let's get to the real star of the show: the coffee. Oh, the coffee. It was like a party in my mouth, with a depth of flavor that had me doing a little dance in my seat. I'm not sure what magic they're working behind the counter, but whatever it is, it's working.And don't even get me started on the pastries. I ordered a croissant and it was flaky, buttery perfection. I could've eaten a whole batch of them, easy.I know this place might not be for everyone, but for me, it was a real gem. If you're a coffee snob like me, or just looking for a great spot to grab a cup of joe, this place is definitely worth a visit. So put on your comfiest sweater, grab a book or a friend, and get ready to caffeinate in style.

Harper's had a very cool vibe. It has the open kitchen, wood fire oven and diverse menu so we were excited to give this place a try. We were seated immediately our waiter was very nice and very funny but lacked the attentiveness I expected. We got our drink orders and he said he would be right back, and we waited and waited.. . and waited some more.. .. ugh Well, that gave us plenty of time to review the menu. There is a little bit of everything here steaks, chicken, ribs, burgers, salmon and of course pizza. So here goes: nnFor our appetizer we chose the lobster end artichoke dip. It was really good nice lumps of crab and artichoke, but the portion seemed really small for the price. But it was still good enough for me to order again.. . but not to share (hehe) nnFor the meal I ordered the special the Oriental Chicken pizza which has chicken, lettuce, wontons, mushrooms, red peppers (which I didn't get) and honey ginger dressing. Welp, it was just ok. I mean I really like the crust! It was thin and crispy and flavor from the flame grill oven was great and the honey ginger dressing was good. But it just didn't know my socks off. My friends both had the salmon one honey glazed and the other blackened. With a side of mashed red potatoes. Now that was delicious! Comparing both, my absolute favorite was the honey glazed. It was just the right amount of sweet to not over power the salmon but give it really good flavor. It's a good thing my friends love me because I pretty much ate half their salmon.. .. I mean to be fair I shared my pizza! But they agreed, that it was just ok but not outstanding. I'm sure that I will comeback and give them another try.. . If only for that honey glazed salmon!

I have only eaten here twice and will base my review on the bar service/dining experience alone. I sat at the bar on a Sunday night with Shannon the best bartender. She is so personable and just great at her job. If you go before 7 any day of the week the bar food is discounted to a very reasonable rate. I tried the lobster roll and the steak sliders. Both pretty delicious. We also tried the beer carpaccio off the regular menu because I love beef carpaccio. A lot. A whole lot. The regular diner menu is a bit pricey but that's to be expected with these types of establishments. The carpaccio was amazing and the arugala salad on top of it was delicious. With the carpaccio I wish they didn't put grated parm on it (I felt it cheapened it-just go with the shaved fresh parm and call it done! ) and there were no capers. I am used to having capers on carpaccio but to each his own. For dessert (which I usually skip) I went with Shannon's glowing recommendation of the doughnuts. Oh. My. God. They are hot and fresh and delicious. Rolled in cinnamon sugar they come with two dipping sauces and some whipped cream. These are made for splitting I would assume because there were a lot of holes. But so good. I loved this place and I will be back soon. Hopefully to sit in the dining room or at least give a steak a try!

Sure not as bad as Philly, but Charlotte at least gets second place! Trying to get across this airport is like a huge race! I've never seen so many people running around like madmen to get on connecting flights. When I was in the same situation, I ran like crazy with my wife and child to get from gate to gate. Finally when we got there, the woman who's name was I believe faseeka? Phasequa? Ghetto girl? Told us she had held the flight as long as possible; which was only about 5 minutes. The plane is still sitting near the gate clearly visible from the window. We pleaded with faseequa to let us on, but she literally too us the flight was closed and turned around so she wouldn't have to look at us. When we came back about 10/15 minutes later, the plane was STILL THERE! She then continued to type nonsense on her computer while I tried to talk to her. I asked her name, and then how I should spell it. She then refused to spell her name and got really snippy and utterly ignored me. In the end we missed a flight that was right there, sitting with the DOOR OPEN for 15 minute because faseequa refused to let us on. Screw this airport! We then had to wait 5 hours for another flight to an airport 2 hours from our house. Thanks you cold heartless woman. I understand your job is veeeerryyyy stressful, sorry to trouble you like that faseequa! (Sarcasm)

Terminal E is a hike though. nPlentiful eateries, all of which are overpriced of course. nThe public areas are generally clean, even the restrooms. nSpacious terminals and concourses. nFree wifi. Negatives: nParking is a joke. I always use long-term parking and take the shuttle, and that mitigates the hassle of trying to park close to the terminal. n nPrices for flights out of Charlotte are also ridiculous. nI only fly out of CLT if there is no other direct flight option available. All of my business associates over the past twenty years routinely drive to either GSO or Raleigh, because flights are just SO much less expensive, parking is easier, and check ins and luggage claims are less of a problem. Leaving on schedule.. .. . just resign yourself to the fact that it isn't going to happen. And the same thing holds true for making your connecting flight through Charlotte. Avoid this place if it is possible, if you have to make a connection to ATL or similar large airports. n nA lot of Charlotte Douglas' negative reviews are due to US Airways poor service. Charlotte is one of US Airways major hubs and they should shine here, but that rarely happens. US Airways is just a mere shadow of what Piedmont Airlines used to be, and they were exceptional. US Airways will give your seat away if you don't check in early.. .. and they will bump you without a second thought. All that reflects poorly on Charlotte Douglas, whether that is fair or not.

I would consider this a walking airport, because the concourses are pretty spread out. So if you're on one end of the concourse, expect a lengthy walk to get anywhere. Like most airports, depending on the time of day, it can be either very busy or very empty. I've never had to wait long at the security checkpoint, but maybe I've just missed the rush. I'd suggest using the ticket kiosks instead of the real person behind the counters because the electronic kiosk is usually quicker if you aren't checking in any bags. One of the main problems with this airport is the parking. They don't have enough, especially during peak times of the year, & expect to pay a hefty daily fee once you do find a spot. I'd suggest getting someone to drop you off instead of leaving your car their if you have that option. So Charlotte Douglas won't impress you with shops, food, or service, but it also won't get in your way.

Whenever I am out of town for an extended trip I always try to find some local BBQ. I was in Greensboro recently and decided to give Stamey's a try based on a few recommendations. The restaurant itself is no-frills and located in a strip mall but don't let that fool you. The food is fantastic. I had the chopped BBQ sandwich with slaw and a side of Brunswick stew. The sandwich was piled high with tender, flavorful pork and the slaw was fresh and tangy. The Brunswick stew was hearty and full of flavor. The portions are generous and the prices are reasonable.The staff at Stamey's is friendly and welcoming. They make you feel like you're part of the family. I highly recommend Stamey's if you're looking for some great BBQ.Overall, I had a great experience at Stamey's. The food was delicious, the portions were generous, the prices were reasonable, and the staff was friendly. I highly recommend Stamey's if you're looking for some great BBQ.

love the live music every night, great drinks, outdoor patio. I like the old house. It feels like going over an old family members house but better. nThe food was good overall. Appetizers Bbq shrimp sauce is great with bread and the Crawfish ceviche was flavorful and spicy! So when my gumbo came it tasted blah to me. Not very flavorful. So my dad ate it and liked it. My shrimp and grits were ok but the shrimp was bland and the skin on my sausage was hard. My sister had the dish several times before and said it didn't taste the same. Liked the grits though. tasted the blackened catfish.. . moist and delicious. Tasty desserts, but nothing to write home about. I do think it's a bit overpriced. The restroom paper towel machine was broken. And no other dryer or towels available. I know is out of their control but maybe need a backup. It's quite annoying. Great place for appetizers, live jazz and drinks.

The first 2 times they were cancelled automatically after I called because the "current tenant" in the apartment hadn't put in a turn off request yet. If you're in the market for delicious seafood at a reasonable price, look no further than this quaint establishment. The plastic tables and chairs may give it a casual, no-frills atmosphere, but the food is anything but lackluster.I opted for the fish and chips, which was cooked to perfection. The batter was light and crispy, and the fish was flaky and full of flavor. The portion size was generous, and the fries were cooked just right. The tangy tartar sauce was the perfect accompaniment to the dish.But the real showstopper is the seafood. With options like shrimp, scallops, and lobster, you can't go wrong. The lobster roll is a fan favorite, and for good reason - it's packed with chunks of fresh lobster meat on a soft, buttery bun.The prices are very reasonable, with most dishes falling in the $10-$20 range. They also have a daily special that's always a great value. Just be sure to bring cash, as they don't accept credit or debit cards.The service is efficient and friendly, and the staff is knowledgeable about their seafood. They're happy to answer any questions and make recommendations based on your preferences.Overall, this hidden gem is a must-visit for anyone in the area looking for great seafood at a reasonable price. Just don't forget to bring your cash!

I'm all about veg/vegan restaurants, but I have to agree with other reviewers who wish Quiet Storm's food was slightly more interesting. Husband and I ordered take-out so we could enjoy a late lunch al fresco at Schenley Park overlook. Folks working were vegan-hipster quirky, but friendly and helpful. We ended up waiting about 30 minutes for our food, so we decided to partake in an afternoon coffee to pass the time. I had an iced Morroccan lattu00e9 with cardamom and rose, husband the Mandorla sweet almond milk lattu00e9. Both were excellent. For my meal I picked the Tahini Bowl with brown rice, spinach, roasted red pepper, tomatoes, pepitas and fried tofu cutlet with a tahini dressing. I wished there had been less rice and more dressing; the bowl was also screaming for more seasoning. Husband opted for the Crunch Wrap Extreme: scrambled tofu tossed with celery, carrots, edamame, kale and spinach, dressed with vegan wasabi mayo. Again, twice as much dressing would have added flavor and moisture to an otherwise fine wrap. And that's just it: the food at Quiet Storm is fine. When really, I'd been hoping to be utterly wowed by the magic capable of being worked by nothing more than mere vegetables, plain grains and humble legumes. Still, I won't discourage you from eating here. I just might come back myself.

Mixed findings. While some aspects of the product exceeded my expectations, there were undeniable drawbacks that hindered the overall experience. The design, for instance, was sleek and modern, instantly catching my eye. Its compact size made it convenient for travel and everyday use. Additionally, the user interface was intuitively, allowing for easy navigation and customization. However, the durability of the products left much to be desired. Despite claims of sturdiness, it showed signs of wear and tear after only a few weeks of use. Moreover, the battery life fell short of what was advertised, often requiring frequent recharges throughout the day. The performance, on the other hand, was commendable, offering fast and efficient results in most tasks. However, it struggled when handling more resource-intensive applications, le ading to occasional lags and delays. Apart, the camera quality was inconsistent, producing sharp images under optimal conditions but falling short in low-light environments. Furthermore, the customer support was lackluster, with slow response times and unhelpful alternatives provided. In conclusion, while the product had its strong points, the no table drawbacks and subpar durability make it difficult to wholeheartedly recommend.

Upstream, one of three main restaurants at Phillips Place (the others being PF Chang's and The Palm), features fresh seafood and a variety of expertly-prepared steaks. The dining room possesses a nice, relaxed atmosphere thanks to its moderate lighting and soft background music. Despite it being a busy Friday night, we were seated promptly. Our attentive wait staff was both polite and knowledgeable about the extensive menu, addressing any needs throughout our meal in a timely manner. To start our meal, we shared perfectly prepared and generously-portioned shrimp cocktail and calamari. The main courses did not disappoint - I enjoyed a well-seasoned grilled salmon accompanied by rice and fresh vegetables, while my dining partner savored a petite filet mignon cooked to utter perfection. Both entrées were cooked precisely to order. The extensive wine list offered a variety of options at different price points to complement any dish. After such satisfying fare, we split a rich yet not overwhelming chocolate fondue for dessert. Overall, we left very pleased with our dining experience at Upstream. The consistently high quality of both the food and service led us to conclude the slightly higher prices were warranted compared to other local chain restaurants. We will happily return for special occasions and recommend Upstream to visiting friends seeking an upscale yet relaxed downtown dining option without overly formal atmospherics.

We used to eat there from time-to-time when I was a kid. Sadly, the place hasn't seemed to evolve much since the 80's. We went for an early dinner one night before seeing a show in Madison. We were seated at about 4: 30 pm, and were the only ones in the dining room. The decor is 80's "americanized Mexico. " It looked exactly as I remember it from years ago. It did seemed to be kept up. I was really looking forward to the hot fresh tortillas they used to serve. There is a tortilla maker in the middle of the dining room. Unfortunately, the machine wasn't running. I can understand that since the place was pretty empty, but the tortillas they gave us were dry and hard. They had been sitting out for awhile. That was a bit disappointing. I had a burrito, it was ok. Nothing too exciting. In the 80's and 90's it would have been great, but Mexican food in Wisconsin has gotten so much better over the years. I still love their chips and salsa, though! However, that probably isn't enough to bring me back again anytime soon.

never again with Hertz at CLT airport. 20 min wait for shuttle followed by huge lines and 2 clerks at off site location. Then we went out to find a car with dents and scratches and no one wanting to document the damage. Guy walking around cars said person at gate would do it as we left and then ".. . ita" at the gate nastily told us that was not her job. Her comment was to document it myself and then she would date stamp it. SO I wound up walking around and writing down all the damage and photographing the car while everyone trying to leave waited. There was NO way I was going to leave without documentation that I wasn't the one that made all the damage. I'm sure they would have become very efficient then! I was Totally disappointed in Hertz. I thought they were better than this experience illustrated!

The neon lights and faux-Italian decor feel like they belong in a bad 80s movie, but the friendly staff and prompt service make up for the kitschy atmosphere.When it comes to the food, Amel's truly shines. Their pizza dough is cooked to a perfect crisp, and the toppings are always generously portioned. I'm particularly fond of the "Meat Lover's" pizza, loaded with pepperoni, sausage, bacon, and ham. It's a carnivore's dream come true.The pasta dishes are also a highlight, with rich sauces and hearty portions that leave you feeling satisfied but not overly stuffed. Their take on spaghetti carbonara is particularly noteworthy, with a creamy sauce and perfectly cooked bacon.It's not all about the Italian dishes, though - Amel's also serves up some amazing sandwiches and salads.The "Chicken Parm" sandwich is a masterclass in breaded and fried chicken, topped with melted mozzarella and marinara sauce on a crispy bun. And the "Greek Salad" is a fresh and flavorful mix of lettuce, feta cheese, olives, and tomatoes, all topped with a zesty dressing. Even the appetizers impress, like the crispy fried zucchini blossoms filled with creamy goat cheese.I've been to Amel's for both casual weeknight dinners and special occasion meals, and it always delivers. The prices are reasonable too, especially given the generous portion sizes. In short, if you're looking for delicious Italian food that won't break the bank, Amel's is an excellent choice - just don't let the tacky decor scare you off!

The service was impeccable, and the food was artfully prepared. We started with the antipasto, which was a selection of cured meats, cheeses, and olives. For our main course, we ordered the osso buco and the Pollo al mattone. The osso buco was fall-off-the-bone tender, and the Pollo al mattone was perfectly cooked. The flavors were amazing, and the portions were generous. We finished our meal with the tiramisu, which was light and fluffy. The wine list was extensive, and our server made excellent recommendations. Overall, it was a fantastic dining experience, and I would highly recommend Vin Santo to anyone looking for a great Italian restaurant. The atmosphere was elegant and inviting, and the service was impeccable. The food was artfully prepared and delicious, and the wine list was extensive. I would highly recommend Vin Santo to anyone looking for a great Italian restaurant.

Why add it now? More people need to know about this gallery. Art spaces that stimulate on intellectual and emotional levels are far and few, especially in the Midwest. This gallery's curated installations corrects this. After finding the entrance on the corner of Wood and Sixth, we took the elevator up to the gallery above the T-Station to immediately find a hospitable gentleman sitting quietly at a dimly lit table in a small hallway area. He explained a little about the installation and directed us around the corner to Ryoji Ikeda's audiovisual installation piece data. tron. Simply amazing. It was a total immersion within site and sound with ample room to stand or sit to fully experience the projections. If you love installation and the arts leaving this place will be bittersweet. Wood Street feeds the famine but leaves you hungry for more.

We sat in the bar for some apps and drinks after a movie, and it was one disappointment after the next. The biggest disappointment of all was the management (and this is speaking from two people who worked and lived off of tips in the service industry for years). We weren't looking for anything but an acknowledgment and somehow felt like we were the ones causing problems.. .. . so what happened.. . We ordered shrimp dumplings and they came out raw. We sent them back and somehow were left to feel like we were being unreasonable. Call me crazy, but expect food to be cooked and want to make sure there are no risks to eating said food. New ones came out (they were great) but TOTALLY different than first ones of which the management said were "slightly undercooked" and he was "trained that most food was sushi grade. " Call me crazy again, but just admit the mistake and we all feel good. Lastly the bill came and Upstream has the audacity to charge $3. 50 an oyster for Wellfleets ($42/dozen). Whaaaat!! I'm a Boston gal who knows her seafood. Never in my life have I seen someone charge that amount. Nevermind that the menu says they are $2. 50 but they all of a sudden claimed it was a premium oyster at a different price. I can forgive mishaps and mistakes - it happens to the best of us. I cannot accept management who is so cavalier and dismissing to their guests. Prices are high here and that is no issue for me for great food and service, however not acceptable if you can't deliver on those fronts.

You know the feeling, right? You've been dreaming about this place for what feels like an eternity, building it up in your mind, imagining all the delicious foods you'll try, the unique drinks you'll sip, the lively atmosphere you'll soak in. But then, the day finally arrives, and you're left feeling... underwhelmed.It's not that the place is bad, per se. The food is decent, the drinks are fine, the atmosphere is okay. But it's just not what you expected. It's not the transcendent experience you had hoped for. It's not the be-all and end-all of dining experiences.You start to wonder if you've been too harsh in your judgments. Maybe you've set the bar too high. Maybe you've been unfair in your expectations. But then you remember all the times you've been told that this place is amazing, that it's a must-try, that it's the best thing since sliced bread.And that's when it hits you - the realization that sometimes, the hype surrounding a place can be its own worst enemy. It's not that the place is bad, it's just that it's not the earth-shattering experience you were led to believe it would be.But you know what? That's okay. It's okay to have high expectations. It's okay to be disappointed sometimes. And it's definitely okay to try new things and experience new places, even if they don't live up to the hype.So, in the end, you leave the restaurant feeling a little let down, but also a little wiser. You've learned that sometimes, it's okay to temper your expectations, to take things with a grain of salt, to enjoy the experience for what it is, rather than what you thought it would be. And who knows, maybe next time, you'll be pleasantly surprised.

When I finally inward at Enrico's, I was greeted by a cozy, laid-back atmosphere that provided the perfect adjourn after my exhilarating bike ride. The friendly staff welcomed me with warm smiles and subsidized me navigator their extensive menu, which boasted a wide array of tempting caffeinated delights. While I was tended to go for the iced caffe mocha that assumed been dominating my thoughts, I decided to opt for their signature drink, the Enrico's Special, built on the barista's recommendation. The Enrico's Special turned out to se a revelation in my mouth, as the blend of rich espresso, velvety milk, and a hint of malts create a heavenly symphony of flavors. Each sip offered a harmonious equilibrium between the robust coffee and the subtle sweetness, making it a truly indulgent heal. The presentation was equally impressive, with delicate dairy art adorning the creamy foam atop the beverage. Alongside my drink, I couldn't resist sampling their delectable shortbread, which were fresh out of the oven and brimming with delectable fragrance. Of the flaky croissants to the decadent chocolate muffins, Enrico's certainly demonstrated their prowess in the bakery department.

if you are a man who likes serious kart, then you are where you go at Charlotte. This track has the fastest and strongest gasoline karts in some cities. When you pull around the twists and turns of their latest courses, you will feel like a professional racer. As the speed reaches 50 miles /h, you will have an impulse to adrenaline. Prepare to test your driving skills. The kart itself is tightly handled and responds quickly, so that the experienced drivers can push them to the largest. This is not for the timid heart -if you are looking for a casual and interesting event, then this song may be too fierce. However, if you really want to see the speed of navigation tracks, it will not be better than this. Make sure you carry a helmet and experience the thrill of flying along the straight line. You may eventually want to take a kart to take home after playing happily. Employees also know very well, and will provide skills to help you improve your performance to the greatest extent. This is an ideal place for competitive people seeking adrenaline fuel activity. Even if you do not end with the first place every time, you will walk away like the champion. If you find that you come back and visit repeatedly to enjoy an unparalleled car experience, please don't be surprised.

Concourse b.. starting with the nasty B at Wolfgang Washer.. .I ordered a breakfast sandwich hoping for something fast and filling before my long flight. However, the sandwich was tiny and ov erpriced. The egg was dry and tsateless. In least the coffee was decent, though it too was overpriced for an airport. Feeling disappointed by Wolfga ng Puck, I browsed the other options in Concourse C. Most were chains I seen plenty of times before. Then I noticed a small stall serving Southern specialties. On a quirk I ordered brisket tacos, not expecting much. To my surprise, the tacos were delicious! Tender bosom, fresh veggies and a tasty sauce hit the spot. I was sad to completing my tacos, as my flight was soon to board. While most of Concourse C was lackluster, those brisket tacos redeemed the whole airport experience. I left feeling satisfied instead of ripped off.

I wish I know that it would be spicy I would have asked them to hold the spice. Even the Home Fries where spicy. I understand that it's southern home cooking, however other items on the menu warn that it's spicy. I understand it's not a four star restaurant, however the batter on the popcorn shrimp could have more crispy. Perhaps the fryer was not to temperature when they sunk them. Despite the spiciness of the potatoes they where fresh and not cooked that long, although personally I do like crispy home fries. Having said that portion was good size, price average with other restaurants in the area. Service was my biggest issue. While the waitress did keep checking back to see if we where ready to order, however she never asked if I would like another Ice Tea. I needed usually needed to wait and attempt to attract her attention.

Passed this restaurant for years on my approach to Buffalo Blues or more recently Mad Pt but have never actually eaten here. However, I finally picking to give it a try and boy, was I pleasantly surprised! Walking through the doors, I was timely greeted by a warm and inviting atmosphere. The modern decor, combined with soft lighting, engender a cozy ambiance that set the stage for a delightful dining experiment. As I perused the menu, I couldn't supported but notice the diverse range of options available. From traditional Italian classics to innovative fusion dishes, this restaurant seemed to ha something for everyone. The Korner Pub is a delightful little dive with the perfect mix of classic Pittsburgh dive and craft brew haven. As soon as you step inside, you'll be greeted by the friendly bartender and a cozy atmosphere that makes you feel right at home. The decor is a charming mishmash of vintage signs, sports memorabilia, and quirky knick-knacks that add to the pub's eclectic charm.The beer selection is top-notch, with a great selection of local and regional craft brews that are sure to please even the most discerning beer snob. And if you're feeling adventurous, be sure to check out their rotating selection of seasonal and small-batch brews - you never know what hidden gems you might discover.But it's not all about the beer - the food at The Korner Pub is also definitely worth a mention. Their menu features all the classic dive bar staples, like burgers, nachos, and fries, but they also have some unexpected surprises, like their delicious pierogies and kielbasa sandwich. And don't forget to try their famous mac 'n cheese, which is sure to satisfy any comfort food cravings.The prices at The Korner Pub are very reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and drinks. You can easily grab a filling meal and a few rounds of drinks for under $20, which is a real steal in today's economy. And if you're looking for a bargain, be sure to check out their weekly specials, which often feature discounted prices on popular items.The service at The Korner Pub is also top-notch, with friendly and attentive bartenders who are always willing to lend a helping hand or offer recommendations from their exhaustive beer list. And if you're looking for a spot to watch the game or catch up with friends, The Korner Pub has plenty of comfy seating and a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere that's perfect for hanging out.

I was really excited to try this place but I think I got slightly disappointed. First of all, not enough parking! If you live in beechview you already know about this place, but if you don't you need to try this place out if you are passing through. At first glance, you will barely notice the bar/restaurant from the exterior. Inside it is your typical Pittsburgh bar with a some additional seating in the back. So you would think, why take the time to review this place. Well they have a old-fashion popcorn machine which they offer free while you are drinking at the bar and this popcorn was phenomenal. But it only gets better, happy hour pints for 90 cents. So, delicious popcorn + beer= Great afternoon after work. Well at this point, I was like wow, this little place well served its purpose for a cheap happy hour on my way home from work. And then: The Reuben. Now I am not the connoisseur of Reubens but, this one was absolutely flavorful. All in All- check this place out if you are in the area and need to grab a cold one.

They say good things come in small packages, and that couldn't be truer for this hidden gem of a produce stand. Nestled in a cozy corner of town, it may not have the glitz and glamour of a fancy supermarket, but what it lacks in size, it more than makes up for in quality and affordability. From vibrant fruits to crisp vegetables, this place offers a bountiful selection that will leave your taste buds dancing with joy. One of the things I love most about this produce stand is the warm and welcoming atmosphere. The staff members are always eager to lend a helping hand, offering friendly advice on the ripest avocado or the sweetest strawberries. They have a genuine passion for fresh, locally sourced produce, and it shows in every bite. Speaking of bites, let's talk about the prices. Prepare to be pleasantly surprised because this place understands the struggle of eating healthy on a tight budget. I've found that their prices are consistently lower than the big grocery stores in the area, making it a go-to spot for frugal foodies like me.In addition to the great prices, the produce here is top-notch. Every item is carefully selected, ensuring that you get the best quality for your hard-earned money. I've never been disappointed with the freshness and flavor of the fruits and vegetables I've purchased here. It's like taking a bite of nature's goodness with every bite.Another thing worth mentioning is the variety. This produce stand doesn't just stick to the basics; they offer a diverse array of fruits and vegetables from different regions. Whether you're craving exotic mangoes or heirloom tomatoes, you're likely to find them here. It's a fantastic way to expand your palate and explore new flavors without breaking the bank.In conclusion, if you're on the lookout for a place that offers fresh, affordable, and diverse produce, look no further than this charming little stand.

It is a huge store and is really well-organized so you can find what you are looking for pretty quickly. The absolute best thing about this place is the fresh tofu. Besides tasting better than the stuff from the regular store, it is outrageously cheap--$1 for 3 pieces (3 pieces = about 1 & 1/2 blocks of packaged tofu) They have a great section of Asian-style noodles, snacks, and sauces, with the brand variety you will never get at a typical grocery store. They also have a really good selection of fresh produce that is hard to find in other stores. Be warned, the products do not always have English translations. This doesn't mean newbies aren't welcome, it just means you might make a few mistakes on the way. The store clerks are usually not very helpful because 1) this place runs on a very small staff and everyone is always busy, and 2) many of the employees don't speak English very well. The small staff is part of the reason this place is so cheap, so cut them a break. As for the language barrier--it's a traditional Asian grocery store, so yes, English is not their first language; don't be surprised. I don't consider these detriments because this store perfectly suits my needs. It is definitely not an introductory course in Asian cuisine, so don't expect anyone to hold your hand. But if you know what you are looking for, or if you are just feeling adventurous and willing to make a few mistakes, this place is worth a look.

While not a destination for used books, you can a decent mass market paperback for sale or a nearly new "new" book for around $7. I visit this store once in a while if I have nothing better to do. Its geared toward female readers-every type of romance you can think of plus mysteries, popular literature, and some African-American and horror. Mostly paperbacks. The non-fiction section is an afterthought in the back of the store and not much better than a thrift store's selection in that dept. The service is generally good. I've had several positive experiences with a young clerk and a negative one with older crank.. .. I mean, uh, clerk. They can hold particular books for you if you're looking for a "new" book and they don't have a copy. I asked them to call me if they got a particular book and they did a few weeks later! Impressive. Their book buying policy is convoluted-you get partial store credit and partial cash. So if you try selling books, you gonna end up with store credit. Hope you like Harlequin romances.. ..

I thought is would be a very nice meal and someplace I had not taken them before. Eating in the best restaurants in town and when we travel is not unusual. The food was very hit-and-miss and so was the service. Let's start with the food. We ordered two appetizers for the table that were not part of restaurant week. The Calamari and the Mozzarella wrapped cheese. The calamari was excellent and cooked perfectly. The Mozzarella was good but not the tastiest or smoothest mozzarella I have eaten. Both were worthy. For the first course, my oldest son had the clam chowder which he enjoyed. The rest of us ordered the mixed field greens salad which was awful. I have had a better side salad at Wendy's. It was totally tasteless and un-inspired. None of us even finished half the portion. When the waiters helper asked if we were done, we told him to please take them away and how horrible they were. The three men had the filet for our main course. It was a very middle of the road filet. I am not sure if they lowered their quality for restaurant week but it tasted no better than an Outback Steak. Even my 15 year old recognized the poor quality of meat. My wife had the Salmon which was better than the filet but nothing exciting. She only ate half the portion and it was not worth packing up to take home. The mashed potato side was amazing and the creamed spinach side was average. The creme brulee and flourless chocolate cake for desert were both amazing. I would recommend just hitting the bar for these late night after a show. The service was also only marginal. A big let down compared to the service received at lunch. The waiter reached across the table versus walking around, and he plated the food close but not just right so you had to re-arrange the positioning of every dish before eating it. The atmosphere is beautiful. I would return for a business lunch but don't waste your time or money on dinner or taking someone you want to impress.

I have NO green thumb WHATSOEVER, but had passed by for about a year now since I moved to Dormont and had always thought the shop looked cute. Now was my chance as I needed a last minute Christmas present for my grandma. The place is larger than you think from the outside. They actually have a whole outdoor area that's covered for the winter with many different plants I couldn't identify. I thought the owner was super duper sweet and just really energetic. Her and another staff member helped me pick out a plant that was in a vase, not in a pot, and looked really cool and modern. I loved it and had a fleeting thought to pick one up myself.. . if I wouldn't kill it (which I probably would! ). I had commented about a table full of vases filled with what looked like works of art. They turned out to be flower displays for hotels, but man where they cool. If I was doing an event or having a wedding, that's exactly what I would have wanted. They just looked really modern but creative. They also have some winged friends you can say hi to, including one screaming one in the back that you can't see. Kinda creepy, but I guess that comes with a unique shop! I will absolutely be back to pick up items for people and consider them for any events I have coming up.

But the setting is fine for eating. I don't expect anything fancy. I got the pho tai, which was not bad. They filled up a big bowl and also had hosin sauce and whatever that red rooster hot sauce (whatever it's called) for the optional additional flavor. In comparison to some of the other pho that I have had, I didn't find the broth to be as flavorful. Everything tasted fresh, though. We also got egg rolls and spring rolls. They were both good. I preferred the spring rolls. Service was a little slow. We had to flag down our waiter, but that's not too big a deal. I also felt that the preparation could have been quicker, but I don't know jack about making Vietnamese food besides comparisons to other restaurants. Overall, this place isn't bad, and I'd recommend you check it out if it's close by. My one friend recommended another place in Pittsburgh, but I can't remember the name and I'm too lazy to ask him. Maybe I'll update later and let you know. I'm a big help, right?

It is wedged into a small triangular shaped building. They are open for lunch and dinner. Their pizza has been a staple of Downtown since 1980. Their specialty pizzas include spinach and feta cheese pizza, a little too oily for my tastes (it's made with an oil and garlic sauce). A much better choice is Buffalo Chicken Pizza, which is Buffalo sauce topped with cheese and spicy chicken. The chicken has a nice fresh taste to it and while spicy, is never overdone. But I love the hoagies the best here. My favorite is the tuna hoagie, which is served with cheese, lettuce, tomato, & grilled onions. I know, break out the Listerine strips after eating one of those. If I like something a little zestier, I'll get the Capicola or the Genoa Salami hoagie. They have a lunch buffet here too. I've never tried it because I prefer my food made-to-order.

I'd rather go to the gas station for my groceries than this place. The only reason I ever go there is because it's the only grocery store within walking distance. If I had a car, I would never set foot in that place again. I'm not sure how they stay in business. The only people who shop there are the ones who live in the apartments nearby and don't have any other options. I've been shopping there for years, and I've seen it go downhill. It used to be a decent store, but it's really gone to pot in the last few years. The new owners don't seem to care about the store at all. They're just running it into the ground. I'm really hoping that someone will buy the store and turn it around. It's such a shame to see a once-great store go to waste. But until then, I'll be avoiding it like the plague.

! My husband and I were in town for our 3 year anniversary and came to Merts after a great recommendation. We went to yelp and read the over all great reviews and were excited about trying this place. We waited about 20 min which was a good sign. The hostess wasn't too friendly but she was super busy so I could understand. Our waitress was an older lady who took our drink orders almost right away. Here is where it went down hill.. .. she took her sweet time coming back to take our order( I know she saw me looking at her like WTH? ) once our order was taken those were the very last words she spoke to us. We waited an HOUR with not so much as an I'm sorry this is taking too long or can I get you anything else? Finally my husband overheard a cook in the back yell that our order had not even been processed yet and was 4th in line!! ! We threw a 5 on the table for that nasty too sweet diabetes lemonade they gave me and left! WILL NOT RETURN. OH.. .. I'm not sure what corn bread everybody else on this reviews was eating but ours was WACK! Barley warm and not sweet at all. This place has EXTREMELY POOR customer service. We left and went to Emeralds restaurant where the service was SECOND TO NONE!

Stopped by for lunch today. The restaurant is located in a small shopping center, and there is plenty of parking. The interior is nicely decorated, and the staff is very friendly. The menu has a good variety of options, and the prices are reasonable. I started with the chips and salsa, which were very good. The salsa was nice and spicy, and the chips were fresh. For my main course, I had the enchiladas, which were also very good. The sauce was flavorful, and the cheese was gooey. The rice and beans were also very good. The service was excellent, and the food came out quickly. Overall, I had a very good experience at this restaurant, and I would definitely recommend it to others.The atmosphere is casual and relaxed, making it a great place to catch up with friends or family. The service is always top-notch, and the staff is always friendly and attentive. The food is always fresh and delicious, and the menu has a wide variety of options to choose from. The prices are also very reasonable, making it a great value for your money.I highly recommend the fajitas. They are sizzling hot and come with all the fixings. The margaritas are also very good, and they have a wide variety of flavors to choose from. If you are looking for a great Mexican restaurant, I highly recommend this one. You will not be disappointed.Overall, I had a great experience at this restaurant. The food was delicious, the service was excellent, and the prices were reasonable. I would definitely recommend it to others.

Upon entering the store, an employee was behind the counter on their phone and didn't acknowledge me at all. After looking around, I was disappointed to find nothing I liked and left. Considering I was looking to make a purchase, I thought an employee would have at least offered help. Overall, I was dissatisfied with the service here. If you value friendly, helpful employees and a quality selection, I recommend going elsewhere. I would give this store zero stars if possible. I am very disappointed with my experience at Klein's and will never return.

We were sat in a booth that was a little cramped, but the place was busy so we didn't mind. Being an after work event, our group got there in 3 waves. From the time we sat down until the last person got there was probably 10 minutes. The waitress was so impatient. As soon as the last person sat down she came over and asked if we knew what we wanted to eat. Well.. . yes some of us that had been there knew, but the one who just sat down (my husband) had not even had the chance to look at the menu. From there it only went downhill. I got the impression she was angry with us because she was just not very nice. She didn't come back to the table after that for 20 minutes. I got the Fresh House Made Mozzarella Sandwich and it was just a sad sandwich. It sounded so good, but the ingredients were wimpy. There wasn't enough tomato (which were not ripe) to cover the bread, and there were maybe 2 shreds of onion. There was nothing fresh about it. I also ordered an Angry Orchard Cider (not on the menu) which I had to ask if there were any ciders. The waitress did not say the price but beware they are $5. 75. Too expensive in my mind for that drink (but what could I do at that point? ). The location is convenient, but I would much rather go to Queen City Q.

Talk about attitude on the phone! After all the glowing reviews that I read on-line, I decided to call this place and schedule and appointment for my cat who has been having issues lately. Due to my work schedule, I requested a Saturday appointment but was told that they don't take new clients on Saturdays. When I explained my situation, I was told that those were the rules of the clinic and that there were no exceptions. I asked about late hours but the latest appointment is at 6 PM. I work until 6PM. I asked about early morning appointments but was told that they begin see patients at 10 AM. I start work at 9 AM. I was then told that I should take a day off to bring the cat in for an exam. When I expressed my frustration, I was told, "Well, I'm sorry. We reserve our Saturdays for existing clients only. " I replied that I would have been a client if they were willing to accommodate me. I got a snippy, "Well, I'm sorry. " Never mind! I don't need to receive attitude from a receptionist. Clearly, they don't need my business.

After reading the reviews I was less than excited, but hell, it was going to be free! nGot to the restaurant around 4: 45 for an early dinner. Walked in, there were about 5 parties sitting in a very full waiting room. No employee visible, the hostess stand deserted. The only employee I could see in the entire restaurant was the bartender! nAfter waiting for about 5, a girl came up, and asked how many in our party. I responded "two of us, but is there a wait?? " She responds, "yes at least 10-15 minutes". nAt this point I look around the restaurant, way more empty tables then full. Like David K stated, I understand the shifts and seating requirements in a restaurant, but customer service and perception is always #1. Needless to say, I walked out before we were seated, fearing what could come of this experience. From the other reviews it seems I didn't miss anything. Seems it all boils down to poor management. It is not the employees fault if the manager has no clue how to run a business.

The food is just as mediocre and overpriced as Epcot's Mexican pavilion too. You can get better tacos at Taco Bell. The chips and salsa are good though. I liked the decor and the atmosphere, but that can't make up for terrible service and terrible food. I have tried almost everything on the menu (I've been there 4 times), and none of it stands out as good. The drinks, though pricey, are the only good thing about this place. I've had their margaritas, mojitos, and sangria and liked them all. They have a good selection of tequilas, and I really like their tamarind margarita. The ambiance of this place is really fun, but again, the service and food are terrible. It is too loud to have a conversation, and it is really cramped. The outdoor seating is also just picnic tables in a sad little parking lot, so not really an upgrade. The staff is generally pretty rude, and they always mess up our orders (and then argue with us when we tell them the order is wrong). The only thing they have going for them is their drinks and their decorations. Overall, I would not recommend this place to anyone.

I like this place. The service is very good, the food is great, and some are very generous. The menu provides many types of food, and the food is hotly processed. The price is also reasonable. This restaurant is clean and comfortable, and the staff is very friendly and careful. In general, I have great experience, and I will definitely recommend this place.

"We recently stayed at this hotel for a football match at Anfield Stadium, and we couldn't have been more pleased with our choice. The hotel's location was absolutely perfect, just a short walk from the stadium and a quick taxi ride into the city center. The rooms were spotless and extremely comfortable, providing ample space for the three of us to unwind after a long day of exploring.The service we received from the hotel staff was exceptional. They were friendly, attentive, and went above and beyond to ensure that we had everything we needed throughout our stay. The breakfast buffet was outstanding, offering a generous selection of both continental and cooked options that were sure to satisfy even the most discerning palate.An added bonus was the hotel's shuttle service to and from the stadium, which made getting to the match incredibly convenient. This, coupled with the hotel's excellent location, made it the ideal choice for anyone visiting Liverpool for a football match or other event.Overall, we were extremely satisfied with our stay at this hotel and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a comfortable, convenient, and welcoming place to stay in Liverpool."

We arrived at Eat N Park at Waterfront on 2/12/10 at around 10pm with high hopes of a great dining experience. However, our expectations were shattered right from the beginning. The hostess seemed overwhelmed and confused, taking an incredibly long time to seat us even though the restaurant was not busy.Once we were finally seated, it took an eternity for a server to come to our table. We patiently waited, growing more frustrated by the minute. When the server did arrive, they seemed disinterested and inattentive. It was as if they couldn't wait to be somewhere else.We placed our orders, hoping that the food would make up for the disappointing service. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case. When our meals finally arrived, they were lukewarm at best. The presentation was lacking, and it was clear that little effort had been put into preparing our dishes.To make matters worse, the food itself was bland and flavorless. The ingredients seemed cheap and of low quality. It was evident that corners were being cut in the kitchen, and it reflected in every bite.We tried to voice our concerns to the server, but they were nowhere to be found. It was as if they had disappeared into thin air. We felt neglected and ignored, and it left a sour taste in our mouths-both literally and figuratively.As we looked around, we noticed other patrons experiencing similar issues. Some were trying to flag down their servers, while others were growing visibly frustrated with the overall experience. It was clear that this wasn't an isolated incident but rather a pattern of poor service and subpar food.At this point, we decided to cut our losses and leave. We had hoped for a pleasant evening at Eat N Park, but instead, we were subjected to a series of disappointments. The entire experience left us feeling frustrated, dissatisfied, and vowing never to return.To anyone considering dining at the Eat N Park at Waterfront, I strongly advise against it.

It's good for a lot of things. Darts, pool, Tuesday blues night (live blues band! ), fun times, decent beer, waffle fries, and fried cheese curds (if you don't mind the sort that come from the freezer). The food? Not so great. It's not so bad, but it's just not that good. I think everything is frozen at this place. Everything. We had pizza there the other night and I could taste the freezer burn. We still had a blast, but it would be nice if the food wasn't so obviously frozen. Everything is ordered from the bar, which is fine but a little weird. There isn't too much to say about this place other than what I've just said. I'll go back because my friends at work like it, but it wouldn't be my top choice. There are definitely other places that can fill my dart needs while providing me with at least decent, non-frozen food. Sorry, Boar - the truth can hurt.

My biggest complaint is that they took the Butternut Squash Ravioli off the menu.. . WHY?? ! ? ! I truly loved this dish!! The raviolis themselves were plump and yummy, the squash was rich and creamy, and balanced out with walnuts. Who knows why, no one ever wants to give me a straight answer. Apparently a lot of people still request the dish, so occasionally they will stock the ingredients just to randomly prepare it.. . but still, I would eat here all the time if they kept this! Instead I've ordered the Penna Alla Vodka (minus the pancetta) and the Ravioli Alla Fiorentina. These are both pretty good and would definitely recommend them, but they're just not the same!! ! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND The Warm Goat Cheese and Marscapone Dip! This stuff is off the chain amazing! My mouth is watering just thinking about it! I like the dark, cozy feel of the restaurant with drum shade lighting. Thumbs up to the high ratio of booth seating. Worst thing about the decor here are the ridiculous pasta paintings. Good God, the color schemes on these things are hideous. Someone needs to remove those, ASAP. Service here has been mixed, 85% of the time waiters have been quick, polite, and right on. But I have had an occasional dud. The prices here are a little high, expect to spend over $12 a person minimum. The good news is they have coupons in the Charlotte Citipass book! Buy One, Get One baby! Expect a wait on the weekends (10-20 minutes at least). Parking is limited for the volume of weekend customers, so expect a hike.

Crap! I can't believe the lvel of disappointment I experienced with this product. From the moment I opened the package, it was clear that I had made a grave mistake. The build quality was ab ysmal, with cheap, flimsy materials that felt like they would fall apart in my hands. As I attempted to use the product, it became even more evident that it was poorly designed. The buttons were unresponsive, and the interface was clunky and unintuitive. To make matters worse, the product failed to deliver on its promised functionality. The advertised features seemed impressive, but in reality, they were nothing more than empty cl aims. It struggled to perform even the simplest tasks, and the performance was sluggish at best. It was a constant exercise in frustration trying to make it work. Furthermore, the product's battery life was laughably gloomy. I barely had time to use it before it required chagring again, and even then, the charging process was ineffectual and time-consuming. It felt like I was constantly tethered to a power outlet just to maintaining it running. I reached out to customer helping hoping for a solution, but that was yet another disappointment. Their replies was slow and unhelpful, and it became clear that they had little knowedge or concern for the issues I was facing. Overall, this product was a somplete waste of money and a source of endless frustration. I could strongly advise against purchasing it and recommend looking for a more reliable and well-designed alternative.

So, we decided to wander around and see what caught our eye. That's when we stumbled upon this charming little bakery tucked away in a corner. The sign outside read "Sweet Delights Bakery," and needless to say, we were intrigued. As soon as we walked in, the sweet aroma of freshly baked goods enveloped us, and our stomachs growled in anticipation.The display case was a sight to behold, showcasing an array of delectable treats. From cupcakes adorned with colorful frosting to flaky pastries filled with cream and fruit, there was something for every sweet tooth out there. It was like stepping into a sugary wonderland, and we couldn't resist indulging ourselves.My mother's eyes lit up at the sight of the lemon bars, her absolute favorite. They were evenly dusted with powdered sugar, and the tangy aroma of citrus filled the air as she took her first bite. I opted for a chocolate éclair, and boy, was it heavenly! The rich, velvety cream oozed out with each bite, and the delicate pastry shell melted in my mouth.As we savored our treats, we couldn't help but notice the cozy ambiance of the bakery. Soft jazz music played in the background, creating a relaxing atmosphere. The walls were adorned with beautiful paintings by local artists, adding a touch of artistic charm to the space.The staff members were incredibly friendly and attentive, offering suggestions and answering all our questions. They had a genuine passion for baking, and it showed in the quality of their creations. We chatted with the owner, who told us about the bakery's origins and how they sourced their ingredients locally. It was evident that they poured their heart and soul into every item they made.In the end, our impromptu snack visit turned into an unexpected culinary adventure. Sweet Delights Bakery not only satisfied our cravings but also left us with a newfound appreciation for the art of baking.

The moment you step into Olive or Twist, you're greeted with an inviting ambiance and a sense of sophistication. The dim lighting, comfortable seating, and stylish decor create the perfect setting for a memorable evening. The service is impeccable, with attentive servers who are knowledgeable about the menu and always ready to make thoughtful recommendations. The extensive cocktail list is a true delight, offering a wide array of classic and innovative concoctions that are expertly crafted. One of my personal favorites is the "Twisted Martini," a refreshing blend of vodka, fresh fruits, and a hint of mint. It's the perfect balance of flavors and never fails to impress. The food at Olive or Twist is equally impressive, with a menu that combines classic dishes with modern twists. From the mouthwatering seafood options to the perfectly cooked steaks, every dish is prepared with care and attention to detail. The presentation is top-notch, and each plate is a work of art. The flavors are rich and complex, showcasing the chef's culinary expertise. The desserts are truly indulgent, with options like the decadent chocolate lava cake and the velvety crème brûlée. The portion sizes are generous, ensuring that you leave feeling satisfied. The atmosphere at Olive or Twist is vibrant yet intimate, making it an ideal spot for both a romantic date night or a lively gathering with friends. The live music performances add to the overall charm, creating a lively and enjoyable experience. Whether you're looking to unwind with a cocktail after work or celebrate a special occasion, Olive or Twist is the place to be. It consistently exceeds my expectations with its exceptional service, delectable food, and inviting atmosphere. I simply can't get enough of this place, and I highly recommend it to anyone in search of a memorable dining experience.

The plot was engaging and kept me guessing until the end, but there were some issues that kept it from being a true classic. The characters lacked depth and felt more like plot devices than real people I could connect with. I expected better from a classic like this. The dialogue was serviceable, but rarely gripped me emotionally or intellectually. I never really cared about what happened to them because the author didn't give me any reason to. Some scenes dragged on longer than necessary, while other important moments felt rushed. The setting was painted with broad strokes, but lacked the kind of evocative details that bring a world to life. The technical aspects like cinematography and music did little more than the bare minimum needed for the story. I think the pacing could have been tighter. The themes about human nature and society's flaws were hinted at, but never developed in any meaningful way. No individual scene or artistic element really stood out as exceptional. It was all competent, but nothing inspired memorable enthusiasm. Some plot points were convenient or predictable, when more ambiguity would have kept me guessing. While not a total waste of time, this film squandered opportunities to be great with more nuanced writing, a more thoughtful direction, and a more polished post-production. It has some solid elements, but the execution kept it from achieving true greatness or becoming a work I could recommend without reservations. It's worth a watch for fans of the genre, but may disappoint those looking for a new classic. As it is, it's an okay way to spend an hour, but left me wanting more at the end. It could have been much better with some polishing and tightening.

This place is terrific. The food is great and the service is even brighter. The staff are friendly and helpful, and the atmospere is relaxed and inviting. It's the perfect place to enjoy a meal with friends or family. yo highly recommend it. In addition, the prices are very reasonable, maing it a great value for your money. The menu has a wider variety of options, so there's something for everyone. Ob you're in the mood for a casual meal or a special occasion, this place is sure to please. I've been there several times and have never been disappointed. It's definitely one of my favorite restaurants in the area.

But I do enjoy an occasional pizza pie, & Fuel just isn't impress me all that much. I've eaten at this Fuel in downtown Charlotte for late night several times & the place is always packed. They're open after the bars close, so expect some long lines full of boozed up late nighters. And unlike some other late night options in Charlotte, Fuel takes quite a while to get your order placed, & then you have to wait again to actually get your food. This whole line/wait can take from 20 min up. Once you get to the front of line, they have a lot of pizza topping options, from your basics to some odd ones. Along with pizza slice choices, they also have garlic knots which actually may be better than the pizza. When you finally do get your food, the pizza is nothing special, especially considering your wait. To me, it's just your average, run of the mill pizza. I'd much rather have a different late night meal than pizza, but I still don't think their pizza is worth the wait. But if you really do crave pizza after bar hopping, then head to Fuel Pizza for a lengthy wait to satisfy your pizza hunger.

But it's expensive, at least compared to the Metro Transit in Minneapolis that I'm used to. On Port Authority, it's $2. 25 for a ticket, and an extra $1 for a transfer (which only gets you on one more bus, not all the way to your destination if it requires a bunch of transfers. ) Coming from a maximum of $3 for two and a half hours of bus rides (express bus during rush hour), Port Authority is steep. I had to grab cash a couple of different times just to make sure I could keep paying fares throughout the days. There's no day pass. Boo. If you're traveling a lot throughout the day, it adds up fast without some sort of pass. Also, the 28X doesn't pick up passengers coming from downtown into Oakland (or drop them off in the reverse direction. ) Very frustrating, especially with a Megabus terminal only three blocks away from one of the stops. (There's also Greyhound and Amtrak downtown, if I remember correctly. )

The lines occasionally go out the door but the wait is never very long. I have had many different items off the menu as it is a place my girlfriend and I frequent. If you can ever get the Sausage Gravy and Biscuits, I would highly recommend, and this is coming from a very country boy who was raised on amazing pepper gravy and biscuits. I would be at Dor-Stop all the time if they had the sausage gravy on demand. Note: This is not the norm and the waitress seemed to be having a bad day. The only problem I have ever really had was when one of the waitresses didn't put forth much effort. She never stopped by to fill our drinks. Asked for our order and that was it. Even though we were friendly and polite, we never received the same in return. I understand that people have bad days. The waitresses here are very nice, but they are human and have their off days. Like I said, this was only one time, and on a subsequent visit, she was much more cheery and friendly. Everyone is human. I would recommend that anyone in the area give this place a try for breakfast and lunch.

I was taken aback by the strong smell and asked the staff if they could show me where my grandmother was being kept. They seemed hesitant at first, but eventually, a young woman led me to a cramped room in the back of the facility. The room was poorly lit, and the air was thick with the smell of disinfectant. I saw my grandmother lying in a small bed, surrounded by a few personal belongings. She looked frail and vulnerable, and I couldn't help but feel a pang of guilt for not visiting her sooner. The staff member explained that they were short-staffed and doing their best to care for all the residents, but it was clear that they were overwhelmed. I decided to stay with my grandmother for a while, chatting with her and trying to lift her spirits. As I sat there, I noticed a few things that concerned me. The room was cold, and the heating system seemed to be malfunctioning. There were also no windows, which made the space feel claustrophobic. I asked the staff if they could fix the heating and provide some fresh air, but they seemed reluctant to make any changes. I left the facility feeling frustrated and worried about my grandmother's well-being. I decided to research other care facilities in the area, hoping to find a place that could provide her with the care and attention she deserved.

I was out this way recently and I stopped to look for a place to eat. Man, talk about a dead mall! Parkway Center Mall even has its own listing on www. deadmalls. com I'd only been here once or twice back in its heyday. Back then it had Chi-Chi's (where thankfully I never ate. A hepatitis scare did them in), David Weis, Pharmor, CompUsa, Syms, etc were all here. Now the mall is mainly deserted. Only one floor is still open, and even that's got a vacancy rate of about 50%! Surprisingly what remains seems to be doing good business. Kmart is doing okay as is the Giant Eagle. Phantom of the Attic is alive and well and so is Pittsburgh Sports Deli. That's not an eatery either. It's a sports memorabilia store. There wasn't much reason for me for me to linger here though. I soon left and went over to Olive Garden for lunch.

I've always found the food to be tasty and fresh. The menu changes daily depending on what ingredients are in season. There is a nice variety of appetizers, salads, pastas, and main courses to choose from. On my last visit, I started with the bruschetta topped with tomatoes, basil and balsamic reduction which was light and flavorful. For my entree, I ordered the pan seared salmon served with roasted potatoes and green beans. The salmon was cooked perfectly and very moist. The sides complimented the fish well. The restaurant has a casual upscale atmosphere with wooden tables and chairs. Soft music plays in the background to create a relaxing ambiance. Most nights, the place is comfortably crowded with diners enjoying their meals. Service is attentive without being overbearing. Prices are moderate for the quality of ingredients used. I would recommend Nightbird for a nice dinner when you want fresh, seasonal cuisine prepared well. It has become one of my favorite neighborhood go-to spots.

We started with the Indonesian corn fritter wraps, which were delicious with the chili-soy dipping sauce. The corn fritters should have either been a little smaller or the lettuce leaves a little bigger, however, because the combo to unwieldy to roll up and eat. The seaweed salad was good, too. My entree was the autumn vegetables and rice cake noodles--which I only realized was very similar to a pasta dish at Casbah after I took my first bite. The dish at Casbah: maccheretto with white beans, wild mushrooms, sun-dried tomatoes, rapini pesto, cheese and walnuts. Soba's version: rice cake noodles with wild mushrooms, butternut squash, green beans, arugula and sunflower seed pesto. The types of vegetables in Casbah and Soba's versions differ, but the pestos taste pretty much the same. Rice cake noodles don't really soak up liquid, though, so Soba's version was drowning in sauce. I probably would have enjoyed another entree more. I guess I should have read the menu description more carefully, but didn't think Asian fusion (Soba) and Mediterranean (Casbah) were anything alike, so I didn't expect to get the same dish at both restaurants. For dessert, we split the five spice apple tart with honey creme fraiche and crispy yam. The tart was more honey creme fraiche with some apple bits on top; it was tasty but I would have liked more apple. I enjoyed the atmosphere on a Sunday night, and our server was pleasant but didn't hover. The food's delicious--just order carefully if you've dined at another Big Burrito restaurant not too long ago, to avoid getting a similar dish.
The atmosphere was nice and relaxing. The service was great. The food was delicious and the portions were large. The prices were reasonable. We would definitely come back here again.

I'm a pretty big book reader & love trying out new book stores, so Park Road Books was a welcome sight to see. Upon entering, I was pleasantly surprised by how spacious and well organized the store was. New releases were prominently displayed at the front, with cozy nooks throughout featuring categories like mysteries, sci-fi, and memoirs. I spent over an hour browsing the wide selection of titles and admiring the charming exposed brick walls. The friendly staff was knowledgeable and offered great recommendations based on what I said I enjoyed reading. During my visit, I noticed many customers of all ages engrossed in books. Towards the back of the store was a lovely cafe with soft armchairs, providing the perfect spot to grab a drink and read a few pages. Park Road Books also hosted author events and book clubs. Though I didn't buy anything on this trip, I look forward to returning again soon to explore new areas of the store and pickup a book or two. This will certainly become my new favorite local indie bookshop in the area, perfect for bookish outings.

After walking into the store a little further, I found my answer. CHEESE! The store was a little on the "sloppy/pack rat/ sweaty/ definitely wouldn't hurt to mop every once in a while" side. My first instinct wasn't to leave so that is always a good thing. Customer service (5/5): I went there because my husband randomly missed Spain so he wanted to make a bunch of mini bocadillos with different types of meat and cheeses. We already got the meat from another place down the street so what better place to get a variety of cheeses than the Macaroni co? The lady that helped us was wonderful!! She was so patient with us even though there were a million people waiting in line. She automatically knew which cheese to recommend based on what would compliment the meat that we had. She was extremely knowledgeable about the various kinds of cheese. I could seriously listen to her talk all day about the history of the cheese.. . she made it so interesting. My husband is VERY indecisive so he couldn't figure out which one he liked more. Food (4/5): We tried at least 7 different kinds of cheese and I didn't like any of them.. . definitely not a cheese person. My husband on the other hand, LOVED every single one of them! We also went there for some Rustic Italian or any hard shelled bread. I know this is not the store's fault be there needs to be a sign that says, "Do NOT touch the actual bread unless you are buying it!! ! " I saw at least 3 people who were squeezing the bread with their dirty hands to see if it was soft. Totally grossed me out. Why would anyone think that is okay?! ? ! I can understand if you are squeezing the bread through the bag but don't TOUCH it! That is only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5. Oh and the fact that it wasn't that clean.

Where do I start. This movie was a complete mess from beginning to end. The plot made no sense and jumped around illogically between different storylines. None of the characters were likable or easy to care about. The acting was atrocious across the board, with no performances that felt genuine or believable. It was also badly edited with confusing jump cuts that often left the audience disoriented. On top of that, the cinematography was dull and lazy with very little visual appeal. To make matters worse, the music selection was jarringly inappropriate for most of the scenes. Around the halfway point I just stopped trying to follow what was happening and waited for it to be over. By the ending, I still had no idea what the movie was supposedly about or what it was trying to accomplish. Overall, it was a grand failure in storytelling that I cannot recommend to anyone. Save your money and time for a movie that respects its audience more than this one did.

Nova inside is what sets this McDonald's apart. With modern decor and furnishings, the dining area feels refreshingly upgraded from the usual fast food restaurant. Booths and tables are made of dark wood with comfortable padded seating. Various mur art and plants add personality to the space. Soft background music plays to mask the routine restaurant sounds. Staff are nicely dressed and attentive to keeping the dining area tidy. Menus are displayed clearly on digital screens to see options without waiting in linea. Overall, the interior makes for a more pleasant dining experience than other area locations.

I recently had the pleasure of visiting Carolina Tire for a routine oil change and was thoroughly impressed with the level of service I received. From the moment I walked in, the staff was friendly and welcoming, making me feel right at home. The waiting area was clean and well-equipped, with comfortable seating and complimentary refreshments.The staff was very knowledgeable and transparent about the work that needed to be done on my vehicle, taking the time to explain everything in detail. They also offered me a complimentary inspection, which I appreciated, as it allowed me to get a better understanding of the condition of my car.The oil change itself was done quickly and efficiently, with the staff taking great care to ensure that everything was properly dispose of and recycled. They also offered me a complimentary car wash, which was a nice touch.What really stood out to me, however, was the level of customer service I received. The staff went above and beyond to ensure that I was satisfied with the work that was done, checking in with me multiple times throughout the process to make sure everything was to my liking.Overall, I was incredibly impressed with Carolina Tire and would highly recommend them to anyone looking for a reliable and trustworthy auto repair shop. The level of service and professionalism I received was truly exceptional, and I will definitely be back for any future needs.

Lebo hype is about this place. The portions are small, the place is small, and the foods no more than average. I have been there twice now, thinking the first time might have been a fluke. We've heard so much about it that I have super high expectations. Their wine bar in the back is cute, but small. We couldn't even lift our elbows to sip our drink. While the waiters and service are good, the food is just not impressive. The pasta I got was good, but nothing to write home about. I got a pizza the second time I visited and it had a horrid taste. I don't know if it was the spinach or the cheese but something was VERY potent. They're pricy as well. The only thing I will give them credit for their Italian wedding soup. There's practically nothing in it, as they use think rice instead of noodles, but the broth and meatballs are to die for! Overall, not impressed. I probably won't return.

We went on a Wednesday night and as expected, we didn't need reservations. The decor was on point, dimly lit (dark enough to be inviting, and bright enough to read the menu). Our server was very knowledgeable and had wonderful suggestions for wines, appetizers, salads, cheeses and entrees. nFor the appetizer, try the arrancini (breadcrumb coated risotto balls filled with mozzerella and panccetta and fried) and the scallops are apparently incredible. The cheese selection is in my opinion the best part of the menu, but my beef tenderloin ala blue was the clear winner of the night. I want to go back again just writing this review! My date tried the Pork Milanese with Heirloom Tomatoes, which was very tasty, but very rich. It defintely won points for creativity, but not for eatability (if that makes sense). He ended up not being able to eat most of it, but luckly for him, I was able to share my steak and risotto

it was a Saturday and "could not call a baker in to fix it so they could refund me the cake and just take this one, go somewhere else to buy a new cake, or try to fix the writing ourselves and just remove the word that was INCORRECT. Won't be back. This place left me with such a claustrophobic and disheartening feeling during my all too brief visit. The cramped seating and lack of windows gave the entire dining room a gloomy, oppressive air that completely ruined my appetite. To make matters worse, the food we received was barely edible - overcooked, bland, and not at all what we ordered. I felt entirely trapped in that dark, dreary space with no alternatives but to choke down the atrocious meal set before me. By the time our server grudgingly delivered our check, I was more than ready to hop, skip, and a jump away from that mouth lighting establishment. Bottom line, nothing about this restaurant was an enjoyable experience.
