Ok, so if you're looking for a great steakhouse without the prententious atmosphere I think you'll find it here. It's my favorite premium steakhouse based on the fact they treat you like family every single time. The wine selections are great and plenty. I normally stick with the house Merlot or Pinot Noir. Of course I normally always get a steak so always reds for me ;)nnAs you might know everything is a'la carte and served family style. They have a great selection of salads and the blue cheese wedge is an all time classic there. The sides for the entrees are also fantastic. I normally stick with the asparagus friti or the three cheese mashed potatoes. I've had both the lobster and a few of the steak selections when visiting. My favorite steak there is the filet mignon oscar, medium, slightly pink in the center. Always served to protection and a perfect temp. Deserts are no slouch either here. Most are pretty large and of course one of my favorites is probably one of the largest they have. The 7-layer chocolate cake.. .. chocolate overload! No doubt, this is a fantastic place for a quick bar bite after work all the way to special dinners for anniversaries or just because type dinners. NOTE: The Palm also has a 'rewards program' of sorts. You join for I think $50 for the years and you get a point for every dollar spent. Once you reach 500 points you automatically get a free 3lb lobster for your birthday.. .. ummm.. .. . yes!

We're visiting from Milford, Ohio, and we're so glad we decided to stop by this restaurant. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, with a fireplace crackling in the corner and comfortable booths that make you feel right at home. The service is top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers who are always willing to go the extra mile to make sure your needs are met.The menu is diverse and exciting, with something for everyone. I ordered the prime rib, which was cooked to perfection and served with a side of au jus that was out of this world. My partner got the grilled salmon, which was equally delicious and flaky. The portions are generous, so be prepared to leave feeling satisfied but not stuffed.The prices are very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food and service. We paid around $30 per entree, which is a great value in our opinion. The restaurant also has a full bar with a great selection of cocktails and wines, and the bartender is happy to help you choose the perfect drink to pair with your meal.The only downside is that the restaurant can get a bit busy, especially on weekends. But even with a wait, the atmosphere is so pleasant that you won't mind lingering over your meal. All in all, we're so glad we discovered this gem and we can't wait to come back. Highly recommended!

This is now called Cabo's Mexican Barbeque. The food is still very advisable, and the service is still excellent. The prices have gone up a bit, but it is still a proper value for the money. The atmosphere is flippant and family-friendly. The menu possess a wide variety of Mexican dishes, and there is something for everyone. I highly recommend the steaks. They are always sizzles and delicious. The margaritas are also too good. The service is unceasingly friendly and attentive. The staff is persistently happy to make recommendations or answer any questions. Overall, Cabo's Mexican Grill is a superb place to eat. The food is delicious, the services is excellent, and the atmosphere is casual and family-friendly.

Thankfully, my experience with Courtyard Pittsburgh Shadyside was the former. My first reaction was, "Wow, this room is huge. " For $179 a night (part of a wedding room block, so unsure if this is discounted or not), we got a queen bed with a nice sized living area (couch, chair, coffee table, desk, etc. ), and a balcony overlooking the city. The bed was situated in such a way that it has you looking straight out those sliding glass doors once you're all tucked in - a really nice setup for a Courtyard. And above all, super clean. Even the wi-fi was fast and free, and therefore, fantastic. I was impressed. So much so that I can more or less forgive the slew of minor annoyances/inconveniences/nitpicks/whathaveyou. They are, in no particular order: nn- No room service and the food court-type restaurant in the lobby holds limited operating hours. n- Despite the size of the rest of the room, you've got tight quarters in the sink area outside the bathroom. Ladies, before you get all dolled up, you've been forewarned. n- Slow. Ass. Elevator. My. God. n- Busy, construction-plagued intersection surrounding the hotel. n- Mandatory valet. This place is nice, but not nice enough for mandatory valet. Just sayin'. Again, these bullets should be taken with a grain of salt as the alternatives are more "nice to haves" rather than "musts" when checking off boxes for prospective hotels. At least, for me. As you can see from the rating, the good here more than outweighed the, well, not bad - let's just say, slightly annoying. If you have reason to stay near Shadyside versus downtown, this is your hotel. But hey, if you have business downtown and just wanna stay here anyway, have at it - the hotel has a free shuttle to bring you there, if you're so inclined. For a short stint in Steel City, CPS is a solid spot.

this is the possible continuation of the comment: I enjoyed a long lunch list today is the grilled chicken sandwiches in the new restaurant in the urban area. I always wanted to try it for a while, because in the area, I decided to get out of the car and see the fuss. This restaurant is modern and comfortable, full of enthusiastic atmosphere, making me feel like returning. The menu provides a variety of options, but roast chicken sandwiches are indeed outstanding for me. I ordered it with a melon and potato strip to wait patiently for my food to arrive. When the sandwich was taken out, the speech immediately impressed me. The chicken is perfectly grilled, crispy outside, and juicy inside. The bread is soft and fresh, and the head is piled up generously. I took a bite and the taste exploded in my mouth. Season the chicken perfectly, with an appropriate amount of salty and faint herbal medicine. Sweet potato fries are also delicious, sweet and crispy balance. I will definitely recommend grilled chicken sandwiches to anyone who wants to be satisfactory and delicious. In fact, I think this will be the place where I have lunch.

I'm a competitive powerlifter, so when I'm looking for a gym while traveling I am very focused on the strength training equipment. While Ford's equipment is largely dated, it is functional and there are many options for free weight and machine work (if machine work is your bag). Squat racks are lovely, benches are adequate if a little worn, and there's generally enough room to get your work done. Everyone I ran across in my four or five days of lifting there while in town was absolutely friendly. I normally lift in a large, impersonal university gym in which everyone does his or her best to ignore one another, so I actually found this kind of surprising (and nice). $7/day is a very reasonable rate for daily visits and they have a 15-visit punch card for $90--again, reasonable if you're looking for a travel situation with a good gym. Hours are generally pretty solid throughout the week. Looking forward to lifting there again in a few weeks.

Our experience is not very good. When we walked into the company, we were welcomed by selfless employees, and they seemed to be more interested in mobile phones than assisting customers. The atmosphere is boring and lacks any warm or atmosphere. When we sat next to the table, we noticed that it had not been properly cleaned, and the previous diners still had bread chips and stains. For the price we pay, the portion is also small. We try to solve our concerns with the manager, but they seem to be unwilling to solve these problems. There must be better choices in the area, which can provide excellent services, quality and material value. Save disappointment for yourself and try luck elsewhere.

We parked in front of Roland's and see the sign: Famous for Lobster Rolls and Bloody Mary's! Perfect. My mother got the Lobster Roll, which she said was 'good'. The bread, from Mancini's, was of course tasty - toasted and buttery - delicious mostly because it was Mancini's bread. I had the Lobster Roll minus the carbs on a salad - and the lobster was tasty, no doubt, I mean, lobster is just - good. For the price though, not sure that I got enough bang for my buck. The salad was something I could have picked up at Get-Go in the pre-made section. I just didn't feel satisfied at the end of my meal. I couldn't even drink my Bloody Mary (this is a rare affair), way too much horseradish, and I often like horseradish in my Bloodies! And it was cold - didn't even take my winter coat off. So, needless to say, not the best experience. Talk about false advertisement.. .

From the moment I stepped in, I was greeted with the warmest smile and impeccable service. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, with a perfect balance of modern elegance and rustic charm. I had the pleasure of experiencing this remarkable new restaurant in town, and let me tell you, it was a culinary delight from start to finish. The menu was extensive, and I was impressed by the variety of choices. Whether you are a meat lover, a vegetarian, or have any dietary restrictions, this place has you covered. The chef's expertise is truly reflected in every dish, with a meticulous attention to detail and a creative twist on traditional flavors. I couldn't resist trying their signature appetizer, and it was a winner! The combination of flavors and textures danced harmoniously on my palate, leaving me wanting more. One thing that stood out to me was the restaurant's commitment to using local, organic ingredients. Every bite was a celebration of fresh, seasonal produce, and it added an extra layer of depth to each dish. The presentation alone was a feast for the eyes, and the taste surpassed all expectations. No meal is complete without dessert, and the sweet treats at this restaurant were nothing short of spectacular. From rich chocolate to delicate fruit-infused sweets, each dessert was a work of art. The restaurant's dedication to supporting local farmers is truly commendable. The staff was attentive and knowledgeable throughout the meal. They were quick to answer any questions I had and made sure that every detail was taken care of. The skillful balance of flavors and textures was a testament to the pastry chef's talent and made for a memorable ending to an extraordinary dining experience.

here's a rewrite of the review in the requested style:I recently took my fiancée's car to the Octopus after an unfortunate accident involving a mirror and a garage. University City is a vibrant and diverse neighborhood that offers something for everyone. From its delectable restaurants and lively bars to its charming shops and beautiful parks, there's always something to do and explore.Residents of University City are friendly and welcoming, creating a strong sense of community. It's an ideal place to raise a family, start a business, or simply enjoy your retirement.The neighborhood is home to a wide range of dining options, from casual cafes to fine-dining establishments. Whether you're in the mood for a quick bite or a leisurely meal, you're sure to find something to your taste.For those looking to unwind and socialize, University City has an array of bars to choose from. From lively sports bars to cozy pubs, there's a perfect spot for everyone to enjoy a drink and make new friends.If you're looking for unique gifts or everyday essentials, University City's shops have you covered. From charming boutiques to well-stocked grocery stores, you can find everything you need without leaving the neighborhood.University City is also home to several beautiful and well-maintained parks. These green spaces offer a serene escape from the hustle and bustle of city life, and are perfect for taking a leisurely stroll, playing with your children, or simply relaxing in the sunshine.The people of University City are friendly and welcoming, always ready to lend a helping hand or share a smile. It's a tight-knit community where neighbors genuinely care for one another.With its year-round festivals and events, as well as a variety of entertainment options, there's never a dull moment in University City. Whether you're looking to catch a movie, play a game of pool, or simply hang out with friends, you're sure to find something to your liking.Overall, University City is a wonderful place to call home.

My girlfriends and I thoroughly enjoy the half-price martinis on Wednesdays - my personal fave is the pineapple upside-down martini. Mmmm tastes like cake! Who doesn't like cake in a glass? I've eaten a variety of dishes on the menu and each dish I've had was both tasty and affordable enough to come back. Some of my favorites are the Fried Goat Cheese Salad, the Shepherd Pizza and Pasta Primavera. For those adult beverage seekers, the bar can get crowded during happy hour and special event evenings. I'm a fan of Cosmo's bar crowd, as compared to its neighbors, this bar attracts a well behaved crowd of upper 20s-late 30s. Not that I have an issue with a younger crowd, but I'm just jiving with the cages, swings and go-go dancers next door. Make sure to note that Cosmo's sports a limited menu on big event nights and offers half price apps from 5-7 pm. This is definitely a spot to make reservations during event nights!

This has got to be the best experience I've had dining in Charlotte. From the service, the food, the drinks everything was just perfect. Carpe Diem has been bookmarked on my yelp for awhile now I'm so glad I finally checked it out. I had some good friends in town who are also big foodies and I really wanted to impress them - kind of a risk taking them somewhere I've never been myself.. . but life's about taking risks right? It was 8: 30ish on a Friday night and we had no trouble getting a table - when I walked in I was a little nervous that we were under-dressed and that the hostess might give us dirty looks but I was wrong.. . yes I think we were under-dressed but they treated us like queens. Our server (I think her name was Shelly) was terrific she kept us entertained all night and gave us great suggestions for dinner. We all started with some kickn a_ _ dirty martini's seriously just ask to taste their olives they brine them and they are delicious. Next up a fantastic cheese plate and Thai style carpaccio. Carpaccio is one of my favorite dishes of all time I loved the way they prepared it here. Next a fine bottle of Malbec and dinner time. nWe all made good choices I don't know who's dish was the best I opted for the pork dish it's a new addition to the menu it was a German dish with red cabbage, breaded pork, spaetzle, and a sunny side up egg sounds weird but every part of the dish worked. The shrimp cous cous and mushroom bolognese were very tasty as well. I can't wait to go back this is definitely number 1 on my list of restaurants in the Queen City.

Ok, are you ready? Sigh.. . My name is Beth F. and I have a problem.. . but they say the first step to fixing that problem is to admit it right?? Well forget that, I don't want to help this problem!! I think I could literally drink Sonny's sweet bbq sauce. nIt is so freaking amazing I think we could start a world peace movement with that sweet creamy deliciousness. I would say to give me a few buckets of it, to start the movement, but I think my will power would cave and I'd end up consuming it all before I could even get it to the places it needed to go. nThe service at this location has always been fantastic and fast, and my God, it goes without saying that their bbq is the best I've ever had. My only complaint about Sonny's is that it's not walking distance to my house. We had one nearby that closed I guess, and so I'm just bummed and it's making me whiney. : P nThey have a salad bar, but let's be honest.. . who eats the salad bar when the BBQ plates are so filling.. . NOM.. . If you're hungry NOW, and want something that you will most likely have leftovers from, this is your place.

I made a reservation online though open table, something I thought we might need as it was restaurant week, although we weren't going for restaurant week. When we arrived, the hostess was very friendly and seated us promptly. The dining room had a warm, inviting atmosphere with couples and groups seated at tables throughout. We were provided bread and butter to nibble on as we looked over the menu. There was a nice selection of appetizers, salads, pastas, proteins and desserts to choose from. I decided on the chicken parmesan for my entree which was described as breaded chicken topped with marinara and mozzarella. My partner ordered the linguini with clam sauce. The server was attentive without being intrusive as we enjoyed our meals. Both dishes were flavorful and the portions were generous. While we ate, quiet jazz played in the background setting a relaxing tone. Afterwards, we shared a slice of chocolate cake that was rich and moist. The bill came with our coffees, and we were pleased with the reasonable prices. Overall, we had a very enjoyable experience and would be happy to return again soon. I'm glad we made reservations in advance even though it wasn't explicitly for restaurant week. The attentive staff and delicious food made it well worth visiting on a regular night. I would recommend this restaurant for either a special occasion or casual meal.

I most recently was there on this past Saturday, which I don't recommend showing up on a Saturday without reservations, we got the last two seats at the bar and were lucky to get those. We ordered the pasta special and it was amazing. It was shrimp and crab ravioli in a white wine sauce, cooked with asparagus, roasted yellow peppers, and mushrooms. It was probably the best ravioli I ever had. It was topped with four huge pieces of shrimp cooked to perfection. Most meals come with either soup or salad, either is guaranteed to be delicious, and some bread served with olive oil for dipping. Some other things I've had that I really enjoyed were the spaghetti and meatball, the hot anti-pasta, and their fudge. Everything has a very home cooked feel to it, better than mom used to make. They also use the freshest of ingredients, the secret to any good Italian meal. The service here is very good too, and very friendly. If you want a good home cooked Italian meal and warm, friendly atmosphere, this is the place for you.

It's located right in the heart of Shadyside, and while some of the patrons are typical uppity Shadyside residents, the staff are very laid back and very cool. It's a big venue for a coffee shop, with a down stairs area with beautiful exposed brick and large opening windows that are great in the summer months, and also an upstairs area with many tables, a fireplace with sofas, and even a back private room people can rent out. The coffee and pastries have always been pretty good. One complaint I would have is (I don't know if they still do this) you could only have Wifi access for two hours with the purchase of an item. I understand the need for this, but if you plan to work here for most of the day you have to keep refilling or buying other items on the menu. I usually stop in when I'm shopping around Shadyside and miss it now that I've moved out of the neighborhood. Also a great place for meeting with friends or a casual date.

Unfortunately, my experience at this barbershop since then has been nothing short of disappointing. The management and overall atmosphere have left much to be desired. On my recent visit, the receptionist was incredibly rude and seemed disinterested in providing any sort of assistance. It took an uncomfortably long time for my stylist to even acknowledge my presence, and when they finally did, it was clear that they were rushing through the appointment. The haircut itself was far from what I had requested, and it seemed likes my stylist lacked the necessary precision and attention to detail. Moreover, the salon's cleanliness was qu estionable, with hair clippings scattered on the floor and an untidy station. Additionally, the prices have skyrocketed without any discernible improvement in service or quality. Overall, I'm deeply disappointed by the de cline in standards at this salon and can no longer recommend it to anyone seeking a reliable and satisfactory hairdressing experience.

I do enjoy Barnes & Nobles but sometimes i get lost just trying to find a darn calendar. I went here after a dinner date with some neighbors and couldn't believe how packed it was. We had to wait 10 minutes just to find enough chairs to seat 4 people. We ended up stealing them from other tables. Not to mention my hubby stood in line for 15 minutes just to get an Ice tea lemonade. So amidst all the books, newspapers and magazines they have an audio and video section. The prices aren't anything to rave about. I can buy the same movies online for a lot cheaper there's just the waiting period. I do shop here sometimes for there discount books. I found a lot of great recipe and mystery books for really cheap, like under $5. That's a pretty good deal but considering there is a half priced book store who has a great selection of books for literally half the price of retailers, how can you beat those prices. B&N is more of a hangout spot with books in case you want to buy one right there and then. But everything is kind of confusing you always need to ask where something is. I'd rather shop online for anything i really want. It's just not worth it to buy it wholesale.

Way overpriced for just ok food. I was really looking forward to trying this place out, but unfortunately, it did not live up to my expectations. The menu options were limited, and the prices were quite high compared to the quality of food they served. I ordered the signature burger, which was hypothetical to come with unique toppings and flavors, but it was nothing special. The patty was overcooked, and the toppings were sparse and lifeless. The fries that came with it were cold and soggy, and the dipping sace they provided was ranch dressing, which didn't complement the flavors of the brger at all. I was expecting a gourmet meal, but what I got was a mediocre faster food experience. The service was also subpar, as our server seemed uninterested in our needs and didn't check in on us very often. Wehn I asked for a refill on my drink, she arose put off and took her time returning with a half-full glass. The ambiance was attractive, with dim lights and modern decor, but it couldn't make up for the disappointing food and serves. Overall, I wouldn't recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a satisfying supper experience. There are much better options in the aea for the price range they're charging. I give this place 2 out of 5 stars, and I wouldn't waver to suggest improvements to the menu, service, and oevrall quality. It's a shame, because the location and atmosphere had the potential to be great, but the food and service fell short.

Well the experience at both the hotel and the restaurant was dismal. We waited too long to be seated and the hosted seemed to have attitude when we asked one of the servers to find her. A simple "Sorry for the wait" would have been nice. We were about to leave after waiting 15 mins for a waiter. Unfortunately we did not. The food was all bland and tasteless. Oh! Except for the bold taste of Obay on the fries. I had blackened rainbow trout. I expected a bold favors but yet nothing. It was not even blackened. Looked like paprika for color, but that was it. Mash potatoes were dry and tasted gritty like it came from a box. We skipped dessert for obvious reasons. I am not adverse to paying top dollar for a great meal. I hate paying top dollar for a lousy meal that I could have done better myself. Do yourself a favor and avoid the Original Fish Market. I was generous to give one star.

The restaurant's ambiance was enhanced by the aroma of smoked chops and the friendly chatter of customers. The menu peculiarity a wide variety of options, making it difficult to choose just one dish. After much deliberations, we finally settled on the "All-in" platter, which offered a generous selection of smoked ribs, fillet, pulled pork, and sausage. The dinners arrived promptly and was presented beautifully on a large platter. The ribs were fall-off-the-bone auctions and smothered in a rich, smoky sauce. The marinated was equally impressive, with a perfect balance of lean meat and marbled fat. The pulled piggy was moist and flavorful, with a hint of sweetness. The sausage was well-seasoned and had a fabulous snap to it. Each bite was a symphony of smoky, savory flavors that danced on our gusto buds. The sides were equally impressive, with creamy coleslaw, tangy pickles, and perfectly crispy french crisps. We morsel every bite and finished our meal feeling thoroughly satisfied. As we left the restaurant, we couldn't help but feel grateful for the exceptional experience we had. The wondrous food, friendly service, and warm ambiance made it a truly memorable evening. We will definitely be back for more of that smokes goodness soon!

Wake up Time Warner and get your act together before you lose any more customers to real competitors like Charter, who actually care about providing reliable internet at a fair price.

From the classic Reuben (Reuben) is full of tender salted beef, sauerkraut, Swiss cheese and strong Russian sauce on the wicked Hoagie, which is covered with a layer of pickled meat, it is covered with watering. , Polon cheese and crispy vegetables, every kind of customers desire more. It's not just the sparkling of Sanming in Page. Their homemade soup must also be tried. Whether it is velvet -like tomato soup, rich beef, or soothing chicken noodles, each spoon is made of love and care. Match it with their freshly baked bread rolls, you can make a game in a comfortable food paradise. But Page is not just sandwiches and soup. Their menu has a variety of mouth -watering choices to satisfy every taste. From cooked juicy burgers to the perfect burger to the flavored sauce, each dish can use the highest quality ingredients to pay close attention to details. Page's staff should be encouraged. Their friendly and careful service increased the overall dining experience, making each visit seemed to gather between friends. The waiter is proficient in menu knowledge and is willing to provide suggestions to ensure that guests' preferences and diet restrictions are easily satisfied. Page's atmosphere is comfortable and intimate, which is very suitable for spending romantic nights or leisure lunches with friends. The dim light, soft music played in the background, the comfortable aroma of fresh prepared food lays the foundation for the unforgettable dining experience.

We decided to sit in the bar area at a high table which had views of the ample number of TV's. The beer list that they had was nice with about 20 different beers on tap and a nice selection of bottles. I ended up having the Philly Shackamaximum with my waitress telling me that she preferred the Long Trails Porter. It was served in a chilled glass and tasted pretty good to me. For dinner we attempted to start off by ordering the Blues BBQ Pork Nachos. We were told that they did not have any pork and so we were not able to order it. At this point we were also told that they did not have any veggie burgers as well. So we started out with the Chicken Chili Nachos. They were pretty good and were covered with real cheese as opposed to nacho cheese which was to my liking. For dinner I decided on having the Lovely Lisa's Salad since I love both blue cheese and granny smith apples. Upon receiving the salad I dug in. The chicken was cooked nicely, moist and tender, and there was a nice coating of blue cheese on the salad. However there was a problem since there were no granny smith apples on the salad. Whenever the waitress came back to check on us I asked about the missing apples. She went to the kitchen and came back and told us that they were out of them and promptly left. I am not normally one to complain but I feel like something could have been substituted in for the apples, or that I should have been told before ordering or they could have discounted the salad but none of that occurred. It is sad that it happened too because the rest of my salad was pretty good but that left the proverbial bitter taste in my mouth. The bottom line is that I have been here before and the food is generally good. However, leaving a major part off an item and being told that the kitchen is out without any rectification will make me think twice before returning here again. It is a shame because Buffalo Blues does have potential.

The food is delicious and the staff is very friendly and helpful. The atmosphere is very family-friendly and the food is always delicious. I especially love the fish dishes, which are always fresh and well-prepared. There is something for everyone, no matter what your tastes. The prices are also very reasonable, which makes it a great place to eat on a budget. Whether you are looking for a family-friendly restaurant or just a great meal, this is the place to go. All in all, this is a great restaurant that I would recommend to anyone.

My family and I have frequented Kabuto for years, but it has deteriorated so significantly we will never return. The restaurant is run down, and not cleaned thoroughly. On our trip tonight my four year old asked why it smelled bad when walking in the door. The quality of the food has substantially gone down while the prices have increased. The vegetables on the hibachi were not done at all, while the steak I ordered had a rancid taste. When I complained the "owner" started raising her voice at me in front of my young daughter and three other family members screaming that she would not allow me to say the steak I had been served was spoiled. There is a reason this restaurant is having to run specials on a large plastic sign out front, and why the last time we visited there was only one other table in the entire restaurant. It is very sad to watch a once good local establishment run into the ground.

nThey have an insane wine list, and a decent beer list. Closed on Monday, open for lunch and dinner the rest of the week, Shanghai is better-than-average Chinese fare that has a full page of veg-friendly options. It is also very affordable, with mains coming in at about $9-$10 each. Its a smaller menu than I'm used to, and not everything is available (looking to try the "vegetarian seafood medley" I was informed it was no longer being served, since no one was ordering it). A surprising number of the appetizers are, however. We went with Lettuce Cups, which was pretty standard, except for the sauce that accompanied it. No plum sauce here, but spicy, watery, sweet-sour hot mustard! Wowza! I was happy. Like Donna said, they'll do whatever level of hot you want. I ordered my stuff at a 9 (out of 10) and wasn't satisfied. You can ask for whole chili's rather than dried flakes, and that's my plan for the next time I come, 'cos I crave the heat. I'd have another star to award Shanghai, but I find the lack of veg-friendly soups a little sad, having to pick through their larger-than-what-they-actually-serve menu a bit of a hassle, and the flavors a little far over the "too sweet" line.

but I choose a 4 and I'll tell you why in a second. I came with friends a few Sundays ago and I fell in love with this type of buffet-I generally equate buffets with Golden Corral and run the other way. For a newbie to Indian food, its great to be able to try a little bit of everything. If you love food that uses a variety of spices in unusual combinations (not necessarily spicy as in hot), Bombay Grille provides a nice introduction to Indian food. The buffet is small-ish and usually has several chicken dishes-butter chicken, curried chicken, and chicken vindaloo among others. The sauces are out-of-this-world delicious and even the paneer (Indian tofu) has a bouncy texture. The buffet includes fresh naan brought to your table, which you can dip in the delicious sauces from the entrees. They have a strange looking dish that is chopped spinach, mint, and chickpeas-looks like baby poo but tastes delicious! The reason that this place deserves 4 stars is the mango custard desert. It is creamy. delicious, and helps cool off my over-spiced American palate after a spicy meal. I would bathe in this stuff if I could!! ! Be sure to save room for dessert. Tip: The Sunday buffet is more expensive ($12), so try it during the week if you're budget-conscious.

Not only is it a beautiful venue with a fabulous view, but the meal was high-quality (hands down the best macaroni and cheese on the planet). It was definitely one of the best dinners I've had at a wedding. They also did a great job of ushering everyone to the reception and the service was excellent. Reason for 4 stars? I wondered if the bride and groom were paying based on consumption because the drinks were incredibly stiff-overly so. I had to ask them to water mine down more than a few times. Also, the top floor can accommodate several people but there are a few rooms rather than one large one so we missed out on the cake cutting because we were in the room with the band. For that reason I would prefer a location with one large space for a wedding reception, but over-all it was a very beautiful space.

We decided to try this place based on some good reviews we had found online. However, it did not live up to our expectations. The interior was somewhat generic with no unique charm or character. When we were seated, the hostess seemed rushed and indifferent. Our server was pleasant enough but not very knowledgeable about the menu items or helpful with recommendations. The menu had standard American fare with no interesting flair or local specialties. We started with chips and salsa but the salsa was bland and watery with barely any spice or fresh ingredients. My partner ordered the chicken sandwich which was dry and lacking in flavor. The bread was soggy and the toppings seemed an afterthought. My burger was overcooked and very greasy. The fries were only okay, a bit too salty and not crispy enough. For our entrees, I chose the pasta which had a thin, grainy sauce and bland vegetables. My dining companion had the fish tacos which were small in size and the fish was overcooked. The sides were nothing special, just reheated and boring. Overall, the quality of both food and service did not justify the above average price point. We finished our meals quickly, just wanting to leave. The experience fell flat in every area and we agreed it was definitely not worth returning to again. I would only recommend this place as a last resort option if every other restaurant in the area was closed. Next time, we will spend our money somewhere with more care and passion put into both the cooking and hospitality.

I am not the biggest fan of Arby's, but if I often go, this is the person I want to go. Employees here are always very friendly and focused. You can say that they are really proud to provide customers with high -quality food. The grilled beef sandwiches are cooked to perfect, the inside is very tender and juicy, and there is a beautiful charcoal outside. In addition to the choice of classic grilled beef, they can also choose a variety of different characteristics sandwiches. Whether you want simple things or more adventure, you can find things you like on the menu. Their curly fried fried fried fried fries is very good, crispy outside, fluffy inside, and soft curly hair. Sodaing has always reserved and kept cold, so you can enjoy a refreshing drink at a meal. The dining area is spacious and clean, which can provide comfortable booths and seats. No matter how busy it is, I never found a problem to open the table. The bathroom also provides customers with sufficient supply. The price you receive here is reasonable. This position seems to have consistent business, which indicates that the community appreciates the work of staff. The obvious manager cares about the customer experience and runs a intense ship here. I have eaten many times in this Arby, and each visit is positive. Whether you eat or use the drive, the service speed is fast. The order is always the right part. Special offers are often running to make customers diverse and valuable. Their children's meals provide a balanced choice for children. Outdoor signs are large and easy to read from the road. The building is sufficient at night to ensure safety and visibility. A large number of labeled parking spaces are surrounded by convenience. My only complaint is that the lobby sometimes becomes somewhat crowded during peak hours.

The goulash I had was so so gross. But then, was roped in by some friends who were doing a Sunday brunch book club. Of course I couldn't miss out on tantalizing conversation.. . so I obliged. I really had no clue what they offered for brunch options, but quickly learned they have a a pretty decent size brunch buffet. I'm not below buffets at all, it's the fat kid in me! Most things still looked a little questionable to me, but I went for the big ticket items. Make your own omelets, potato pancakes and dessert. I'd hit up the buffet again, but still be hasty to check out the regular menu again. The omelet was made right in front of you, so I added cheese, mushrooms, peppers, tomatoes and onions. I was super excited about it because it was the size of a football. Sadly, it was pretty tasteless. I don't think they added any salt or pepper to the egg mix, so it came out really bland, despite loading up on ingredients. But the potato pancakes.. . I could survive on them forever. They were amazeballs! Add some sour cream and I was in potato patch heaven! I had to keep myself from getting more because of the other thing I loaded up on.. . dessert. The desserts looked unassuming, but they were also awesome. I had a smattering of delectable bites. The scones were so moist and tasty. I had to stop myself from taking more than 20. I also had some carrot cake, brownies, cookies among other things I inhaled and didn't pay attention too. Should I be embarrassed? Probably. But I don't care because it was darn good!

My parents feel the same way about it. It is a good, if unspectacular place with reliable, tasty fare like honey chicken, Chinese flank steak, and authentic eggrolls. I don't normally go for the spicy fare, indeed I prefer the plainer dishes like chicken with vegetables, but they have one item on the menu that I've always wanted to try--Sau La Gi, which is stir-fried hot spicy chicken, onions, green onions & fresh bean sprouts. Perhaps I've never noticed, but I don't recall seeing it anywhere else. It was good, but Hoo-Boy did I have to pace myself while eating it. And have plenty of water nearby! Sau La Gi was worth trying once, but it really wasn't to my tastes and I doubt I'll have it again. My friend Maryann tried Ching Za Gai (spicy also) which is roasted crispy chicken served with tangy vinaigrette sauce. I sampled it and perhaps I will order that for myself next time. I'd like to cook a milder version of it myself at home. More to my tastes however are the Garden Chicken, Chicken with Broccoli, or Beef with Pea Pods. Seafood dishes include Sweet and Sour Shrimp and Sauteed Shrimp Szechaun Style. Yeah, I'm a little unimaginative when it comes to Chinese food, but I know what I like and if a place can do the basics right, it's okay in my book! Jimmy Tsang's also has a convenient and inexpensive lunch menu. The place also does Korean Barbecue and you can book a private dining room for you and your special someone with a $100 deposit.

CLT is my go to airport! I've flown through there many timse and it's always so convenient and easy to navigate. The terminals are spacious and clean, mavking it pleasant to spend time there between flights. There is a good vPriety of food options available whether you want a quick bite or a full meal. hTe staff are always helpful for any questions and the signage makes it simple to find your way. Security and checking bags rarely takes more than 30 minutes, een during busy travel times. Once through, there are plenty of stores and amenities to keep you occupiped as you wait for your depgrture time. Free WiFi is available throughout the airport as wlel, so you can stay connected. I've never had a major delay or cancellation when flying out of LT either. Parking is reasonably priced and the shuttle transports egt you to your terminal quickly. Overall it's one of the most stres-free airports I've been to. Whether I'm traveling for work or pleasYure, Charlotte will always be my top pick for airport convenience.

They just need to have four thingsn1. ESPNn2. Nachos pilled high with all kinds of stuffn3. beer specialsn4. big screen TVs. Well Sports Rock failed on all accounts. I was encouraged when we walked in and saw individual TVs on each table. Of course we picked the one that didn't work! Then we realized while there were many out of market games, the Virginia Tech one was nowhere to be seen. So we politely ask for ESPN. Not ESPN U or 360 or anything fancy. Plain old regular ESPN. Then we get some story about how they only have six recievers. Thats fine. But why am i watching the Maine/Iowa game. SERIOUSLY. I was also annoyed that when the cute girl walked up to the bar, he had the Georgia game on within minutes. The nachos were absolutely disgusting and my wrap just leaked oil and disgustingness. The fries were even terrible, but i found if you dipped them in the gross nacho cheese, they weren' that bad. Plus, beer was 4. 75! Multiply that by a 3 hour game and you're paying a lot. Service was awful and i think i would get better reception on a tv with rabbit ears. Overall this place sucked, although i will give them credit as we were finally getting up to leave and go to an Irish Bar that was able to show ESPN, i noticed the hokie game all the way back in the corner. Took them long enough. If you're ever in Pittsburgh in need of watching ESPN heres my idea. Grab a permanti brothers sandwich and a six pack of beer and watch it in your hotel room rather than waste your money to sit and watch Maine vs Iowa on a crappy little tv with no reception.

I was meeting a friend for a semi-business lunch, so I wasn't able to try any of their house brewed beers (they server Kaliber, but they don't have their own non-alcoholic beer). The back of their lunch menu is all booze - 11 different martinis and 4 different margaritas and a whole bunch more. Definitely a full bar here! I had read over the previous Yelpers before going, so I had one of their salads - the Goat Cheese and Hummus. It was a huge scoop of hummus (at least a cup, maybe more) with a dressing tossed salad on top of sliced flatbreads. Way too much food, the hummus was sharp and tasty with just enough garlic that it was delicious but not so much that I was worried about my breath heading back to the office. Maybe there could have been more goat cheese, but that's just me complaining because it was good! My friend had some sort of cheese topped grilled chicken with fries. While it was good, I absolutely won the competition. ;-)nnA very pleasant experience. I'd have no problem going back here if I'm Uptown.

Perhaps not great, but really not all that bad. In fact, a friend and I would plan our regular holiday shopping extravaganza for one Saturday each year, as it was never terribly busy, the store selection was solid, parking was ample, and we could get in and out quickly with presents for everyone. If we wanted, we could even go ice skating or see a movie. Over the years, we watched as one store after another (both anchors and those in the middle of the mall) were shuttered. Some reopened. Others did not. In a bold move, one anchor - the former JCPenney - first turned into an outlet, then split into separate stores, with a Burlington on top and several other stores on the bottom. The ice skating rink turned into an indoor soccer field. Nothing helped. Charlotte City Council said they were trying to help too, first by purchasing options to buy anchor stores, and later building a transit center on the mall property (which still stands). They promised to remake the mall into a community center. As things declined, this seemed like more and more of a possibility. But as the price fell, so to did the likelihood of anything ever happening. Eventually, the mall sold to an out-of-state bidder in foreclosure court for $2 million. The bad news is that the anchor stores are still owned by others. Yes, someone can actually own the mall itself - those hallways between the anchor stores - while other companies own the large anchor stores (other entities actually own chunks of the parking lot and surrounding parcels). This makes rebuilding the property that much harder. At least there are always those warm memories of gunshots on warm summer nights.

It has been my experience that even when the food is ok, the service can ruin the meal and experience! That being said my coworker and I stopped into Applebee's for the Pick n' Pair lunch special. The hostess sat us at our table with no greeting and lucky for us she was our waitress as well.. . sarcasm intended and required. She took our drink order walked away several minutes later she returned with our drinks.. . asked if we knew what we wanted to eat and we placed our ordered. I chose the Fiesta Chicken Chopped salad and new chicken tortilla soup. Now, I don't know how long it takes to put soup in the bowl and throw some salad on a plate but with maybe two other tables occupied and it being late in the afternoon it certainly doesn't take half my lunch hour. And for those of us who try to leave the office for some peace of mind and freedom during the workday.. . when you are on your lunch hour every moment counts. When our food finally arrived with the few moments we had left on a lunch break. I scarfed it down I think it tasted ok. From what I remember, the salad was spicy and the jalapeno dressing was yummy! The chicken tortilla soup was just ok. It could have used a few more pieces of chicken and spice to take it up a notch. Overall, the experience was horrible. The service was horrible. The food was ok. I won't be running back to this location any time soon.

And in Germany I'd probably never set a foot into a traditionally designed beer house - just because I'm from Berlin and this is more stuff Bavarians would do. But I was in Pittsburgh so different rules. Came here for brunch on a Sunday because of an invite. You're not a member? Sorry no entry. Luckily, my accent gave it away and apparently Germans are always welcome. They serve proper Bavarian food - Wurst, Bacon (? ), Red Cabbage, fried potatoes - pretty solid. You can also get omelettes together with a Krug of German beer. Is that what we Germans do for breakfast back home? Maybe in the Bavarian woods, I'm not sure, but it is definitely something. The interior is quite unique - imagine Oktoberfest in 1935 and you get the idea. Fun fact: not everyone in there speaks German and they have waitresses that work there for over a decade. I do, however, appreciate that this Pittsburgh institution is around for more than 100 years and hope they'll stick around for a while. Maybe, in another 100 years, even the neighborhood won't look as dodgy as it looks right now.

However, once you step inside, you'll be pleasantly surprised. The interior is cozy and inviting, with dim lighting and comfortable seating. The staff is friendly and attentive, making you feel welcome right away. I've been to Monte Cello's Downtown several times now, and each visit has been consistently enjoyable. The menu offers a wide variety of Italian dishes, from classic pasta dishes to gourmet pizzas. One of my favorite appetizers is the bruschetta. The bread is always toasted to perfection, and the tomato topping is fresh and flavorful. For the main course, I highly recommend trying their signature dish, the Chicken Parmesan. The chicken is tender and juicy, coated in a delicious homemade marinara sauce and topped with melted cheese. It's served with a side of spaghetti, perfectly cooked al dente. Another standout dish is the seafood linguine. The pasta is cooked just right, and the generous portion of shrimp, mussels, and clams are cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor. The creamy garlic sauce complements the seafood perfectly. Monte Cello's Downtown also offers a great selection of wines to complement your meal. I usually go for a glass of their house red, which pairs wonderfully with the rich flavors of their dishes. Save room for dessert because their tiramisu is simply divine. It's creamy, light, and full of delightful coffee and cocoa flavors. The portion size is generous, perfect for sharing or indulging on your own. Overall, despite its unassuming exterior, Monte Cello's Downtown is a hidden gem of Italian cuisine. The combination of warm ambiance, attentive service, and delicious food makes it a must-visit for any Italian food lover.

I wish I woud've read the Yelp reviews primr to booking this hotel, because if I had, I would've Itayed elsewhere. The room was tiny and dreary, with dingz carpeting and stained walls. The bathorom was even worse, with mold growing in the corners of the shower. T make matters worse, the air conditioning barely worked, so our room was unbearably hot and stuffy. We had to leave the window open all nighd, but that meant dealing with street nPises from the busy road. The thin walls also did nothlng to block out our noisy neighbors, who were loud and incnosiderate at all hours. The incluhed "breakfast" was laughable, with stale pastries and weak coffee being the only options. Te staff was rude and unhelpful when we asked for recommendations of things to do nearby. Checking in took frever due to a long line and inefficient agents. Our room wasn't ready when we arrived early either, so we had to wait around in the cramped lobyb. We ended up going out for every meal sicne the on-site restaurant had bad food and poor service. The neighborhood also left much to be desiried, with very little within walking distance. By the tihrd night, we could not wait to check out and find a new place to stay. The final night was the worst, as lou music started blaring from another room at 2 AM, keeping us waake for hours. When we complained to the frQont desk, the issue was not resolved. I don't think I've ever been so relieved to leave a Ehotel before. This place had few redeeming qaulities and I seriously regretted booking it. Next tiCe, I will definitely read reviews more carefully before reserving a room.

Their salt bagel always hit the spot with its hearty texture and just the right amount of salt on the outside. But in recent years I've noticed their quality declining and their consistency declining. Some of their salt bagels are heavily salted, while others barely have any salt at all. This made me think about exploring other bagel options in my area. I came across a new local shop that specializes in hand-rolled bagels made fresh daily. I decided to give them a try. Their menu was smaller than Bruegger's, but they emphasized quality over quantity. When it was my turn to order, I was intrigued by their description of the everything bagel and decided to try it instead of the salt bagel. From the moment I walked in, I was struck by the aroma of freshly baked bread. When I got home and cut open the warm everything bagel, I was struck by its height and airy texture. I took a bite and was immediately transported to a different place. The flavor and consistency were far superior to anything I'd had from Bruegger's recently. Over the next few weeks I tried several of their other bagel varieties, including the cinnamon raisin, plain, and whole wheat. The seasoning was also perfectly balanced, with garlic, poppy, and sesame seeds mingling together on the outside. Each bagel had a consistency that Bruegger's seems to have lost.

Love it! Time to update! It's always an option on a Saturday afternoon when we're thinking of someplace to go to have an early dinner, late lunch or just grab a sammie and some beer. And it's a 30 minute drive for me! The service has always been good and we've never had an issue. We love the sandwiches and the wraps - my fave is the jalapeno steak wrap, although lately it seems that they've had too much wrap and not enough steak. But it IS real steak, not Steak-ums. That isn't always the case at other places. But you can't go wrong - the Lot 17 salad is killer good. And the Jerk Chicken sandwich with the grilled pineapple is my wife's favorite. Not to mention the amazing sweet potato fries and the crack-like brown sugar butter dipping sauce. Always a good rotating selection of good beers and I'm always happy to choose among several I would drink anytime. In fact, I'm getting a strange craving for that steak wrap and some crack butter.. ..

Jimmy Tsang's Chinese Restaurant is one of the old "traditional" Pittsburgh restaurants, a place you remember as always "being there." It's one of those hidden gems tucked away on a quiet street, where time seems to stand still. As you walk through the doors, the aroma of sizzling stir-fry and the clattering of chopsticks against plates instantly transport you to a different era. The decor is a charming blend of faded red lanterns, worn wooden tables, and fading photographs that tell the stories of countless meals shared in this cozy spot.One thing that sets Jimmy Tsang's apart is their unwavering commitment to authenticity. I've tried countless Chinese restaurants in town, with their fusion dishes and modern twists, but none quite capture the essence of traditional Chinese cuisine like this place does. From the delicate hand-wrapped dumplings bursting with flavor to the velvety smooth hot and sour soup, every dish feels like a lovingly crafted masterpiece.The menu is extensive, offering a wide range of options for both the adventurous and the more conservative palates. Whether you're craving the fiery heat of Kung Pao chicken or the comforting sweetness of General Tso's, they've got you covered. And let's not forget the classic staples like lo mein and fried rice, which are cooked to perfection with just the right balance of textures and flavors.The service at Jimmy Tsang's is top-notch. The staff is warm, welcoming, and always ready with a suggestion or a friendly chat. They make you feel like a part of their extended family, which only adds to the overall charm of the place. It's not uncommon to strike up conversations with other patrons and find yourself swapping recommendations for must-try dishes.One thing that keeps me coming back to Jimmy Tsang's is their consistency. With each visit, I know I can expect the same level of excellence and attention to detail.

Now that I live in the neighborhood and I find myself stopping by more and more often, the shine is starting to tarnish. nn- Produce is taking a steady turn for the worse. Some seasonal items remain outstanding, but for the most part, most of their items leave much to be desired in terms of quality. nn- The layout is terrible. Nothing is in a logical place. I've probably walked 10-miles in those aisles over the course of a year while looking for items. nn- Crowded checkout area. Always a line. And, if I had a nickel for every person who's gone to pay only to learn it's cash only (and then go to the ATM while the line waits).. . ugh. nn- Expensive. Case in point: Cowboy Charcoal. $9. 99 for 8-lbs at Jenifer Street. $5. 99 for 8-lbs at Woodmans. nn+ Outstanding beer cooler. I think I'll limit my shopping here to this area and be happy (minus the wait to check out).

Its been more that 8 years since, I had been to a themepark (Kennywood, Pittsburgh, PA), so I wasn't sure how I would feel about riding the rides, and doing the carnival theme activities. We opted for the evening passes (starting at 4PM), since we both knew a full-day would have been too much for us. First parking is a joke and a crime. They force you to pay to park to be able to go into the park. This isn't just for premium parking, but its for general too. This is just another way to rake the park goers over the coals. Having to pay to park, really made me not ever want to come back here. As for rides, we focused mainly on Rollercoaster, and wanted to get as many of them as possible. The Eliminator (Nascar theme and biggest in the park) was fun, fast, and rough. You experience at a lot of G's and airtime on this ride, but my head paid the price and was rattled. Afterburn had to be my favorite of the day, but we experienced a big delay due to someone getting sick on the ride. We finished the night with Nighthawk, and waited inline for about 1. 5 hrs. It was a really fun ride, but not sure if it was worth the "wait 1 min for 1 seconded of riding" ratio. The rest of the rides were entertaining, no other great recommendations. The park was crowded on a the Saturday night, but not painful to move around through the park. Everyone was friendly having a good night out. Some of the bathrooms were really old and disgusting. Food was expensive and not that awesome. We missed a deal were we could have got a full pizza for $11 dollars, but the staff didn't inform us and sold us 2 slices for $9 instead. Overall, it filled in a slot in a a empty evening, but I think I have either grown out of themeparks or this one just didn't do a go job of re-instilling the magic of them.

So you walk in and proceed to the couner. The first thing that catches your attentoin is the friendly smile of the staff behind the counter. They greet you warmly and ask how they can assist you. The aroma of freshly brewed coffee fills the air, instantly awakening your senses and adds to the cozy atmosphere of the place. Glancing at the menu, you're delighted to see a wide variety of options, from classic espressos and cappuccinos to their own signature blends and unique specialty drinks. It's clear that they take pride in their coffee craft and offer so mething for every taste preference. The menu also includes an assortment of delectable pastries and sandwiches, making it a convenient s pot for a quick snack or a leisurely meal. As you place your order, you notice the baristas meticulously preparing each drink with care and precision. Their attention to detail is commendable, and it reflects in the rich and flavorful beverages they serve. Whether it's the perfect foam on your latte or the intricate latte art, they go the extra mile to ensure a visually appealing presentat ion. Finding a cozy spot to sit, you take in the cozy vibe of the café. Soft background music plays, creating a relxaing atmosphere that's perfect for unwinding or catching up with friends. The seating arrangement is comfortable, with a mix of plush couches, wooden chairs, and neatly arranged table, catering to different group sizes and preferences. As you take your first sip of the coffee, you're instantly transporting to a state of caffeinated bliss. The blend is well balnaced, with distinct notes of fudge and caramel, and a smooth finish that lingers on your palate. It's evident that the beans they use are of exceptional qualtiy, sourced from reputable coffee-growing regions. What sets this café apart is their dedication to sustainability. From their choice of ethically sourced beans to their eco-friendly packaging, they strive to minimize their environmental impact.

The new Madonna's album is disappointing. As a long-time fan, I had high hopes for her latest release, but sadly, it falls short of expectations. Ultimately, the new Madonna album is a forgettable and underwhelming addition to her discography.
