It was a lovely surprise, as I had been wanting to try this restaurant for a while. The atmosphere was cozy and intimate, with dim lighting and comfortable seating. Our server was friendly and attentive, helping us navigate the menu. I ordered the filet mignon, which was cooked to perfection, and my partner had the seafood risotto. The dishes were both delicious, and we shared a side of roasted vegetables. The portions were generous, and we ended up taking some leftovers home. The wine list was extensive, and we chose a bottle of cabernet sauvignon to accompany our meal. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and service. Overall, we had a wonderful dining experience at Alexander Michael's and would definitely recommend it to others.

Update: July 2013I recently paid a visit to my alma mater and decided to stop by D's, a place I treasured during my college days. Stepping through the door, a wave of nostalgia engulfed me. I was eager to see if D's had maintained its charm. The bustling atmosphere filled with students and locals instantly transported me back to fond memories.I settled down at a familiar table by the window and eagerly examined the menu, hoping to discover any new additions since my last visit. To my delight, I noticed a few intriguing options that caught my attention. Starting with their renowned loaded fries, a dish that always managed to impress me in the past, seemed like the perfect choice.As I anxiously awaited my order, I couldn't help but admire the cozy decor. Adorning the walls were photographs and memorabilia reflecting the university's history, evoking memories of countless gatherings with friends. The staff, just as friendly as I remembered, buzzed around the place, offering genuine warmth and attentiveness to customers.Finally, my loaded fries arrived, and I was immediately reminded of why they had become a staple at D's. The crispy golden fries were generously topped with melty cheese, crispy bacon, and a tangy sauce that delivered a delightful kick. Each bite transported me back to late-night study sessions and spontaneous celebrations.Enthused by the pleasant beginning, I decided to venture into trying one of the new items on the menu-a juicy bacon avocado burger. The burger arrived adorned with fresh toppings on a perfectly toasted bun. The first bite revealed a harmonious blend of flavors, with the creamy avocado complementing the smoky bacon. It was a gratifying choice, and I relished every morsel with eagerness.The food's quality left a strong impression on me, and I was equally amazed by the impeccable service I received. The waitstaff remained attentive without being intrusive, ensuring that my every need was promptly met.

It's always fresh and good! Whenever I'm in the mood for Japanese and have approx 1 hour to enjoy my lunch (and have a healthy appetite! ) I come here on my lunch break. The noodles are by far my favorite part of the meal, I just love them! I've had the chicken, shrimp, steak, scallops over the years many times and they've all been delicious. Fried rice is super yummy too but is an up charge - $2 I think? (outside of lunch hours) which I think is crazy. Other places in the area don't do this and I think it's just a way for them to make an extra buck. I do pay it though bc I really like the fried rice. Unless you really want an alcoholic beverage save your $$, the beer on tap is often flat and mixed drinks are expensive and nothing that great. I'm not a huge sake fan but it's your average sake. The chefs are so-so, of course they can cook! But I like a show.. . it's hit or miss if you get a good one. They do good for coming out, talking with you, making adjustments, etc. Wait staff is pretty good but there are some bad ones as with all restaurants. If you get a good/great chef & waitress please tip them well (20%) as they share with each other. I do think that's fair as we out the chef through some grief at the table! nCan't speak on the sushi as surprisingly I've never had theirs.. . but looks like others have so be sure to read their reviews! nOn Friday & Saturday nights you will have a long wait so I'd recommend a reservation, even if it's just 2 of you, which will get you placed in a sectioned off portion where you have to take off your shoes.. . be forewarned! All tables seat about 10 on each side so you'll sit with strangers if you don't have a large group. Enjoy!

I work near this Walgreens, and I often find myself falling in and catching fast water, soda or a bottle of drugs (Tylenol, Advil, etc.) Essence Employees are always friendly and helpful, they always have what I want. The store is clean and tidy and the price is reasonable. I am very happy to have this Walgreen nearby! This is the first choice store for all my fast demand. I can always expect them to have what I need, and I always welcomes with a smile. I have been to this Walgreens for many years, and I have always had great experience. The employees are very friendly and helpful, and they do their best to ensure that I have a positive experience. They are always willing to answer my questions and help me find what I want. I am very grateful to this Walgreens for their convenience. It is located near my work, so I can easily stop and grab what I need without doing everything. This store is always clean and organized, and it is easy to find what I want. The price is also reasonable, this is a great advantage. Overall, I strongly recommend this Walgreen. This is a great store with friendly and useful employees. I am very happy to have this Walgreen nearby!

terrible... honestly, I don't even know where to begin with this. From the moment I walked in, I could tell it was going to be a disaster. The place was filthy, with food scraps scattered all over the floor and an unpleasant odor that lingered in the air. The staff seemed completely disinterested and unhelpful, giving off an air of indifference that made me question why they were even there in the first place.As if the ambiance wasn't bad enough, the food was a whole other level of disappointment. I ordered the chef's special, hoping for a culinary delight, but what arrived at my table was a sad excuse for a meal. The presentation was sloppy and unappetizing, and the taste was even worse. It felt as if the ingredients had been sitting in the fridge for far too long, resulting in a bland and stale dish that I couldn't force myself to finish.To make matters worse, the service was incredibly slow. It took ages for someone to take my order, and when the food finally arrived, I had to flag down a passing waiter just to get some utensils. It seemed like the staff was more interested in chatting amongst themselves than attending to the needs of the customers. It was beyond frustrating, especially considering the exorbitant prices they charged for such subpar service.Throughout my dining experience, I couldn't help but notice the overall lack of cleanliness and hygiene. The tables were sticky, the cutlery looked unclean, and to my horror, I spotted a cockroach scurrying across the floor. It was truly revolting and unacceptable, and I quickly lost my appetite.In addition to the appalling conditions, the noise level in the restaurant was unbearable. Loud music blared from the speakers, making it impossible to hold a conversation without shouting. It was clear that the establishment prioritized creating a "hip" atmosphere over providing a pleasant dining experience.

I took never heard of this restaurant before, but before I had the gift card, I decided to give it a try. The exterior of the building sounded a bit worn down, but I was hoping the dining would make up for it. After entering, I was greeted by a friendly host who showed me to my table. The decor was cozy, with dim lightweight and comfortable seating. The menu had a diverse of options, but I decided to go with the own of the day, a pasta dish with locally-sourced ingredients. I was happy to voir that the restaurant supported local farmers. My edible was prepared quickly, and the presentation was impressive. The flavours were rich and vibrant, with a perfect balance of seasoning. I was thoroughly impressed with the quality of the caterer. The portion size was generous, and I ended up taking some remains home with me. The service was precautionary and friendly, with my server checking in on me multiple times throughout the meal. The rewards were reasonable, especially considering the high-quality ingredients used. Overall, I was superbly surprised by this restaurant and would definitely return. It's a hidden gem in the area, and I'm persuaded I was able to experience it. I would recommend it to anyone trying for a delicious, satisfying meal in a cozy atmosphere.

My visit to Five Guys was outstanding. The service was extremely fast and friendly. I ordered a double bacon cheeseburger along with Cajun fries. The burger patty was thick and juicy. It was topped with crisp bacon, melty American cheese, shredded lettuce, and ripe tomato. With each bite, flavors of meat and cheese exploded in my mouth. The toasted bun held it all together perfectly. The Cajun fries were also delicious. They had a light crunchy coating with a nice spice level. Not too hot, just right for my taste. I enjoyed dipping the fries in the complimentary peanut oil based sauce. It added another layer of flavor. The seating area was clean and spacious. I had no problem finding a place to sit and enjoy my meal. The prices were very reasonable for the high quality of food. I could tell that everything was made fresh to order. All the employees were busy but managed to keep things organized. I will definitely be returning to Five Guys for another outstanding burger and fries experience. This is now one of my go-to spots for a tasty and affordable meal. Five stars all the way!

I wish I could give this quarter superstar. This experience was simply horrendous from start to finish. From the moment I arrived, it was clear the staff was disorganized and uncaring. I awaited over an hour just to check in, as no one seemed to know what they were doing. Wh en I finally got to my room, it was dirty and clearly hadn't been cleaned in some time. There were stains on the sheets and crumbs on the floor. The bathroom was an eevn bigger mess, with mold growing in the corners of the shower. I immedia tely called down to the front desk to request a new room. However, after multiple phone calls, nobody ever came to deal the issue. I ended up having to spend the night in that disgusting room. The free breakfast in the morning was laughable, offering only stale pastries and weak coffee. Onto my stay, the WiFi cut in and out constantly, making work nearly impossible. Other gusets I spoke to had similar complaints about the conditions and service. I won't be returning to this place, and I can't recommend it to an yone. There are much bet ter options in the area that are worth a few extra dollars. This hotel needs to improve its cleanliness and customer service significantly to earn even one star from me. My stay here was rock bottom for hotel exp eriences.

This is my local Taco Bell, and my Taco Bell of choice. I've been going here for years, and the food is always good. The service is also great - the staff is always friendly and helpful. One of my favorite things about this Taco Bell is the $5 cravings box. It's a great value, and you get a lot of food. I usually get the beefy 5-layer burrito, the crunchy taco, and the chips and cheese. It's always more than enough food, and it's always delicious.Another thing I like about this Taco Bell is the location. It's right off the highway, so it's easy to get to. There's also plenty of parking, so you don't have to worry about finding a spot.Overall, I'm very happy with this Taco Bell. The food is good, the service is great, and the location is convenient. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a good Taco Bell.In addition to the $5 cravings box, this Taco Bell also has a number of other great deals. They have a happy hour from 3-6pm, where you can get $1 tacos and $2 burritos. They also have a family night on Tuesdays, where kids eat free.If you're looking for a great Taco Bell, I highly recommend this one. The food is always good, the service is great, and the location is convenient. You won't be disappointed.

Went here last night after an tiresome day taking care of a newborn. My husband and I were pursuit for a place to eat that was close to home and had good eat. We ai heard good things about this restaurant, so we decided to give it a try. Myself were not disappointed! The eatin was delicious and the service was great. Our server was very warn and made sure that we had everything we needed. We boot off with the bruschetta, which was amazing. The bread was perfectly baguette and the toppings were fresh and flavorful. For our primordial course, I had the chicken parmesan and my husband had the steak. Both dishes were cooked to perfection and the flavors were inconceivable. We also directs a bottle of wine, which was very good. The atmosphere of the restaurant was also tremendously nice. It was cozy and visiting, and the lighting was dim and romantic. We absolutely enjoyed our experience at this restaurant and we will definitely be back. We would highly advise this restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal and a nice atmosphere. The food is wondrous, the service is great, and the atmosphere is very cozy and inviting. You won't be dispirited!

Being that this is the closest club to my location, I do shop here regularly. However, the customer service here leaves much to be desired. The staff is consistently rude and unhelpful, and they always seem to be out of the products I'm looking for. I've also had several issues with the pharmacy, including long wait times and incorrect prescriptions. Overall, I'm not impressed with this store and would not recommend it to anyone.In addition to the poor customer service, the store is also often dirty and disorganized. The shelves are often stocked haphazardly, and it's hard to find the products I'm looking for. The checkout lines are also always long, and it's not uncommon to wait 15-20 minutes to pay for my purchases.I've been shopping at this store for several years, and I've seen a steady decline in the quality of service. It's gotten to the point where I'm now actively avoiding this store and taking my business elsewhere. I would not recommend this store to anyone.

Oh boy, let me tell you about the good acts that come around here! I've been to this place a couple of times, and they sure know how to bring some awesome talent to town. From live bands to stand-up comedy, there's always something exciting happening. And you know what's even better? They often give out free tickets! I mean, who doesn't love a freebie, right?Especially in the summer, this place really amps up the fun. They know how to take advantage of the warm weather and put on some epic outdoor events. Picture yourself lounging on a blanket, sipping your favorite drink, and enjoying some great live music. It's pure bliss, my friend.The atmosphere here is electric. The crowd is always pumped up and ready to have a good time. You can feel the energy in the air as you walk through the gates. It's contagious, and it's impossible not to get caught up in the excitement. The staff is friendly and welcoming too, which adds to the overall positive vibe.Now, let's talk about the venue itself. It's spacious and well-designed, with different areas to suit various preferences. Whether you prefer standing up close to the stage or chilling at a table with your friends, they've got you covered. The acoustics are on point too, ensuring that you get the best sound experience possible.One thing I appreciate about this place is their dedication to supporting local talent. They often feature up-and-coming artists, giving them a platform to showcase their skills. It's fantastic to see them nurturing the local music scene and helping artists grow.Of course, no review is complete without mentioning the food and drinks. They've got a decent selection of snacks and beverages to keep you fueled throughout the night. I recommend grabbing a refreshing cold one and maybe some nachos to go along with it. Trust me, it's the perfect combo.Overall, I can't recommend this place enough. The combination of great acts, free tickets, and a lively atmosphere make it a must-visit spot.

Inside, it's a mix - diner meets hall, flags and Spaten gear everywhere. Most importantly - this is the only place in CLT to get a full liter of delicious, German beer. 10 bucks. Reasonable. Even Erk's huge paws get dwarfed by such a stein. I figured eating here would be spatzle only - fine, I'll have more bier - but no, there's actually a sweetly-done entree to be had - veggies wrapped in puff pastry, sliced, sauced with red pepper puree that had a creamy, somehow sharp bite. $13 makes it a tad pricey, and dinner entrees climb from that. Latkes (er, whoops) were lovely - croquettes as well. Kasespatzle on the kiddie's menu rounded out our carb party and was super-enjoyable - sliced thin, like linguine, seeking a Fettucine Alfredo-style dish - I like mine more dumpling, but still satisfying. Pretzal rolls? Hot mustard? Huge booths? Great service. OMB's Dunkel on tap, along with the big hits - Franziskaner (light AND dark, huzzah), Bitte burger, Warsteiner, Weihenstephaner. Wish it was closer.

Wanted to check out another neighborhood in Pittsburgh. To an ignorant outsider, North Side didn't seem much more sketch than South Side or Oakland. After picking up two bottles of red at Wine and Spirits on Ohio Street, my team and I got a table at the warm, homey Legends of the North Shore, where it's BYOB. For appetizers we ordered the margherita bruschetta (best choice), fried polenta, and greens 'n beans (mainly because we went on a Tuesday when they had a special deal for 99 cents with any entree). The focaccia bread is great with the homemade mixture of olive oil and herbs. I ordered the mussels bianca over linguine--terrific. Also comes with shrimp. The portions are generous but delicious, in part because it's clear that the tomato sauces are all made fresh and in-house. I tried my coworkers gnocchi--good, but I was quite satisfied with my own dish. My coworker who ordered the eggplant parmigiano really enjoyed her dish as well.

As far as Starbucks go, this is a pretty nice one. I mean, I've been to my fair share of Starbucks all across town, and this one stands out in a good way. First off, the ambiance is really inviting. They've got these cozy, oversized chairs by the windows where you can just plop down and get lost in your thoughts. It's like your own little corner of peace amidst the hustle and bustle of the city.And let's not forget about the staff. They're always super friendly and make you feel right at home. I remember this one time when I couldn't decide what drink to order, and the barista actually took the time to explain all the different options to me. It made me feel like they genuinely cared about my coffee experience.Speaking of drinks, they've got a wide variety to choose from. Whether you're into the classic Espresso Macchiato or you want to venture into more adventurous territory with a Caramel Brulée Frappuccino, they've got you covered. And they're always open to customizations, so you can really make your drink your own.The food selection is also top-notch. I can't resist their bacon and gouda breakfast sandwich - it's the perfect combination of savory and cheesy goodness. And their pastries, oh my. The butter croissants are flaky, buttery perfection, and don't even get me started on their blueberry muffins. They're simply heavenly.Another thing I appreciate about this Starbucks is that it's not too crowded. You know how some of their locations can get insanely busy, and you end up waiting in a long line just to get your caffeine fix? Well, that's not the case here. They manage their flow really well, and I never find myself getting impatient or frustrated.Oh, and did I mention the free Wi-Fi? It's a godsend for someone like me who often needs to get work done outside of the office. I can grab a spot near one of the power outlets, connect to their speedy internet, and tackle my to-do list while sipping on a delicious latte.

Quit with the 'it's too small, ' 'it's a Pittsburgh thing, ' and 'it's so greasy' statements. That's what Primanti's IS. It's a compact, greasy Pittsburgh right. Yes, the place is small, it is in Market Square, and will remain there, wouldn't you be disappointed if one day you wanted Primanti's and no more Market Square location? I know I would. If I were in the downtown region and had that craving I wouldn't want to have to work my way up to the Strip just for a bite of that Pittsburgh goodness. The 'it's a Pittsburgh' thing comments baffle me. If you have food shows featuring the sandwich, magazines writing about it, and it's considered the 'Manliest Restaurant in America, ' I think that means it's more than just a Pittsburgh thing. Why else would Primanti's be featured on such media? Why else would these people centered around shows and magazines venture to a Primanti's? I mean that has to show you it's more than just a Pittsburgh thing. And 'it's so greasy? ' Did you not watch them makes your sandwich, which you picked from their extensive menu, on the griddle in front of you? Expect it to be greasy, they are frying it for you and melting that cheese on it. Maybe don't even pay attention to the greasy factor, especially with that crunchy coleslaw and heap of fries placed between those two thick slices of Italian bread. Better yet, move out of my way, I'm about to chow down on that Pittsburgh grease fest awaiting my attention.

I never get super excited to go to Monty's but it is never disappointing. Possibly except for the 30-45 minute wait. This last time, I went in seriously craving me some pie. I ended up filling up on their mac and cheese. No room for pie. All of their pies at the time also just did not sound exactly to be what I wanted either. I was craving a fruity cherry pie or something and it was just turning to fall so it was either chocolate or fall flavors. Not their fault, but a curse of my pie needs. The food is good. I am not a huge breakfast person so pancakes are not usually my thing but they do have a few options I do eat, like breakfast potatoes and sometimes I even venture out of my comfort zone for the eggs. I honestly do not think I have tried the same thing twice because they have so many options.

A co-worker who always gives Madonna's rave reviews picked the new location for a lunch date. He had talked about the spices, the flavor, the service. Well, it was one for three. The service was friendly, even during the lunch rush. I had the chico chicken quesadilla. For $4. 81 (with tax), it was a pretty big quesadilla. However, it was just Monterrey jack, chicken, and a soft shell. No spices, no onions, no peppers. It was still decent for the price. But I'm 99. 9996% sure that the chicken was from a can. How would I know? Because I've cheated and used that same canned chicken in quiches when I was in a rush. It's good canned chicken, but c'mon! My lunchmates also complained that their burritos were bland. I'm giving three stars because I believe Madonna's can (and will) do better. P. S. CASH ONLY!

I'm no expert on Chinese food. I have heard people rave about Italian restaurants that I, as an Italian, find lacking; so I suspect that someone of Chinese ancestry might think First Wok falls short. Take that as a caveat. Anyway, I like their egg rolls and boiled dumplings. The crab rangoons don't impress. Their hot and sour soup is good. Gentle kick to it. I often get Pork Lo Mein and enjoy that. Servings are ample. The General Tsao Chicken is good, as are all the entrees I have tried. The usual unappetizing photos of their dishes adorn the wall. I often wonder about those photos. A friend living in Taiwan sent me a cookbook that was popular there and it contained the same quality photos of the food. Curious. The menu lists a plethora of items and the wall has posted another list of dozens of entrees. What these all are escapes me and there is often a language barrier when asking for an explanation. Sometimes I feel adventurous and plan to order something I never had before but I always end up going with something familiar. For a sit-down dinner, I prefer Rainbow Gardens on Neil Street, but for a quick and satisfying Chinese dinner, First Wok should not disappoint.

We told them this and they seated us anyway. We called them knowing they were a few miuntes or better away. We ordered drinks and food for them. About 5 minutes later the hostess who sat us came back and started trying to talk us into squeezing into a table for 6. I told her they were down the street and we had just ordered for them so there was no reason to switch. She said there was another large party that was all here. .. . Just then the rest of our group showed up. If they had not I would have left. The server and the food that night were great and almost made me forget about the hostess. Then we came again with some friends raving about the food. Must have been a new chef. The service was still great but EVERYTHING was really salted. The pizza, the calamari, the pasta. 3 of us ordered a home made pasta with portabello mushrooms, it was so salty we could not eat it. The waitress tried so hard, she apologized and even offered us a free tira misu for desert. Sorry to say cause the servers are great, but Mama's is off our list.

Sadly Wiener World does it worst. A bad fish sandwich in Pittsburgh is like bad BBQ in Texas or a bad cheesesteak in Philadelphia, an offensive abomination that denigrates the pride and reputation of the region. I have never had a worse fish sandwich anywhere (including in fast food hole in the walls) and at $10, this assault on your taste buds doesn't come cheap. It was bad in every way it could be bad. Frozen, greasy, tasteless, heavy on bland batter and light on fish. To add to it, even though the inside of the establishment is large, there are no chairs to sit down (just counters), they don't take cards (cash only, but they do have an atm) and the inside was freezing, I was shivering in the 60* temperature even though it was 80 outside in July. So why do they get 2 stars instead of just 1? My server was very nice, the fries with the sandwich were prepared fresh and were good, and I've heard from many reputable sources that their ice cream is fantastic. That said, I'll be licking my wounds from disappointment for a while before I lick their ice cream.

I took a Subaru Outback here for the annual state safety and emissions inspections, and boy was it an ordeal. I mean, I had heard good things about this place, but my experience left much to be desired. First of all, let me tell you about the staff. They were not the friendliest bunch, to say the least. It felt like I was interrupting their day just by showing up. Now, I understand they probably deal with a lot of customers, but a little bit of courtesy wouldn't hurt, right? Anyway, after waiting for what seemed like an eternity, they finally got around to inspecting my car. And guess what? They found not one, but two issues that needed immediate attention. I couldn't believe it! I had just gotten my car serviced a month ago, so how could there be these major problems already? It felt like they were trying to pull a fast one on me, like they wanted to make some extra cash by "discovering" these issues. But here's the kicker: they quoted me an exorbitant price for the repairs! I couldn't believe my ears when they told me the amount. It was outrageous! I mean, seriously, I could get the same work done at another reputable garage for half the price. Talk about taking advantage of unsuspecting customers. Needless to say, I took my car and got out of there as fast as I could. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone I know, not even my worst enemy. They may have some nice reviews online, but my personal experience tells a completely different story. Do yourself a favor and steer clear of this place if you value your time, money, and sanity.

It's a bit out of the way for me (Sunset Blvd. ), but when I'm in the area it's a classic stop for some tasty Carolina 'cue. I think I kick up my 3. 5 rating to 4. 0 as the service has been just so kind. Bubba is one of the nicest restaurant owners I've ever met and the servers are truly salt of the Earth people. Plus, Bubba often donates product to a local charity for events, which makes this place aces in my book. As for the food, you'll be in and out in no time as the food comes out in a flash. I typically order the petite plate as and I unfortunately enjoy the included hush puppies a bit too much. : ) It's not the best 'cue I've had in Charlotte, but I do enjoy it quite a bit! The digs are pretty basic and nondescript, but I'm usually there to grab a quick bite of 'cue and if I'm in the need of a major sugar rush - a sweet tea.

I got there just to try the new triangular steak sandwich. It did not beguile. The bun was juicy and flavorful, and the cheese was melted and gooey. The bun was soft and sweet, and the whole sandwich was just the right size. I also become a side of fries, which were crispy and delicious. The service was terrific, and the atmosphere was casual and inviting. I would clearly recommend this place to anyone looking for a great sandwich. The restaurant is locating in a tiny strip mall, and it's easy to miss if you're not looking for it. But it's helpful seeking out. The menu is limited, but everything is made fresh to orders. In added to the triple steak sandwich, I've also tried the chicken parmesan sandwich and the pulled pork sandwich. Both were unbelievable. The chicken parmesan sandwich is made with a lightly breaded and fried chicken hoagie, topped with marinara sauce and fusing cheese. The pulled beef sandwich is made with slow-cooked pork that is tender and flavorful. The sideways are also very good. The cheddar are crispy and well-seasoned. The onion rings are thick and mistreatment. And the onion is creamy and tangy. The service is persistently friendly and attentive. The staff is happy to make recommendations and answer any questions you be. The atmosphere is casual and enquired. The cantina is decorated in a rustic style, with lots of wood and brick. There are a few tables inside, as satisfactorily as a few outside on the patio. The prices are radically reasonable. The meatloaf are all under $10, and the sides are all under $5. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great hamburgers. The supper is delicious, the service is great, and the prices are reasonable. Overall, I had a great experience at this deli. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a great salads.

We came here to celebrate my college graduation. The restaurant had been recommended by some family friends as a nice spot for a celebration. When we arrived there was a bit of a wait, but we were able to get a table more quickly than expected. The dining room had a warm, inviting atmosphere that seemed perfect for the occasion. After being seated, we had a chance to look over the menu. There was an intriguing selection of pasta dishes, seafood options, and steaks. I decided to go with a shrimp risotto while others in my party selected chicken Parmesan or salmon. The service was excellent from the start, with our server being attentive without being overbearing. She gave helpful recommendations on wine pairings. It didn't take long for our meals to arrive once we placed our order. Everything looked beautifully prepared and the portion sizes were generous. I found my risotto to be flavorful and creamy with big, tender shrimp throughout. The others remarked that their entrees were equally delicious. For dessert, we shared a few homemade tiramisu and cannoli. It was the perfect way to finish the meal. Overall, the food, service and atmosphere made it an ideal place to celebrate such a happy event. I'm glad we chose this restaurant and would be happy to return for another special occasion in the future.

Their chips and salsa are complimentary and the salsa has just the right amount of spice to it, not to hot but enough that you know it is there and that it is homemade. The taco loco has just the right amount of everything on it to give you the full experience of its flavors and textures in every bite. It is very filling for only being a taco and the rice and beans on the side are a perfect compliment to it. The service is excellent and the restaurant is always clean. The prices are very reasonable, with the taco loco being one of the least expensive items on the menu and the most filling. I could go on and on about how much I love this place and why it is my favorite Mexican restaurant in town, but I guess I should probably stop now and let you come experience this place for yourself.

Maybe it's because I didn't try the custard. But seriously, I didn't need more weighing down in this weather.. . so I ordered an orange crush float instead. For something that would have cost me MAYBE 50cents to make at home, I paid close to $5 for a 12oz cup. That is ridiculous. In general, I think their prices are pretty steep for what you get.. .. you'd probably have to order a burger to really get a bang for your buck.. . Like RB, I also had an issue with the service. It was slow, disorganized, and not very friendly. The line was almost out the door, but the employees behind the counter didn't even ATTEMPT to speed up the service. One of them just disappeared into a back room. tsktsk. Unfortunately, what I experienced was mediocre food and some of the worst service I've ever experienced. My dining companion and I were seated promptly. After 10 min., the waitress came over and asked about drinks. After another 10 min., she brought our drinks and asked what we wanted to order. I ordered the special, which was listed on the chalkboard (don't recall what it was exactly). The waitress took our orders and went back to put them in. Fifteen minutes later, the waitress returned, but not with our food. Instead, she apologetically informed me that the special was not available because they were out of one of the necessary ingredients. Um, why didn't she mention this immediately after she'd put the order in? I chose a different entree (this time one of the regular ones), and the waitress went back to put that order in. It took at least another 15 min. for the food to come out (we'd been there for 50 min., for those of you keeping track), and when it finally did, I was quite underwhelmed. I don't recall what I ordered, but I know it had chicken and I recall the chicken being dry and bland--clearly, not what I was hoping for in a Peruvian restaurant! This shouldn't have surprised me, since I noticed the waitress preparing it in the microwave. Pro tip to restaurateurs: If you need to use a microwave in your food prep, it's best to hide it in the back. Having been to Ecuador, where the food is similar to Peruvian fare, the food here certainly didn't seem very genuine. Unsurprisingly, the check took at least 10 min. to show up once we'd finished. By this time, I was through with this place. Yeah, it has interesting decor, but that didn't make up for the abysmal service I received here. After taking off from LaGuardia, the plane was hit by a flock of geese, which disabled both engines. Captain Sullenberger quickly decided to ditch the Airbus A320 in the Hudson River, and his quick decision and skillful landing saved the lives of all 155 souls on board. Investigations later confirmed that there was no alternative to ditching the plane in the river, given its location and altitude. The crew and passengers huddled together on the wing, stunned but overwhelmed with gratitude for Sullenberger's heroism. The rescuers rushed to the scene and within minutes everyone was safely out of the sinking plane. The nearby ferries and pleasure boats joined the rescue effort, pulling the shocked but grateful passengers out of the icy water. The "miracle on the Hudson" made Sullenberger an instant hero and he was held up as the gold standard for pilot skill under extreme duress. For days afterwards, the world's news channels showed riveting images of the impossible landing and its aftermath.

If the air conditioning, elevators, and Wifi had worked properly, it would have been a different story. But the fact that these essential services were out of order, and the roof leaked, made for a very unpleasant stay.

We decided on a whim to try something different for a bar and this place indeed was. Saturdays there is a cover for the DJ which was $3. This didn't seem so bad to me after coming from other cities where the covers are $15 and $20 and higher but I feel like the place could use the money. Peanutz is a small venue. The bar area is narrow and cramped then to the left of it there is a dark area where the DJ is along with some tables and then the stairs to the bathroom. If you weren't at the bar then people were just sitting at the tables starring at the DJ or at you.. . Maybe one or two people were dancing to the music. I thought the music was awesome though - a mix of old school and underground hip hop. Beers were so cheap - I think we paid $5 for three draft beers. Woot!! However some folks were smoking and the bathrooms were gross. My jacket took a few days to air out the smell of the smoke. I won't be returning even if Peanutz offered some peanuts.

Even if the price of $ 30 is $ 15, the price is still too high ......... I was disappointed with the experience of this restaurant. The food is not good, and the service is even worse. The waiter was rude and dismissed, and he would always spend our order. When the food finally arrived, the weather was cold and tasteless. I will not recommend this restaurant to anyone. The atmosphere of the restaurant is also not attractive. It was dark and dirty, and the table was dirty. The walls are covered with graffiti, and foods are scattered on the floor. Obviously, this restaurant has not been well maintained. My experience of this restaurant was very disappointed. I will not recommend it to anyone. If you are looking for a meal, it is recommended that you watch it elsewhere.

We used to come here after going to Pirates games since its right up the road. Now its one of my favorite places to go out with my friends. Its a bit pricey (~$15/person), but the quality and quantity is superb. The service is pretty good. The atmosphere has a nice feel to it, perhaps its the antiquity.. I love the cuckoo clock and tapestries they have. Now, to the food: nThe bread they give you.. . with apple butter!! .. . is very fresh and tasty. Try not to fill up on it while waiting on your huge main course.. The Bavarian soft pretzels were warm and soft when we ordered them. Also delicious. The sampler platter is a great deal if you don't know yet what you like. You get 3 entrees and the typical sides for ~$16. My favorite, though, is the schnitzel liechtenstein, with sauerkraut and potato pancakes. Fresh and delicious everytime. I would definitely recommend this place to anybody who likes ethnic, or German/Bavarian food, or just trying new stuff. It's awesome.

If I could give them zero stars, I gotta, without a doubt. My experience with this company has been absolutely horrendous from start to finish. The customer service is non-existent, with representatives who are rude and unhelpful. They seem to have no regard for their customers' concerns or needs. Furthermore, the product itself is of such poor quality that it barely lasts a few uses before falling apart. It's clear that this company prioritizes profit over providing a satisfactory experience to its consumers. What's even more frus trating is their lack of accountability. It's tremendously disheartening to see a company that cares so little about its customers. I srtongly advise anybody considering doing business with them to think twice and look elsewhere for a more reputable and reliable option. Save yourself the frustration and disappointment that I've endured by steering clear of this company. Trust me, you'll be best off.

Time Warner Cable is awful. Their customer se rvice is unacceptable, with long hold times and unhelpful representatives. It transpires like they actively avoid helping customers and just want to end calls as quickly as possible. The equipment they provide is cheap and unreliable, with the cable Boxes and modems incessantly needing to be reset or replaced. Upgrades and new installations also take forever to complete, leaving customers without service for weeks at a time. Even ordinary maintenance often disrupts service for hours or days without warning. The speeds we p ay for are rarely actually delivered, especially during peak hours. Outages are also far too common, whether planned or unplanned. Their website and billing are an endless source of confusion and frustration as well. It's nearly impossible to get an accurate bill or make meaningful changes to your account online. Their rates moreover increase annually at an unjustifiable rate but we have no other real options for service in our area. At this point, I thinks anything would be better than Time Warner Cable. If another provider offered servicing here I would switch immediately, no matter the cost, just to get away from the poor service and outdated equipment. Time Warner Cable may have once been a leader in the industry but they have clearly fallen very far behind. Unless they make drastic improvements soon, I fear they will continue losing more and more customers to cord cutting and nwer competitors. Their poor reputation is fully deserved based on my many negative experiences as a long time customer.

My Ist time experience was GOOD! I was pleased with how easy everything was to set up and get started with. I'm happy I took the leap to try this for the first time and I feel like my quality of life has improved because of it. The price was reasonable for the great service I got. I had no side effects or lingering issues after leaving. I'm a believer now in this method and approach. I'm a satisfied repeat customer because of how well it worked for me initially. They made what could be a stressful experience into a relaxing one. I'm really glad I chose this place and I hope others read this review and decide to give it a try for themselves. It's well worth it for the results.

I ordered take out from this P. F. Chang's on Tuesday night and have to say that is was terrible. The food was cold and soggy by the time it arrived, over an hour after I placed my order. All of the items I received were lukewarm at best. The chicken was dry and flavorless, completely inedible. The rice and vegetables had no taste remaining, likely from sitting under a heat lamp for too long. I will not order from this location again since the quality is so poor. Better to just avoid P. F. Chang's altogether if this is what you can expect for takeout. It was definitely not worth the price I paid. I am surprised such a large chain would allow food to be delivered in that poor of condition. Do not make the same mistake - find a restaurant that actually cares about customer satisfaction.

If you happen to find yourself transferring (and many of you there will, since most of you do not actually live in Charlotte), you will invariably be dropped at the end of one concourse and have to make it to the end of another with about 17 minutes to make your connection, what with the airline industry being what it is and all. We even have a cell phone lot where you can wait for you loved one to let you know they have arrived, at which point you can go pick them up from the baggage claim.

It just has to be a parody of a vegetarian restaurant. Like, every time I start reading the menu I think Ashton Kutcher is going to pop out and tell me I've been Punk'd. A small disclaimer: I am not vegan or vegetarian and I never will be. I love meat. But I also love vegetables and fruits and pretty much the entire food pyramid. And these things can be combined to make tasty vegan food. But "Texturized vegetable protein hydrated with seasonings" is not food to me. Yep, that description of their "chorizo" comes directly off their menu. Eating vegetarian does NOT mean you need to subject yourself to these highly processed "foods. "nnLess processed substitutes like tofu, tempeh, and seitan are used as well, but they are mostly treated as a stand-in for meat. I guess if you are a vegetarian that misses eating meat, this may satisfy you. However, as an omnivore, why would I eat a faux-BLT when I can eat a real one? How about instead of trying to imitate the flavor and texture of meat, we actually come up with creative combinations of vegetables, fruits, and legumes that are delicious in their own right. What a concept! Have you ever eaten a vegetarian dish and thought, "Whoa, I can't believe I actually like this better than meat"? I have! But don't expect that feeling here. It will be more like: "Umm.. . I guess tofu mixed with nutritional yeast is kinda reminiscent of scrambled eggs? "nnTwo stars because I really like the drinks here. The ones I remember trying were the ginger lemonade, the Mexican hot chocolate, and the root beer with a shot of espresso. They have some really wonderful sounding tea options that I wish I could try, but I generally avoid this place because of the food.

We went to the one at "PPG. " The place was busy but not crowded on a Friday night. The menu was on the wall along with murals of Pittsburgh's finest sports starts. Our server was quick and efficient and we never were in need of refills or anything else. I got the Pitts-burgher cheese steak and we tried an order of the Smallman Street Fries. The fries were truly loaded. The chili had a nice kick to it and there was literally an ice cream scoop of sour cream on top. However, the fries were actually seasoned that well and were under done in my opinion. That didn't bode well for the fries on the sandwich, but I kept my hopes high. The sandwich comes out and its a monster. I love the italian bread, the beef patty and cheese, the slaw was good (shredded cabbage, not like southern cole slaw). Everything was fresh but, again, the fries were the worst part. Underdone, underseasoned. Definitely my least favorite part. Nonetheless, I would definitely return because I want to try some of the other menu items. I've heard double-meat is the way to go. I'm intrigued.

Carolina appliance was sent by out Best Buy Geek Squad protection plan to fix our brand new dryer when it started overheating and making a scratching noise. They came quickly - only three days from when we reported the problem. They said they needed to order a part and would be back within 7 business days to install it. When two weeks go by, I called to check in. No one answered the phone during business hours. My husband called back later. Neither of our messages were returned. We called Best Buy who contacted them and requested they get in touch with us. After about 15 phone calls from Best Buy, my husband, and myself, we just have up. Not one of these calls was ever returned and no one answers the phone during business hours so it is impossible to follow up. THE WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER! Now we are working with another Geek Squad recommended company but having problems since our dryer was under warranty and the company already paid for the part Carolina Appliance ordered for our dryer (and is apparently holding hostage). Not to mention, it will now be another week and a half or two weeks for the part to come in again - leaving us without a dryer for a month and a half. I would never recommend this company to anyone. There isn't a day that goes by that I think of what we could have done with that $400 we spent. We could have gone on a weekend getaway to a nearby city, or splurged on a nice dinner at a fancy restaurant. Instead, we decided to spend it on a private dining experience at Ancala Country Club.I had heard great things about the club's food and service, but unfortunately, our experience fell short. The atmosphere was stiff and formal, and the service was slow and unfriendly. Our server seemed put off when we asked for recommendations and took a long time to take our order.The food was also a letdown. We opted for the three-course Chef's Tasting menu, which was supposed to be a reflection of the chef's creativity and expertise. However, the dishes were uninspired and lacked flavor. The presentations were also underwhelming, with one dish consisting of a few slices of duck confit placed on top of a bed of what looked like canned baked beans.The second course was equally disappointing. The tomato soup was bland and overrun with liquid, and the goat cheese was rubbery and tasted more like feta than goat cheese. The third course, rack of lamb, was the only redeeming quality of the meal. It was cooked to perfection and flavorful, but it wasn't enough to make up for the disappointment of the first two courses.To top it all off, the club's ambiance was stale and outdated. The decor was tired and lacked any real character, and the overall vibe was stuffy and exclusive. We felt out of place and uncomfortable, and we couldn't wait to leave.In the end, we left feeling disappointed and ripped off. We could have spent that $400 so much better elsewhere, and we vowed never to return to Ancala Country Club again.

The menu offered a wide variety of choices, making it difficult to choose just one dish. After much deliberation, we finally settled on the "All-in" platter, which offered a generous selection of smoked ribs, brisket, pulled pork, and sausage. The food arrived promptly and was beautifully presented on a large platter. The ribs were tender and smothered in a rich, smoky sauce. The brisket was equally impressive, with a perfect balance of lean meat and marbled fat. The pulled pork was moist and flavorful, with a hint of sweetness. The sausage was well-seasoned and had a nice snap. The sides were equally impressive, with creamy coleslaw, tangy pickles, and perfectly cooked fries. Each bite was a symphony of smoky, savory flavors that danced on our taste buds. We savored every bite and finished our meal feeling completely satisfied. As we left the restaurant, we were grateful for the wonderful experience we had had. We would definitely be back soon for more smoky goodness!

This lpace was recommended to us about, twenty miles away? It was a little out of the wa, but we were so glad we made the trip. Thf food was amazing! We started with the fried calamari, which was lightly battered and cuoked to perfection. The mrainara sauce was also very good. For our main course, I had the chicken parmesan, which was one of the best I've eveA had. hTe chicken was tender and juicy, and the sauce was flavorful and not too heavy. My husband had the seafod risotto, which was also delicious. The seafood was fresh and plentiful, and the risotto was cooked pefrectly. W were too full for dessert, but we will definitely be back to try some next time. The serveice was also excellent. Our waiter was attentive and friednly, and he made sure we had a great experience. Overall, we highly recommend this rstaurant. The food is amazing, the service is excellnet, and the prices are reasonable. We will definitely be bCack! The atmosphere was woarm and inviting, and the staff was very friendly and attentive. The food was delicious, and we especially enjoyed the fried calaOari, chicken parmesan, and seafood risotto. We will definitely be back to try some of the other dishes on the mneu.

We were a party of two on a Sunday night -- the restaurant was moderately busy. Our server was a bit of a space cadet. We had to stop another waiter to ask for more water.. . I was never offered a refill on my diet coke (which sat empty for over 30 minutes). The salmon was very good, but drenched in so much olive oil and garlic that an oil slick was left on the plate at the end of the meal. The pasta tasting was.. .. kind of weird. One of the selections tasted like feet, the other tasted like something I could make at home with a bottle of Prego. The best was a mushroom ravioli in olive oil -- but there was so much oil (see a theme? ) I had to scrape it off before eating. Long story short, we passed on dessert. The food was adequate, the service was sub-par, and it was just kind of a "meh" experience. I won't go back.

The restaurant was intimate and cozy, with a fireplace crackling in the corner. We ordered a bottle of red wine to share, and our waiter, Mihály, was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. The menu offered a variety of delicious dishes, including fish, steak and pasta. My boyfriend and I shared the grilled shrimp appetizer, which was delicious and perfectly cooked. My parents ordered the Caesar salad, which they said was fresh and well-dressed. He recommended the best dishes and was always available to fill our glasses. My boyfriend ordered the filet mignon, which he said was tender and juicy. My parents both ordered the beef tenderloin, which they said was cooked to perfection. I had the salmon, which was moist and flaky. We also ordered sautéed mushrooms, which were earthy and savory, and garlic mashed potatoes, which were rich and garlicky. As we were enjoying our meal, the chef came out to greet us and chatted with us for a while. He was very friendly and proud of the food he had created. For dessert, we shared the chocolate lava cake, which oozed a thick chocolate sauce when we cut into it. It was rich and delicious and the perfect way to end our meal. Our experience at this restaurant was excellent. The food was outstanding, the service was impeccable and the atmosphere was warm and inviting. We would definitely go back and recommend it to others.

Years ago, this was a regular spot. I remembered the room was dark, food was good, and the infamous pole in the lady's room. So on a recent cold winter night, while Melissa & I were trying to figure out where to eat, knowing this is her regular spot, I said Alexander Michael's! Parking is always a challenge. Luckily we got a spot down the road off the side street. However the darkness is a little creepy.. . I feel like I need a buddy system to park there (find a friend, hold hands, and walk together like we were in grade school). The embiance was perfect for a cold night with the lit candles and closely spaced seatings. We got a table very quickly, but that's as much service as we got that night. There wasn't any incident. The waitress wasn't rude, but she just wasn't there. For a small place like this, it should be pretty easy to take good care of every table. The food was ok as well. I ordered the london broil sandwich with the soup as side. I forgot the "crab" soup was made with fake crab, which I think should be illegal to be called crab. My sandwich had enough meat on it that I pretty much just ate all the meat, which was average. Tender enough, not too much taste to it. I guess for $9. 50 I couldn't complain. Years later, I felt that their menu was limited, a little overpriced, and seems to be lacking a spark in general with food and service. I will give it a 2nd chance and visit again, maybe not anytime soon.

My first day in Charlotte and I had checked Yelp reviews to plan my meals. The only good thing I can say is service was friendly and the cornbread was good. nHowever, that wasn't enough to even warrant a second star because the rest of my food was so unpleasant. I started with the soul rolls, but thought the mixture of flavors and textures did not harmonize well. It seemed to be a fried app just for the sake of being fried. But without the pleasing crunch I expected. nBut the real let down was my shrimp and grits. What they served me was a bowl of lumpy grits (one particular lump was too big for my spoon to handle) swimming in a truly awful brown mess. The color made me think the sauce might be rich, but it was the opposite. I could probably recreate the flavor with water, thickener and food color - that is just how tasteless it was. The shrimp had a strange texture that made me think it came from a can. Then someone had chopped raw green onion and stirred it in. That was it. No seasoning. No flavor.

Personally, I love this bar. This place is 5 miles from my office and 5 miles from my house, no wonder I made it to 200 beers so easily! The Flying Saucer literally has approximately 300 unique beers, with at least 100 on tap, and some of them are rotating beers. Additionally, they have daily specials, like pint night with $3 pints and biggie beers for the price of a pint and even beer poker. Their loyalty program is also rad, drink 200 unique beers and get a $100 tab on the house to have a party with your friends (I'm 421). Fear not non-beer drinkers, they also have liquor drinks. Their food menu is decent, I mean, it's bar food.. . The pretzels with queso dip are the best! And the scenery, aka the waitresses, aren't bad to look at either.. . in their school girl uniforms. They have pool tables in the back and good music streaming, unless a crappy band happens to be playing. If a band is playing and there is a cover, Beer Knurd members get in for free. Prost!

But despite their warnings, I decided to give it a shot and see for myself. From the moment I walked in, I could tell something was off. The atmosphere felt stale, and there was a strange smell lingering in the air. I tried to ignore it and focus on the menu. The selection seemed decent enough, so I decided to order a classic burger with fries. Little did I know, it would be a decision I'd come to regret. After placing my order, the wait began. And let me tell you, it was excruciatingly long. It felt like time had slowed down, and I couldn't help but notice how understaffed they were. The few waiters running around seemed overwhelmed and stressed. Finally, after what seemed like an eternity, my burger arrived at the table. But to my disappointment, it looked nothing like the picture on the menu. The burger patty was overcooked and dry, lacking any juiciness or flavor. The toppings were haphazardly thrown together, and the bun was stale. It was a complete letdown. I called the waiter over to express my dissatisfaction, hoping they would offer a solution. However, they seemed indifferent to my concerns. They simply shrugged and walked away without offering an apology or any attempt to make it right. That level of customer service was unacceptable. As I looked around the restaurant, I noticed I wasn't the only one disappointed. The tables nearby were filled with frustrated customers and plates of subpar food. It became clear that my experience wasn't an isolated incident. I felt deceived by the positive reviews I had read beforehand. How could this place have such high ratings? Maybe people had different expectations, or perhaps they were swayed by other factors that I couldn't comprehend. But from my perspective, this restaurant failed to meet even the basic standards of quality and service. In the end, I couldn't finish my meal. It was simply too unappetizing to bear. I left the restaurant feeling disheartened and vowing never to return.

The service was horrible. We waited 35 minutes before our waitress came to take our order, and then it took another 45 minutes for our food to arrive. When it finally did arrive, it was cold and unappetizing. My mother ordered the chicken pot pie, and it was nothing more than a bowl of tasteless soup with a few pieces of chicken and vegetables floating around in it. I ordered the meatloaf, and it was dry and flavorless. The mashed potatoes were lumpy and the green beans were mushy. To top it all off, the prices were outrageous. We will never be going back to that dump again.We should have known better than to go to a restaurant that was advertising a "Best in Madison" award. Those awards are usually nothing more than a scam. The only thing that this restaurant has going for it is its location. It's right on the main drag, so it gets a lot of foot traffic. But don't be fooled by the crowds. The food is terrible and the service is even worse.I would rather eat a bowl of nails than go back to that restaurant. If you're looking for a good meal in Madison, there are plenty of other options that are much better than this place. Save your money and your taste buds, and stay away from this dump.

Food is only fair - burger was pretty flavorless and dry. Onion rings were awful - crunchy on the outside but mushy and wet (actually had onion "juice" or water run out after biting in to one) on the inside. Service was ok. My only complaint is that the server left the check on the table before asking for dessert orders. If it was a. ) busy and b. ) we appeared to be a business lunch (not likely - me and the parents) I would understand that move. But the restaurant wasn't busy - worrysome at 12: 30 pm on a Friday - and we obviously were not a business group. Thought it was overpriced too - almost $9 for a dry tasteless burger with a side of onion rings and $5 for a chocolate malt? Would not rate it a great value. Fake 50's decor and kitsch - primary reasons for visiting here. Need more really GOOD casual (not fast food) eateries near the Arboretum.

Items are well organized, and easy to find. As others' state, it ain't cheap! One way we lowered our Whole Foods bill was to go for their 365 in-house brand, which is typically priced at the same pricepoint as similar items in the regular chain grocery stores. We don't use Whole Foods for all of our supermarket needs, just the specialty items, great produce, and seafood. I docked two stars for absolutely terrible parking - yep. I know that's harsh, but every time we come here, we need to factor in another 10-15 minutes to get a parking spot and be able to leave safely (there are always cars behind us looking for a spot when we are trying to leave, and so we often can't just pull out of the space and leave quickly.. . ) Even being careful, we have almost been hit multiple times by people losing their cool with the terrible parking. That being said, we will continue to come here to stock our home when we plan to entertain at home.

85.. . DEAL! I asked for the eggs to be scrambled and it came with home fries and toast. I know my meal wasn't that exciting and can you really mess up eggs, toast or potatoes?! ? ! The eggs and toast were fine - something I could've made at home. But the home fries left something to be desired. They had no flavor - it's like someone boiled some potatoes and slapped them in a pan and served them on a plate. I put some salt and pepper on them, but it didn't really help - it's like the potatoes were determined to be tasteless. I ate a few forkfuls and just gave up. I came here for a meeting in the morning and it wasn't crowded. Looked like there were some regulars but fairly low key. I could definitely see how peeps who come here after a night of being out. I'm not sure that I'd make it a point to go to Ritters unless it was a night out and I needed a place open 24 hours. They are CASH only!

Stopped in on Saturday before dinner across the street. We were seated right by the register which was a major bummer at first but ended up being nice to watch the game. It was freezing out so a fancy cocktail was just what we needed to warm us up. I got a maple old fashioned that hit the spot. We had a whole bottle of wine too since they had a decent corkage fee. The bartender was super friendly and chatty which made us feel right at home. Most of the tables filled up as the night went on and it got louder and more festive in there. They had a good selection of beers on tap too if cocktails aren't your thing. We almost pulled the trigger on dessert but weren't too hungry after our meal across the street. All in all it was a nice pre-dinner stop, even if the seating wasn't ideal at first, but I wouldn't wanna hang for too long - might need to nope out of there if it gets too rowdy!

I recently had a frustrating shopping experience at [Store Name]. The lack of price tags on items was a significant issue for me. I found myself constantly approaching staff members to inquire about prices, which took up a considerable amount of my time. Even when I did manage to find a price tag, it was often faded and unreadable, giving the impression that the store didn't want customers to know the prices.I resorted to using my phone to scan barcodes to get an idea of the prices, but that didn't always work. We were seated promptly even though it was a busy Saturday night. The ambiance inside was beautiful with high ceilings, soft lighting and elegant decor. The menu had a nice variety of appetizers, salads, pasta, fish and steaks to choose from. My husband had the filet mignon which came with potatoes and vegetables. The filet was cooked perfectly to order, a nice medium rare and very tender. We started with the truffle mac and cheese bites which were rich and delicious. Both of our meals were delicious and the perfect portion sizes. I had the pan seared salmon with risotto and spinach. The salmon was moist and fresh tasting. We also enjoyed the bottle of wine we ordered, a nice cab sauv from California. Our server was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. She gave us some recommendations based on our food preferences. The bill came to a little over $100 for two people with drinks and appetizer which I thought was reasonable for the quality of food. For dessert we split the chocolate mousse which was rich and creamy. It was the perfect way to end our meal. The atmosphere and service made for a very enjoyable dining experience. The interior design had an upscale yet comfortable feel. We would definitely go back to try more items on the menu. Our server mentioned they are always busy on the weekend with regular customers and people trying them out for restaurant week.

Primanti Bros is my indulgent guilty pleasure that I succumb to once a year, and without fail, it reminds me why I keep going back. From the moment I enter, the tantalizing scent of sizzling meats and freshly baked bread permeates the air, instantly arousing my taste buds. The ambiance exudes a cozy and unpretentious vibe, adorned with sports memorabilia on the walls and lively conversations filling the space. Settling into my seat, I can't help but eagerly anticipate the forthcoming gratification. The menu, an expansive array of options, consistently impresses, catering to both traditional and adventurous palates. I frequently find myself torn between the classic Pittsburgh-style sandwich, generously piled high with succulent meat, crispy fries, and tangy coleslaw, and the temptation to explore uncharted territory with their audacious and imaginative specials. The sheer magnitude of the sandwiches is both daunting and exhilarating, and with each substantial bite, my guilt intensifies while my satisfaction soars. And let's not overlook the fries-crispy and flawlessly seasoned, they serve as the perfect complement to every mouthful. Every visit to Primanti Bros is a brief intermission from my healthier eating habits, an indulgent diversion into a realm of unabashed flavors and gluttonous bliss.

If you are traveling through, you definitely have stop here, at least for the novelty factor. Overall, food is good for a.. . well, for a sandwich shop.. . But in the end, I didn't leave with a sense that I really had to come back. The real novelty at Primanti Brothers is that all of there sandwiches include french fries and cole slaw inside that sandwich. And to that I say.. . "who cares". I personally didn't care for the fries and slaw inside my sandwich, but I am also not a huge french fry or cole slaw fan. (I like the good ones, but I can easily pass on average, ) I will say that their cole slaw, which was vinegar rather than mayonnaise based, was quite good. And there fries were above average, but not as good as somewhere like say, Five Guys. The ingredients in the sandwich were all pretty good. I had the Pastrami and my friend had the Angus steak. The bread, meat, cheese, etc., were all good quality and were distinct when tasted individually. The sandwiches also seemed to work OK as a package, but for some reason for me--aside from the novelty factor--they didn't stand out. I think that maybe with the fries and slaw in there, there is just too much going on and those two tend to dominate the whole sandwich. It really takes over and you hardly taste the quality of the other ingredients. On the plus side, the sandwiches average about $7 each, and for that price, your get a pretty decent sandwich. In the end, Primanti Brothers is a definite must try if you are passing through, but I don't see myself craving these babies any time soon.

On one hand, Eddy does wonderful work with curly and wavy hair - the main reason I switched stylists and found him. The receptionist didn't apologize at the time but kept saying, "I don't know why he's late" though I saw him talk to Eddy on the phone. No one ever apologized or gave a legitimate reason (things happen! ). I'm a reasonable person, but I haven't gone back. This breaks my heart because he's such a wonderful guy who does great work, but if I can't rely on a stylist to show up, that's a deal breaker. Also, when I was bleached platinum, I was going in to see Joel for root touch-ups. I told him the first time around that I used toner to create a white-blonde look, yet he didn't use a toner on me saying I didn't need one. After a couple of months, I noticed that the areas he bleached were definitely more brassy than the rest of my hair and no matter what I did, I couldn't tone down the brassiness.. . so I had to go darker all over. Later, he saw me in the salon with darker hair and asked why. When I explained the situation, he claimed that I'd never mentioned toner. Oy.

I was invited to go with friends, who were old enough to remember when it was probably good. nThe prices are outrageously high for the quality of the food and portions. I had the Chicken Marsala, which was alright, but something I normally eat served out of a chafing dish at a funeral buffet. This was comparable to a catered version and the restaurant itself deserves a funeral.. . It's outdated and just a factory for getting people in and out and on time to the cultural events they're going to. nThe waitress was nice enough, seemed a bit embarrassed to respond 'no' when I asked if certain menu items were fresh. On the other hand, she disappeared quite a bit and didn't ask if we wanted any desserts -- which we probably would've if we'd been asked. nEven though Downtown after business hours isn't the most exciting place to eat, there are other places I'll insist on going instead of back to Tambellini's.

The weather was pretty nice so it was a good day for a drive in. I always try to keep an open mind when eating at a place for the first time which can be tough after reading reviews about the place. I ordered BBQ plate which comes with 2 sides. I got fries and slaw. My visit was on a Saturday between noon and 1 pm. The place seemed pretty busy with about 50% of the stalls occupied. It took a little while to get my food, but not so long as to start thinking, "where is my food. " The server dropped my tray off and quickly moved on the the next car without getting my money. Odd, but probably the most efficient. The pork was minced with sauce on it. The slaw was also minced rather than being shredded. There was also a sandwich bun along with the fries. I was able to get some pork without sauce to try first. The pork was moist and tender, but very bland. I then tried some of the pork with the sauce and the sauce was bland too. There was no smoke flavor at all. The fries were good, fluffy on the inside, but not quite crisp enough. The slaw was crunchy and fresh, but it too was bland. I don't really care about the sauce. Tastes vary and some like it spicier than others. But the pork although being tender and moist was disappointing. Overall it wasn't a bad meal, but it wasn't good either. Again there are better places to go for much better BBQ.

While I feel compelled to love you since I visit you every week, I have mixed feelings. You're a great location for those who live or work Uptown.. .. but that's about it since you're in the center of Uptown with no parking lot which could isolate yourself from a lot of patrons who would like to visit you. n I love how I can go to B&N, write down the names of the books I am interested then go to your convenient online catalog to see if you have the books. You have to order carefully, it is true. The pork barbecue is good, the rainbow trout is pretty good if not fried, but the main reason to go is the GREENS. They have flecks of meat in them which is what makes them good. This is the reason that i like southern cooking. The biscuits and cornbread are also very good. I would avoid all other of their meat entrees, particularly their meatloaf which has a really weirdly fluffy and light consistency, as if meat had been aerated and transformed into a different substance with different properties, and the "chicken n noodles, " which is like condensed chicken soup from a can, but with extra slime. Beef stew is a disaster; even the waitress described it as "fatty. " nnDesserts are insanely huge and can be shared if you are a family of 4. Three of us all had a go at the apple dumpling and barely made a dent in it. It went back looking more or less the same as when it arrived. The thing I like the most about this place is its multicultural democratic bent. Despite the downhome theme of this place, which might seem off-putting if you are not a white person from the midwest, I have always had excellent service here. It is also the only restaurant in our town that I have seen that has both a white and a black clientele (I have never seen Asian people here, except for some people who were clearly part of a bus tour and therefore not there of their own free will).

I found that Brothers Main promises low prices. I went in one evening to look around and was hoping to settle on something that evening. The gentleman working the floor was extremely nice, wasn't pushy at all. He was very patient with me (I think I looked over some refrigerators like 20 times! ). He was very knowledgeable and if he didn't know something, he looked it up or consulted with another colleague. Once I found the refrigerator that I wanted to purchase, he showed me that they were indeed the lowest price (he brought up other competitor's prices via internet), and he even knocked off additional money to be sure. He discussed that within 30 days if the price became lower somewhere else, they would refund me the difference. I had my refrigerator delivered and the two gentleman who installed it were VERY nice and a pleasure to work with. My whole experience with Brothers Main was a very positive one. It's always a pleasure to support local businesses, and they do show their appreciation for their customers. Will definitely be getting future appliances through them.

It's a short bike ride from the 53597 and the Alterra Coffee (or is it Colectivo now, I'm so confused) they serve beats the pants off of what you can get from the neighboring Starbucks. I wish the outdoors seating area took advantage of the nearby Pheasant Branch Conservancy. Sipping coffee and watching the locals pick-up their dry-cleaning just isn't the vibe I'm looking for I guess. I can't vouch for the breakfast or lunch selections, since I'm just a coffee and baked goods sort of guy. As for baked goods, I've had some excellent scones and muffins at Prairie. Like scream it from the rooftop great. But not every time. Just when I'm ready to proclaim Prairie my go to coffee and a scone hangout, I get a scone that's as dry as Atacama Desert. And since I'm dropping some decent coin here, I want better consistency. Things I like: n * Love the staff here. Even when the place is getting slammed by waves of morning commuters looking for their sugar and caffeine fix, I always get a smile and courteous service. n * Always love me some free wi--fi. Never had a problem connecting or with download speeds. n * The noise level indoors always seems to be a soft murmur, with some relaxing music wafting in the background. Never had a problem carrying on a conversation with my table mates. n * When the FDA approves Alterra Coffee for intravenous use, I'll be first in line. There are always are four or five roasts to choose from and I've never had a skunky cup. Things I don'tn *The "cash only" thing was so hip in the 18th century, but it's 2013 now. Start taking plastic, people. n * The baked goods are not inexpensive. It's usually worth it, but it's annoying as hell when I lose the muffin lottery. It's a solid three star option with lots of upside if the bakery improves its consistency.

But it is one of the oldest punk/hardcore/metal/rock venues in Charlotte, and legend has it that Nirvana played there WAY back in the day. It is sort of an assault on your senses.
