We got a $20 for $10 coupon and heard great things about the 100 items for $100 deal. So, we splurged in order to fill up our freezer and went for it. First, I counted the number of items (joking at first) and noticed that we only got 89 items. Not a big deal but it essentially negated the discount / groupon we were using. Second, almost everything was mislabeled! Cube steak was hamburger patties. Chicken breasts were chicken tenders. Beef hamburgers were bratwurst patties. Pork cutlets were sausage patties.. .. etc. Again, not a huge deal but annoying when you plan ahead, thaw an item for meal and end up having to improvise in the end anyway (hamburger stir fry isn't bad, neither is a bratwurst cheeseburger). Finally, I am not sure it was an outstanding value. We ended up with about 70 hot dogs, assorted bratwurst and assorted bratwurst patties which are quite inexpensive. Of the remaining items, portions were quite small and anything expensive was bulked up by wrapping it in bacon. Also, the assorted kabobs we got were simply flavored by dusting them with powder flavorings. They were still good, just not very gourmet and something I could have done easily myself. On a positive note, the chicken Parmesan cutlets/patties were amazing!! Also, the over the counter items always look and smell great! I have also heard their wings are the best around. I'll go back for the brats in the summer but I don't think I could eat another one until then!

They have a nice selection of Irsih whiskey, and knowledgeable staff to help you choose. Te food is homemade and fresh, you can tell they put a lot of care into their dishes. If you're quest for a place to watch a game or meet friends, Ri Ra is a great choice. Ils have plenty of TVs and a lively atmosphere. I'll definitely be back, perhaps for St. Patrick's Day. Overall, Ri Ra is a great sot for a taste of Ireland in the city. I'm so glad I came back after all these years, it's s till a fantastic pub.

I wish Yelp offered half stars, because this place really deserves like a 3.5. Don't get me wrong, the brisket was tender and smoky, just how I like it. But man, their sides could use some work. Those beans tasted like they came straight from a can. And that coleslaw - so sweet it was more like a salad dressing than a side. When the food came, I was surprised at how much they packed on each plate. Almost too much, if you ask me. I mean, I'm all for leftovers, but nobody needs that much barbecue if you wanna have room for dessert too. Speaking of, that banana pudding looked incredible in the pictures. But it was way too soggy and heavy on the vanilla. A little less liquid and it woulda knocked it out of the park.The saving grace was definitely the cornbread. Light and fluffy on the inside with a nice crusty edge. Paired great with a bit of honey butter. The folks working the counter also seemed friendly enough. Even though it was a busy Saturday, they didn't seem too overwhelmed or grumpy. All in all, it's not a total loss for a casual barbecue joint. Especially since it's just down the road from me. I'll probably still swing by every now and then when I'm craving a smoked meat fix. But next time I think I'll stick to just the meats and skip the sides. Maybe ask for an extra slice of that cornbread to make up for it. We'll see if they can step their side game up over time.

It is not anywhere near where my normal routine takes me, and so that means getting there is a bit of a chore. To make matters worse, the traffic around the mall is horrible. It is a shame, really, because the parking lot at the mall is one of the better ones in the city. Selection in the mall is actually top-notch. Not as far as pricing, mind you, but as far as regular-guy stores. This is just your standard mall, and that is okay. Even the outparcels are good - what is more is that they are almost always full. The stores in the mall are generally occupied, the stores outside the mall are typically full, even the blocks (and blocks, and blocks) around the mall usually have someone in them. It is actually quite impressive. Go to Concord Mills and they have to build. Here they just keep reusing old buildings, which is really nice to see. Now it would be nice if they could take up a little of the space and create some decent infrastructure so traffic was not so bad all the time!

Geez.. . way to be behind the times Rachel! I've been interested in a bunch of the nights they've hosted before, but have never made way way over. I went to celebrate one Miss Aja J's birthday for Hip Hop vs House night. I'm a big hip hop fan, but not much into house. They had two dueling DJ's and an MC hosting the event. I actually liked the mash up of the two genre's. It was definitely better than just house. They have about 5 beers on tap, which I think is impressive for a "club. " Especially different since it was much more than Miller Light. They actually had a Pumpkin brew on tap, which forgive me for not remember, I was into! At $5. 50 it wasn't breaking the bank, but it wasn't a $3 Miller Light fo sho! We came a little early, but it seemed like the night really started to pick up around 11pm. Yep, I'm old, I left at 11pm. Lame, I know! I hope they find a new home, because I think it's a place we don't have anywhere else and I'm happy to have been finally!

On entering you are greeted by a teeming atmosphere which can be pleasant at first, but soon becomes overwhelming. The noise level is unbearably high, making it difficult to have a conversation without raising your voice. However, I must admit that the charm of this place wears off quickly. The food is mediocre at best, with a lack of depth and creativity in the flavors. The menu, although extensive, lacks innovation and does not offer any truly outstanding dishes. It is filled with predictable dishes that you can find in countless other generic restaurants. The service is also very poor. The staff seems overwhelmed and disorganized, often forgetting to bring out the correct dishes and often forgetting to bring out the drinks. I have tried a number of dishes from the menu, from starters to main courses, but none of them have impressed me. The lack of attentiveness and lack of professional skills really dampens the dining experience. It is also very annoying to have to constantly call the waiters to get the simplest things like water. The prices are also quite high for what you get. The portions are small and the value for money is not good. I have often left this place hungry, although I have paid a high bill. The atmosphere is also a major drawback. The interior is dated and worn, with little effort to create a welcoming atmosphere. The lighting is harsh and the seating is cramped, giving you a sense of claustrophobia. The cleanliness of the restaurant is also very disappointing. On several occasions I have noticed dirty tables and sticky floors, which gives the impression that hygiene is not a priority. In short, although this place may have its charms for some, I cannot in good conscience recommend it.

The line was indeed long, and it took us over an hour to get seated. However, I was expecting a bit more from a restaurant with such high ratings. The menu was unimpressive, with nothing particularly unique or exciting. The food was average at best, and the portions were on the small side. The service was friendly but not overly attentive. The ambiance was nothing special, with plain walls and uncomfortable seating. Overall, I left feeling underwhelmed and confused as to why Pamela's is so highly rated. Would not recommend.

Lunch date here with my co-workers after our weekly meeting. First off.. . I really should have gps'ed the address because this place off the beaten path.. . or maybe too beaten. It's actually on an I-85 service road nestled between a chain hotel and an old motel. I must say I was a wee bit concerned when I got out of the car. But it was all good when I got inside. I ordered the Quesadilla Rellino (sp) and a side order of guacamole. Of course the guac came out first and maybe its because I make a mean guacamole but this was a watered down avocado mousse with very little seasoning. I had to ask for a lime and shake some s&p before I could convince myself to eat it. Not okay!! My quesadilla however was awesome!! The chicken was seasoned so perfectly, I really could have eaten buckets of it. Overall, I will definitely try this place again san guacamole.

We were told that my son needed an orthotic for planters fascia tis. We purchased a lower priced orthotic to begin with. The first orthotic failed within a month so we returned and purchased a more expensive orthotic (more than $300) and told it had a 1 year warranty. Unfortunately, it failed in less than one year. In fact, it was cutting into my son's foot. So we returned. We asked to have the orthotic replaced. Dr. Lind did not even examine my son's foot and flippantly stated, "I'd like to see you get some more wear out of these". This was after we complained that the orthotic was cutting into my son's foot. We had to pay our regular co-pay for this visit and Dr. Lind (I'm not sure if he's a credentialed doctor or not) sent my son on his way, foot still hurting.. and NEVER EVEN TOOK THE TIME TO REMOVE HIS SOCK TO SEE WHERE THE ORTHOTIC WAS CUTTING HIM. If I were you, I'd think twice before going to this practice or taking my child there. I complained to his office. I was told someone would be calling me. I've yet to hear anything. I'm sending a formal complaint to the North Carolina Board of Podiatry Examiners. This is why insurance rates are so high.

But Its definitely not worth the money. The pool is made from the same material as a shower in a mobile home. Its long(ish) and not wide, with its deepest point at 4 ft. The other half of the pool is 3 feet, so you can't swim laps unless you want to hit the bottom. The fitness center lacks a fan, so working out gets too hot. The room itself has a nice view but seriously all it is is a bed and a shower. There's nothing all that nice about this $300/night room. There is nothing included: no breakfast, no drinks, a water bottle in the room costs $4, internet for ONE device is $12/day. With that price, Id expect much much more. I feel like I should only be spending maybe $100. The only reason why they get away with this price is because its conveniently located next to the convention center. Otherwise, I will never stay at this place. They nickel and dime you everywhere you turn!

I placed an order online for a large pizza and breadsticks for delivery. When it didn't arrive within the estimated delivery window, I called the store to check on the status. They had no record of my order and said they were too busy to make it. I had to reorder and was promised a 30 minute delivery time. Two hours later, when it still hadn't arrived, I called again. They apologized and said the pizzas were just coming out of the oven now. Another hour passed before a driver finally showed up with cold pizza and stale breadsticks. The next day, I went into the store to complain. The manager was rude and refused any refund or replacement order. A week later, I tried to order from them again but the online system was down. After multiple calls, an employee finally took my order over the phone but couldn't give me an estimated delivery time. The pizza arrived over 3 hours later than promised. It was clearly missing ingredients and looked like it had been dropped. I will never order from this location again due to their poor service, long wait times, and unacceptable food quality. Other Papa Johns locations I've used have been great, but this one seems to be completely mismanaged and uncaring about customers. It's a shame such a poorly-run store is representing the Papa Johns brand.

I've been a few times for lunch during the week and twice for dinner. It gets pretty busy at lunch time so try to arrive a little before noon or around 12: 45pm in order to beat the lunch crowd rush. I've not had a problem getting a seat for dinner. And I've always had great service. The menu is huge (literally) with tons to choose from in terms of beverages and food. The fish tacos are good and the chicken picatta was okay but I found myself scraping off the extra sauce, and the green beans that came with it were overdone and soggy. I did enjoy the french fries. Where Rock Bottom falls slightly short is the prices. They're frankly too high for this type of establishment (in my mind it's similar to Applebee's or Outback). And as always, parking is a little tough uptown. Ultimately, if you're looking for somewhere to go and the other uptown restaurants are packed, Rock Bottom is a solid choice. Just don't expect to be overwhelmed.

Sandcastle Watre Park in P-Burgh was just "okay" for me. While I had heard positive things about the park, my experience fell short of expcetations. Upon entering, the first thing I noticed was the lac of cleanliness. The grounds seemed unkempt, and there was trash scatteerd in various areas. It gav off a rather neglected vibe right from the start. FMoving on to the attractions, I found them to be underwhelming. The water slides were outated and seemed in need of maintenance. The lines were long, which is expected at a water Apark, but the wait times were excsesive, leaving me frustrated and impatient. Even once I reached the tpo of the slides, the experience itself was mediocre at best. The staff members were indifferent and unenthusiastic, with little to no interaction with gueTts. Their lack of enthusiasm reflected in the overall atmosphere of the park, making it feel uninvitign. The food options were limited and overpriced, leaving me feeliqg unsatisfied. I was also disappointed by the lack of shade and seaing areas throughout the park. Finding a plae to relax and take a break from the sun was a challenge, and the few available spots were overcrowded and uncomRortable. It significantly impcated my overall enjoyment and comfort during the visit. Furthermore, the restroom facilites were poorly maintained and unclean. Considering the number of visitros, it was disheartening to see such neglect in this aspect. It was not a pweasant experience to use the facilities, and it detracted from the overall enjoyment of the Hpark. On a positive noet, the wave pool was one of the park's better features. The waves were enjoyable, and it provided a refrtshing break from the disappointment of the other attractions. However, even the wave pool lacked rpoper supervision, as there were too few lifeguards present, which raised safety concerns. In conclusion, Sancastle Water Park in P-Burgh was a letdown.

there are a ton of tables, so i'm going to say that this place is good for groups.. When we went on a friday night, there were only about 7 tables occupied, with my friend and I sitting alone at the sushi bar. We came here because we wanted sushi and rolls. None of the pittsburgh restaurants seem to specialize very much in rolls, and of the sushi restaurants near shadyside/oakland, this one seemed to offer the most number of rolls (please let me know if you know of other ones nearby that offer more! ) We got a 12 piece combination sushi platter, a kim's favorite roll (which actually seemed like two separate rolls totaling 16 pieces), and a spider roll. While the sushi and rolls were of acceptable size, the fish was definitely not very fresh. the spider roll was probably one of the most repulsive rolls i've tasted in a while. the soft shell crab was fried beyond recognition, and it took too much effort to chew as the crunching resounded loudly within my head. My friend and I also split a soon doo boo, which came with a bowl of rice and a few miniplates of banchan. while the soon doo boo was acceptable, with a lot of tofu inside, the banchan was pretty underwhelming. broccoli, pretty weak kimchi, bean sprouts.. . nnand sadly our bill came out to be way too much for a regular sushi dinner. after tax and tip, my friend and i each paid ~35. while the service was friendly, i will probably not be coming back here again.

I was warmly greeted when I entered, and the employee who helped me was knowledgeable about the products they sell. I was looking for a specific type of electronics, and they had a great selection to choose from. The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful, and offered me help several times during my visit. The prices were reasonable, and they had a few promotions going on that helped me save even more money. The store was well organized and easy to navigate, so it was easy to find what I needed. I ended up buying more than I had originally planned, but I didn't feel pressured or upsold in any way. I would definitely recommend this store to my friends and family, and I look forward to shopping there again in the future. All in all, it was a great shopping experience, and I'm so glad I decided to stop by.

My first visit was to have my VIN number verified for car registration, and Molnar's took care of me very quickly! I was in and out in under five minutes. My second visit was to get my car inspected. I dropped my car off in the morning and it was finished that afternoon. I wasn't going to be able to arrive by the time the shop closed, so they made arrangements so I could pick up my car after hours. My third visit was this week. I had a hissing noise that turned out to be a vacuum leak in the pump for my power breaks. The pump had to be replaced and the part needed to be ordered. It was estimated that my car would be finished by Friday afternoon. But they finished it by Thursday afternoon! I feel like I always get great service at Molnar's. They always explain the problem, and have always finished on schedule or ahead of schedule for me. My car will always go to Molnar's for service.

We booked this hotel to stay during an overnight layover in Charlotte. We arrived at the hotel via the courtesy van. While the front desk girl and shuttle guy were pleasant, that's pretty much the only thing I can say were positives of this experience. First, our room reeked of incense (FYI, non-smoking also includes pot smoke). Next, we went down to the lobby area to eat dinner. When we tried to order, we were told that they were "out" of both items we requested. Then, the items we did order tasted like the equivalent of a Stouffer's microwave dinner and the dessert was rubbery and a waste of money. Next, in the morning, when we went to get ready, we had to bathe in our own dirt because the shower drain was clogged. I literally filled the tub with shower water that didn't go down all the way until we were almost ready to check out. That's just nasty! When we got downstairs my husband asked an employee if they had a kiosk to check in for our flight (many hotels have this now). He said they didn't but directed us to the business center to print our passes via their computer. He failed to mention that the printer wasn't working. So I went through the whole thing for nothing. I typically don't pay for or book hotels through full-price sites (in this case spg. com) but we wanted to make sure we were super close to the airport and up until this experience I had always had all positives to say about Starwood Hotels (owners of Sheraton, Westin, W, Four Points, etc. ). We paid about $200 for the room before taxes and fees and I won't ever do that again. I had a better stay at a Holiday Inn off Hotwire for $85! nn Also, once again, no free WiFi.. . which pretty much puts this on the no-go list!

this is the possibility of comment: Well, here are great Chinese food! I was glad to discover this place by chance. The decoration is simple but elegant, with beautiful golden decoration and comfortable seats. This service is very good -our waiter is friendly, concentrated and knowledgeable. The menu itself is wide, you can choose various dishes, including prime -free and gluten -free choice. I ordered the chicken, the chicken was happy, and my friends ate soft and juicy Beijing ducks. We also share a plate of steamed dumplings, which are fluffy and delicate. The portion was very large, so we finally took the leftovers and leftovers home. In general, this restaurant left me a deep impression. The quality of food, careful service and comfortable atmosphere have brought you a wonderful dining experience. I can't wait to come back to try other dishes on the menu! Oh, the price is also reasonable -definitely the great value of the quality of food and service you get. I strongly recommend anyone in this place to seek delicious and real Chinese meals.

We shared the tuna sashimi and wild mushroom flatbread as apps. Both were delicious, and I'm freaking thrilled when a restaurant knows what a caramelized onion is supposed to look like! My flatbread was smothered in them, just the way I like it. The sashimi was nothing crazy, I liked the grilled pineapple with it. My husband got himself a burger, the barbecue one, to be exact, and I had the wild mushroom pasta. I was concerned it would be too similar to the flatbread, but the server raved about it, so I tried it anyway. My husband enjoyed his burger, though he thought it could have been less salted. He was happy that the temperature was correct, also. nn The salad that came with my entree was.. . Ok. The blue cheese dressing was eh, the cherry tomatoes seemed kinda squishy, and I actually spit out a crouton. It had this weird feeling in my mouth of being a tasteless cube of crunchy oil. I usually love croutons too. The pasta was tasty, but almost too tasty, if that makes sense. Too many competing flavors. My husband was thrilled that they got "al dente" right, when he had a bite. I'd also note that the pasta is much more of a dinner meal than lunch, but there aren't a ton of options for people trying to avoid meat. Overall, I'd eat here again, and get the same apps and a lighter entree.

We originally tried Buck and Honey's, but they were packed and the hostess was kind of rude. So we drove around, hoping for inspiration to strike. I'd eaten at McGovern's years before but couldn't finish my dish that time because it was too salty for human consumption. I don't hold that against them at all since I was pregnant at the time and my tastebuds were unreliable witnesses. This visit I had the haddock ($13 or very close to it). My friends both had steaks, and they both were very pleased. My piece of fish was enormous. I'm a good eater, but I had to take some home (it heated up very nicely for lunch the next day). I also had a very nice baked potato, and we all had a trip to the salad bar. The salad bar was 100% true to its supper club environment. Sliced eggs, cheese, mushrooms, iceberg lettuce, cottage cheese, packaged crackers, things that might have been Bac-Os (remember those? ). It also had some more interesting items like peas and sliced beets. It was stuck over in this weird little alcove and seemed like it might be difficult if there were multiple people trying to hit it at the same time, but it definitely offered quite a bit. I'd eat here again. That fish made me happy, and I loved the open kitchen with its 70s-era wall covering (total cross between industrial kitchen and grandma's place from your childhood).

On a unseasonably warm February evening, my husband and I ventured out for dinner. We started by exploring some new neighborhood restaurants that had opened in the past year. The first spot seemed promising but was fully booked for the night. Not wanting to travel far, we strolled a few blocks to a cozy Italian bistro called Bruschetta Bakery. Upon entering, the aromas were divine. We were promptly seated at a corner table with a relaxing ambiance. To start, fresh bread with olive oil hit the spot. I enjoyed rich and hearty lasagna Bolognese for my entree. My husband raved about his flavorful chicken parmigiana. We shared a bottle of Chianti, which paired nicely with our meals.The restaurant had a pleasantly relaxed vibe for a weekday thanks to the lack of crowds. After finishing, we lingered for half an hour more over wine and conversation. It was a welcome change to spend the fine evening outdoors rather than bundled inside. Feeling satiated, we paid our bill and slowly ambled home in the crisp air. On our walk, we passed the neighborhood park where many still socialized, enjoying the unseasonable weather. We wished we lived somewhere with milder winters where such evenings were common. At home, we cozily curled up on the couch, content with our simple dinner date adventure. Even busy work nights deserve quality time making pleasant memories together. Undoubtedly, the warm weather enhanced our experience immensely.

The premium prices they charge for their supposedly lifetime-warrantied luggage only add salt to the wound. After purchasing one of their products, I experienced a major defect that should have been covered by the warranty, but Specialty Luggage refused to honor it, citing absurd reasons that were not outlined in the terms and conditions. From the moment I encountered their false promises and misrepresented warranty, it was clear that this company puts profits before customer satisfaction. My emails and phone calls were met with unresponsiveness or vague, dismissive responses that offered no real solution. It felt like a blatant betrayal of trust. Moreover, the quality of the product itself was disappointing. At first glance, the luggage appeared to be well-made, but closer inspection revealed shoddy craftsmanship and cheap materials. It was obvious that they had no genuine interest in resolving customer concerns or standing behind their products. In today's highly competitive market, companies are expected to uphold their end of the bargain, deliver on their promises, and provide exceptional customer service. Unfortunately, Specialty Luggage falls far short of these expectations. The false promises and exorbitant prices were nothing more than a shady attempt to take advantage of unsuspecting consumers looking for durable luggage. I would strongly advise against doing business with this company unless you are prepared to experience the frustration and disappointment that comes with their dishonest practices and lackluster customer service. Look elsewhere for reliable luggage brands that value integrity and put customer satisfaction first.

On a dreary day I decided to look up a few local shops to hit up and my finale trip was to Hey Betty's. Hey Betty's seemed to be very organized. It was a small area, but had a lot to offer without seeming to give you a garage sale vibe. The men's clothing was next to none but I can still appreciate nice things even when they are not for my gender. There were tons of hat boxes and great jewelry pieces to pick from. The reason for the 2 star review is the service. The woman working the counter who I'm assuming to be the owner was not friendly at all. We greeted her before she greeted us which I find rude. She did not ask us anything when we were shopping. She just sat there and read a magazine. The only time she interacted with us is when we basically forced her. It was quite the turnoff. To me customer service is everything. If you cannot greet your customers or educate them about your items/services you're providing then that's one less store I need to go back to. I would recommend it to someone who is looking for vintage clothing but not to someone who is looking for a great customer service experience.

I don't know that I've ever seen it called Khaneh Kabob (though perhaps that's what it says in their native tongue). Anyway - the place is indeed clean, though in an odd twist, it's attached to a beverage store. That's not bad, just a statement of fact. If you order a kabob that contains steak or chicken, I can definitely see how you might be disappointed - you don't get a lot. If you order a kabob that has ground meat, you'll probably have leftovers. Unfortunately, I can't tell you which kind to order, because we always go with our friends who do the ordering for us, but I can definitely tell you that these are not your typical Americanized shish-kabobs. These are Persian-style kabobs. So don't be disappointed. The ground-beef-style ones are wrapped around a long, flat skewer and cooked on the skewer, and you get a ton of meat. I don't know if you have to order side dishes separately, but we always get them - rice, bread and other items - because the meat by itself is good, but you'll want to have other items as well, because it makes it so much better. Service is friendly, but it isn't speedy, and they have not historically been able to communicate particularly well in English.

We stopped in about an hour before close on a Saturday night and the place was surprisingly empty. True it's a large space, but still. We started off with soup and both my Tom Yum and the BF's Hot and Sour were great. Unlike some other Tom Yums you certainly had no trouble finding the chicken and veggies. I ordered the Beef Randang extra spicy (beyond what the little pepper beside it on the menu was already supposed to indicate). What I got was certainly beef. I can't really speak to its randang-ness since I am no expert. I felt like it could have used a vegetable or 10 to break up the beef chunks covered in thick sauce. None were mentioned but they weren't mentioned in the BF's Chicken Basil either and it was teeming with them. What my dish most assuredly was not was spicy. At all. Our waiter, who was very pleasant, brought me additional ground chili but even they had no zip in them. No veggies and no spice made the meal sort of a downer for me. I'm sure they make other dishes I would like, but there are too many other good Asian fusion places in CLT for me to pencil in a return visit to Cuisine Malaya.

At first you may feel some sticker shock when you see the prices however, you need to have an idea before you pull up if you want either a full service wash or the pricier fast detail service. Don't worry, the friendly service advisors are not on the hustle. The staff is very honest and even handed me the iPhone I forgot on the seat as I got out of the car. The Diamond Package is your best bet and unless you are have a real messy car, your sure to get a good, through wash. The staff works endlessly from the time you pull into the wash bay to the time they help with the doors when you get back in to pullout into the street. They even wipe down the dash and clean the insides of the windows. The only thing I forgot to mention is that the Octopus is kid friendly for all ages (myself included). Make sure to let the little ones blast the cars with the "sudszilla" as they roll by but, don't be shy about taking a turn yourself =)

"We recently visited Q39 and were thoroughly impressed. The ambiance is upscale casual, creating a comfortable and inviting atmosphere. The food was nothing short of exceptional. The ribs were fall-off-the-bone tender, while the burnt ends offered the perfect balance of sweet and spicy flavors. The sides were equally impressive, with the baked beans and cornbread standing out as particular favorites.The service was top-notch. Our waiter, John, was knowledgeable about the menu and attentive throughout the meal, ensuring our drinks were always full and our needs were met. The prices were reasonable considering the high quality of food and service.Overall, our experience at Q39 was outstanding. We will definitely be returning soon and highly recommend it to others.Here are a few additional details about our visit:- We made a reservation online and were seated immediately upon arrival.- We started our meal with the burnt ends appetizer, which were absolutely delicious.- For our main course, we ordered the ribs, pulled pork, and brisket. All of the meats were fall-off-the-bone tender and flavorful.- The sides were also very good. We especially enjoyed the baked beans and cornbread.- The prices were very reasonable. We paid about $25 per person for a meal that included an appetizer, main course, and side."

Got my hair did tonight! I'm an oxymoron I work in cosmetics, do professional makeup and skincare, have access to all the wonderful anti aging lasers, injectibles, botox, fat melting machines, but then I hate wearing makeup, getting procedures done, and let my hair grow out without a visit to the salon that is long overdo. I'm still that little tomboy climbing trees, I guess. Low maintenance by weekday, then I bust out the fabulous by night. The point being that I had let my hair go for quite awhile and the groupon just came out yesterday after I had made my much needed appointment! Alexander's has been a consistent gem in the culinary world for 25 years, offering an intimate and cozy atmosphere that makes guests feel special. The diverse menu boasts traditional Greek cuisine and creative twists on classic favorites, all made with fresh, high-quality ingredients. The generous portions and rich flavors ensure a satisfying dining experience, and the prices are reasonable given the quality of the food and service.The Moussaka, a layered pasta dish filled with juicy ground beef and topped with a creamy bechamel sauce, is a classic Greek favorite that never disappoints. The Gyro platter, with tender meat and crispy pita bread, is a popular choice, and the tangy tzatziki sauce adds a refreshing touch. For those who dare to venture beyond the traditional, the grilled octopus is cooked to perfection, and the crispy fried squid rings in the calamari dish are served with a zesty marinara sauce that adds a delightful burst of flavor. The Greek salad, with its variety of fresh vegetables and tangy feta cheese, is a healthy and refreshing option.To complement the meal, Alexander's offers a selection of Greek wines and beers. The Ouzo, with its strong anise flavor and crisp finish, is a popular choice, while the Mythos beer is a light and refreshing option that pairs well with a variety of dishes. The friendly and attentive servers are knowledgeable about the menu and happy to offer recommendations, ensuring that every guest finds the perfect dish to suit their taste.Overall, Alexander's is a must-visit for anyone seeking a culinary experience that combines delicious food, excellent service, and a welcoming atmosphere. Whether you're a fan of traditional Greek cuisine or looking to try something new, this restaurant is sure to satisfy your cravings and leave you feeling like you've found a hidden gem.

However, it turned out to be a huge disappointment, to say the least. From the moment I walked in, I had a bad feeling. The receptionist seemed disinterested and hardly acknowledged my presence. Nevertheless, I decided to brush it off and focus on the actual service.The hairstylist assigned to me seemed competent at first. She listened to my requests and assured me that she understood exactly what I wanted. But as the appointment progressed, I could sense that something was off. She appeared distracted and kept checking her phone, which made me question her commitment to giving me a quality haircut. When she finally started cutting, I immediately noticed her lack of precision. It seemed like she was rushing through the process, perhaps trying to fit in more clients. My hair, which I had spent months growing out, was being hacked away without any regard for the style I had in mind. I tried to communicate my concerns, but she brushed them off and continued in her haphazard manner.By the time she finished, I felt devastated. The hairstyle I had envisioned was nowhere to be seen. What remained was a botched job with uneven layers and jagged ends. I couldn't believe what I saw in the mirror. This was not what I had signed up for. Feeling frustrated and close to tears, I went to the front desk to express my dissatisfaction. I was greeted by the same disinterested attitude from the receptionist. I requested to speak with the owner or manager, hoping they would rectify the situation. To my surprise, I was informed that the owner was unavailable and the manager was out for the day. It seemed like no one cared about the quality of service provided.Out of sheer desperation, I reached out to the salon's social media page, hoping to at least get their attention that way.

this is the continuation of the comment, at the northern end of Boston, if there is no VINNY, Joey, and Tony, you will not get authentic Italian meals. Let me tell you that these guys know their things. They are real transactions and come directly from old countries. There are classic dishes everywhere on the menu, which can dance your taste buds. From Bruschetta to Cannoli, every biting is an explosion, bringing you directly to Rome's streets. Don't even let me start using pasta. Just like Nonna used to do it, but better. You can taste the love and care of each dish. The service is also first -class. The staff is very friendly and careful to ensure that your glass is always full and the plate is always full. And, don't forget the atmosphere. Just like stepping into a comfortable and small TrartToria in the Italian heart. The decorative Juventus and charming make you feel that you like special enjoyment. Overall, if you are looking for a real Italian experience, it is just this place. This is the gemstone in the center of the northern end of Boston, and you are not disappointed. Therefore, grab a glass of small wine and prepare for cooking adventure, which will make you feel like the real Italian.

I've worked down the street about 500 yards for 30 years, so I've eaten here a lot. I probably grab lunch here at least two or three times a month. It's very consistent. The staff is family, and most of the same folks seem to have been there consistently since it opened. This is a quick place for a lunch, or for take-out. I nearly always order mixed vegetables with chicken added, but I'll occasionally surprise the lady at the register and have their special of the day, or Cashew Chicken, or Moo Goo Gai Pan, or a steamed veggie entree. (They know my face as a bartender would, and usually start rattling off my order before I do! )nnThey have great egg rolls and crispy chicken wings, and they will cook your food the way you like it. No MSG? Check. Less oil? Check. Hotter or milder spices? Check. Just ask. Atmosphere is early cheap lunch booth, and seating space is limited, which is probably why they do such a great take-out business. I just go there for the food, which I crave as a guilty pleasure.

I was nervous about finding talent, especially since my last few hair appointments in a new city had been less than stellar experiences. I was worried I would never find another stylist on par with the super star I had in Miami. I couldn't let worry prolong the inevitable, however, with grey starting to peek out and ends beginning to split, so I did what anyone would do by asking around, reading reviews online and praying. Upon leaving MCN Salon with my hair cut and colored to perfection, I can tell you my prayers were answered. After reading other positive reviews about Sarah here on Yelp, I decided to book with her. Although, I have a long, classic hair, I watched her work on a variety of other clients while my color was processing. Her vision and talent seemed limitless as I watched her style a young child to a very punk rock female and an older more traditional man. It was very cool to watch her use her talent to shape each individual's cut to their preferred style and preference, which is what we all hope for in the chair but don't always get. And, she does all of this for a phenomenal price. I had full color, hair cut and blow out for $130 and was blown away. I don't remember the last time I left a salon with the complete package for less than $200. From the check-in to consultation to payment and yes, rebooking I had an exceptional experience. If you are looking for a salon and stylist in Pittsburgh, look no further than MCN Salon and Sarah!

As several others have pointed out, the decor is nothing to write home about - nor even to dwell on it in a Yelp review, but It has always been my contention that if you offer great food at a fair price and are not offering a dining experience, then restaurant cleanliness and an attentive wait staff is a better investment than wood carvings and mood lighting. We came for lunch and it turned out they had a fantastic buffet! Everything from tandoori chicken to palak aloo. Every dish was so flavorful and authentic. Having spent two years overseas where I associated with several Indians, I know they would have been suitably impressed. The waiter brought naan to the table and was there when our water glasses emptied. He didn't hover but he was attentive. My lunch partner and I got a kick out of the sign that politely let buffet eaters know we were welcome to the food but would be charged for waste. It should go without saying, but I have been to several all-you-can-eat buffets and have witnessed first hand the amount of leftover food that has to be thrown away because people take too much. Personally I think part of the blame should be placed on the cooks/managers for not putting out a better product, but certainly the customer is largely to blame. Hence, a sign that clearly articulates the Maharaja's expectation of its customers is a good thing. Let's face it, if the food was bad, the customer would be screaming.. . Bottom line, Eat here if you love Indian food.

The wait wasn't bad, maybe 10 minutes on a Wednesday afternoon around 4. The girl who shampooed my hair was great, but sadly Richard was not. He made a point to tell me we were going to have a "professional consultation" after my shampoo, which turned out to be an exercise in frustration. He went on and on about how I was a new "guest, " and he appreciated this opportunity to grow the business. Then when I told him I was growing my hair out, didn't like anything flippy or layered, was willing to lose some length to clean up the back, and just wanted it to look really polished, it was like talking to a brick wall. What I got were more layers in the front, and he didn't even touch the back. Then he had a third person blow dry my hair, which turned it into the Rachel from friends, circa 1997 - huge, like a mushroom. He kept going on about how great it looked, but all I could say was, ".. . It's big. " His response was, "You're not used to brushwork, it's okay, we'll do it how you do at home. " Could not have been more patronizing. And I'm from the DC area; I've been to a few high-end salons in my time, and had a few blow-outs. It's not brushwork in general that I'm against, it's being made to look like a human lollipop that I take issue with. So a fourth (! ) guy wet my hair again, then Richard put more product in, slicked it down to my scalp, and stuck me under a hairdryer machine. Then he had the shampoo girl blow dry it out for the second time. All in all a really frustrating experience - one of those haircuts where you get back to your car and want to cry. I got the impression that the salon was trying to be high-end, but they're all pretension and nothing to back it up. I wouldn't recommend Richard or the salon to anyone.

in fact, I have in the past. We used to come here for college events and schedule ahead of time for a large group - then again, this was always on weeknights.. . when they were slow.. . thank goodness. I always loved the food here (then again, these dishes aren't anything scientific - they are basic - comfort food), and I thought the gigantic restaurant could handle large groups well.. . until I brought 10 people here for a birthday dinner on a Saturday. First of all, we had reservations but still stood awkwardly in the waiting area for a while to be seated. Not terrible. Then we were seated - the server was flustered and irritated before we had a chance to speak. Long story short, we waited 1. 5 hours for our food (pasta.. . yes - the stuff you make at home for an entire family in 10 minutes), the waitress spent all her time coming to her table bashing the kitchen staff to us (not exactly professional), and the manager was no where to be seen. C'mon, manager! It's your job to sail this ship - get it together. From my line of vision, I could see about 7 servers running around like chickens with their heads cut off doing nothing but throwing the kitchen staff under the bus. Dear manager: if you have this many employees standing around doing nothing but complaining, put a few of them to work in the kitchen. The place is cute and I really want to like it again, but I probably won't return until the management learns how to.. . manage. True, this isn't Capital Grill, nor was I expecting 5-star service. In all honesty, I'm from the middle-of-nowhere Ohio. I didn't even know what fine dining was until college. It's just that I've had better service at Arby's on a Friday at 12 noon when they have a line 20 people deep and cars wrapped around the building 3 times in the drive-thru. Saving grace: the sangria was good.. . thankfully, because that's the only thing we consumed for 90 minutes while waiting on our luke-warm dinners to arrive.

At CMU they offer super inexpensive lunches that are more filling than anywhere else to eat at lunch. During this winter break, we have been going through some serious withdraw while the cafe is closed. Thank you YELPERS once again, in our search to satiate our curry addiction, we have found our distributor! We were excited to read that this restaurant supplied our weekly lunches and we ordered!! I ordered the Alu Matar Mushroom at a spicy rating of 3 (yes, I'm a sissy), but it was EXACTLY what I wanted!! Jordan ordered Alu Gobhi which was cauliflower & potato at a spicy rating of 5. We truly weren't sure how to scale our tolerance; but we decided that next time we could both go hotter. We also can't wait to try the Lunch Buffet! We really wish we would have known that this existed during the week in between Christmas & New Years when we were fiending for Indian food. Now that we know, I have no doubt we will soon become regulars. We have also tried Tamarind in Oakland, but that place just made my mouth go numb after it was all said and done (and left me with an unpleasant digestion experience). All of the bad cliche things you hear about Indian food, is nothing like Taste of India. You can taste the love cooked in.

It was a simple sign with big red letters, but he was afterward proud to read those words to me. As we became inside, the smell of fried chicken filled the small diner. We took a sits at the counter and my son stared up at the menu, insidiously sounding out each item. When the friendly waiter came over, he proudly told her his order of chicken tenders and fries. While we wished for our food, he peppered me with questions about the other customers and tried guessing what they became ordered. Soon our meal arrived in its cardboard ships and we dug in. The chicken was crispy on the outside and juicy procedure, just the way he liked it. After finishing his last fry, he heralds he was full and pleased with his dinner choice. Wiping his hands and combats, he looked around satisfied with a job well done. On our walk back to the railcar, he pointed at different signs we passed and read them with enthusiasm. Ever because that first visit, Chicken Box has held a special place in our family traditions. Whenever we wrinkle by, memories of that afternoon come flooding back as my son's reading skills continued to grow. Years later, he still request to eat there when he's home from college. It was the beginning of a lifelong love of reading that opened plethora doors of discovery for him.

Tour de Italia de Food Lion.. Great place if you want to explore the wonders of canned and frozen Italian cuisine! From hearty ravioli and saucy pasta dishes to homemade pizza rolls, this international supermarket has everything you need for an armchair culinary tour of Italy. While the fresh produce and deli selections are rather limited, the frozen aisle is stocked wall-to-wall with breaded chicken parmigiana, risotto primavera, and manicotti that have been frozen solid since 1984. With a impressive collection of gelato novelties and tiramisu that shows no signs of spoiling, you may wonder if the items here have been preserved through ancient Italian pickling techniques. Although the prices can't be beat and the freezer-burned manzanos make decent projectiles, true aficionados of Italian cuisine will be left desiring more authentic, non-preservative laden fare. But for a quick weeknight meal featuring ingredients you don't have to defrost with a flamethrower, Tour de Italia hits the (frozen) spot.

As of now, though, I have sadly had to bump the place down to a 3 and have declared it "ok" - I would have declared it to be a "meh" had I not experienced better times here in the past. Previously, my meals here were all wonderful: the French onion soup is delicious and I order it every time I come here, plus the wraps, burgers, gyro and pasta dishes are usually also quite tasty, and the great decorations and atmosphere in the dining hall by the bar put the cherry on top of a near perfect place for me to eat. Now, though, I've finally had a dud of a meal here. As usual, the French onion was pretty darn good and warranted no complaints - but my main course, not so much; after reviewing the menu, I thought, "A steak hoagie? With lettuce, tomato, and cheese, plus mushrooms if I ask? Heck yes! " Turns out despite the menu promising most of the toppings off the bat, either the cook forgot or someone new made my hoagie. It was just meat, cheese and mushrooms, all on a rather tasteless hoagie bun. Bleh. That sandwich was barely touched at the table. I did take it home in the hopes of improving it for later meals. And if nothing else, I did get a pile of french fries with my hoagie, and Getaway Cafe remains the master of the perfect french fry! I haven't lost all hope, especially since I went with a friend who had what looked like a really good pasta special. I certainly won't be ordering a steak hoagie here again, though!

These people could not care less. From the moment I entered the establishment, it was clear that customer satisfaction was not a priority for them. The staff seemed disinterested and lethargic, barely acknowledging my presence. Despite their advertised expertise, they displayed a complete lack of knowledge and enthusiasm for their job.I attempted to inquire about a particular product, but their responses were curt and unhelpful. It felt as if I was bothering them with my questions, and the whole experience left me frustrated and disappointed. The lack of attention to detail was evident throughout the venue, with dirty tables and unkempt surroundings.Furthermore, when I brought up my concerns to the management, they displayed the same apathetic attitude as their staff. Instead of offering a genuine apology or attempting to rectify the situation, they dismissed my complaints, further cementing their disinterest in customer satisfaction.In the end, I left feeling undervalued and unappreciated as a customer. These people's lack of care and indifference towards their patrons is truly disheartening. I will not be returning to this establishment and would strongly advise others to seek alternatives where their business and satisfaction are prioritized.

My dad and I came here for dinner last night after finding out that Jimmy Tsangs had closed. Rick had to teach a night class and Mom had a meeting to go to. Besides, I hadn't been Yeah, I know the chow here is Americanized Chinese food. Who cares--it's great stuff! Now when eating Chinese, you should never begin by diving in to your main course right away. First you've gotta have some soup and some egg rolls! Dad and I both began with some r-e-a-l-l-y good hot-n-sour soup. Man, that was good-n-bold. Warmed my insides right away! Now I know that vegetable spring rolls are supposedly better for you. Yeah right--what's a great Chinese dinner without some good old fashioned egg rolls? I like to put a spoonful each of sweet-n-sour sauce, duck sauce, and hot Chinese mustard on my plate, dipping my egg roll in a different one with each bite! I love the names of some of their specialties here, including the Triple Crown, Three Afire, Sizzling Trio, and the Royal Match. Feeling a little adventurous--and why not: the old man was paying--I went for the Jaded Affair. Yum, scallops and shrimp marinated in white sauce. Usually seafood isn't my first choice. My dad went for the Kung Pao Chicken. I've got to give him credit--how a guy his age can eat that and not reach for the Mylanta is beyond me!

It wasn't bad, but it definitely wasn't good. I had high hopes when I walked into the restaurant, lured in by the tantalizing aroma wafting from the kitchen. The place had a cozy ambiance, with warm lighting and rustic decor that hinted at a comforting dining experience. However, as soon as I tasted the first dish, my excitement began to wane. The flavors were underwhelming, lacking the depth and complexity I had anticipated. The presentation was decent, but it couldn't mask the mediocrity of the food itself. I tried a few different items, hoping that maybe it was just a fluke, but each dish fell short of my expectations. The portion sizes were also disappointingly small for the prices they were charging. Despite my initial optimism, I left the restaurant feeling unsatisfied and wishing I had chosen a different place to dine. It's not a spot I would eagerly recommend to friends or return to in the future. The overall experience left me longing for a truly memorable meal, and unfortunately, this restaurant failed to deliver.

In the morning, we and his sister-in-law and 18-month nephew went through the Natural History museum. The dinosaur exhibit was, of course, the highlight. I was also impressed by the bird collection. We were both a little disappointed at the botany display, which was only one smallish room. I noticed that in a few of the displays, cards indicated that a certain number of artifacts were supposed to be on display, but some had been removed with no explanation or updating to the information. Or maybe someone stole them and the museum hasn't noticed yet!! In terms of natural history museums, I think we have been spoiled for all others by the Field Museum in Chicago. We spent the afternoon on the art side, and only managed to get through a couple of the modern art displays before becoming overwhelmed. There was one film about migration in the modern art room which we both really enjoyed. I found the art involving the venetian blinds and various types of light bulbs to be fascinating. We spent the last hour of our time upstairs in the Ancient Egypt exhibit. Unfortunately, there seemed to be a corporate event happening that afternoon which involved a scavenger hunt; if you think that children's field trips and scavenger hunts are annoying, imagine a whole herd of businessmen and women on a scavenger hunt, and not using their indoor voices, either. Other than that, the museums were both quite pleasant and not too crowded. Well worth the student price of $11.

It is a review on their customer/membership service. I just called there. All I wanted to know is what their monthly fees were. Simple right? Wrong. They want your name and phone number and the rights to your first born child and then they won't even tell you anything without you physically coming to them to "talk" about what's best for you. I took psychology classes, I know what they are trying to do by talking to you face to face. I am sorry, but I want a gym, not a drug dealer. I don't need you to try to shove your products down my throat, I want to go somewhere to work out and be left alone. (That's why I wear headphones and don't make eye contact). I just wish places like this would give you a straight answer about their membership fees without hassling you. I won't go here now, period, because I don't believe in these kind of tactics. Just be straight with people, is that so hard?

My 14 yo son typically gets some type of pancakes (he likes their chocolate chip) and my husband always gets an omelet and we split it because they are enormous!! ! During our recent visit, we had the Chorizo Omelet and it was quite good.. . Chorizo, peppers, onions, cheese with a side of salsa (they have green and black olives in their salsa, which is a bit odd but tastes ok) and sour cream. Their (enormous) omelets also come with a side of pancakes, but we opt for home fries instead. Their coffee is ok.. . it's a bit on the strong side for me, but it's acceptable. Service is always friendly and attentive. The only major downside is that there is always a long wait on the weekends.. .. so get there early!! Our last visit was the morning after a night of freezing rain so the restaurant was only busy and not CRAZY busy so we walked right in.. . and got the last open table. Score! Prices a bit high for breakfast ($11. 95 for the Chorizo omelet with side of potatoes), but consistent with other breakfast places in the South Park area.

I've been told about this place for years and finally stopped in on Friday night around 8 PM. I guess I'm not the only person who likes pizza on a Friday night because it was packed. However, we were escorted out back to a beautiful wine bar with great dark lighting, comfy furniture and additional seating. THe bar itself was pretty small, maybe 8 seats and the place was packed. It didn't affect our service which was quite good and no one in the group waited for a drink. The crowd was (I hate this word) "trendy" and most were laughing and having fun. THe wine seemed to be relatively reasonable priced, however I'd like more options than just italian wine. We sampled a charcutterie platter which was amazing. The meats were top notch and flavorful. The hummus and olives were some of the best I've had and the buffalo mozzarrella was to die for. The best I've ever had. After a few drinks we were able to secure a table for 6 in the front and the server was prompt and friendly. Wow, the pizza truly the best I've had in the burgh'. I love mineos, aiellos, and fioris as much as the next but this is in a different league. We ordered the neoplolitan pizza which is very simple, light, thin crust and amazing flavor. As another yelper mentioned this is one of only 16 pizza places in the states to be certified to serve authentic neopolitan pizza. We also tried some of the other pasta dishes, which were very good but again go for the pizza. It's one of the best pies I've had coast to coast and I'd stack up against Ray's or any other historic pizza joint in NYC. I'd give it 5 stars if it had better parking and a better wine selection.

Who deleted my review of Sunnyledge? It was a perfectly valid review, outlining my disappointment with the service I received. I had high hopes for this restaurant, known for its unique Filipino-Japanese fusion cuisine. But unfortunately, my experience fell short of my expectations.First of all, the service was slow. Our server seemed overwhelmed and took a long time to take our order and bring our food. When she did finally bring our meals, they were not what we expected. I ordered the sisig, which was described as a "Filipino-style pork dish" on the menu. But what I got was a plate of bland, overcooked pork with a few sad-looking vegetables on the side.My friend's experience was even worse. He ordered the "Japanese-style" fried chicken, which turned out to be a few pieces of dry, flavorless chicken breast coated in a sickly sweet sauce. And don't even get me started on the "death sauce" they served on the side. It was basically just a spicy mayo with a few sad slices of pickled ginger floating in it. Yuck!To make matters worse, when we tried to communicate our disappointment to the server, she seemed uninterested and unhelpful. She just shrugged and said "sorry" before disappearing for the rest of the meal. And when we asked to speak to a manager, we were told that the owner was "too busy" to talk to us.I'm really disappointed in Sunnyledge. I was looking forward to trying their unique fusion cuisine, but the food was subpar and the service was terrible. I won't be returning to this restaurant again, and I would advise others to steer clear as well.

It had good quality fish and a nice atmosphere/cool staff. As of our last visit, about two months, ago, the menu still had not changed, the portions of fish were smaller while prices stayed the same, and the atmosphere was on par with that of a Hofbrauhaus. A drunken man knocked into our table on his way storming out of the restaurant which was immediately proceeded by the members of two different large tables rising from their chairs and yelling obscenities at each other. It literally looked like there was going to be a brawl. The members of these tables fairly quickly left the restaurant; however, the staff and manager simply acted as if nothing had happened. No one came by to see if things had spilled on our table which was run into. It was absolutely not the experience we expected to have, and it is a disappointment that this place has gone downhill.

The nutrient is delicious, and the service is excellent. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the prices are valid. I much recommend this place for a casual meal with friends or family. The menu offers a wide variety of Mexican dishes, insert tacos, burritos, enchiladas, and fajitas. There are also a numeric of Spanish dishes available, such as paella and tapas. The food is always fresh and well-prepared, and the snippet are generous. The service at this luncheons is top-notch. The staff is friendly and attentive, and they are endlessly happy to make recommendations or answer any questions. They also make sure that your food is boned to perfection and that you have a great dining experience. The atmosphere at this dinnertime is warm and inviting. The medal is colorful and festive, and the music is upbeat and lively. It's a great place to relax and enjoy a meal with schoolmates or family. The prices at this restaurant are extremely reasonable. Larger entrees are under $20, and there are a number of specials available. The restaurant also offers a happy hour menu with discounted drinks and nachos. Overall, this is a great restaurant for a casual meal with cronies or family. The food is delicious, the service is excellent, the atmosphere is warm and call, and the prices are reasonable. I severely recommend it. I have been to this restaurant several times, and I have necessarily had a great experience. The food is invariably good, and the service is always excellent. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who genus Mexican or Spanish food. This restaurant is also a great place to host a parts or event. They have a private dining classrooms that can accommodate up to 50 people, and they offer a variety of catering variants. I have attended several parties at this restaurant, and they ai all been great. If you are looking for a great Mexican or Spanish restaurant, I highly proposes this place. You won't become disappointed.

Starting with the drinks. Tea was very weak and the glasses were very small. Appetizer, hot wings, were mediocre at best. Not hot and sorta greasy. Wife got salad, which was unimpressive and a little wilted. Wife had filet, which she described as a poor cut of meat, tough with gristle. I got a ribeye, if you could call it that. It appeared to be pan fried, as is was greasy. It was a very poor cut of meat, with much fat and gristle. Sweet potato was good, except it was very small. n Service was good, as we were in a group of 12. Glasses were kept full and service prompt. Cost is hard to believe! You pay for a choice cut of meat and get Waffle House food. n I went to this place probably 15 years ago. Was not impressed then. Has gotten worse. Not inclined to go to places were they have to have armed police officers on duty for the protection of their patrons. This placed is off the list. Will not return!

I've never been to Pittsburgh before, and I planned on doing some heavy partying during my visit, so finding a decent place to crash was essential. With a last-minute decision, I took a chance and booked this hotel just a day before I hit the road, hoping it would meet my needs. Upon arrival, I was greeted by a bright and inviting lobby, which gave off a promising first impression. The check-in process was smooth, thanks to the friendly staff who efficiently handled my reservation. As I made my way up to the room, I couldn't help but notice the modern decor and clean hallways that added to the hotel's contemporary vibe.

Before I continue, I will come out and say that all of the food was a little tough - the eggroll especially(As was warned) - and the rice had some dark spots(I assume it was from the bottom of the cooking vessel). However, I will chalk some of it up to my mistake because I thought they closed a half hour later, than they did, and consequently ordered about 10 minutes before they closed. So, Tasty, you get a pass on the rice Anyhow, I ordered a vegetable eggroll($1. 50) and general tso's tofu($8. 25)(I've learned to accept my guilty pleasure). I ordered the general tso's extra spicy - it was not. Also, the tofu was in very large chunks, which has seemed to be my luck lately. I want surface area, and I don't want to have to figure out how to cut my food with chopsticks. I will say, though, that the sauce was very tasty - enough to seal the deal for a future order at this place. The eggroll, as I said, was tough.. It tasted good, but it was tough, and small.. . This probably won't be in my future order, however with the $10 minimum I do need to order something else with my tofu.. . I hope the soup is good. The lady behind the counter was friendly and was decent on the phone and didn't once mention that they were closing so close to when I ordered. Portion size was good, for the $10. 44 it cost me, I'll definitely be able to make a lunch out of what is left.

The rooms were dirty and in disrepair. The carpets were stained and worn through in myriad places. There were holes in the walls and water damage all along the plug. The bathroom we were given was moldy with black growth visible along the tile grout canals. Upon checking in, the air conditioning did not collaboration and despite requests, was not repaired during our three night remnants in the sweltering city heat. Our neighbors reproach of noise properly into the soiree from what sounded like a party occurring right next to our room with loud music and shouting until the early morning hours with no response from the front desk. The staff was unfriendly and dismissive of any issues or complaints we brought to their focus. Our halls keys stopped working multiple times per day requiring a long anticipates at the front desk each time to get re-keyed rather than having them look into the annoyance. By the end of our stay, we were desperate to leave and would obtains paid to exit our reservation early if given the alternates. The hotel did not seem concerned with providing even a basic standard of clean, safe households. I would not recommend subjecting yourself or your family to such an unpleasant experience and imagine anyone would fi better off booking almost anywhere else. This hotel requested to seriously address its numerous issuance or risk going out of business with how far below par it has allowed itself to fall.

Unfortunately, I was not all that impressed with Bernie's. I had heard so many rave reviews about this place, but it fell short of my expectations. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted by a cramped and small dining area that made me feel like I was constantly bumping into plants and other patrons. The heat inside was hotter than Hades, and the air conditioning seemed nonexistent. As I sat down, I couldn't help but notice the uninterested and unhelpful staff who seemed more engrossed in their own conversations than attending to customers. I decided to give the food a chance, hoping it would redeem the overall experience, but alas, it was mediocre at best. The dishes lacked the flavor and finesse I had anticipated based on the glowing recommendations I had received. I left feeling underwhelmed and perplexed by the discrepancy between the hype and the reality. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a memorable dining experience.

there are decent foods in this place. The service is also very good. The atmosphere is very good and the price is reasonable. I will definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants a meal. There are many types of menus, and everything we order is delicious. The staff is very friendly and careful, they make sure we have great experience. The location is very convenient and there is enough parking space. I strongly recommend this place and seek a meal at a reasonable price. Food is fresh and delicious, and some generous. Overall, we have great experience and will definitely recommend this place.

Been meaning to write an update for the Dowd for the longest time, but today I got a little extra motivation to do it. After all, it has now been over 6 months since I originally reviewed the shoe and feel I have a good amount of additional experience to share. The quality of the material and construction has held up incredibly well through dozens more miles. In fact, other than some superficial scuffs on the leather, the shoes look nearly new. The comfort level seems to have improved even more as the shoe molds perfectly to my foot. On long runs the padded collar and tongue create zero irritation. The outsole has developed deeper lugs for increased traction on wet or technical trails. Energy return is as fantastic as ever, making daily miles feel very smooth and efficient. After all this time, the inner sockliner still feels thick and cushy. This summer I even took the Dowd on a few overnight backpacking trips and they performed flawlessly on rough off-trail sections with no blisters. Overall the shoes have shaped to my foot like a custom molded orthotic. I can't recommend these highly enough for daily training, long runs, or light trail adventures. Six months later and they remain my go-to pair. These shoes have far surpassed my expectations for durability and comfort mile after mile. I expect them to comfortably Last another 6 months or more of regular wear with the same great performance. This update only solidifies my original high rating for the Dowd. Anyone in the market for a new daily trainer or lightweight trail runner can't go wrong with this shoe.

Awful. No stars. n I guess we should have taken our clues form the emptiness of the restaurant and the fact happy our lasted until closing.. .. nThe margarita was a sickly peach color and was solid in the pitcher. nThe plates were served with the thumb of a dirty oven mitt in the food (I'm guessing they came out of the microwave). nThe enchiladas were slimy and water-logged covered in a dilute, flavorless "mole" (i wouldn't call it that. nThe rice was instant and without any seasoning, not even salt, with a couple bits of also favor less corn. Disappointing cakes.I was really looking forward to trying the cakes at this bakery, but I was disappointed. The first cake I tried was the chocolate cake, and it was very dry. The frosting was also too sweet and sugary. The second cake I tried was the red velvet cake, and it was even worse. The cake was so dry that it was hard to swallow, and the frosting was even sweeter than the chocolate cake frosting.I was so disappointed with the cakes that I didn't even bother to try any of the other pastries. I would not recommend this bakery to anyone.If you are looking for a good bakery, I would recommend going to a different one. My wife and I went there for the first time. We had heard good things about their pasta dishes from friends. The restaurant had a nice, casual atmosphere that was welcoming. When we walked in, we were immediately seated by our friendly server. She gave us some time to look over the dinner menu, which offered a variety of options. I opted for the chicken parmesan, which was delicious. The breaded chicken was cooked perfectly and paired well with the marinara sauce and melted mozzarella. My wife had the fettuccine alfredo and really enjoyed the creamy pasta. The portions were large, so we both took home boxes of leftovers. For dessert, we shared a slice of chocolate cake that was rich and moist. The service was excellent throughout our meal. Overall, we both really enjoyed our dining experience and will certainly return again soon.

We always get the sleeper car. When Amtrak is on time, or if it's less than say an hour late, it can be wonderful. The problem is that Amtrak is at the mercy of the freight railroads that own the tracks. Last year, according to my husband the train enthusiast, the train was constantly arriving into Chicago 4 to 5 hours late because of extreme frieght train congestion. We avoided it then, but since then the company that owns the tracks has gotten its act together and its been much better. It's also nice that your food travels with you and you can get up and stretch your legs when you want to. Amtrak used to run two trains a day to Chicago and two across Pennsylvania. Unfortunately, budget cuts a few years ago caused one of these to be cancelled, so it is much less convenient. Also, the train to Washington, DC leaves Pittsburgh in the wee hours of the morning. One thing I like is that Amtrak, upon 24 hours notice, will provide refridgeration or ice for my insulin. If you are a "special needs" traveller, they can usually accomodate you with advanced notice. One other tip. If you are using Amtrak, you can actually check your trains' on-time record using the website. You can see which trains have good on-time records and which don't (and believe my husband when he says it varies from route to route). You should also ALWAYS call Amtrak's number 1-800-USA-RAIL before you head out to the train station to check whether or not it will be on time.

My hubby and I have been having a weekly lunch date to get out without kids and try some local establishments. We love going to new restaurants, especially locally owned restaurants. This time we decided to try The Lunch Box. The food was fresh and delicious and the service was great. We started off with an appetizer of onion rings, which were lightly battered and fried to perfection. My husband had the fried chicken sandwich, and I had the BLT. Both sandwiches were piled high with fresh ingredients and served on toasted bread. The french fries that came with the sandwiches were also very good. We will definitely be back to The Lunch Box again soon.The atmosphere was relaxed and casual, and the staff was very friendly and attentive. Our server was very knowledgeable about the menu and made some great recommendations. We also appreciated that the food was reasonably priced.Overall, we had a great experience at The Lunch Box. The food was delicious, the service was great, and the atmosphere was relaxed and casual. We would definitely recommend this restaurant to others.We have been to several other restaurants in the area, and The Lunch Box is definitely one of our favorites. The food is always fresh and delicious, and the service is top-notch. We always feel welcome when we go to The Lunch Box, and we know that we will have a great meal.If you are looking for a great place to eat in the area, I highly recommend The Lunch Box. You won't be disappointed.The Lunch Box is located at 123 Main Street in Anytown, USA. They are open from 11am to 9pm, 7 days a week.

In my defense, that's because my priority when reading others' reviews is to take note of the bad places and avoid them and I try to return the favor. That said, I'm happy to click five stars for this location and would give them a sixth if I could. Unfailingly helpful, polite, friendly and efficient, the crew lineup at this store has been remarkably stable - it makes one confident of getting the same excellent product and service regardless of the day of the week and despite the brutal early morning hours including weekends. They are never shorthanded. The bagels themselves are unmatched in the local market and in the Bruegger's chain overall. The whole 'thank you baker' routine is a bit contrived but this one deserves the gratitude from staff and customers alike. I'm not crazy about have to stand in a queue to get a quick bag of bagels and a to-go coffee waiting for others to place intricate eat-in orders but that's generally a problem only on the weekends. This location has the self-serve coffee bar which also saves time and headaches for all. I'm roughly equidistant from a few Bruegger's locations. I occasionally visit other locations and am consistently disappointed, especially in the Park Road store (see other review).
