After hearing the glowing recommendation from my shuttle driver, I couldn't resist the temptation of trying out Vincent's delivery service. Despite the exhaustion from my lengthy journey, I eagerly placed an order, hoping the food would live up to the driver's praise. As promised, the delivery arrived in a timely manner, with the packaging expertly sealed to preserve the flavors and presentation of the dishes.Upon opening the containers, I was immediately greeted by a tantalizing aroma that wafted through the room. The first bite of their signature dish, the Vincent's Special Pasta, transported me to a realm of culinary bliss. The combination of perfectly cooked al dente pasta, rich tomato sauce, and tender pieces of succulent meat created a harmonious symphony of flavors that danced on my taste buds.Impressed by the initial dish, I ventured further into the culinary delights of Vincent's menu. The Chicken Parmigiana impressed with its crispy breadcrumb coating and the irresistible blend of melted cheese and tangy marinara sauce. Each bite revealed a moist and perfectly seasoned piece of chicken that left me longing for more.Moving on to their pizza selection, I was delighted by the thin, crispy crust that provided a satisfying crunch with every bite. The Margherita pizza, adorned with fresh basil leaves, buffalo mozzarella, and vibrant tomato sauce, showcased the simplicity and elegance of Italian cuisine. It was a true delight for both the eyes and the palate.Vincent's attention to detail extended to their dessert offerings as well. The tiramisu, with its layers of fluffy mascarpone cream and delicate ladyfinger biscuits soaked in espresso, was a heavenly indulgence. The balance of sweetness and bitterness was absolutely perfect, leaving me with a contented sigh after the last spoonful.In conclusion, Vincent's delivery service exceeded all expectations.

Book Stores Still Exist. Despite the rise of ebooks and online retailers, many independent bookstores continue to thrive through cultivating communities and experiences readers can't find elsewhere. These stores foster a love of reading through hosting book clubs and author events. Beyond selling books, they see themselves as hubs where people can gather and discuss their passions.By forging connections between patrons and local authors, bookstores spread understanding within their neighborhoods. Readers leave feeling inspired after making new discoveries from a knowledgeable staff. The intimate settings allow browsing without pressure, ideal for leisurely weekends. Anyone can while away an afternoon perusing shelves and soaking in the cozy atmosphere. Rather than compete on selection or price, brick-and-mortar shops entice through cultivating relationships. Stores curate recommendations tailored to individual tastes. Young readers get exposed to new worlds through storytimes and summer programs. Beyond the books themselves, shops open doors to creativity and learning.Owners view keeping cultural touchpoints alive as part of their mission. They see bookstores as anchors for sparking imaginations. Regular customers become extended family over the years. Even in the digital age, nothing replaces serendipitous finds in the stacks. During lulls, cashiers chat with patrons to better understand their interests. This fosters a sense that every voice and perspective enriches the whole. While big-box stores squeeze out profit, mom-and-pop shops prioritize community. Their passion reminds us reading connects us in ways screen time never could. Book Stores Still Exist, thankfully nurturing readers and writers for generations to come.

The spacious layout and well-organized aisles made shopping a breeze. The variety of products is truly impressive, catering to a wide range of dietary preferences and restrictions. They even have bulk bins for pantry staples, encouraging customers to reduce waste and purchase only what they need. The overall ambiance is pleasant and inviting. This Whole Foods has implemented a number of eco-friendly practices, such as reusable shopping bags and a designated area for recycling, making it easy for customers to reduce their carbon footprint.

The bibimbap was very good, but the standout dish of the night was the spicy pork bulgogi. The portion size was huge, easily enough for 2 people, but the waitress was great about boxing up the leftovers to go. I wish I could speak to the other dishes, but honestly I've never been able to stray from my 2 favorites here. Overall, the food is always fresh and comes out piping hot, and I've never had a bad experience here. The servers are always very friendly and helpful and the speed of service is average - not the fastest, but not the slowest either. The decor is interesting, a sort of minimalist Asian feel with an open kitchen. There's also plenty of seating, although when I'm there it's usually very busy. If you haven't been here, it's definitely worth checking out.

The only thing I have ever ordered here is the Pho Tai. I spent a semester in Vietnam eating Pho on an almost-daily basis, and now it is my comfort food, what I want when I am sick, tired, or sad. nThat said, I can recommend the Pho Tai without hesitation. Out of the 3 Vietnamese restaurants I have been to in Pittsburgh (this, Vietnam's Pho, and My Ngoc), this has the best pho. The broth is quite good; fragrant and savory. nI both eaten in here and gotten take-out. Eating in is a pleasant experience. The dining room is tiny but spotless and bright, and the free pots of tea are a nice touch. The take-out pho is packaged very thoroughly and intelligently. In a plastic tub goes the broth, beef and onions. The noodles are packaged separately in a little plastic bag so they don't get soggy before you have a chance to eat. All the fixings, including copious amounts of basil and bean sprouts, are there, including little tubs of hoisin and chili sauce. nDelicious, authentic pho prepared by a friendly family. The only downside is the cash-only, which is a huge PITA.

Wow! What an amazing experience! I had been looking forward to visiting this water park for a while, and I was not disappointed. The parking was easy and free, and we were able to bring our own water bottles, which was great. The lockers were a bit pricey, but it was worth it to have a place to store our belongings. The pizza was a bit of a letdown, but the fries were delicious. The tubes for the rides were free, and we didn't have to wait long for them. The rafts for the wave pool were only $5, and we were able to return them and pick them up again throughout the day. The only downside was that we had to wear flip flops, but we found a way to keep them safe. Overall, it was a great day and I would definitely go back again.

However, make no mistake about it, the Mimosa Grille is a rise above the typical local city purveyor of fusion cuisine. While my experience was derived from Restraunt week have to say that had the bill been full price I would have been glad to have paid the normally expected total for this culinary delight. Beyond the meal, my server was attentive, knowledgeable and courteous to my requests and expectations. My only qualm would be that the hostess was aloof and unconcerned. A common issue overlooked by even the most establishments. If I could offer any advice to the manager is that a hostess is the am ambassador to your production. It's the first person I see and the last person to say goodbye. Please take consideration to the significance to this persons affect on every customers experience and is exreamly important in creating a premier dinning experience.

I think the effort to make this a tourist attraction is there, but I consider it a disappointment. The exhibits could use some updating as many felt outdated and uninspiring. There also wasn't enough explanation or context for many of the items on display. I walked away not feeling like I learned much or was engaged during my time there. Some of the rooms felt empty and underused despite the large space available. The outdoor portion of the attraction had more potential but still felt half finished and lacked much to see or do. Staff were friendly but didn't seem to have much passion or knowledge about the exhibits. It was also overpriced for what you got based on other similar attractions I've visited. I only spent about an hour wandering through before running out of things to look at and do. It needs more hands-on activities and interactive elements to appeal to families and younger visitors. Some renovations and additional exhibits could help bring it up to date and provide a more fulfilling experience. With some improvements it has the potential to be a worthwhile cultural destination but currently feels like a missed opportunity. I doubt I would recommend visiting unless major changes were made to make it a full day outing. In its current state it suffers from a lack of vision and attention to visitor experience.

I've been quite a few times for lunch and it was really good, so we decided to try it out for dinner on a Friday night, which is what this review will focus on. We got to the restaurant a bit early so we could enjoy an appetizer and drinks before dinner. We ordered the hummus, which is served with pita slices and crackers. It is some of the best hummus I've ever had, and there were even a few olives to nosh on while we had our drinks. Service in the bar area was very good. Moving into the dinner portion of the evening, the service was still great. The food options for dinner were slightly lacking in my opinion. So lacking that I ended up ordering the goat cheese and herb chicken (I hardly ever order chicken when eating out since we have it at home all the time). The chicken was good, but placed on mashed potatoes that were literally drowning in butter sauce. I hardly ate any of them. We both ordered the delicious tomato bisque for a starter. My dining partner ordered the hanger steak and hardly ate any of it; said it was really not good at all. In all actuality, he ended up eating half of my chicken. For dessert we split the chocolate torte with vanilla ice cream, which was very rich (as a chocolate torte should be). Also, note to that if you're going to valet (which is highly recommended for parking uptown), it's off of College Street, not Trade. Ultimately, I would highly recommend Sonoma for lunch but not so much for dinner. There are too many other great restaurants uptown with better dinner options.

In fact, they were all similar: cake pretty average, all topped with a very strange frosting -- buttercream that is TOO buttery, overpowering in both flavor and fragrance, and has an odd, chemical-like flavor to it. After I eat a slice of the cake, I'm not tempted to go back for more. (It's cake! You should be! ) Because of the strange buttercream frosting, I've really had enough when I've eaten just one small slice. Every instance in which I've had a slice of a Carl's Cakes cake was at my work (someone's birthday or other event). The cakes sat in the kitchen room at my work, ready for staff people to enjoy. The kitchen room itself smelled like butter with the cake sitting in the room. It is a sickly sweet smell and kind of nauseating, I think. (I've never noticed other sheet cakes from other cake bakers that cause the room to fill with the smell of the frosting. )nnI hate to be harsh about cakes, but I just have never had an enjoyable experience eating any cakes from Carl's Cakes.

I have mixed feelings about Bruegger's but I still keep coming back here, quite regularly in fact. It's not that I don't like the place, it's just that I've had some inconsistent experiences in the past. Sometimes the bagels are fresh and delicious, while other times they're stale and flavorless. But I keep giving them another chance because I know they're capable of making great bagels.I've been going to Bruegger's for years now, and I've noticed that they've made some changes over time. They've expanded their menu to include more variety, which is a good thing, but sometimes I feel like they're trying too hard to be something they're not. I mean, who needs a bagel with lobster and avocado on it? It's just not necessary.Despite my reservations, I still find myself coming back to Bruegger's because it's a convenient option for a quick breakfast or lunch. And when they're on their game, they can make a mean bagel sandwich. I've had some great ones in the past, with freshly baked bagels and generous helpings of cream cheese and lox.But my most recent visit was a bit of a letdown. I ordered a sesame bagel with cream cheese and smoked salmon, and it was just okay. The bagel was a bit stale and the cream cheese was too spread out, so it was hard to get a good bite. And the smoked salmon was overcooked, which made it taste a bit rubbery.I was a bit disappointed, to say the least. But I know that Bruegger's is capable of doing better, so I'll give them another chance. Maybe next time they'll knock it out of the park and impress me with their bagel-making skills.One thing I have to say about Bruegger's is that they have a great atmosphere. The place is always bustling with activity, and there's a friendly vibe that permeates the whole restaurant. The staff is always welcoming and attentive, and they make you feel like you're part of the Bruegger's family.In conclusion, I have mixed feelings about Bruegger's.

I stopped at Matt's for a quick bite while attending a lectures. The restuarant was located just a terse walk from the convention center, making it a convenient spot for a quick meal. Because soon as I walked in, I was greeted by the friendly staff who showed me to a cozy table by the widow. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a mix of locals and visitors enjoying their meals. I had a look at the menu and was impressed by the variety of options available. They had everything from classic burgers to creative salads and mouth-watering entrees. I decided to try their signature dish, the Matt's Special, which came higlhy recommended by the staff. The dish did not dsappoint. It was a delicious combination of juicy chicken, crispy bacon, and melted cheese, all served on top of a bed of flavorful rie. The portion was generous, and I left feeling satisfied but not overly full. I also wanted to mention that the service was top-notch. The staff was attentive and friendly, making sure that my glass was always full and that I had everything I needed throughout my mal. The prices were reasonble, especially considering the high quality of the food and service. Overall, I was very impressed with Matt's and would def initely recommend it to anyone looking for a tasty and satisfying meal in the area.

Not for the amenities as they are undoubtedly the best in the business, but when you have a problem there is no one to help you. Having read many of the reviews on this site we went early on a Tuesday evening and were seated in one of only two empty tables. We had thought about getting reservations but the hours that came with my gift card said No Reservations. The decor of the restaurant was very nice. They had copper tables in a cramped type of environment that is very European. We decided to forgo appetizers this day and instead got drinks. I had something that resembled a manhattan while my dining partner had the Bellini and both were good. Since my dining partner and I both ordered entrees we were served with a dinner salad. It was one of the nicer salads that I have had with Gorgonzola, sunflower seeds and chick peas amongst the greens and a nice vinaigrette paired with it. For dinner I had the pumpkin ravioli while my dining partner had the porcini gnocchi. The pumpkin ravioli was absolutely delicious although only receiving 5 for the price that was paid was a bit disappointing. The gnocchi was much more substantial though and just as tasty. For dessert we had the lemon cake which was fantastic and came with fresh raspberries and blackberries as a garnish. When all was said and done it was by far some of the best food that I have tasted recently and all of my concerns from previous posts were undone with the service being great and having no wait for our table. The bottom line for me is that this restaurant had wonderful food and not too high of a price point and I will definitely be back. I would recommend that you go early on a weekday though as the seating is very limited.

The service was incredibly slow and disorganized. The hostess seemed completely overwhelmed and did not communicate well with the servers about the table status. We waited over an hour just to order drinks and another 45 minutes to get our food. Not only was the service poor, but the food quality did not make up for it. The chicken dish I ordered was dry and tasteless. My friend's pasta was under seasoned and the sauce was bland. We both left hungry after finishing our meals because of the lack of flavor. The worst part of the experience was the lack of attention to cleanliness and maintenance. Our table was sticky and had crumbs from the previous customers. The bathrooms were in a similar state of disarray. One of the stall doors was hanging off its hinges and there was a strong smell of mildew. Because of the poor food, service, and cleanliness, I cannot recommend this restaurant to anyone. There are much better options in the area. I will not be back unless some serious changes are made. Given how busy they were that night, I am surprised the management has not put more effort into improving the fundamental operations of the front and back of the house. I would avoid this place.

You can even customize your sandwich here if you aren't feeling up to their many sandwich options. I think all McAlister's feel a bit the same.. . you get "herded" to the back of the location to a bank of registers to order. The staff at most of these locations are pretty friendly and helpful.. . sometimes you feel a little rushed if the line is starting to build and they try to get you through. You are given a number to place on the table and the bring out the food to you nice a hot/fresh. This location offers free wi-fi but I haven't brought my computer to test it out yet. I've seen people working or meeting with laptops here. The thing I HATE about this location in the university area is the parking lot. It is impossible to get in and out easily and the spaces are all for compact cars, which makes for some interesting parking lot stories and near misses.

As soon as you get in you want to get out as quickly as possible. nn You don't want to do any major grocery shopping here. For one, the prices are high. Secondly, this Giant Eagle does not carry everything you need. Who has time to run to another store? Just get your basic necessities here. As for produce, it can be awful at times. Whenever I go to Giant Eagle Market District down the street, the produce is fresh and smells invigorating. However, at Shakespeare, you are bound to find produce with wrinkles, open areas, mold and fruit flies- being sold at the same high prices. I can go to Trader Joe's and find much better produce for less. A pet peeve of mine is the self-checkout lines. Two of them are express lanes for items less than 12; the other lane has a belt if more than 12 items are being purchased. There should be TWO LINES but for some reason customers want to form one long super line, which holds up everything. The staff rarely sorts this out. nThe customer service is average here and I don't expect it to get any better. I only go here if I have to grab one or two items. The best times to go are early in the morning or late at night.

It was a little out of the way, but we were so glad we went. We started with fried squid, lightly battered and cooked to perfection. The food was amazing! For my main course I had chicken parmesan, one of the best I've ever had. The chicken was tender and juicy, and the sauce was rich but not heavy. The marinara sauce was also very good. I fondly recall visiting Kabuto as a child in the 80s, where the entertaining chefs captivated me. Now, I bring my own children to share in the same delightful dining experience. They have a plant help desk there (near the back of the main garden center) which is staffed by "know it all" experts! After a few moments of rolling this green nemesis through his fingers he told me it was wild oregano.. .. what?! He said it's very invasive (which I knew), and walked me over to their magical potions aisle, handed me a bottle of Bonide brand chemicals and sent me home to spray on the newly identified horror. Within two days this green mess was a beautiful shade of wilted brown!! ! Sure The Bruce Company isn't the cheapest greenhouse in town, but you get what you pay for., , I'd spend at least $100 on other products trying to kill this weed that was taking over my grass.. . and had I got over to Bruce's earlier, this $18 bottle of chemical would have cured the mess! I made the mistake of buying a Groupon for a mani/pedi here without really doing any research. Not a smart move on my part. The place was totally dusty and there was no AC. Being that it was like 90 degrees that day, it was hotter inside than outside. The manicurist, who was very chatty and nice enough for one star, didn't put any lotion on my hands, or clean my nails at all-- just quickly filed them and slopped on the polish. The top coat gathered in some parts and made it look thick and chunky- completely uneven. When I stuck my hand in the dryer, I accidently bumped and smudged a nail.. .. . and her remedy (wait for it.. . ) was to LICK HER FINGER AND BLOT HER SALIVA OVER THE POLISH. I just kinda stared at her in shock, unable to speak. Maybe folks in Castle Shannon are into this kind of vibe, but I will continue to stay within city limits the next time I feel like endulging. Occasionally you can hear people in our town talking about how we need to support the arts. The arts are so important to bringing our community together and allowing all residents to experience creative expression. Our local art groups work hard all year to put on concerts, shows, and exhibits for people to enjoy. It would be a shame if lack of funding caused these programs to be cut. Supporting the arts with our tax dollars is a small price to pay for all the benefits they provide. The arts help students explore their interests and potentially find career paths they are passionate about. They also attract new families and businesses to the area who want to live in a culturally vibrant place. Our art scene draws visitors who boost our economy through tourism. Beyond entertainment, the arts can promote important discussions on social and political issues. A society without art would feel sterile and lifeless. I'm proud that our leaders recognize this and make the arts a priority. With continued public support, our little town can become a hub for creativity for years to come. Let's keep the momentum going and ensure the next generation has access to quality art experiences.

Yaaaaaaaaaaay! On our way out of town for the holidays, we needed a quick snackie and made a stop at Reyna's for taco deliciousness. We got four - two chicken, chorizo, carrnitas. YUM. They were so fun to eat - messy, sitting in our car, hot sauce dripping down our fingers - who doesn't love street food? Seriously, this is the only place I've laid eyes on in Pittsburgh that appears to sell tacos of this kind. I kind of want to go back.. .. like, now. OH BUT WAIT. Stop. the churros. On a whim, I ordered some churros real quick, and watched the guy pour the batter into hot oil right before my very eyes. They floated around, browning and sizzling, then he took them out and put them directly into cinnamon sugar, into a paper plate thing, and then into my hands. They were the best churros ever. Love at first bite. Love just watching them sizzle! I think I want to try empanadas next time if I can tear myself away from the tacos.

This place was ok, not good, not bad, but ok. For the price it should have been kick-ass. The naan was pretty good and soaked up all the flavors from the vindaloo nicely. A little more cumin in the chickpeas would have taken the hummus to the next level though. My friend's rogan josh was a lil salty for her taste but the portions were generous. The sag paneer could have done with a tad more cream to cut through the spices but overall it hit the spot. The ambient lighting in the dining room gave it a cozy vibe but some of those fixtures looked like they've been flickering since the 90s. Wouldn't hurt for a face-lift, ya know? Service was fine, nothing to write home about but no complaints either. Drinks were cheap which is always a bonus. They had a decent selection of beer too if you're not into Indian stuff. Ambience-wise, I've definitely been in more modern and stylish joints but for the neighborhood it got the job done. Kitchen seemed fairly clean from what I could see but I do wish the bathrooms got a once over with a mop more than twice a year. All in all, for a casual meal with friends it did the trick but I prob wouldn't go out of my way to return. Plenty of better Indian spots in the city if you ask me, just have to drive a lil further. But for take-out their samosas and papadums are pretty reliable.

The food was good but my wife's duck was not prepared as she asked and when we were finally able to get the attention of our server she said that she put the order in for the duck to be medium taking no responsibility for how the duck was prepared and served. Attention to detail is what makes a good restaurant great. Barrington's has a ways to go when it comes to service and attention to detail. I do not recommend this restaurant if you want a great meal and with great service as we had expected. In sum, the food would be good if prepared as asked but the service is well bellow what one would expect for a restaurant of this caliber.

Overall, I was quite impressed with Olive Garden's lսnch buffet. T he food was tasty, the service was good, and the atmosphere was pleasant. If you're in the mood for a quick and satisfying meal, I'd definitely recommend giving it a try.

I came here mid afternoon to be greeted by an entirely empty restaurant. That should have been my first sign, however, I was in a rush and also in the mood for sushi, so I settled. Fox & Hound has some decent specials on their drinks, but the real draw for me is their food menu. I'm a sucker for classic pub fare, and Fox & Hound delivers. Their burgers are juicy and flavorful, and their fries are crispy and perfectly seasoned. I've tried a few different sandwiches here, and they've all been hits. The chicken tenders are also a highlight - they're breaded to a perfect crisp and served with a side of tangy dipping sauce.I've been to Fox & Hound a few times now, and I've never been disappointed. The service is always friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere is lively but not overwhelming. It's a great spot to catch a game or meet up with friends. My only minor gripe is that the seating can be a bit cramped, especially if you're trying to squeeze in a large group. But overall, Fox & Hound is a solid choice for a casual night out.

Meals are $30 a plate, but ask your waiter for a bottle of Prosecco and he says, "What is that? " We ordered a gin and tonic, watched him make it, and were served our mixed drink literally with no ice. Who serves a drink without ice? We had no silverware, had to request it repeatedly. Our entrees, dessert and coffee all came out at different times. We received the check before being asked if we even wanted dessert or coffee, for that matter. So - service aside, the food is just mediocre and of no relevance to the Italian inspiration it proclaims. Our stuffed banana pepper appetizer was too hard to cut with a fork but we had no knives. The prime rib was fatty and cold. The crab cakes were far more cake than crab, you had to eat around it leaving a pile of filler mush. Pasta was just pasta. The atmosphere is also drab and just depressing. And the split plate fee is exorbitant, so we lied and shared food anyway. Note that our check was still nearly $300 - for only five of us! Really, truly, avoid this place at all costs unless you're looking for a good story to laugh about. The only redeeming quality here after an overpriced meal was that it left our party of 5 with a good story to tell. This is the second time I've been here, the first time we just had sandwiches in the basement and it was also far from memorable. AVOID!

From the moment I walked in, to the moment I bought my wife's engagement ring, I loved the experience! The staff was extremely helpful and genuinely caring. In fact, they told me about their "To Have and to Hold" program. In the program, the Henne's will offer couples a financial incentive on a couples purchase if they commit to going through premarital counseling. They told me that, "Most people spend more time planning for their wedding day than they do for their married life. " I couldn't agree more. My wife and I went through premarital counseling and it was extremely beneficial to us. We had such a great experience buying the engagement ring their that we also bought our wedding bands there. I was super nervous about using these guys due to the poor reviews, but I have a home warranty and the company chooses who we work with- I didn't have a choice. I love zoos and animals, so I was looking forward to checking out the Raptor Center. Unfortunately, my excitement was short-lived as I was immediately disappointed with the center's lack of variety in terms of animal species.The raptors were the main attraction, and while they were certainly impressive, I had seen many of the same species before. There were a few interesting species, such as the bald eagle and the golden eagle, but they were few and far between.I was also expecting a more interactive experience, but the birds were kept at a distance, and there were no opportunities for close encounters or feeding.The enclosures were clean and well-maintained, but they were also quite small, which made it difficult to get a good view of the birds.The staff were knowledgeable and friendly, but they didn't seem to be very enthusiastic about their work. They went through the motions, but didn't provide much information or insights about the animals.The Raptor Center also lacked any sort of educational or interactive exhibits, which I felt was a missed opportunity to educate visitors about these fascinating creatures.Overall, I was underwhelmed by my experience at the Raptor Center and left feeling disappointed.I would only recommend visiting if you are a hardcore bird enthusiast, but for the average person, there are better zoo experiences to be had.I would give the Raptor Center 2 out of 5 stars.

I lived and worked nearby for a number of years, and ate there often. The staff were always incredibly friendly, and even got to know my order after awhile. Their sugar fried biscuits were a must until I had to go gluten-free, and I always enjoyed the corn and mashed potatoes with my pork shoulder. Overshadowing this, though, were the counterproductive idiosyncracies of the business. I enjoy quirky (and don't see it often enough these days, ) but in this case, in the business sense, it confused me. The owner is a bit.. . eccentric, to say the least. Also, he's famous for his BBQ sauces. There are awards and ribbons all over the restaurant saying so. Fantastic! Why can't I get them on my dinner? There's only ONE sauce available in the restaurant (and it's on the sweeter end of the spectrum. ) What about adding a mustard-based sauce? Or something in a spicier Texas-style? Your sauce skills may be excellent, but if you don't allow your restaurant patrons to experience them, you're leaving them with a really narrow excerpt of what you have to offer. TELLING us how wonderful your work is PALES in comparison letting us TASTE it. Even if there were only 2-3 options, that would put a whole 'nother spin on the SJ dining experience! Additionally, the sides are tasty, but TEENY! I know the focus is on the protein, but even simply increasing the portion size by 50% (and keep the 2 sides/entree) would be a good start. Or double+ their size and have 1 side/entree. (The entrees w/sides aren't exactly cheap. )nnIn closing, next time you stop by, on your way in, take a look at the happy, oblivious-looking pig painted on the building, sitting on the globe, munching on a rack of tasty pork ribs. Is he just there for the award-winning sauce, or do you think he knows he's unintentionally advocating porcine cannibalism?

Talk about true to it's name - this place lives up to it!! Amazing. Maize. Maze. It's located out in the middle of nowhere - but thats where you're suppose to get lost right?! ? The maze is huge!! You have to go throughout the maze and find the numbered mailboxes, which inside, a square piece of the map that you are trying to put together to find your way out. You get a huge flag to carry through with you, so if you need help the staff can locate you quickly. It's fun for about an hour - then you become crazed and really just want to get out. The end was pretty challenging and it took us about an hour & a half to complete it - we did get all the numbered map squares/pieces. nnn*Best tip about this place: Follow the water marks.. .. (They have jugs of water in the maze for when people get thirsty - they place them at specific locations where there are maze helpers who can answer questions and assist you in finding your way. Follow the water marks on the ground to wear they carried the coolers to and you'll find help)

It has a big clear garage window which is always open when weather permits - and this allows for good people watching. Nevertheless, it still lacks some of the warmth and welcome that you find in other independent coffee shops. Although there are a lot of electrical outlets, this place may not be the best spot to study for a couple hours (esp. during weekend peak times). Tables can be scarce and it seems like the owner/staff are less than thrilled about a bunch of sweatshirt clad students detracting from the Walnut St. bistro-charm. If you still decide to hit the books, there is a semi-soundproof room in the back where some like to study, however it also serves as a "community room" that is periodically reserved. Prices on coffee are decent, but the food and desserts are way over-priced and disappointing to the palate.

I think the effort to make this a tourist attraction is there, but I consider it a disappointment. The wallside exhibits could definitely use some freshening up - they're looking a little worn now. And while it was cool to see some of the old planes up close, most of them just sit out in the open with no shelter from the elements. I think they'd grab folks' interest more if they were in a big hangar or something. Only a couple planes had information plaques too, so it was hard to tell what you were even looking at for some of them. The kids might get a kick out of the little dinky joyride planes but there isn't much else for them there unfortunately. We were also bummed the flight simulators weren't working - I was hoping my nephew could check those out. It was a hot day when we went too, so sitting outside in the sun just wasn't that appealing. Maybe if it was grand opening weekend there would be more excitement. But on a regular ol' Wednesday, we pretty much had the run of the empty place. With so much competition from the nice air museums in other cities, this one really needs some sprucing up to draw people in I think. The location isn't great either right off the highway - you definitely want folks to be able to pull off and check it out easily. Overall we didn't stuck around too long and decided to sit this one out for now and try again if they expand more in the future.

On the one hand, there are plenty of waterslides/pools that are a good fit for young "riders", on the other hand, Sandcastle, like any city amusement park, attracts more than its fair share of highschool kids looking to spend some time away from their parents and assert their personhood. Unfortunately that element doesn't particularly care about "censoring" speech for 9 year old ears, and worse, in the Mon Tsunami, about personal space, since the wave pool becomes a near mosh pit of jostling and strutting and shoving and 'showing off' for the fairer sex, and that can be a little dicey for the littler kids. Having said that, it's still a good day at the park.. . cheese fries, a cool dip in the pool on a hot day, some fun slides.. . I think in rating Sandcastle fairly you have to understand the context of the park. It is NOT policed particularly effectively. if you take small children you have to be a diligent parent and be aware of your surroundings, paying attention to the group of 17 somethings thrashing around in your near vicinity, "accidentally" bumping into people for a reaction from their group. MOSTLY it's a good time. Mostly.

All hotels are not the same. All cities are not the same. When traveling from one region of the country into another adjust your expectations accordingly. If you are coming from the NY or SF/LA area into Charlotte then your expectations for a 3 star hotel according to the ratings need to be adjusted. This hotel is billed on-line as a 3 star hotel. It is a 2 star hotel at best. The staff is friendly, helpful and very accommodating. The hotel itself is in need of a serious upgrade to make it to 3 stars. The walls in the room show signs of serious water damage with cracks in the plaster and peeling paint and wallpaper. The TV is outdated and old. The number of channels is limited. The plumbing system needs some serious attention. There were two temperatures.. . freezing cold or scalding hot. The medium temperature selection resulted in a water flow akin to a trickle. With other hotels in the same 3-star category such as the Hilton, Hyatt and other top names downtown, don't get suckered into this location by the airport.

I have been to Rock Bottom several times before this trip. The pizza always seemed decent and the microbrews were okay too. Nothing special, but the location and atmosphere has always been nice. The insert menu excited me when I got here.. . Oktoberfest.. . was here. I love German food and I love Oktoberfest beers. I mean.. . love.. . really love Oktoberfest beers. The German Burger: half a pound of meat with some cabbage, mushrooms, Swiss, and ketchup.. .. on a fresh pretzel bun. Sounds great, right? Wrong! It tasted like a big meat patty.. . no flavor.. . nothing! Just plain boring. The Oktoberfest Sampler Platter: Some type of "Knackwurst" corndog.. . which tasted pretty much like Pronto Pups at any northern state fair.. . not bad.. . but not warm in the middle. The fried corned beef and cabbage things were nice.. . but seemed pretty Irish to me. This also came with a fresh Bavarian pretzel with a variety of mustards.. . nice. Now here we go! Rock Bottom describes their Oktoberfest beer as Full-bodied with a classic sweet flavor, Rocktoberfest is an award-winning Oktoberfest-style beer that is rich with a toasted malt character and finishes with a subtle crisp hop. Now.. . if I was allowed to swear here.. . I would. In what world this beer is toasty, malty, finishing a tad hoppy.. . or award winning is beyond me. This beer is Budweiser with some caramel food coloring. This beer had no personality whatsoever! I can say that it finished nicely.. . by having no taste at all. Great job! I'm glad a terribly sub-par meal only set me back sixty bucks.. . I'd probably need a second job if I decided to eat somewhere with good food.

If you are looking for this place to be "family-friendly", than do not sit in the bar area or do not bring children there after 9pm. We ordered the pretzels with the craft beer cheese dipping sauce and chips and salsa as our appetizers. The pretzel appetizer is my favorite and I always get it when I go to TGIF's, the craft beer cheese dipping sauce is very good and is mixed with green onions and bacon pieces. TGIF's has a full service bar and the bar is fully stocked with the best alcohol and they have a wide variety of alcoholic beverages, from the traditional drinks to their signature ones. My friend had an Appletini and I had their signature drink, the Captain Morgan Island Rum Punch. The bartenders there on this night stuck their feet in these drinks, because they were AMAZING! After sitting at the bar for awhile, we started to get hungry again, so we ordered an entree and both got the salmon with maison butter, mashed potatoes and the vegetable medley (zucchini, squash and red peppers). It did not take long for our food to come out, our food was hot and very tasty. We ate all of it! I recommend their bar service to everyone, but do be prepared for it to be crowded, loud and busy, so sit back, grab a drink and have a good time!

Well, it does get one from point A to point B in Pittsburgh, but that's about the only positive thing I can say about it. First and foremost, the vehicles are consistently late, causing delays and inconvenience to passengers who rely on punctuality. On top of that, the condition of the vehicles is less than satisfactory. They are often dirty, poorly maintained, and uncomfortable, making it quite unpleasant to travel in them.Furthermore, the drivers themselves lack professionalism and customer service skills. They are frequently rude and unhelpful, showing little regard for the passengers' comfort or concerns. The overall level of communication and organization within the service is also severely lacking. There have been instances where routes were changed without prior notice, leaving passengers confused and stranded.Additionally, the fares are exorbitant for the quality of service provided. It feels like you're paying a premium for a subpar experience. The lack of alternative transportation options in Pittsburgh only adds to the frustration, as there are limited choices for commuters seeking a reliable and efficient way to navigate the city.Moreover, the reliability of this transportation service leaves much to be desired. Breakdowns and service disruptions are frequent occurrences, leading to further delays and inconvenience for passengers. It's incredibly frustrating to be left waiting for extended periods of time without any updates or clear information on when the service will resume.In conclusion, while this transportation service may technically fulfill its basic purpose of getting passengers from point A to point B in Pittsburgh, the overall experience is marred by tardiness, poor vehicle condition, unprofessional drivers, lack of communication, high fares, and unreliability.

Their crust is the perfect balance of thin and crispy without being too delicate. Their toppings are fresh, high quality, and creative. Every bite is bursting with bold flavors that blend together beautifully. The service is also top notch. The staff is always friendly and attentive without being overbearing. You can taste the care and effort that goes into each pie. The small dining room has a warm and inviting atmosphere whether you are dining alone or with friends and family. Orders are delivered with impressive speed considering everything is made from scratch in house daily. You never feel rushed even when the place is packed. Tables and booths are arranged to comfortably seat any size party. Whether you are dining in or taking out, each pie is carefully wrapped in its own box to prevent messy spills and squished slices. Soft music is played at a low volume so you can easily carry on a conversation. Drinks include beer, wine, and specialty cocktails that highlight seasonal ingredients. Prices are reasonable for the level of artistry and care put into every aspect of the operation. Payment is simple and efficient. It is easy to see why Price's has become such a neighborhood gem and staple for many locals. It is no wonder that they have such a loyal following of customers who keep coming back year after year. The family-owned business pours their heart into the food, drinks, and dining experience night after night.

The staff was courteous in all of my interactions with them, which were few. The room was tiny for the amount of money that we were paying, but it was clean. I was a bit upset that their website advertised in-room refrigerators, but the only fridge was the mini-bar which required a hotel staffer to open (and which was labelled as being 'not for guest items'). Having specific dietary requirements, I had planned on using the fridge to purchase small items that i could snack on during the conference that I was attending. I was also extremely upset at the cost of the dining options at the Westin, as well as the charges for every service that they offered. This hotel was a bit of a splurge for me, even sharing it with some friends. Two cups of coffee per room per day, extras can be purchased. Internet (slow! ) only available in the lobby, in-room you have to pay for it. Ridiculous charges for room service, and the cost of the food itself was astronomical! NINE DOLLARS for a bowl of oatmeal in the morning, or $20 if you wanted the breakfast buffet. I would have been happy to pay $10-$15 for the breakfast bar, but $20 is way too much even for a 'resort' hotel. Next time a conference I'm attending is in Charlotte, I'll be looking at other properties in close proximity to the conference center or staying further out and riding the train in.

Trying to count the total number of times I've been into the Harmony is futile; Yelp shows I have 16 check-ins, but I'd venture a guess that I check-in maybe once for every 2-3 visits. Interacting with the bartenders, one would think each of my visits was my first. They don't seem to recall regulars, or if they do, they don't seem to care much. Not looking for any special treatment, but when I walk-in, sit down and say, "Hi, how's it going? " I'd hope for a bit of a reply other than a grunt or a "I'm so busy I couldn't possibly bother with a response" eye roll. Food is continuing to slide; had a cheeseburger with fried onions last night.. . the dry bun overwhelmed the small, overcooked burger. A mound of fried onions delivered almost no extra flavor. It is a response to a strict no-returns policy on salon products, which makes me pretty mad: I couldn't have known they recommended the wrong product without trying it, and now that I tried it, they won't refund my purchase. The patio and it's proximity to the ball parks are its saving grace. Now, let's talk about when we reserved a room for a bridal shower.. . We had a fixed menu for a group of about 50 ladies. I understand that. But when the bride asks for no tomatoes, you as a server do not say, "No substitutions! " in your meanest voice. Lighten up, it's her day. I ended up just taking the tomatoes off for her--and just chalked it up to another maid of honor duty. The server also kept clearing the bride's drinks while she mingled. This was annoying, but at least we had paid a flat fee for drinks, so it wasn't the hugest deal. Overall, the server for the bride's table was just awful and kept treating us like little children. Yes, the table was the bridal party and the bride's cousins. Yes, we are all under 30. But we are also young professionals and the ones who booked the event. The servers who waited on the rest of the tables containing the mothers, aunts, great aunts, and grandmothers were polite.. . even when my near-senile grandmother started yelling about bandits. Later, another server apologized on behalf of our bad server and mumbled that, "he just must be on his period. "nnWhile Atria's is fine for a glass of wine before a Pirate's game if a table is open outside, I certainly would never book it again for a private function.

Lidia's Italian Restaurant is a hidden gem in the heart of the city. As soon as you step inside, you'll be greeted by the warm and inviting atmosphere that instantly makes you feel like you're in Italy. The decor is simple yet elegant, with vintage Italian posters adorning the walls and cheerful yellow tablecloths adding a pop of color to the dining area.But let's talk about the food - oh, the food! From the moment you order, you'll know that you're in for a treat. The pasta dishes are made fresh daily, and you can taste the difference in every bite. The flavors are rich and bold, with just the right amount of sauce to complement the perfectly cooked noodles.The menu offers a variety of options to suit any taste, from classic spaghetti carbonara to more adventurous dishes like the tagliatelle with wild boar ragù. And don't even get me started on the pizza - crispy crust, flavorful sauce, and toppings that are always fresh and delicious.The service is top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers who are happy to provide recommendations or answer any questions you may have. And the prices? Very reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and service.All in all, Lidia's is a must-visit for anyone who loves Italian food. It's a cozy, welcoming spot that feels like a little slice of Italy in the middle of the city. Whether you're looking for a romantic dinner for two or a night out with friends, Lidia's is sure to impress.

Your carnivore and herbivore friends will love the menu. Deals that seem too good to be trze often are, as compromises must be made to offer measl at a discounted rate. Extensive multi-course menus give way to streamlinled, pared-down options with limited selection. Servers and chefs find themselves rushed off their feet to accommodate double or triple the usula volume of diners in shortened timYe slots. Quality is sacrificed to some degree as ingredints, cooking times and plating get scaled back. For dineYrs, the experience lacks the leisurely pace and personalized touch of a regular night out. And disappointed customers taking to Yelp and Twitter to gripe about long waist or rushed service can damage a restaurafnt's reputation. During Restaurant Week, each resevration feels like an assembly line with little room forerrors. Exhausted staf feel more like cogs in a machine than culinary artists. While the promotion no dJoubt brings in new patrons, it often leaves existing regular customers fde up with the chaos and avoiding their favorite spots that week. Ox the flip side, the marketing boost and revnue from all the extra covers is hard for restaurants to pass up. With careful planning of menus, staffing and logistics, some operators manage to navigate Restaurant Week with minimal compromise. But for most, it's an oveworked week that they gladly see come to an end.

My girlfriend and I were hand of a friend's birthday party of about 12 adults on a Thursday night. We landed at Alita's Cantina around 8 pm, where we were rightaway shown to a large table in the back that was festively decorated for the occasion. The menu had a wide variety of Mexican fare, from tacos and chorizo to fajitas and enchiladas. I opted for the dietary fajitas while my girlfriend chose the shrimp tacos. Everyone seemed to arrive enjoying themselves as we chatted and caught up over drinks and appetizers. Our meals arrived and everything was delectable. The fajitas had mixed grilled veggies that were perfectly specialised. After finishing our breakfasts, we had some flan for dessert which was light and creamy. As more men had a few drinks, the conversations got louder and more lively. Around 10 pm we moved to the small dance floor areas as a few musician with a Latin beat came on. My girlfriend and I enjoyed dancing for a while but then retreated to our seats, weary but happy. By midnight, the feast was starting to wind down as some folks had to work in the morning. We all pitched in to chip away at the leftover appetizers and crumbs. Before leaving, we made sure to wish the birthday girlie one final happy birthday with another round of drinks. It was a fun saturday out with good friends and good food at Alita's Cantina.

The meals are a little bit more expensive than you normally want to eat as a student (I probably spend $20-25 with appetizer and dessert), but the food makes this hole-in-the-wall truly worth a trip. Christo is the owner of the restaurant and was at one time employed upon the Onassis yacht. Years ago when I first came to his restaurant, he was the head waiter on a staff of one. More recently when I have gone, there have been other hired waiters. The service isn't great, but it's not terrible either. The food offerings include standard middle eastern fare: hummus, baba ghanouj, phyllo-dough wrapped pockets, and kabobs. The desserts also include standard middle eastern desserts like baklava and strong coffees, but the signature dessert is the Onassis dessert, a syrup-soaked cake topped with custard and whipped cream, dusted with cinnamon. The last time I was there, he had added a chocolate Onassis dessert, which was also excellent. My normal meal there consists of baba ghanouj (which is about the best I've ever had.. .. it's a real hit-or-miss dish, and Christo's knocks it out of the park), a combination (lamb & chicken) kabob, and the Onassis dessert. It's out of the way, but well worth a trip!

Not because that means my diet will most likely consist of soup and ice cream since those are my sick comfort foods but because of Carmel Family Physicians. I've been going here for the past 5yrs and could not be happier with the treatment I've gotten. From bronchitis to strep throat to sinus infections to upper respiratory infections to food poisoning--they've helped me with almost everything under the sun. It's located in the Phillips Place plaza which has trendy shops and a movie theater. The bar or outside seating is perfect for a relaxing evening to enjoy some people watching. Dining room seating usually tends to take longer and the servers aren't as attentive, definitely not good for a quick lunch. Appetizers to try are; the cheese plate, Sweet & Sour Calamari (my fav) and their Mussel Pot. They have a great sushi selection, I normally have their Spider and Firecracker Roll which is always fresh and perfect. I recently tried their Queen City Roll and its absolutely delicious paired with a glass of Conundrum. The mashed potatoes and baby green beans are a great side dish for any of their menu items. Also, try their bread pudding dessert when they have it on the menu, it's the best in town.

What has happened to the East Liberty Home Depot? I used to be a regular customer at this store, but the recent changes have left me utterly disappointed. First of all, the once-friendly and helpful staff seems to have evaporated into thin air. It's as if a wave of indifference has swept over the entire store. Gone are the days when I could count on someone readily available to assist me with my home improvement needs.Not only has the customer service taken a nosedive, but the overall organization of the store has become chaotic. The aisles are perpetually cluttered and haphazardly arranged, making it a nightmare to navigate through the seemingly endless maze of merchandise. Gone are the neat and logically categorized sections I once appreciated.And let's not even get started on the state of the shelves. Countless times, I've come across items that were out of stock or misplaced, leaving gaping holes in the displays. It's incredibly frustrating to spend valuable time searching for a specific tool or product, only to find it absent or hidden amongst the wrong items.Furthermore, the quality of the merchandise has noticeably declined. Items that used to be reliable and durable now seem flimsy and poorly constructed. I recently purchased a set of power tools that broke within a week of use, and when I attempted to return them, the staff's apathetic response was utterly disheartening.Adding insult to injury, the prices at East Liberty Home Depot have skyrocketed without any reasonable explanation. It's disconcerting to witness such a blatant disregard for the loyal customers who have supported this store over the years. The exorbitant costs coupled with the diminishing quality make it difficult to justify continuing my patronage.Perhaps the most frustrating aspect of this whole ordeal is the lack of accountability from the store management. I reached out to express my concerns, but my feedback seemed to evaporate into the abyss of indifference.

In spite of their appearance, each cake was also a little dry. The devil's food cake was so dry that it actually tasted stale. Even when accompanied by a glass of milk, the dryness of the cake was overwhelming. On the other hand, the carrot cake, which seemed moist, also suffered from a lack of flavor. The frosting on each cake tasted like standard grocery-store frosting, and it, too, was overly sweet. The chocolate frosting on the devil's food cake tasted slightly better than the cream cheese frosting on the carrot cake or the vanilla frosting on the red velvet cake, but none of the frostings were anything special. There really wasn't much difference between any of the cakes; they all tasted pretty much the same. To be fair, the red velvet cake did have a slightly better flavor than the other two cakes, but all three cakes suffered from a lack of quality ingredients. The red velvet cake was a little less dry than the other two cakes, but the cream cheese frosting on it was overly sweet. The carrot cake, which looked very moist, tasted bland and had a gritty texture. Even though the devil's food cake had a good chocolate flavor, it was dry and stale.

The hotel had several issues despite the cleanliness and spaciousness of the room. The inoperable air conditioning made the room uncomfortably warm. Additionally, the elevators were out of service, forcing us to use the unpleasant stairs. The lack of Wi-Fi hindered my ability to work. During a storm on the second night, the roof leaked water into our room. When requesting a different room, the unapologetic front desk staff informed us that none were available. The non-functioning AC, elevators, Wi-Fi, and leaky roof made for an overall disappointing and uncomfortable stay.

Was recommended by my coworker. However, I was a little unsure as I've read some bad reviews about this place. The first visit was great. The receptionists were helpful and gave me guidance on how to get my dog licensed. Everyone seemed happy and talkative. Dr. Bezak was very nice. He had a smile on him the entire time I was there. He was very quick to give me information about anything and everything relating to the dog. Overall, I had a good first visit and definitely going back. The only thing that made it didn't earn a five-star is that my appointment is at 12: 15pm. The entire office have their lunch at 1pm. So I can tell there was alot of hustle to get me out of their asap. I don't mind that it was a quick visit, but I would have liked to had time to ask more questions. If you want adequate time with the doc, consider making your appointment after their lunch.

The mWuseum is cOleverly located inside a hangar, on a winding road near the airport. While the outside of the building is unassuming, inside reveals an impressive colleciton of aircraft from across the decades. Rows of planes are carefully arranged in chronological order, allowing visitors to track the evolution of flight from the Wright BrothBers' fifrst aircraft to modern passenger jets. Dioramas bring each plane's history to lift, with detailed cockpits, mannequins dressed in period attire, and informative plaques. Beyond the aircraft themselves, exhibits also showcase innovations in aviation technology like early navigational instruments and parahutes. It was fascinating to learn about the daring tes pilots who pushed boundaries to break speed and altitude records. The museum does an excellent job of makding aviation's achievements accessible even to those without a technical background. By the end of the visit, I felt I had gaiend a new appreciation for all those who contributed to advances in air and spVce travel. With its engaging exhibits and educational approach, I wouAld hiqhly recommend this museum for people of any age interested in the story of flight.

I was neither particularly pleased nor dissatisfied with my lunch enjoy here. The restaurant had a cozy ambiance with soft lighting and comfortable seating, produce a relaxed atmosphere. The menu featured a innumerable range of options, catering to various dietary preferences. I have tried various dishes at Soba, and each time, the flavors and presentation have been impeccable. Their sushi rolls are a work of art, with unique combinations of ingredients that never fail to impress. The service is always attentive and friendly, making sure that my glass is always full and my plate is never empty.I particularly enjoy their miso soup, which is rich and savory, with a generous amount of tofu and seaweed. The edamame is also a highlight, cooked to perfection and seasoned with just the right amount of salt. And of course, their soba noodles are a must-try, with a pleasant chewiness that pairs well with the variety of sauces they offer.On my most recent visit, I tried their tempura, which was crispy and flavorful, and their chicken skewers, which were juicy and well-marinated. The portions are generous, so I always leave feeling satisfied but not overly full. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and service.Overall, Soba is a standout in the city's culinary scene, and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious and satisfying meal. Whether you're in the mood for sushi, noodles, or something else, Soba is sure to please.

I had high hopes for this restaurant, based on the many positive reviews I had read on the Internet. But from the moment I walked in, I knew something was wrong. The atmosphere was dull, the lighting was dim, the decor was outdated and seemed to lack a theme. When the food finally arrived, I was even more disappointed. I scanned the menu and couldn't find anything that really excited me. The choices were limited and unimaginative, the same tired classics you can find in any generic restaurant. The presentation was sloppy, with a haphazard garnish. The flavors were flat, with no depth or complexity. The dish lacked the vibrant flavors and creativity I had expected. It was obvious that the ingredients were of poor quality, which resulted in a bland, forgettable experience. To make matters worse, the service was incredibly slow and inattentive. The waiters seemed disinterested and untrained, often forgetting simple requests and neglecting to check on our satisfaction. It was obvious that they lacked the enthusiasm and professionalism you would expect from a reputable establishment. The overall value for the price was poor. The portions were small and overpriced, leaving me feeling unsatisfied and a little cheated. Perhaps this restaurant has seen better days, or perhaps it just never lived up to its reputation. I had hoped for a memorable dining experience, but instead I left the restaurant feeling underwhelmed and completely unimpressed. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for an exceptional dining experience. There are far better choices in the area that are more worthy of your time and hard-earned money. Save yourself the disappointment and look elsewhere for a truly remarkable dining experience.

As someone who dabbles in various crafts, this store can be overwhelming at first glance. However, upon closer inspection, the extensive selection reveals its hidden gems. From yarns and fabrics to paints and beads, the store offers a wide array of materials that cater to craft enthusiasts of all disciplines. Navigating through the aisles, you'll be greeted by an impressive assortment of tools and equipment, making it a one-stop-shop for any creative project.Special commendation goes to the knowledgeable and helpful staff members. They are not only familiar with the products but also eager to provide valuable recommendations and suggest alternatives when needed. The friendly demeanor of the staff creates a welcoming atmosphere that enhances the shopping experience.To help customers navigate the vastness of the store, there are clear signage and categorization systems in place. Even those new to the world of crafting can easily find specific items. The store regularly updates its inventory, ensuring that customers have access to the latest tools and trendy materials for their creative pursuits.One standout feature of this store is its commitment to affordability. Despite crafting being an expensive hobby at times, this store offers competitive prices without compromising on quality. Budget-conscious crafters can shop with ease, knowing they won't overspend.The store also fosters a sense of community by organizing frequent workshops and classes. Crafters of all skill levels can enhance their techniques and connect with like-minded individuals. These events are well-received and create a lively environment where creativity and knowledge intersect.Another commendable aspect is the store's dedication to sustainability. They prioritize eco-friendly materials and offer a range of products made from recycled or upcycled sources. This commitment resonates with customers who strive to create in an environmentally conscious way.

You know that going on. You're probably going to feel a little sick or regretful after your meal. You know that going in, too. But still, this place makes the tastiest, worst food. While their chicken sandwiches are awesome, I love their tenders too; I often combine these with a meal of mashed potatoes and/or slaw. Again, probably the least healthy option in the world, but as far as fast food--what a tasty option.

I visited this restaurant with my family on the day before Thanksgiving, and I must say, it was a truly delightful experience from beginning to end. The establishment exuded a warm and inviting atmosphere, with cozy lighting and comfortable seating. The friendly staff promptly greeted us and seated us, providing menus without delay.The menu offered a wide selection of options to cater to various dietary preferences. From mouthwatering appetizers to delectable main courses, there was something to satisfy everyone in my family. We decided to start with a variety of appetizers, including crispy calamari and flavorful bruschetta.The attentive and knowledgeable waitstaff assisted us in choosing our main courses. I opted for their signature dish, a succulent steak cooked to perfection, while my spouse chose a fresh and vibrant seafood pasta. Each dish was impeccably plated and bursting with flavors. The steak was tender and juicy, complemented by a savory sauce that enhanced the overall taste. The dessert menu featured an array of tempting treats, from classic cheesecake to innovative creations. We decided to share a slice of the rich chocolate lava cake, and it was an absolute delight. The warm, gooey center paired perfectly with the cool vanilla ice cream.Overall, our dining experience at this restaurant was truly exceptional.

I've been a client at Modern probably a dozen times over the past few years. The stylists are very talented and provide a consistent quality haircut each visit. Prices are reasonable for the top notch service. Parking is conveniently located right next to the salon. I've also had some coloring services done at Modern which came out beautifully. My hairstyle has always looked fresh and stylish after a visit. If I ever have any issues, the staff are quick to address them. After our meal, we walmked around the uptown area and saw that it was bustling with people enjoying the many sohps and restaurants. I was super nervous about using these guys due to the poor reviews, but I have a home warranty and the company chooses who we work with- I didn't have a choice.So, I was stuck with them. The appointment was scheduled for the following Monday morning and I was told that I would receive a call between 8:00 and 10:00 AM with an estimated time of arrival.I get the call around 9:30 saying the technician is on his way. He arrived around 10:30 and he was the rudest person ever. I told him the issue and he looked at the unit outside. He came back in and gave me an estimate of $1000 to fix the unit. When I questioned why it was so much, he shrugged and told me it was the cost of labor and the part.I know nothing about air conditioning units and I don't know if he was trying to take advantage of me or if it was actually the going rate. Since I didn't have any other options, I just let him go ahead and fix it. He left and came back the next day with the part. He said he would call me when he was done to check out the unit to make sure it was working properly. He never did. I called the office multiple times and left messages. No one ever returned my calls.I finally went to the office during the week to see if I could speak to someone in person. When I walked in, there were two women behind the desk, but no one acknowledged me. They continued their personal conversation and ignored me for at least five minutes. I finally interrupted them and they reluctantly helped me. I told them what happened and they said the technician was out of town and would be back on Monday. They said he would call me then.He never called. I tried calling the following week and still no answer. At this point, I'm thinking the whole business is a scam.I ended up calling my home warranty company again and requesting a different company to come out and take a look at the unit. The new technician came out the following Monday and took a look at the unit.

Also, I wanted to bring my dog along for some company (my husband and daughter stayed home for work/school). I'm so glad I found this place! As other reviews have noted, you get an actual suite with a door and everything! There is a kitchen with a full sized refrigerator, microwave, stove and sink. It also comes stocked with silverware, plates, and pots and pans. The hotel has a small convenience area in case you don't want to go out for food. There are a few frozen meals, etc. Free wi-fi as well. The full breakfast was pretty good, too. Waffles, eggs, sausage, biscuits and gravy (on most mornings), pastries, coffee, etc. My only complaints (and these are pretty minor) was that the TVs weren't very new. And the shower curtain was so thick and heavy that it kept touching me. A curved shower curtain would do wonders. The front desk staff was so nice! There was an issue with my check-in (they didn't have me on record), but they were accommodating. And one of the desk guys said that if someone had to leave their dog all day, he'd walk the dog for the guest! Cool! All this for under $100 a night. Can't beat it! I'll stay here again.

Our waitress, a friendly and attentive young woman, came to take our drink order. We both ordered a classic burger, my girlfriend the Bloomfield BBQ, which was topped with a generous portion of caramelized onions and a tangy bbq sauce. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a mix of classic rock and pop music in the background. We didn't have to wait long for our burgers to arrive, and when they did, we were both impressed by the generous portions and the quality of the ingredients. The beef was cooked to perfection, juicy and tender, the toppings fresh and flavorful, the buns soft and slightly sweet. I ordered a side of golden-brown fries, which were seasoned with just the right amount of salt and pepper. We both agreed that the burgers were everything we'd heard about them and more. The bbq sauce on my girlfriend's burger added a nice depth of flavor, and the caramelized onions were a perfect complement to the savory beef. The prices were very reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food. We were both very pleased with our meals and the friendly, attentive service. We'll definitely be back to try some of the other menu items and enjoy the welcoming atmosphere.

For location this place is a 4 star. The rooms are small and they even gave me a corner room that said was bigger. I would hate to see what a normal room looks like. The corner room has 2 full size beds and is like a triangle. You do have space but very little and the bathrooms well the toilet and the shower are like touching each other. You can barely close the bathroom door if you want to do business in private! The corner rooms also that face 4th street just expect a night of loud music as that side faces several rooftop bars and they play music loud late into the night. Only saving grace is putting in the AC fan but that is loud as well. Either music or white noise. The signature lounge.. . again.. . small. Overall the lobby is nice, nice restaurant and attached to BofA and the center of town with everything in walking distance. As I said.. .. for location unbeatable. For a luxury hotel for the price NOPE.

OK, from a distance, this looks like a good hotel. However, after the inspection, I noticed that the lobby was very small and needed to be renovated. My room is small and dirty, which is very different from the online photos. The bathroom is clean, but outdated, you can use updates. When I was sitting on the bed, it squeaked loudly, obviously very old and dilapidated. I tried to fall asleep, but I found that the mattress was very uncomfortable and provided a bad rest for the break at night. In the morning, I went to the breakfast area, hoping to get a good start in my day. Unfortunately, there are few choices, and most foods look old. Coffee is very weak, there is very little water, and I have almost made me awakened. I went to get some fresh air outside and noticed that the landscape beautification was weed everywhere. It seems that it rarely strives to maintain the outside of the property. When I checked it out, I was not sad after this tired old hotel was left behind, and it was not recommended that you live here. In general, if facilities provide a happy experience for guests, the facility needs to be renovated and maintained.

I typically enjoy the standard "tex-mex" type restaurants, but this was a pretty poor example of the style. Like most of these places the experience starts with chips and salsa; this salsa was bland and watery. The chips were cold and stale; not sure when they made them, but I'm sure that it was not the day they served them to us.. . At this point I should have left and drove up the road to Azteca, Don Pedro or any of the other taco shacks the Queen City has to offer; but sometimes I am not so sharp so we proceeded to order lunch. I ordered the chimichanga; now usually a chimichanga is a flour tortilla filled with a wide range of seasoned flavorful ingredients and deep fried until it is a golden brown color and slightly crispy on the outside. This thing was filled with bland, unflavorful, grayish colored "shredded beef" and was soggy, they then smothered it in some sort of unseasoned canned tomatoes that they tried to pass off as salsa, I assume to mask the lack of flavor in the dish itself. On the side was some wilted lettuce with sour cream and something that vaguely resembled guacamole, and some oily rice that was nearly as flavorless as the rest of the meal. Phenomenal. I managed to eat about a quarter of this flavorless, oily, soggy train wreck before I gave up and threw in the towel. When the server finally came back around several minutes later, she acted like she didn't even notice that none of us had eaten more than half of their meal, and quietly picked up the plates and brought us our checks. None of us were asked how our meal was, if everything was OK, if we wanted any desert or more chips and salsa, and none of us received a refill on our drinks. All in all, this was one of the worse restaurant prepared meals that I have had the pleasure of experiencing. Kudos to the good folks at El Cancun

Only two words are needed to describe Dean's Barbershop in Newport Beach: Man Spa! This is a place where you will be treated like royalty, from the moment you walk through the door until the moment you leave. The ambiance is warm and inviting, with dark wood paneling, leather chairs, and a fireplace. The staff is incredibly friendly and professional, and they are always happy to make recommendations or answer any questions. But it's the haircuts that really set Dean's apart. The barbers are true artists, and they take their time to make sure that each and every cut is perfect. I've been going to Dean's for over a year now, and I've never been disappointed.
