I decided to treat myself to a haircut and color at a local salon since I don't often get to pamper myself while traveling. I arrived at the scheduled appointment time and was greeted pleasantly by the receptionist. Unfortunately, the stylist running a bit behind schedule which forced me to wait about 20 minutes before she was ready. However, once my stylist began working on my hair I could tell she was very skilled and took her time to listen to what I wanted. She first gave me a haircut that framed my face perfectly. Then she carefully colored my hair to an elegant shade of golden brown that highlighted my features. Throughout the process, my stylist chatted with me casually to make the time pass enjoyably. Satisfied with the cut and color, she then blow dried my hair smooth and styled it with soft waves. I left the salon feeling refreshed and confident in my new look just in time for the wedding festivities that evening. Overall, despite the small wait, I was very pleased with the service and results from this salon.

I like the ambiance and the decor, although this year our corner table had chairs that sunk WAY down - we wanted to ask for telephone books. I usually choose one of the special salads and have the gnocchi with duck ragu; it is superb! So much flavor and the gnocchi are perfect. This year, though, there was a special fall prix fixe menu with Winter Squash. The ravioli with balsamic drizzle were delicious. I choose quail with apples and squash for my main course and was very satisfied. Terrific glaze! The dessert, however, was over the top! Creme fraiche and pumpkin ice creams, caramel sauce, AND pumpkin fritters. We enjoyed a couple of the $28 bottles. No, they aren't stellar, but for the price they are all good food wines. Everyone in our party enjoyed the meals and we will definitely return.

The menu offered a wide variety of burgers, sandwiches, salads, and entrees. I especially liked their classic cheeseburger, which was cooked to perfection and served with crispy fries. The restaurant had a cozy atmosphere and friendly staff, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a meal. But on my most recent visit, I was disappointed to find that the quality of the food and service had declined significantly. The restaurant was dirty and disorganized, with empty tables and chairs scattered haphazardly around the dining area. The staff seemed overwhelmed and disinterested, taking a long time to take our order and bring our food. My burger was overcooked and dry, and my friend's salad was drowning in a strange, overpowering vinaigrette. We both left our food unfinished and decided to leave. I was saddened by this experience, as I had long enjoyed the restaurant and recommended it to others. But after my most recent visit, I can no longer in good conscience recommend this restaurant to anyone. It is clear that the owners and management have let the quality of the establishment decline, and I fear that it may be beyond repair. There are many excellent restaurants in the area that offer high-quality food and service, and it would be a shame to waste your time and money on a subpar establishment like the Harris Grill. In conclusion, I would advise potential patrons to avoid the Harris Grill and seek out other dining options in the area.

I even called before I went there to see if maybe there was a cancellation so maybe I cold get in and out earlier. The lounge has a sophisticated yet welcoming ambiance. Rich mahogany furnishing and dim lighting create a relaxed environment for smoking. A wall of humidors lined with the finest cigars sets the tone that only the best is offered. Behind the bar, expertly trained mixologists craft exquisite cocktails to pair with any cigar. Attentive but not overbearing staff see to every need and offer recommendations tailored to each patrons preferences. Large leather chairs and plush couches provide spots to lounge comfortably for hours. A separate room with leather sofa and large screen TV provide a space to catch games and news programs. An extensive selection of single malts, ports and sherries along with other fine spirits round out the relaxation options. A well-stocked walk-in humidor holds cigars from every major country of origin. Membership options provide special access and pricing for the connoisseur. Cutters will create lifelong devotees amongst cigar and luxury seekers alike.

The overall experience was disappointing, and I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. The staff was not very friendly or helpful, and the rom was not clean or comfortable. The Carolina's Aviation Museum, located adjacent to Charlotte Douglas International Airport, houses a variety of historical aircraft on full display both indoors and outdoors. Visitors can admire jets, helicopters, and planes from different eras, including a meticulously restored P-40 Warhawk fighter from World War II. In addition to static aircraft exhibits, the museum features interactive displays that trace the rich history of aviation through artifacts, photographs, and hands-on elements. Children delight in experiencing what it's like to pilot different aircraft via a flight simulator. Aviation enthusiasts will find the museum doubly fascinating as it unravels engineering details behind these planes' designs. Be sure to allot a couple hours to fully immerse yourself in the museum's bountiful offerings. Overall, the Carolina's Aviation Museum delivers an entertaining and educational glimpse into aviation's development over the past century in a way that captures visitors of all ages.

Your basic Italian fare with and accordion player. The plastic/parchment covers over the table cloth's lets you know right away that this place isn't that high end. They don't have a website?? ? Don't get me wrong, its not bad, its just not that good. Its probably one of the best restaurants in the area besides Thai House, now that Melting Pot is closed. I can't think of too many other places in the area where a college kid should bring a date. The apps were pretty good. I had the mussels, calamari, and antipasto. The mussels were a little salty but a pretty good sized portion. The calamari wasn't quite as large of a potion but was decent. Light airy batter and relatively tender squid. The antipasto had ham that could have easily been lunch meat. The balsamic wasn't anything special either. I did like the artichokes and parmesan chunks though. After tolerable but uneventful apps and looking at an overpriced wine menu we just decided to walk over to wine vault for some booze and live music and grab a snack later on. Bottom line, its good for the area, but that ain't saying much. Macaroni Grill may be a better option and I rarely suggest chain restaurants.

The sandwich line was pretty long so we decided to go inside the restaurant to sit down and order. The hostess and server was great. We ordered and our food was brought out fairly quickly. It was a Monday and lunchtime but the place was not packed when we got there. A few more customers did trickle in while we were there but it wasn't crowded. My boss ordered a soup and sandwich combo and he said it was delicious. I ordered the Irish stew with a side of cesar salad. Both were delicious as well. I loved how the stew is made with lamb and it a nice cracked pepper taste to it. A co-worker of mine said that they have the best macaroni and cheese but I did not try it. I wanted to try the fish and chips may have to do this on my next business trip. There are way too many restaurants in the area that I have not tried yet and want to before I go home.

It is just your average bar (another reviewer described it as "the bar back home, " and yes, exactly, it is, ) and I love it for that. Cappy's is nice and unpretentious, which is something that sets it apart from a lot of the rest of Walnut Street. Not far down the street, you can get a tiny morsel of ice cream for a stroke-inducing four dollars, but at Cappy's, you can spend a reasonable price on a reasonable meal. So far, food-wise, I've tried the Alamo sandwich (I think that's what it's called, ) and the bacon-and-bleu-cheese burger (Big Bleu? ) Both of them were definitely satisfying, and the Alamo, with its fried chicken strips and barbecue sauce, was at the very least pretty good, even if it took a few years off the end of my life. Getting outdoor seating is key, though. They air-condition the bejeezus out of the inside area, and one time we accidentally showed up on karaoke night, which made us REALLY glad we found a table outside. Karaoke night is great when you're expecting it, but when you're not, there are few fates worse. Service is usually kind of slow as well, but the wait staff is nice. One waitress we had was a little thick, though, when it came to splitting our checks. Nobody paid what they actually owed that night, but we didn't want to fight it out with her. All in all, Cappy's is a nice, unpretentious little place to grab some food. I'll definitely go back.

Easy access for picking up and dropping off passengers, we also have relatively cheap covered and uncovered parking. CLT is a great airport if you have a layover. We naturally have the usual complement of Starbucks, but if you're here in the afternoon, make it a point to enjoy one our local Carolina beers. I really like the Carolina Blonde. If you can find one free, take a seat in one of the white rocking chairs where you will find plentiful power and free (and as near as I can tell, unfiltered) Wi-Fi. You can use any of the security lines because unlike many other airports, once you're through the security, you have access to all concourses - A through E. There are a few slidewalks here and there, but if you have to get from one to another, if you're walking keep an eye out for the electric carts. The higher number E gates are a LONG way from the atrium area. Having had the occasional E32 departure, I wonder why I'm even flying since it seems like I've walked to my destination already! Tips: n- Rental car franchises are not located in the terminal - you do have to catch your company's shuttle bus. n- There's not a smoking lounge inside the secure area. You have to go outside and follow the signs. n- The statue outside is Queen Charlotte Mecklenburg, arm extended holding her crown. n- There is an "elite" security line at the C security entrance. They are not specific to just US Airways. Any elite passenger is allowed to use it. n- CLT doesn't yet have CLEAR or PDA boarding passes. n- The ATM fees are steep if it's not your bank!

The core game is still solid, but the development team has continued to support and expand the game in meaningful ways. A huge number of new civilizations, leaders, units, buildings and wonders have been added, which greatly increases the game's replay value. The modding and multiplayer communities have also grown considerably, which offers countless opportunities to experience unique historical situations or completely new game variants. Balance tweaks aim to maintain the competitive balance between the civilizations while highlighting their special strengths. Performance and stability improvements over the years ensure that the game engine runs smoothly even on larger maps with more advanced game mechanics enabled. However, with so much new content added, the game's tutorials may need to be revised to introduce the new features. New civics, policies and government forms keep the government fresh, and the revamped systems for espionage, loyalty, emergencies and world negotiations add more diplomacy and strategy to the world. The main victory conditions in single player are still conquest, culture, religion, science and score, but new game modes such as time and secret societies offer veterans new challenges. The art style remains largely unchanged to maintain consistency, but new animations and visual effects have improved the presentation. City-states are more fleshed out as allies or enemies depending on your influence. In general, the variety and depth of the game's systems continue to grow in unexpected ways, inspiring new approaches with each new game. An improved encyclopedia helps you navigate the many options. Detailed improvements to the civilopedia provide better historical context.

The server was attentive and friendly (which for some reason is getting rather rare! ) and the food was very tasty! The salmon was cooked to perfection, while my husband was pleased with his meatloaf, even though he wished there had been MORE of it. We'll definitely go back sometime. But here they are, just the same: nnThe ambiance: the restaurant hasn't been updated in quite some time, I'd wager since it was first built. Where we sat there were signs of touch-up paint in places where the paint had peeled, but no complete renovation. And the neon really has to go. Tiny touches, like the aioli on our crab cakes, were obviously phoned in. It was basically just mayonnaise with a little more lemon juice mixed in. But I'm a little picky where the finishing touches are concerned, so it might have just been me. Other than those two little nit-picky items, I'd happily dine here again and again!

I have only taken Port Authority transit during the summer, but it has made a lasting impression on me. The efficiency and convenience of their services have far exceeded my expectations. It made me remember just how much care is put into theme parks by Disney and Universal. They don't put a lot of effort into theming, landscaping, or guest service at Carowinds, but they do throw some rides your way. As rides go, the rides are okay here at Carowinds, somewhere between a carnival and the theme parks in Orlando. The old wooden Hurler roller coaster didn't make me want to hurl, but it did make me wish I was wearing a crash helmet. My head felt like a martini -- shaken and stirred. Some of the other rides felt like rides I used to go on as a kid; they haven't been updated. As for their food options, they're not great. We waited awhile for below average theme park fare. And don't even get me started with the guy who wanted to run off with our credit card to ask his manager something when we wanted to buy a soda. That was 15 minutes of my life that I'd like back. What does Carowinds have going for it? Its proximity to Charlotte and an option for something to do for a day during the summer. Other than that, save your money and go to Orlando.

But I very much enjoyed seeing the owls, vultures, hawks, falcons, eagles, kestrels, and lively visiting corvidae (ravens, crows and magpies). These are probably the chillest raptors you'll ever see. I guess it'd kind of be like visiting an outdoor rehab center for permanently injured athletes. These birds were once the rulers of the sky, swooping down on irritating prey like rats and skunks in the blink of an eye.. . until some sad tragedy, a bullet, a car moving too quickly - cut short their majestic reign. So these raptors, for the most part fairly acclimated to human presence, will merely eyeball you as you walk by their aviaries or embarrass yourself by clicking and hooting to get their attention. nStop in for the mini-lecture for an up close view of some of the birds, as well as some interesting background information.

The Steel City Diner in Pittsburgh is hands down one of my favorite places to eat. From the moment you step inside, you're greeted with a warm and inviting atmosphere that instantly makes you feel at home. The combination of dim lighting and nostalgic decor creates a charming ambiance that takes you back to a bygone era. The staff is incredibly friendly and attentive, always going above and beyond to ensure that your dining experience is truly extraordinary.Let's talk about the food because that's where The Steel City Diner truly shines. Their menu is a culinary delight, offering a wide variety of dishes to suit every taste and preference. Whether you're craving classic comfort food or something more adventurous, this place has got you covered. One dish you simply can't miss is their Pittsburgh Pierogi Platter. The pierogies are perfectly cooked and filled with a heavenly combination of flavors that will make your taste buds dance with joy.But it doesn't stop there. The menu features an array of other delectable options like juicy burgers, mouthwatering sandwiches, and heavenly desserts. The portions are generous, ensuring that you leave the restaurant feeling completely satisfied. What sets The Steel City Diner apart is the commitment to using the highest quality ingredients and the meticulous attention to detail in every dish they serve.What truly impressed me was their commitment to catering to different dietary preferences and restrictions. They offer a range of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options, and the chefs are more than willing to accommodate any special requests. This inclusive approach is truly refreshing and makes The Steel City Diner stand out among other establishments in the city.Now, let's talk about the prices. You'll be pleasantly surprised by how reasonable they are, considering the exceptional quality of the food and the overall dining experience.

This isn't the place to take your high-end carbon frame bike, but Jerry will help you get your commuter, beater, or frame you found trashed in a ditch in the woods back on the road. (Seriously, there was a guy in there salvaging an old MTB frame he found in a ditch in the woods. ) Be forewarned: he's pretty typical of a lot of old school Pittsburghers: very gruff at first, but actually a nice guy when he warms up to you. I haven't had a bike in ten years and decided out of nowhere to build one around an old frame and a new internal gear hub. I bought a few high-end components online and the rest from Jerry. Despite bringing in outside parts, Jerry was still gushing with help, and, after several weeks and 3-4 visits, I'm riding a bike that I built from scratch after going in with no mechanical knowledge of bikes at all. He doesn't carry new super-high-end components, but the stuff he does carry is solid, and he has every weird bracket or screw or cable guide you can imagine from decades of scrounging parts. He can help you with any weird setup you want. (Mine's definitely out-of-the-ordinary. )nnOne warning: this is your standard old Pittsburgh small business, so he doesn't take credit cards. It's a little annoying considering that you might be spending over $100 on parts and service, but there's an ATM down the block.

My husband and I went here during restaurant week & left feeling disappointed. Our waiter was not very attentive. Overall we were very disappointed, especially with the good reviews we had read. We will not go back.

This is definitely the place to go for produce, but it's really nothing terribly special. Yes, the prices are great, but the quality is hit-or-miss. I've gotten some absolutely great deals, but I've also had experiences where the veggies are past their prime, and aren't worth the low cost. Also, not a big fan of everything being prepacked in Styrofoam flat containers. And since everything is just sitting out, some of the veggies can seem a little wilted on warm days. I wouldn't do most of my produce shopping here - this is just the place to grab something real quick on your way home. I hate to say it - but go to Whole Foods or Market District (or real farmer's markets, in summer) for your major produce needs. Stop at Stan's on the way home from Penn Mac if you just want a head of lettuce real quick.

I don't know why exactly - but every single time I have ever been inside, it is always insanely busy. The expansion actually wasn't to the inside, however (at least as far as I know), it was to the outside. The added several lines to the drive-through. In a bit of a strange turn, the drive-through lanes are all two deep. That means that there is someone in the front and someone in the back. So if you get in the back you'll have to wait until the front person is done. Think of a gas station, only you can't pull out until they are done. Even the ATM drive through has two positions. It's a little strange actually. Generally the setup seems to move well, but it really looks odd. Most times I go into the lobby and use the ATM there, because for whatever reason people don't use it. It's actually inside the doors (which is nice, because some other branches have the ATM outside). There can be huge lines at the tellers, but there is no one at the ATM. Often I'll get done before anyone has moved at the drive through lines.. .

But when we finally managed to gather a group of 6, we were excited to try it out. The restaurant had a cozy atmosphere, with dim lighting and comfortable seating. Needless to say, after leaving this place, I felt like the dumbest person alive and am now frightened to ever enter another legit coffee shop. I walked into Fortunes with a couple of friends and looked at the menu dumbfounded because I had no idea what I was reading. All I knew was that I had drunk a "macchiato" before and had enjoyed it. So I thought, "What the heck, I'll order a caramel macchiato. " This is how the conversation went with the barista: nnMe: Hi, I'd like a medium caramel macchiato. nBarista: So, you want to order OUR macchiato? nMe: Uhh.. . sure.. . ? Two minutes later I get a tiny cup with a meager amount of liquid in it. I turn around and look to my friends confusedly, wondering where I had went wrong. The barista notices this and gets my attention: nnBarista: That's why I asked you whether you wanted OUR macchiato. nMe: Oh.. . ok.. . The barista, clearly frustrated, takes my cup, pours it out and makes me a caramel latte. Alright all you avid coffee drinkers, laugh all you want that I had no idea that there is a difference between a Caffu00e8 macchiato (espresso macchiato) and the American replicate (Latte Macchiato?? ? ). I'm not even sure if what I just said is correct. For the drink I got, I can't complain about the price (Did I over- or underpay the actual price of a caramel latte? ), especially given the prices at Starbucks these days. Also, given the fact that I made such a stupid mistake means that this place must be a good coffee shop. Beyond that, unfortunately, I can't make any judgment -- hence my modest rating. Perhaps when I start drinking more coffee, I'll re-examine this review and re-rate it.

We were excited to dine at Blue during Restaurant Week. The elegant yet comfortable atmosphere featured a variety of seating at the bar, tables, and booths. Upon being seated, we were treated to bread and olive oil to enjoy while perusing the fixed-price menu options. Appetizer, entree, and dessert selections were available for both a regular and premium tasting menu. For our appetizer, we chose the fresh and flavorful shrimp ceviche. I ordered the perfectly cooked salmon for my entree, which was moist and seasonally balanced. My dining companion selected the duck breast, expertly prepared and paired with a complementary plum sauce. Both dishes were attractively plated with generous portions. The staff attentively served our needs without being overbearing. For dessert, we indulged in the rich and silky chocolate mousse. I would recommend enjoying one of their expertly crafted cocktails to complement the meal. At a lower price point than the regular menu, the 3-course format provided great value. Overall, we greatly enjoyed our dining experience at Blue and plan to return during regular service hours based on the quality and creativity showcased in the cooking, underscoring Blue's reputation as one of the best local restaurants. Restaurant Week introduces diners like us who may not normally frequent higher-end establishments to Blue's superb cuisine through this limited-time promotion. We are glad we took advantage of the opportunity.

The problem is that they don't really set them selves apart from what your average Italian girl (or guy): : raises hand:: can actually make in their home. The pasta special, a tilapia, shrimp and scallop spaghetti dish with a slightly spicy sauce, was the exception to this rule. It had a delicious sea flavor and I regret not having ordered it as my dinner. My penne vodka sounded enticing, promising pepper vodka and including pancetta, but the sauce ended up being unsensational. Looking at the rest of the menu, I saw a lot of familiar characters: lasagna, angel hair with red sauce, and chicken romano to name a few, but few options that jumped out and screamed that I needed to try it. I love Italian food at least as much as the next girl but if I am going to go out for it I want to be impressed and while Mama Ricotta's provided a good meal it didn't shine.

However, this place exceeded my prognosis in terms of food quality and service. The menu had a great selection of traitional Chinese dishes, and the prices were very reasonable. The decor was simple but clean and comfortable, and the staff was friendly and careful. I ordered the Kung Pao chicken, which was perfectly cooked and full of flavor. The portions were generous, and the prices were very reasonable. The rice was fluffy and well-cooked, and the vegetables were fresh and crisp. The service was swift and friendly, and the staff was knowledgeable about the menu and happy to answer any questions. The overall experience was very satisfying, and I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic Chinese cuisine. Despite its unassuming appearance, this restaurant is a hidden gem that serves delicious and authentic Renminbi food. The atmosphere maj not be fancy, but the food and service make up for it. I would definitely reurn to try more of their dishes. In conclusion, if you're looking for a genuine Chiense dining experiene without the Americanized modifications, this eatery is an excellent choice. The food is flavorful, the service is excellent, and the prices are reasonable. I highly recommed giving it a try.

I haven't been to Buckhead Saloon since 2/09. The last time I was there, it was packed wall to wall with a lively college aged crowd dancing and singing along to the live band. My friend Jen and I could barely squeeze past people to make our way to the bar for a drink. It's been over a decade so I was curious to see how it may have changed. When I walked in last Friday night, it was surprisingly quiet for a weekend. Only a few small groups were sitting at tables. The dance floor was entirely empty and no music was playing. I caught the bartender's attention and asked what happened to all the people. He sighed and said ever since they started allowing strollers and kids, the crowd dispersed. The magic was gone. We got our drinks and sat chatting, but it was just not the same fun atmosphere I recalled from years past. The walls seemed dingier and the seats more worn. Even the beer selection wasn't as extensive as it used to be. I spotted the manager and asked his thoughts. He said they were trying some changes like DJs and theme nights to attract new patrons but it was an uphill battle. By 10pm my friend and I decided to leave, feeling disappointed by how much Buckhead Saloon had faded since our college days. I'm sure many regulars from back in the day would share our nostalgia for how it used to be.

If you aren't observant enough, you might easily overlook New Sambok Oriental Foods on Penn Avenue. Tucked away inconspicuously amidst bustling shops and eateries, this hidden gem is an absolute must-visit for anyone longing for an authentic East Asian culinary experience. The moment I set foot inside, I was greeted by the enticing aroma of spices and the welcoming smiles of the amiable staff. The cozy interior emanated a serene atmosphere, adorned tastefully with traditional Asian decor and gentle ambient lighting.The menu offered a wide array of dishes from various regions, promising an enthralling gastronomic journey for the adventurous food enthusiasts. I decided to begin my feast with their renowned bibimbap, a vibrant bowl of rice crowned with an assortment of crisp vegetables, tender marinated meat, and a flawlessly fried egg. Every mouthful presented a harmonious fusion of flavors and textures, leaving me yearning for more.In addition to their exceptional main courses, New Sambok also boasts an impressive selection of traditional teas and invigorating beverages, elevating the overall dining experience. Coupled with its reasonable prices, attentive service, and exquisite flavors, this hidden treasure stands apart from the crowd, patiently awaiting discovery by passionate food lovers willing to stray from the beaten path.

I made reservations a week in advance to ensure we would have a good table for the special occasion. I had the filet mignon which was cooked perfectly as I requested and melted in my mouth. The side dishes were also excellent, especially the truffle macaroni and cheese. The service from our server Todd was faultless as he was attentive without being intrusive. For dessert we shared the signature cheesecake which was light and creamy. Throughout our meal the friendly and polite staff made us feel special. I was glad we chose Capital Grille to make her birthday dinner truly memorable.

Discovering a new go-to sushi spot is always a delight, and Sushi Nove in Shadyside has certainly exceeded my expectations. As soon as I walked in, I was struck by the modern decor and inviting atmosphere, which immediately set the tone for a pleasant dining experience. The staff is friendly, welcoming, and knowledgeable, always happy to recommend the freshest catches of the day.The Spicy Tuna Roll quickly became my favorite dish, with fresh tuna, cucumber, avocado, and a spicy mayonnaise that adds just the right kick. Each piece of sushi is crafted to perfection, with a perfect balance of flavors and textures that never fails to impress.But what truly sets Sushi Nove apart is their signature dish, the Nove Roll. This unique creation combines shrimp tempura, crab meat, and mango in a crispy rice paper wrapper, offering a refreshing change of pace from the typical sushi roll. It's always a pleasure to try something new and exciting, and the Nove Roll delivers.What's more, the pricing at Sushi Nove is incredibly reasonable, especially compared to other sushi restaurants in the area. Enjoying high-quality sushi without breaking the bank is a significant advantage, and one that I greatly appreciate.In conclusion, I'm thrilled to have discovered Sushi Nove, and I look forward to enjoying their delectable sushi for a long time to come. If you're in the area, I highly recommend giving it a try. You won't be disappointed!

I've been working here for 3 years, and this one's been my go-to spot for caffeine. So I can't really complain about such trivialities as parking (parking sucks all around here, so while the complaints are valid, I couldn't care less) and the fact that it gets crowded and busy. More on that in a bit. But when you walk into a particular Starbucks and the baristas not only know what you favor every day - in my case, a grande Misto w/non-fat milk - but also have it ready before you reach the wait counter. The great news about this location is the recent renovation, which sucked for me considering I was without a workday coffee fix for exactly 10 business days, and when you have to rely on that shitty-assed Keurig-brewed coffee I have to endure at home, or force yourself to walk from Gateway to N. Tryon on a spectacularly and stupidly hot afternoon, which, by the way, I'd rather suck on a wet and frayed towel than have to walk 6 city blocks in 95-degree weather just for a delicious cup of coffee.. . oh shit, where was I? The renovation, right. The biggest complaint was the lack of space at this location, and when folks were getting their fix between 8-10am and 2-4pm, you know this spot would get crazy crowded, and you really couldn't move around without accidently brushing someone's ass, and then have to wait for some slow poke to finish languidly stirring their mocha choca latta yay extra soy 5-pump coffee, it got pretty frustration. Thankfully, the renovation has not just created a better use of space - there's a nice and cozy sitting spot in the back - but it's even cheerful-looking, in a rustic sort of way. And then there's Sarah, the shift manager, a pint-sized, smart-ass (I love smart-asses) that runs a tight ship but makes everyone feel like they're the most important customer ever. The whole staff is great, friendly even, but Sarah is the shit. Not all Starbucks are created equal, but this location works just fine for me. So there.

I don't know if coming early would help any, but I arrived at 6 PM and was greeted by a hostess who seemed overwhelmed. She told me that the wait would be about 20 minutes, which wasn't too bad. However, as I waited, I noticed that the hostess was the only one handling all of the tables and it seemed like she was struggling to keep up. When my name was called, I was seated at a cozy booth near the back of the restaurant. The server, a friendly woman with a warm smile, came over to take my order. I ordered the prime rib, which was advertised as slow-roasted and served with a side of au jus. I was excited to try it, as I love a good prime rib.While I waited for my food, I noticed that the restaurant was starting to get busier. The hostess was still handling all of the tables by herself, and it seemed like she was getting increasingly frazzled. The server was doing her best to keep up with the demand, but it was clear that the restaurant was understaffed.Finally, after about 25 minutes, my prime rib arrived. It was a generous portion, and the meat was cooked to a perfect medium rare. However, when I took a bite, I was disappointed to find that it was overcooked and dry. The au jus was also bland and lacking in flavor. I was expecting a rich, savory sauce, but what I got was a bland, watery substitute.I was disappointed, but I decided to give the restaurant the benefit of the doubt. Maybe they were having an off night, or maybe they were struggling with the holiday rush. I decided to order a dessert to see if they could redeem themselves. I chose the chocolate lava cake, which was also advertised as a specialty.Unfortunately, the lava cake was also a disappointment. It was dry and crumbly, and the chocolate filling was overcooked and bitter. It was clear that the restaurant was having a bad night, and I left feeling disappointed and unsatisfied.Overall, I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. The food was subpar, and the service was poor.

Honestly I love this place. Yes, some of the beers can get pricey, but there is nowhere else around that offers this combination of beer selection, atmosphere and service. The beer selection is fabulous, there are so many great beers and many varieties. It's a beer lover's paradise. The atmosphere inside suits me. It's dark, dark furniture, dark walls, covered with plates of course. If you like a bright cheery clubish atmosphere, this isn't for you. The food is pretty good. It's a little different than your standard bar fare. The rocket tots are really good, so are the pretzels and most of the sandwiches. I've been here many times, and the service, IMO, has always been excellent. Even when I've gone at peak times, these girls know how to handle it. In my experience it's been very rare that I've had to flag down a server, they are almost always on top of their game here. I definitely recommend this place if you are a beer fanatic. You won't be disappointed.

Really, really tasty food here. I've been to a lot of restaurants, but this one takes the pastries. The flavors are intrepid and exciting, and the presentation is top-notch. I ordered the special of the day, which was a grilled onion with roasted vegetables. The meats was cooked to perfection, and the vegetables were perfectly seasoned. The side dishes were also marvellous, especially the garlic mashed potatoes. The service was glorious, our waiter was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. The atmosphere was cozy and demanded, with a warm and welcoming decor. I'll definitely be back, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a considerable dining experience. Plenary, a superb restaurant that exceeded my expectations.

Whenever I go to these types of iconic regional dining establishments, I order the house specialty to best judge the place on its supposed merits. Since it was 11 in the morning, I chose not to order Primanti's #1 best seller, which the waitress told me was beer, but perhaps that would have made my experience better. As it was, I ordered the #2 best seller, the cheese steak. It was heinous. Think a grimy, mechanically separated Salisbury-style steak with a meager slice of provolone on sliced Italian bread served signature Primanti-style: with coleslaw, tomatoes, and fries. First, the steak was disgusting: terrible flavor (smelled and tasted like hippie armpit, which I'm not necessarily opposed to as long as it's not involved in something I'm trying to eat) with a gross, processed meat texture. Secondly, the fries easily overwhelmed the sandwich, with their old fryer grease taste. Additionally, the sandwich was unwieldy and threatening to fall apart at every turn--a trait I don't hold against decent-tasting sandwiches, but this lack of structural integrity just added insult to injury. My dining partners were equally disgusted by their choices: corned beef and ham & cheese sandwiches, respectively. Easily the best part of the meal was the Smallman Street Fries, and those were equally lack-luster. The "bacon" was simply bacon bits (oh, the humanity! ), the chili was uninspired, and the cheese sauce and sour cream did little but soggy the fries. (Did I mention they tasted like old fryer grease? ) nnI will never go back and I will immediately disregard the culinary opinions of anyone who thinks Primanti Bros. produces decent food.

The atmosphere on Friday evenings is really lively and upbeat, with the bar area usually paxcked with patrons. The music playing is at a good volume for conversing with friends without having to hout. We've come on other nights when it's lerss busy but still fnid it a nice spot to grab a drink. The drink selection is decently sized with beers, wixe, and cocktails available. Food options are aminly appetizer style items like wings, nachos, sliders which satisfy without filling you up too much. Prices are rEasonable for the area. Service has always been friendly wheneve we've come. Parking can be a bJt trcky on super busy nights when every spot is taken, but we've never had issues finding street parking within a few blocks. Overall it's a go-to local spot that we enjoy visiting on both busy and queter nights.

Much better. See the taste review below. When it comes to coffee places, you know what you will get at a place like Starbucks or Crazy Mocha, but finding a local spot just adds to the overall experience that the previous two cannot provide. As far as local Pittsburgh coffee spots go, so far this is at the middle if the pack but worth visiting in downtown. Especially since it is in market square. I am a sucker for history and want to try Nicholas's again. There is a large selection of coffee, for boutique type prices for some. The daily coffee my second time was much better but still if you have been in existence since 1919 I would expect a great product, or one that is different from all the rest due to your almost 100 years. The 5 senses review: nnSight: 8-the main saving grace. It is really cool, quaint, and charming. This is where the history helps. Smell: 6-just like other coffee places it is always nice to walk in and get nailed with the aroma of the brewed and ground beans. Taste: 6- UPDATED! Much better coffee of the day. So lesson learned. Get a "coffee of the day" at your own risk. Sound: 3-remember a low number is good. Nice and relaxed with the just the sounds of a working coffee shop. No over powering shitty music, thankfully! Touch: 2-only because you aren't really using your hands for anything. I did get a biscotti there which was very good. So since I used my hands I need to add some rating.

Location of the restaurant was in a run down (kind of Old Pittsburgh style) and parallel parking was a must, be aware that you may have to park far and walk to the restaurant if you're not able to get front door service. Inside I didn't expect much, tablecloths were vinyl and chairs with uneven stands. All I care about was the authenticity of the food & cost for what it's worth. I started my meal with an appetizer of Goi Cuon with shrimp. I was highly disappointing when disecting what was in it. There was 1 shrimp cut in half lengthwise, mainly bun (rice noodle) for fillers along with a few strands of beansprouts & lettuce to make it look presentable. I quickly devoured the tiny appetizer in 2 bites. My main entree was Pho Ha Noi. It took forever for the food to arrive, it was a big bowl. Until I stirred it around to find out it was mainly broth and green onions. The broth was flavorless, actually it didn't have any flavor; so I had to add hoisin sause to give it a little of whatever to go along with the sliced pork. I was confused about the noodle itself, Pho is usually served with flat vermicelli noodle; but this Pho Ha Noi was served with round vermicelli noodles usually for Bun Bo entree. I asked the old man with the amputated arm, why it was served with bun (round rice noodle) instead of pho (flat rice noodle) noodles, he laughed and insisted it was pho (flat rice noodle). Ok I may be young but I wasnt born yesterday, I think I know my pho noodle and sorry it wasn't. Next visit to the 'burgh, I think I'll try Pho Minh & see how their PHO compares to Tram's Kitchen. While the space and service warrant a 4. 5 star rating, one can summarize most dishes as high quality yet forgettable rip-offs. Soba's seasonality is something that makes it stand out, and I appreciate the sourcing of the ingredients. Speaking of the ingredients, everything is a rather high quality, which is to be expected at the price point. My scallops were deliciously meaty and sugar sweet, and my vegetarian dining companion's vegetables all tasted quite fresh. The rhubarb in my desert had a perfectly tangy, subtly sweet flavor. Proteins and veggies stand out. But the dishes, as a whole, don't warrant the price point. Soba tries to communicate subtlety in flavoring of its food, and it carries this principle of subtlety a bit too far. For example, the broth in my entree tasted only vaguely of the soy and ginger promised, and my friend's red curry exhibited anemic spicing. Flaws in execution are similarly prevalent; my noodles and my friend's rice were too mushy. To that end, Soba fails. The meal was fairly enjoyable, and perhaps I went on an off night, but my sticker shock for good but not great food has yet to subside.

An eclectic playlist fills the compact room at a volume just above the din of conversation. Booths and tables line the perimeter, enclosing the space in an intimate setting. Yet each finds their own niche, and the arrangement works. The beer list showcases a wider selection than anticipated, with options spanning mainstream and craft brews. Shots flow freely, so pace oneself to avoid an unhappy morning.The pub grub proves surprisingly decent for the cost - burgers and appetizers hit the spot after rounds. The lack of cell service or wifi keeps interactions focused solely on in-person dialogue. Time passes imperceptibly as the evening progresses and lines between regulars and newcomers blur with the sharing of stories and laughs. Beyond its rough-hewn shell, an authentic spirit draws one back to this hole-in-the-wall. It may lack polish but gains character in turn.

I have had the pleasure of dining at Papa J's on two occasions, and my experiences were somewhat mixed. During my initial visit, I was delighted by the exceptional service provided. The staff members were friendly, attentive, and swift in taking our orders. Not only were we promptly seated, but our food also arrived promptly. Personally, I opted for their renowned signature pizza, which turned out to be a delectable masterpiece. The crust was thin and crispy, while the toppings were abundant and bursting with flavor. The service was noticeably slower, and it took quite some time for someone to acknowledge our presence. Once we finally received our menus, there was a considerable wait before our order was taken. The wait for our food felt agonizingly long, and when it finally graced our table, it was disappointingly lukewarm. The quality of the pizza was a far cry from my previous encounter. The crust turned out to be doughy this time, and the toppings appeared to be scant.The inconsistency between my two visits is puzzling to say the least. Perhaps it was simply an anomaly, as I firmly believe they possess the potential to deliver both outstanding cuisine and service. I will remain optimistic and keep my fingers crossed for a more satisfying encounter on my next visit.

It was disappointing to encounter such lack of knowledge and professionalism.When our food finally arrived, we were met with a range of experiences. My girlfriend's steak, cooked medium-rare as requested, was tender and flavorful. She enjoyed every bite, her face lighting up with each mouthful. However, I opted for the seafood pasta, and it was underwhelming to say the least. The dish lacked seasoning and the seafood tasted slightly off, leaving me questioning its freshness. It was a stark contrast to the delightful steak my girlfriend had chosen.As the evening progressed, we couldn't help but notice the noise level steadily increasing. The once cozy atmosphere became inundated with loud conversations and clattering dishes, making it difficult to engage in meaningful conversation. It was a shame that the restaurant's ambiance lost its charm due to the noise.To their credit, the dessert selection was impressive.

The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with upbeat musci playing and several tables full of customers enjoying their meals. We were quickly seated by our friendly waitress and givAen menus to look over. There was a variety of apptizers, burgers, sandwiches and entree options to choose from. I decided on the chickem tenders and fries, which were cooked to perfection. The chicken was crispy on the outside and jlicy on the inside. My parents and I were excited to try it out, particularly after my dad's glowing recommendation. The restaurant had a cozy atmosphere, with dim lighting and comfortable seating. The menu offered a variety of options, including traditional American fare and some unique twists on classic dishes. We ordeed a few appetizers to start, including the buffalo wings and the queso fundido. The wings were crispy and flavorful, with a nice balance of sipcy and tangy sauce. The queso fundido was a highlight, with a rich, creamy cheese sauce and generous portions of chorizo and poultry. I asked the cashier at Hatoya for an authentic Japanese restaurant, she gave me Musashi. When I arrived at Musashi, I was immediately impressed by the traditional Japanese interior decorated with paper lanterns and bamboo details. A host showed me to a small table where I was given an English menu to browse as well as hot green tea. There was a wide selection of dishes including soups, rice dishes, noodles and teriyaki options. I decided to start with the miso soup and edamame to begin. Both were light, fresh and flavorful. For my main dish, I chose the beef sukiyaki which came bubbling in the iron pot right to my table. I enjoyed dipping thinly sliced beef and vegetables into the savory broth. The meal was very hearty and satisfying. After I finished, the waitress brought me a sample of seasonal fruit for dessert. It was the perfect way to end such a filling meal. The service throughout my dinner was attentive yet not overbearing. As I left well fed, I saw many families and groups of friends enjoying their meals. It was clear Musashi has built a loyal local customer base. I would highly recommend this gem for anyone looking for authentic and well prepared Japanese cuisine. The generous portions and reasonable prices also make Musashi a very good value. I'm thankful to the Hatoya cashier for the dining recommendation and am sure to return to Musashi again soon during my next visit to the city.

The restaurant is very intimate, and if I remember correctly, it only has twelve tables. I made reservations a few weeks in advance just because my schedule is annoyingly tight right now. Turns out I was lucky as I have heard it can be hard to get if you wait until the last minute. The service was essentially perfect, they were attentive and knowledgeable without being intrusive. The pricing wasn't excessive in my opinion and was in line with what I would expect to pay for a very nice dinner out. If I was going to compare it another restaurant in town it would be Bon Terra, but the intimate setting makes for a different experience here. I won't go on and on about the food and will just say that we both loved it. Everything we ordered was better than we expected it to be. I had the foie gras, the osso bucco, and the re-imagined coconut cream pie. I would highly recommend this place to my friends and family or anyone looking for a nice place to take a date. I will definitely be back soon.

Had a mid-week lunch here recently with a client at his request, and let me tell you, it was an experience I won't soon forget. The restaurant was trendy and had a cool vibe, but that's where the positives ended. As soon as we walked in, it took forever for someone to acknowledge us. I swear, we could have built a house with the amount of time we spent waiting at the entrance. Finally, after what seemed like an eternity, a grouchy hostess led us to a cramped table in the corner. Did I mention how uncomfortable the chairs were? I felt like I was sitting on a pile of rocks. The menu looked promising, with a variety of options to choose from, but unfortunately, the food didn't live up to the hype. We ordered the chef's special, expecting a burst of flavors, but it fell flat. The presentation was lackluster, and the taste was underwhelming, to say the least. The "special" felt more like a microwave meal that someone hastily threw together. It was a disappointment. To make matters worse, the service was abysmal. Our waitress seemed disinterested and barely checked on us throughout the entire meal. We had to flag her down multiple times just to get water refills. After 10 min., the waitress came over and asked about drinks. After another 10 min., she brought our drinks and asked what we wanted to order. The lack of attentiveness was shocking. Now, let's talk about the prices. This is where it gets really outrageous. The menu boasted high-end dishes, but the quality didn't match up. I mean, seriously, for the prices they were charging, I expected to be blown away. Instead, I left feeling ripped off. This is a crime against humanity, charging top dollars for subpar food and service. On the bright side, the ambiance was decent. The dim lighting and soft music created a cozy and intimate atmosphere, which helped somewhat in salvaging the overall experience. However, let's be real here, the ambiance alone can't save a sinking ship.

During my stay, I had the opportunity to try various Chinese restaurants in the area. One of them was China One, located in the Charleston at Desert Foothills Albertson's Shopping Center. I had walked by the restaurant several times before deciding to give it a try.The interior of the restaurant was typical of a take-out style Chinese restaurant, with a few tables and a large menu board on the wall. The menu options were similar to those of other Chinese restaurants I had tried in Las Vegas.I ordered the lunch special, which included noodles with duck sauce, egg drop soup, pepper steak, fried rice, and chow mien noodles. The food was decent, but nothing exceptional. My only complaint was that the plate was filled mostly with chow mien noodles, which I consider to be filler.The employees were friendly and attentive, greeting me as soon as I walked in and checking up on me to ensure that the food was satisfactory. However, it was the last impression that left a positive mark on my experience at China One.As I was about to leave, the nice woman who worked there refilled my large cup of soda, allowing me to take it with me and drink it later. This small gesture left a lasting impression and influenced my decision to give China One a three-star rating.Overall, China One was a decent Chinese restaurant, but it didn't stand out from others in the area. The food was average, but the service was good, and the last impression was positive.

Wow, they were not kidding about this place being small! I think my living room is bigger. In total, there were only 9 groups in the entire place and they were at capacity and we were less than a foot away from the group dining next to us (who were rather uppity and kept looking at us as if we were intruding on their dining experience by sitting near them) so I understand why they require reservations. I would say the average age of the people dining was around 50-60+. I felt a little young being there, but I wasn't treated that way by the staff, it was more from the patrons, who I think were a little full of themselves (most had that 'I'm SO important' vibe going on. ) nnI did not get the pretentious air at all from the staff that I was expecting while I was at the restaurant, but I did while making the reservation (don't contact them online or leave a message, they don't call you back and the people on the phone aren't very pleasant -they were even snippy when we called to confirm the reservation). I had the shrimp with the cole slaw and corn bread for an appetizer. While it sounds like an odd mix, I was actually sad when I finished it. I don't even like cole slaw and I was tempted to start licking my plate just to get the last parts that I couldn't pick up with my fork. For my main course I had the chicken with spinach and mashed potatoes. Yum. Yum. Yum. Everything had so much flavor and tasted fresh. All of us at the table ordered something different and every serving was met with mmm's to near moaning so I think my entire party was pleased with their meal. The food is excellent and the portions are large (the mussels appetizer could be a meal) so you aren't left feeling hungry and bitter and when the $$$ check shows up. We never felt rushed and the evening was very relaxing and pleasant. We even got to meet the chef/owner Bruce, who is very friendly, which was an added plus.

I came here a few months ago and had a great meal, but my recent visit was a huge disappointment. The restaurant seemed understaffed and disorganized. We waited almost 40 minutes to even place our order and the server seemed frazzled. Our food took over an hour to arrive and it was lukewarm at best when it did. The pad thai used to be so flavorful but it now tastes bland and soggy. The portions are much smaller than before too. Even the decor seems tired and outdated now. The chaotic atmosphere made it hard to relax and enjoy our meal. I asked our server what happened but she didn't have any answers. My friend said she overheard the manager yelling in the kitchen, so maybe there is trouble behind the scenes. At this rate they will soon lose regular customers like me. If things don't improve soon, I worry this place may not be around much longer. It's a shame to see a once great restaurant decline in quality so quickly. Has there been a change in ownership or chef? I hope they can turn things around before it's too late to save this place. Next time I may just go elsewhere to avoid the disappointment and poor service.

Don't be confused this place consists of two establishments and one kitchen. One is a bar with waiters and liquor, the other is a fast food style place. I chose the latter. Walk in and you will find a menu board with a few specials printed out hanging off of it, no frills, no credit cards, all local flavor. I went with the Titanic special $10. 75 Which included a "monster" fish sandwich, and two sides, I chose fries and onion rings. Everything is made to order, which means crispy fries, rings and a crust on hot flakey fish. The fish here is the real thing not some unnatural square, a large fillet of mild white fish with a great breading on a simple bun. The condiments are on the table and up to you, tartar sauce, hot sauce, a spicy "famous" vinegar and ketchup. It was a big sandwich but not titanic maybe just queen marry. Bottom line if you want some fried food and have cash give this a try.

The decor is a jumble of mismatched furniture, worn tablecloths, and faded paintings clinging desperately to the walls. The lack of professional competence of the staff is truly astonishing. They saunter around with a look of indifference, barely acknowledging your presence, let alone providing attentive service. If you manage to catch their attention, don't expect them to know anything about the menu. When asked about the ingredients or the preparation method, they shrug their shoulders and give vague answers. The menu lists a variety of Italian classics, but what arrives at your table is a far cry from authenticity. It is obvious that they have little understanding of Italian cuisine. Now let's talk about the food itself, or rather, the culinary disaster that it is. The pasta is overcooked and mushy, drowning in a watery, tasteless sauce that is a blasphemy. The pizzas are pathetic, with a thin, tasteless crust and toppings that lack both freshness and flavor. If you have any food allergies or dietary restrictions, I implore you to avoid this place. They not only ignore your requests, but they also have no regard for basic hygiene. I witnessed a waiter handling food with his bare hands, wiping them on his dirty apron, and then touching utensils without washing his hands or putting on gloves. It is disgusting and utterly unsanitary. It is a true testament to their audacity that they charge such high prices for a dining experience that can best be described as a comedy of errors. The prices are exorbitant for the quality of food and service you receive.

This was my first time at Soba after spending many visits at Umi. I would argue that Umi is the better sibling with excellent sushi options (with a hefty price tag) but Soba is a bit more approachable to the person who is less familiar with or doesn't want sushi. In all, it's a good place for a date with a desire for reasonable and modern Asian fusion. Ambience: nTrendy, dimly lit and very clean decor. It suits the cuisine and is well set for small groups or a date. Not too loud but certainly not dead either. I loved the bar area- has a mix of bar and casual couch/lovechair seating that's well suited for a date or small group. Based on the clientele and set up, I'd lean towards trendy attire if you come here- not a casual place by any means. Food: nThai corn chowder- so good and very rich. I would return just for that dish. For an entree, I had the seared rare tuna. They definitely didn't skimp on my portion of tuna and cooked it well. Granted tuna is a bit bland, I was hoping for more seasoning and oomph from the Korean barbecue sauce. The ginger fried rice made up for any disappointment I had with the tuna. For dessert, the chocolate pretzel stack was fantastic- perfect mix of chocolate, sweet caramel and the salty wonton chip. Drinks: nThe old fashioned was well-executed. Went back for a second. Can't speak for any of their other cocktails.

The Herb O'Vores Tacos are one of the most delicious things I have ever had. I've had them twice in State College and once here. I was tempted to try something new on the menu but our waitress said you can never go wrong with the tofu tacos and she is right. I didn't regret it one bit. I can always try making my own thai burrito or spicy buffalo wrap at home. You get three tacos filled with fried cubes of tofu which have been tossed in a light sweet General Tso's type sauce topped with bean sprouts, a green salsa with avocado and served with lime wedges, rice, and black beans. So delicious and it all came out of the kitchen pretty quickly. I love reading their menu. The Mex-Asian dishes all sound awesome. If I lived in Pittsburgh, I would come often to try everything. They also have Daiya cheese and vegan cheesecake always on their menu. How sweet is that? My only complaint is that we went just after 5 and it was so dark in the restaurant I could hardly see the menu.

Awesome atmosphere, good food, good service. My evaluation: nnFacility: Good- Really cool place, apparently the bar and most of the accoutrements were shipped in from Ireland. Relaxing atmosphere, great place to kick back and enjoy a meal. The stools we sat in were not the most comfortable, but nothing to really complain about. Food: Excellent - The food here is great. The menu selection is not too vast, but it's decent. I had the Lamb Roast Pie which was phenomenal. It had a goat cheese and potato bake on top, and I was pretty happy. My wife, who is picky, got the Hot and Smoky burger, which was great as well. The fries were ridiculously crispy, and just had that beautiful crunch to them. We had Creme Bru00fblu00e9e for dessert, which I wasn't crazy about. It was cold on the bottom, and wasn't completely "burnt" on the top. Service: Good - The waitress was attentive and helpful, but didn't get in the way. Food came out in reasonable amount of time, and everything came out as ordered. Overall we had a good time, good food, and a fun night. I give Ri Ra a thumbs up!

5 stars for food. I won't reminisce over the first visit as it was quite some time ago, but hubs and I strolled in there to grab a quick bite before heading to a show in Concord. Our server Colleen was fantastic - she seriously should work at Disneyland because that woman is so happy. She was also incredibly friendly, professional and efficient, making sure that we were in and out of there for our show with plenty of time to spare. Beyond the tasty (I presume freshly baked bread), I ordered the cavatelli primavera - an large portion of finely cooked cavatelli pasta loaded with tons of veggies in a light marinara sauce. The pasta was just what I was looking for and the veggies were fresh - my complaint? The sauce was quite bland. Perhaps more crushed red pepper? More garlic? More BAM? Regardless, I had leftover to eat for lunch for another day and for the price, $14. 95, it was a ton of food. One an alternate note, make sure you note the price of the specials if you're interested in them.. . hubs and I were both surprised that his chicken & pasta dish was $22. It was roughly the same portion and similar ingredients to my dish and seemed as if the chicken breast cost added $7 to the price. Strange. Regardless, next time I'm in the University area I definitely want to try their tiramisu - I hear it's phenomenal!

They started out easy to work with, but that was short-lived. Scheduling apartment viewing was simple, and the people who showed me the units were relatively friendly. The issue came when I actually went to sign a lease. I was told on the phone and in person by the person showing me apartments that I would not need a cosigner, but as soon as I showed up for my lease application appointment, they told me I would need a cosigner. I scrambled to contact my mom, who was willing to cosign, but they said they needed BOTH parents to co-sign, and they wanted me to sign an agreement saying I would forfeit the $1000 deposit I had to pay upfront if I did not return all of my cosigners' documents within 7 days. This was an issue because 1 of my parents was out of town for the week. I tried compromising with them and seeing if they could change the agreement to give me an extra few days to get the cosigner paperwork in, or to see if I could just have my mother (who was more than financially stable) be the sole cosigner. They were unwilling to compromise at all, and I left after about a half hour of unproductive back-and-forth discussion. I could have gone back a week later, when both parents were in town, as the unit was still available, but I figured any place that difficult to work with when I was trying to give them money would be even more frustrating once I was contacting them for things like maintenance requests. I wouldn't say "never ever rent from them", but I would definitely be aware of how rude / difficult they can be.

Walking into the cozy establishment, I was greeted by warm lighting and a welcoming ambiance. The staff was friendly and attentive, making me feel right at home. It had been a struggle to find a budget-friendly restaurant that didn't compromise on quality, but this hidden gem exceeded my expectations. The menu offered a wide variety of dishes, from classic favorites to unique specials. I started with the crispy calamari, which was perfectly cooked and accompanied by a tangy dipping sauce. For my entrée, I chose the grilled salmon, which was accompanied by a medley of roasted vegetables. The salmon was moist and flavorful, and the vegetables were cooked to perfection. One of the highlights of this restaurant was the attention to detail in the presentation. Each plate was a work of art, with vibrant colors and elegant arrangements. The portions were generous, and I left the restaurant feeling satisfied. It was clear that the chef took great pride in his creations. As I savored each bite, I couldn't help but admire the harmonious blend of flavors and textures. The ingredients were fresh and of the highest quality, which elevated the overall dining experience. To complement the meal, the restaurant offered an impressive selection of wines and craft beers. Despite the affordable prices, there was no compromise on quality or taste. I opted for a rich red wine, which enhanced the flavors of the dish. The knowledgeable staff was happy to recommend pairings that enhanced the flavors of the dishes. Dessert was a delightful conclusion to the meal. I indulged in a rich chocolate lava cake, which oozed with a molten center. The balance of sweetness was perfect, and the dessert left a lasting impression.

Newly relocated to Pittsburgh's east end from Miami, I wasn't sure where to turn for my hair. Luckily, I stumbled upon a hidden gem in the neighborhood: Salon Elegance. From the moment I walked through the door, I was greeted with warmth and professionalism. The sleek and modern interior design immediately caught my eye, creating a sophisticated ambiance.The staff at Salon Elegance truly exceeded my expectations. The hairstylists were highly skilled and knowledgeable, taking the time to listen to my hair concerns and desired style. They offered valuable suggestions and worked with me to create a look that suited my personality and lifestyle perfectly. It was evident that they were passionate about their craft and dedicated to providing exceptional service.During my appointment, I noticed that the salon used high-quality products, which contributed to the overall experience. The shampoo and conditioning treatment left my hair feeling revitalized and nourished. The hairstylist's attention to detail was commendable, as they carefully crafted each strand to achieve the desired outcome.The salon's commitment to customer satisfaction was evident in every aspect of my visit. The staff provided complimentary beverages, ensuring that clients were comfortable throughout their stay. The salon's cleanliness was impeccable, and the equipment appeared to be well-maintained. It was clear that Salon Elegance prioritized a hygienic and pleasant environment for their clients.What impressed me the most was the affordable pricing at Salon Elegance. Rich, dark colors. Low lights. Supple leather furniture. Exquisit bar. Attentive staff. The waft of smooth smoke. Not what I expected when a few friends suggest I meet them at Cutters. I had no idea what it was - it sounded like a really sad emo club. Pleasantly surprised was I! If you have been looking for that classy place to relax, have a drink and perhaps a cigar and a nice chat with friends on furniture that looks like it was taken from Bogart's conservatory, this is the place. The hours are very accomodating to the atmosphere - hours seem to fly by in that place, and before we all knew it, it was 1 am. As some other people previously mentioned, this place does have a very limited selection; a few cohibas, some Monte Cristos, and your usual Romeo et Julietas, but that's about it. nAlso, the mark up is pretty ridiculous, about 2x-3x times what you'd pay in a cigar store or more if you're used to a J. R. They do, however, have a very good wine/bourbon/whisky/scotch selection. I was very happy with their port selection, and I highly recommend the tawny with the Monte Cristo White. Will be back, though I'll probably just foot the fee and bring my own selection.

The store has typically had the supplies that I need from cake and cupcake baking and icing to scrap booking supplies. This location is pretty average compared to other Michaels - it's exactly what you would expect when going to this store. It's not a large store, but it's not a small store -- just average. I do enjoy using the Michael's coupons when shopping. I definitely save a lot of money! Instead of toting around the paper versions, I actually have the iPhone app that has coupons available to use from the app. My only complaint is that sometimes it takes a while to check out at this location. I don't normally have a problem - usually only one or two people ahead of me - but sometimes it can be much slower. Today, for example, there were only two customers ahead of me, but one of them was having issues with a coupon. The line began to get longer and longer, and though a couple associates were lingering up front, they kept calling for someone else. From personal experience of being a manger in a retail store, do not linger or let your associates linger near the cashiers without jumping on register. Whatever the reason may be that you are not helping customers, it still appears rude and make everyone more impatient.. ..

I must say, TGIF's is one of my favorite places to unwind after a long week. The atmosphere is always lively, and boy did we definitely have some fun there last Friday. As soon as I walked in, I was greeted by friendly staff who showed me to a cozy booth. The interior is adorned with vibrant colors and funky decor, giving the place a funky and upbeat vibe. The music playing in the background was just the right volume - not too loud that you couldn't carry a conversation, but not too soft to make it dull.Now, let's talk about the food because that's what keeps me coming back for more. The menu is extensive, with a wide variety of options to choose from. My go-to appetizer is their pretzels with craft beer cheese dipping sauce. The pretzels are warm and soft, perfectly baked, and the cheese sauce has just the right amount of tanginess to complement the pretzel. It's pure heaven in every bite.When it comes to drinks, TGIF's definitely knows their stuff. Their bartenders are skilled mixologists who whip up some of the best cocktails in town. I recommend trying their signature Long Island Iced Tea - it packs a punch and is incredibly refreshing. The drinks were not watered down, I could taste the alcohol, and we got our money's worth!One thing I have to mention is the exceptional service. The waitstaff was attentive and made sure we had everything we needed throughout the evening. Our glasses were never empty, and they made great recommendations for both food and drinks. The service really enhanced our overall dining experience.Now, I do have to mention a little hiccup we encountered. Unfortunately, there was a small stain on my coat caused by a spill at the table next to us. I brought it to the attention of our server, and although they were apologetic, they didn't offer any assistance in removing or addressing the stain. I was a bit disappointed because I expected better customer service in such situations.

I recently stayed at the Courtyard by Marriott in downtown San Francisco for a conference. The location was fantastic, just a short walk from the convention center and surrounded by plenty of restaurants and shops. The staff was friendly and helpful, especially the girl at the front desk who checked me in. She was very welcoming and gave me a great recommendation for a nearby restaurant.The room was clean and comfortable, with a nice king-sized bed and a separate living area with a sofa and desk. The bathroom was a bit small, but it had all the amenities I needed, including a large walk-in shower.One of the best things about this hotel was the free Wi-Fi, which was fast and reliable throughout my stay. I was also impressed by the modern decor and the nice touches, such as the flat-screen TV and the Keurig coffee machine in the room.However, there were a few things that didn't quite meet my expectations. For one, the hotel's fitness center was a bit disappointing. It was small and lacked some of the equipment I've come to expect from a hotel gym. Additionally, the breakfast buffet was a bit pricey and didn't offer as many options as I've seen at other Courtyard hotels.Despite these minor issues, I would still recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a convenient and comfortable stay in downtown San Francisco. The location and the staff make it a great choice, and I would definitely stay here again in the future.

I will continue the review But I was pleasantly surprised! The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful, and the food was delicious. this is one of my favorite venues to see a live show anywhere! The inside has multiple levels and there is not a bad place anywhere - standing room only unless you get there early enough to grab one of the few bar tables and stools. The bar is large and can handle many people wanting drinks at one time. You get the feeling that you are on top of the bands when they are playing - a great intimate experience and makes you feel like they are playing at your house. Tip the bartenders well and they remember your drink orders, so by the time I bellied up about the 3rd or 4th time - my drinks were placed in front of me in what seemed like 10 seconds or less! The free self serve water next to the bar is a nice touch too. The bathrooms are large and nicely located. From Australia to Singapore and London to NYC, the place can not be beat. Settle in to any of the leather nailhead wingback chairs and prepare to be pampered. The staff is awesome. Alicia and Sam are the 2 longterm veterans and they will treat you right. The drink prices are a bit to the high side, but you will never suffer the indignity of an empty glass, or the lack of a good story if either of them are there. The cigar selection is reasonable; prices also a bit to the high side, but you are paying for a rare privilege of having a wonderful venue to chill out, enjoy a smoke, and NOT have a sports bar feel to the place. The back room has a full size pool table (no charge! ) where it is not uncommon to see an executive of one of the banks in town playing the role of 'shark'. The middle room feels like a library at a regally appointed home with a fireplace and more comfortable chairs and tables. Among my favorite haunts. Grab your favorite smoke, a liberally poured cocktail and let the days stress depart in the blue smoke of your cigar.

The cover is usually pretty cheap, the beer is REALLY cheap, the sound system is OMG LOUD! and the place sure has a lot of character. It's the kind of place native Charlotteans think of fondly because they snuck in to see Black Flag when they were 15 back in 1983. Or had their first sexual andor alcohol experience in the parking lot. Or some such other fond teen memory that makes them overlook the place's serious shortcomings. For those of us who are Charlotte transplants? It's.. . something. Let me say this: the bathrooms here are (by FAR) the nastiest in Charlotte. And I'm a GUY. I can't imagine the poor ladies having to hover over the toilets there, afraid of the as-yet-undocumented pathogens lurking on the seat. Seriously folks, the bathrooms here are BEYOND NASTY! And points off for cutting out indoor smoking. They used to not care about the NC statewide ban on indoor smoking ("yeah, like the cops ever come HERE", the bartender told me), but a few months ago they decided to ban it.. . thus removing the one thing I really liked about it. Don't get me wrong folks. If you go there with good friends to hear a good band you'll have a fun time. It's just that now that I'm 41 years old I'm a bit less tolerant of subpar facilities than I used to be,

My son and I were driving back from the Wisconsin Dells and decided to pull off for lunch and we found Fat Jacks on my GPS. The outside of the place isn't very impressive, but some of the best bbq places I've ever been to have been dumps. The inside is much nicer, decorated with local Wisconsin artifacts and pictures. My favorite was the old beer bottle collection by the entrance. Anyway, we got sat and our waitress came over right away.. .. super friendly and super nice lady. We asked for a recommendation and she basically went over the whole menu and said everything was great, and after eating there, I believe her. I ordered the pulled pork lunch and my son got the fish fry. When she brought over the plates, I knew we were in trouble.. . there was sooo much food! My son's fish was very good, not greasy but light and flaky. My pork was excellent. The waitress asked if we wanted a hotter bbq sauce, I love spicy, so she brought it. Excellent! Smokey, spicy flavor. The sauces on the table were really good too. If you are looking for some good, casual, non-pretentious BBQ, Fat Jack's is the place for you! Don't let the outside fool you, the inside is clean and the food is excellent and they give you a ton of it!

Located in the heart of the city, Soba offers an intimate and cozy atmosphere, perfect for a night out with friends or a romantic evening. The decor is sleek and modern, with a focus on clean lines and natural materials. The menu is diverse and exciting, offering a range of dishes that blend traditional Japanese flavors with modern twists and ingredients.The service is exceptional, with friendly and attentive staff who are happy to guide you through the menu and offer recommendations. We came for dinner on a weekday evening, and it was not very busy. The dining room is spacious and clean, with booths along the walls and tables in the middle. The service was attentive without being intrusive. The appetizers we had were egg rolls and fried wontons, which were average, not bad, but nothing special. The main dishes were kung pao chicken, sweet and sour pork, and broccoli with garlic sauce. The flavors were fairly bland, and the sauces tasted heavily of cornstarch. The portions were large, but the food seemed to lack depth of flavor. The meats and vegetables were also a bit overcooked. We also had white rice, which was soft and bland. For dessert we shared a fried banana, which was adequate but boring. All in all, it was a decent meal, but we would not be rushing back. There are better Chinese restaurants closer to home that we enjoy more. This place would do in a pinch, but I would not go out of my way to eat here when there are better, more authentic Chinese restaurants to be found.
