My wife got a small greenhouse salad with Jalapeno ranch dressing to start off with which she enjoyed and the lobster & shrimp enchiladas as her main entree. I ordered the New York Strip with mashed potatoes and it came with green bean as well. My strip was cooked perfectly and has a decent taste. Longhorn has a much, much better quality of steak though. The green beans were pretty good and my mashed potatoes very bland and pretty average. The kitchen sounded like an live episode of Hell's Kitchen. The waiters were repeatedly asking for orders at least 5 to 6 times. The kitchen was backed up the whole time we were there. On a different note, our waitress Susan was very good. Come here for drinks and the bar food. Skip everything else.

When the restraints locked down over us, we realized we were in for a longer experience than expected. All roundabout us others were zipping along the tracks while we remained stationary. After several minutes, an employee finally approached and informed us there was an issue that needed resolving. It took the technicians close to an hour to determine the problem and get us moving again. Para that time, the ride had been shut down for maintenance. My wife was uncomfortable the entire time we waited immobilized on the ride. I considered bad there was nothing I could do to help the situation. The staff tried their best to keep us updated on progress but it was a frustrating delay. Finally, with a loud jerk we were released and able to continues the rest of the ride. When we finished, we were given tickets to come back for a libre rerun. While the technical difficulty was out of your control, the lengthy wait without better communication was dissatisfying. In the future, more updates during long Resolution times would be thanked.

I know a fair amount about hair, and could have done it myself, but I love the ritual of going to a salon and having 'a girl. The service sounds attentive but could improve in some areas like drink refills. I absolutely love this place. It's a super thrift store if you will. No matter when I come here, I always find something. It quite the experience. I always make sure it's a day when I am off of work because I can literally spend hours here just looking. It's a good thing that I do this, you can't just show up here and think that you will be able to gran an item and then leave. Like a fellow reviewer said, there are not fitting rooms here, so be prepared to walk into someone trying on a potential great new garment for them self in the middle of an aisle. Sometimes you just can't avoid this, I blame the fact that they have mirrors set up throughout stores. They have everything you can seem to desire here. Clothing to electronics, furniture to bedding, books to movies. EVERYTHING is under this roof. nn*Cash only, ATM on premise.

From the outside the place looks like a bomb shelter with dresses in the window. The show room is upstairs, but you would never know it from the drab, basement-like entrance. As I walked up the stairs I notices ZERO customers in the store, however; two employees were working on the sales floor. I stood there like a jerk for a bit while both employees (one was the owner) kept to themselves. The owner did not respond to me for, at least, 10 minutes even though the store was empty and another employee was just walking around "dusting" (the store smalls like the inside of a mascot costume). When the owner, finally, saw me she made a little annoying noise like "What the hell are YOU doing here!! ". She walked over slowly, like a zombie looking for fresh brains and giving a crap why I was there. She asked me to follow her as she took me downstairs to an absolutely empty storeroom (by that I mean: what was she doing that was was so important that she couldn't wait on a customer) and took her sweet-ass time to get the dress which, by the way, was a second alteration. You see, they screwed up the first time they altered the dress (even after my wife tried it on there and markings or whatever were made! ). So everyone is entitled to a mistake even a business that claims perfection; it's important to give them a chance to redeem themselves. But, to my surprise, she handed me a bill for the second alteration!! ! ! ! ! Are you kidding me?! ! ! I argued a bit, but then gave in; what was I supposed to do? We were leaving to go 200 miles away the next day for the wedding. So I paid. Do not go here ladies! Oh, if you think I'm exaggerating, feel free to Google this company and read the many reviews that make mine look like a compliment. If you have ever needed a dress for a wedding or YOUR wedding, these reviews will scare you!

Mert's is awesome! I was craving some good grub after a long day and decided to check this place out. Walked in and the vibe was real chill. We got seated right away even though it was kinda busy. The menu had all sorts of options so it was tough to choose! Ended up getting the chicken shawarma which hit the spot perfectly. It was tasty with all the flavors mingling together. The pita was fresh and fluffy too. My friend tried the kofta kebabs and they looked juicy and tasty. We grabbed some hummus for dipping too which was creamy and not too tangy. The service was quick even with a full restaurant. Our server was nice and helped us pick out some good Turkish beers to try. The baklava for dessert looked too good to pass up. It was sweet without being overly rich. Overall everything was reasonably priced for the quality. I'd definitely come back to try more dishes for sure. The atmosphere and food made for a very enjoyable meal. Thanks Mert's for the awesome grub!

After getting stuck in Charlotte due to weather in Chicago, we were able to book this hotel for our unexpected stay. As a nursing mother I was hoping for a fridge in my room, however a pageant taking place at the hotel meant all were taken. The staff were nice enough to let me keep some things in the employee fridge which I really appreciated. The beds are very comfortable so you can get a good night's sleep. The food at the main restaurant/bar was decent with very large portions. In typical southern style, it was covered in sauce(s) but good enough. The not so good: The main picture posted on Yelp (and on SPG. com) leads you to believe the hotel is nicer than it actually is. The hotel is very average and does not appear to have been significantly updated in the last 10-15 years (except for the beds which were quite nice). The website advertising a 24-hour on-demand shuttle, however the on-demand part is only when being picked up from the airport not to be dropped off (which would have been helpful for them to mention at check-in). There were 3-5 of us that were ready to go at 5: 45am (because our flight departed at 6: 50am) but were told that we had to wait until 6am because it only leaves on the half hour. They also would not let us ride with an earlier van that carried crew members and informed us that a taxi would take 15-20 minutes to call. Overall, seemed frustrating as to why they could not have a van make a trip to the airport when there are 5 people waiting to go. I'm not sure if this is an SPG systematic problem or not, but the hotel charged me for internet on my bill and I had to ask to have it taken off (since I'm a platinum member). This has happened at several hotels, and I feel they are trying to pass through charges and hoping that guests don't notice.

A bit off the beaten path, but an easy bus ride from my Oakland hotel (and bus originates from Downtown, so should be easy ride from there, too). Ds did not disappoint: creative craft beer list of 25+ taps, plus hundreds of bottles in the Beer Cave that you can have onsite or take to-go, and some of the best dogs I've ever had. Was there on a Friday, so got the Scorpion (cheddar jalapeno kielbasi) & fries deal for $5. 50--excellent. Also tried the very good Ds Brat (cheesy bratwurst) & fries (same price), and they do a terrific version of the Chicago Dog. There are also 20+ toppings options if you want to DIY. Nice, friendly service from the guys behind the bar/in the kitchen made this a fine time. Next time I'm in PGH, Ds will be at the top of my list to visit. Can't wait to try their other dogs and whatever they have on tap (or in the Cave). P. S. There is also sit-down service in a room between the bar and Cave that seemed more family-friendly. I noticed several tables had pizzas and burgers, so I assume those are decent, too.

We live on Lake Wylie so it is a nice boat ride. The reviews I read about the cleanliness is right on. Tonight was the worst in service and food. The kid that waited on us got our order incorrect. My fish and chips came without the chips. I had ordered slaw as an extra side. The slaw came and was awful. I was afraid to eat a lot of it. My fries came after we were pretty much through eating. They tasted like they had been cooked in burnt grease. Then he charged me for them. We always leave a great tip because we know how hard it is to be a server but tonight my husband left a tip saying bad service ; bad tip. This place needs renovation and cleaned up desperately. Some of the best flounder I have ever eaten used to come from here. I am sad to see it go down hill. We also had a family near us that couldn't control their kids and I think they thought we were at a McDonalds Play land. Tonight was a miserable time here. We will probably come back home to eat from now on when going on a boat ride.

Simple layout, screens at every turn updating flight status, and overall a clean facility. I had no problems when checking in for a flight. TSA staff were extremely gentle and handled me with care, I walked out of there with no pain or discomfort. But in all seriousness, security check was your typical long delay, but its to be expected for an international airport. Once I got past security, I was able to find my gate with no problem. The Enterprise shuttle ran every five to ten minutes, which is very convenient when in a hurry. Although i didn't use the pick up or drop off lanes, they seemed to be running smooth with no delays, my shuttle was able to get through with relative ease. Simple layout, modern facility, customer service was good. Overall, I wouldn't mind flying back through this airport in the future.

Could eat it every day. On a recent to trip to Pittsburgh I tried alot of pizza and this was good pizza. One thing about Pitt pizza.. . it is slightly different than true NYC style: the crust is not as thin and there's a whole lot more cheese. As a rule Pitt pizza also has a slightly sweeter tomato sauce. The sum of its parts is still a delicious close cousin to NYC pizza. The pizza I tried in Pitt in my order of favorites: nFiori'snPizza Sola (Penn Circle Branch)nPizza PerfecttanAiello's (Murray Street)nBeto's Save for Beto's, I thought they were all delicious. Wish I had a chance to try Mineo's. A Pittsburgh native friend of mine calls this his favorite but they were closed July 5th when I went by their place on Murray.. . I'll try them next time I'm in the 'burgh. Pizza Perfectta has a few stools and a counter but really it is a take-out place.

Otherwise I would have brought him with me and we could have dined in! nI'd never eaten here before, so I thought it would be great to give their food a test run. Unfortunately, my experience at Barb's Country Junction fell far short of my expectations. As soon as I stepped inside, I was met with a dated and poorly maintained interior. The decor seemed stuck in the 1970s, with faded wallpaper peeling off the walls and worn-out furniture that looked like it had seen better days.The service was equally disappointing. The staff appeared disinterested and lacked the warmth and friendliness that I had hoped for. It took forever to get someone's attention just to place my order, and when my food finally arrived, it was lukewarm and uninspiring.I decided to give the menu a chance, hoping that the food would redeem the experience. However, the dishes I ordered lacked any sort of creativity or attention to detail. The flavors were bland, the ingredients tasted stale, and the presentation was haphazard at best. It felt like the kitchen was merely going through the motions without any passion for their craft.To make matters worse, the portion sizes were incredibly small for the price charged. I left the restaurant feeling unsatisfied and still hungry, which left a bitter taste in my mouth both figuratively and literally.Furthermore, the cleanliness of the establishment was questionable. I noticed crumbs and spills on the tables and floors, giving the impression that the staff did not prioritize cleanliness or proper hygiene practices. It was certainly not the kind of environment where one could enjoy a pleasant dining experience.Even though I had hoped to find a gem in Barb's Country Junction, it was clear that the restaurant was past its prime and desperately in need of an overhaul. The lackluster ambiance, mediocre service, and subpar food made it nearly impossible for me to find anything to like about this place. I left feeling deeply disappointed and regretful of the time and money I had wasted.If Barb's Country Junction wishes to regain its former glory and attract customers, it needs a complete transformation.

It looked like almost more than half of the tables had "Reserved" signs. There were people behind us waiting for a table.. some left. It's not that it's overly crowded or anything, but there's constantly people milling about everywhere you look. You practically have to weave in and out of crowds just to walk from one end of a terminal to the other. On top of that, it always seems like half the airport is under some kind of construction so there's fences and barricades blocking off different areas. Don't even get me started on trying to find a bathroom around here. You'd think with how many people are always coming and going that they'd have more than just a couple scattered about each concourse. But nope, you often have to trudge all the way to the other end and there's always a huge line. By the time it's your turn, you're about ready to go right then and there just to avoid the wait! The food options are pretty boring too. It's all basically the same old chain places you can find in any other airport. Nothing unique or local to get excited about. And forget about finding a decent meal for anything under $15, it's all snacks and pre-made sandwiches at inflated prices. Sometimes I just skip eating altogether rather than dig into my wallet that deep.Even getting around the terminals is a slog sometimes. Escalators and people movers are always packed so it takes forever to move a few gates over. Forget wheeling a bunch of luggage through that mess too. By the time you're where you're going, your arms feel like jelly. And good luck navigating with any kind of delay - the signs are confusing and it's too easy to end up on the wrong concourse altogether. WiFi is spotty at best and forget finding an open power outlet near your gate. Those things are more scarce than the bathroom stalls. The seats are worn out too, so you're either sinking into one hoping the cushion releases you or perched on the edge of a metal bench praying your tailbone survives the wait.

The rooms were clean with some wear and tear in the bathroom. Beds very comfortable. I grew up in Pittsburgh but have never stayed at the Renaissance. I wanted to like this place, so I'll start with the positive aspects. First of all, the gym in pretty cheap. And the bouldering area is really quite good. To be honest, this should only be a bouldering gym. There were a lot of different volumes, nice routes, some top outs, and a good cave area. Even a small crack with a few problems set on it. It seems like whoever is in charge of setting the boulder problems really has some talent. I might be back to bolder once in a blue moon. The other climbers here were pretty cool, so the place might have a good vibe/community aspect. n Now the downsides. The staff wasn't very helpful. The rules regarding the top rope area are nonsensical, and the only reasoning offered up was insurance. I wanted to belay for a friend, but he wasn't allowed in the top rope area unless belay tested. Belay testing also cost $5, and I hate when gyms charge for a test. It's poor form. The ropes aren't doubled up, and with the short wall it gives way too much pull. They require you to clip into daisy chains on the ground. I wanted to lead climb, but there was no one at the gym that could give a lead test. The TR routes were really hit or miss, a lot of them just confusing and not fun. They aren't rated properly, just easy, medium, or hard. The walls are painted plywood, so smearing is basically impossible. Further, I question if the holds have ever been cleaned. Some of them are so polished to the point that it's dangerous. There's only once changing room, and overall the place isn't very clean. I believe there is some potential here, but it seems to be mismanaged and on the whole, a missed opportunity.

but when we got there at 8pm, the place was hoppin'. There were people seated from as close to the kitchen and all the way up the stairs by the sidewalk. There were hopefuls milling about a bit to get down and place their name for a seating. When we were able to reach the desk, the wait time was 50 minutes. We went to Mercurio's for a while, took a stroll around Walnut, and eventually sat down by some very convenient benches nearby. After what we thought was 'adequate' wait time, we peered a bit over the fence and down towards the man (who we think may have been the owner). After a bit, he nodded at us, and started moving a couple of tables around inside. We took that as a signal, meaning, "Come on down. I'm wrestling these tables apart for you. "nnWe ordered the carne special (steak with alfredo for $30) and the torcia ($15). I wouldn't say that they were the best that i'd ever had, but they were pretty good. The vegetables are fresh; the pasta was just right and sauced/souped enough to my liking. The service, provided mostly by Diane, was excellent. She was friendly and attentive, despite the throngs of customers. The crowds are loud, the atmosphere very.. cozy.. and the walkways very narrow, and, yet, the food and drinks keep coming, accident-free. It seems like it could be highly stressful for the servers, but Diane was smiling every time she came back. Awesome.

I know this is a difficult one to rate, since he runs a stand within another establishment (Wholeys) but I am giving 5 glowing stars nontheless for the amazing sushi he makes (right in front of you) and his stellar personality. I have never met a person with blood flowing in their veins that didn't get a total kick out of Andy. When I worked in the Strip, I ate here almost daily. After only two visits, he remembered exactly what I ordered and would start making it as soon as he saw me: spicy yellowtail with avocado. Or just yellowtail with avocado. Maybe some cucumber. Have I mentioned that I am obsessed with yellowtail? Ahhhh, the buttery-ness, the texture, the slight taste of the sea.. .. oh wait, this isn't a review on a singular fish, i got a little carried away (even though Andy serves up some damn fine YT)! Sometimes he gets creative and mashes different flavor concepts together for you to sample as you wait. He once came up with a maki roll made of salmon, basil, cucumber and mango.. .. brilliant!! Wholeys is such a fantastic people watching spot anyway and it's always amusing to see random people of all ages/genders/sizes walk in and yell "ANDY"!

However, my experience in this specific chain store is impressive, so that I have to share with others. You may have heard recently that curling is all the rage since the Winter Olympics came through. And let me tell you, it's not hard to see why. There's something so satisfying about watching those rocks glide across the ice, the sound of the brooms sweeping frantically, and the thrill of a well-placed shot.As a long-time curling enthusiast, I was excited to try out the new curling rink in town. And let me tell you, it did not disappoint. The ice was smooth and well-maintained, the equipment was top-notch, and the staff were friendly and helpful.I started out by watching a few games to get a feel for the place. The atmosphere was lively and fun, with people cheering and laughing all around me. And the competition was fierce - these people were serious about their curling!But don't worry, you don't have to be a pro to enjoy the rink. They offer lessons and instructions for beginners, so don't be afraid to give it a try. And the prices are very reasonable, especially considering the quality of the facility.I decided to take a chance and sign up for a league. And let me tell you, it's been one of the best decisions I've made in a long time. The people are friendly and welcoming, and the competition is just enough to keep things interesting.Plus, there's something so satisfying about getting that perfect shot. I mean, have you ever felt the rush of adrenaline when your rock curls just right and lands in the perfect spot? It's exhilarating!And the best part? It's a great workout! I never realized how much exercise I was getting until I started curling regularly. My arms and legs are toning up, and I feel more energized than ever.Of course, there are a few downsides. The ice can be a bit slippery, so you have to be careful not to fall. And sometimes the brooms can get in the way, but that's all part of the fun.Overall, I'm so glad I gave curling a try.

"I've been a loyal customer of this laundromat for years, and I've never had a single issue. The staff is consistently friendly and helpful, and the facilities are always spotless and well-maintained. I particularly appreciate the convenient pick-up service, which makes doing laundry a breeze. The prices are reasonable, too, especially when compared to other laundromats in the area. I've tried a few others before, but this one is my top choice. I highly recommend it to anyone seeking a reliable and hassle-free laundry experience. The only minor drawback is that it can get a bit busy on weekends, but it's well worth the short wait. Overall, I'm extremely satisfied with the service and will continue to be a loyal customer."

It was dead, but we were early on a Tuesday night, and it picked up. We started with the fried zucchini. The consensus was thumbs up. Bread was average. I ordered the veggie pasta. Asked for it w/out zucchini but was told it wasn't possible as it was pre-made. It was ok. My daughter had the cheese raviolis and enjoyed them. The other three people had the seafood platter special. Didn't go so well. The shrimp and scallops were good, the sole was ok, but all three sent theirs back because the lobster wreaked of ammonia. Our waiter appeared overwhelmed by having to serve a bad product, and was only semiapologetic. They then brought out two manicotti dinners which were fine. Service was average at best. Feel bad given how long it has been around, but it is hard to imagine making a return trip.

Well, Cajun Queen happened to be one of those meals. Neither of us eat cajun/creole very often so we were a little hesitant at first. After holding on to a Groupon for a few weeks we finally made the trip.. . what on earth took us so long?! One step through the doors and you're immediately transported to a raucous, lively setting reminiscent of 1980's New Orleans. Tables are tightly packed; patrons share drinks and laughs; and sounds of jazz echo from upstairs. The walls are adorned by "Nawlins" inspired artwork and an appropriate purple, gold and green palette is interwoven throughout the house. The Gumbo was the only thing that I wasn't completely impressed with. It had good flavor and an ample helping of shrimp but I felt it was missing something. The consistency was thinner and more watered down than I anticipated. Keep in mind I am no cajun aficionado. The boyfriend ordered the pasta special: Two blackened chicken breasts over a heaping portion of tortellini in a spicy pesto cream sauce with peppers, Andouille sausage, peppers, and artichokes. WOWEE MAMA. This was one of the most delicious meals (yes, it wasn't even my meal) that I've had in a while. My u00e9touffu00e9e was delicious as well, thought admittedly, not quite as impressive as the pasta dish. It did kick some heat but it was good flavorful spice heat. Large portions seemed to be the theme of night and despite force-feeding ourselves to the point of pain, we both managed to leave with decent-sized leftovers. From the camaraderie and excellent service to the food and drinks.. . everything seemed to be perfect and I cannot wait to return!

My time at the company was certainly a learning experience. Over the years, I was able to expand my skills and take on more responsibility. However, there were also consistent challenges that tested my patience. Communication seemed disorganized, which often led to confusion. Deadlines were frequently missed due to poor planning, and meeting productivity goals felt like an uphill battle daily. On the positive side, my coworkers became like a second family who helped maintain morale even during stressful periods. We developed a strong team dynamic that made the long hours more enjoyable. While the work itself could be interesting at times, the environment was not always ideal. By the end, I felt burned out and ready for a change of scenery. In summary, it was a mixed experience - I gained valuable skills but also saw the limitations of working within such an dysfunctional system long-term. Overall, unless significant changes have been made since my departure, I could not fully recommend the company.

Recently, this is a place for me and my friends on Sunday. Enjoy drinks and snacks at the same time. A comfortable lounge furniture and large TV can relax and focus on action. During a business rest, we chat and debate our fantasy team or the forecast of the rest of the day. The staff is always friendly and quickly with replenishment. There are all typical bar fares you want on the menu, such as wings, corn slices and sliders and other football. They also provide some signature dishes, such as barbecue pig Bake and truffle Pamerson fries. This place is very beautiful on Sunday on Sunday, so we try to get a good place earlier. The crowd always returns to the game leisurely, but it will never be too noisy. I like the existing bar area and some high top tables, so we can choose according to our group scale. They do well and keep their voice balanced, so you can hear the sound of TV. Overall, this has become our new home on NFL Sunday. We look forward to more football and friendship here. The staff remembers us every week, which adds a sense of familiarity. Whether our team wins or loses, we always have a happy time and look forward to the next Sunday game. This place must have won the conventional position in our football watching rotation.

Since we both had fairly light lunches we were starvin' marvins. After attempting to stop by a handful of places (closed on Monday or an hour long wait) we settled on Snoop's, hopin' for a hot and fresh burger. Inside, Snoop's leaves a lot to be desired. I'm not a dull knife in the drawer, and it took me a little while to figure out the, um, theme of the burger joint. Snoop's.. . as in detectives.. . snooping.. . i saw a Bond poster too. Ok, sure.. . I didn't really care about the overall ambiance as long as the food was solid. And how about the food? Well, it's pricier than other old school grilles - to the tune of $15+ for two 1/3 lb. burger combos and a corn dog. This wouldn't really bother me much if the food was better. The burger was fine - passable, but very well done (as in quite brown) and essentially flavorless. Onion rings were clunk-ily breaded and with little flavor and fries were "meh" overall. I was looking for the salty little slivers of love with some crisp! Service wasn't super inviting and the cash register attendant didn't even hint at a smile when we ordered. As soon as cash was in hand, she went back to her computer - adjacent to the counter. With a sanitation score barely above 90 and the flavorless eats, I have indeed experienced some better burger joints in the QC.

The meal was good and reasonably priced. They also have a good beer selection on draft and in bottles. We had a party of 6 going for a 7: 30 dinner on a Thursday. Bigger parties tend to chat a little more and take longer in my experience. I felt like they were sort of rushing us out. That might be because they closed the dining room door and started vacuuming the front bar room while we were still finishing up our dinner. I'm not sure if anyone was eating out there but I'm very happy we weren't because it seems really gross to me to vacuum around food. This was around 9: 15 and I'm pretty sure they serve until 10. Besides that, our service was good and so was the food. We all split the stuffed pretzels and potato skins as an appetizer. The pretzels are delicious, I could have eaten them all myself! Deep-fried and stuffed with cheese, yummy! I ordered the Chicken Viennese and was pleased with my meal. It came with a choice of two sides and I went with a delicious sweet potato casserole and my favorite thing of the night: POTATO PANCAKES. I prefer sour cream, but you can also get applesauce. Yum yum yum get lots of potato pancakes! The chicken was delicious and was served over spaetzel, which was just ok. I've had the kase spaetzel there before which is served in a cheese sauce and much better than the regular. There was a variety of entrees ordered from sausage platters to wiener schnitzel and everyone seemed pleased with their meals. You get a lot for your money and I'll never turn down a chance to eat potato pancakes!

nn1. The staff works hard to make sure you are getting the best prices on parts and they charge reasonable rates for labor. n2. They stand by their warranty. Many people could not believe it. But honestly, from the outside, this place did not appeal to me. It looked like it would be some kind of shabby bar inside. This is not he case. Well, first, I should have looked more carefully or asked, because it came on a croissant. Eww. All I spied and at was the meat and provolone cheese on top. The onion rings were good. Overall, this place was ok. I probably wouldn't come back again if I had my choice.

"I had high hopes for this sushi restaurant, but unfortunately, it failed to impress. The atmosphere was lackluster, with dim lighting and uncomfortable seating that didn't quite live up to the expected ambiance. The service was also subpar, with a server who seemed disinterested in our needs.The menu offered a variety of options, but the sushi rolls were overpriced and lacked creativity. I opted for the Spider Roll, which was disappointingly bland and had too much repetition of ingredients. The sushi rice was also underseasoned and had a strange texture that didn't quite agree with my palate.I was eager to try their signature dish, the Dragon Roll, but it was a letdown. The tempura shrimp was overcooked and tasted more like fish stick than shrimp, and the avocado and cucumber were fresh but not enough to save the roll from its overall lack of flavor. The roll itself was also too large and difficult to eat, making it a bit of a challenge to enjoy.The sushi bar was clean and well-stocked, but the chefs seemed inexperienced. I watched as they struggled to make simple rolls and exhibited weak knife skills, which was evident in the poorly made rolls that were served to us.The drinks menu was limited, with only a few options for beer and wine. The sake selection was particularly weak, with only a few unimpressive choices. The tea and coffee options were also lacking, with only a few uninspired selections.I was looking forward to trying their desserts, but they were unimpressive. The mochi was overly sweet and had an odd texture that didn't quite work for me. The green tea ice cream was better, but it wasn't quite authentic enough to impress.Overall, I was underwhelmed by this sushi restaurant. Despite its promising location and atmosphere, the food and service were subpar, which is why I wouldn't recommend it to anyone looking for a great sushi experience. Rating: 2.5/5.

Fine Italian dining at a reasonable price and by reasonable, I mean, it's less expensive than a Michelin-starred French restaurant. But don't let the price fool you, the quality of the food and service here is top-notch. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with a warm smile by the hostess and were promptly seated at our cozy table by the window. The decor was modern and stylish, with a sleek wood-paneled bar and comfortable booths.The menu offered a diverse selection of traditional Italian dishes, including pastas, risottos, and osso buco. We started with the bruschetta, which was perfectly toasted and topped with fresh tomatoes, basil, and a drizzle of balsamic glaze. The Insalata Caprese was a highlight, with juicy heirloom tomatoes, creamy mozzarella, and a tangy vinaigrette dressing.But the real star of the show was the pasta dishes. We ordered the Spaghetti Carbonara, which was cooked to a perfect al dente and tossed in a rich, creamy sauce made with free-range eggs and guanciale. The Pappardelle Bolognese was also exceptional, with tender, slow-cooked beef ragù and a generous sprinkle of shaved Parmesan cheese.The main courses were equally impressive. The Branzino was pan-seared to a crispy perfection and served with a flavorful cherry tomato sauce. The Chicken Parmesan was breaded and fried to a golden crisp, topped with melted mozzarella cheese and a side of creamy mashed potatoes.We finished off the meal with a slice of Tiramisu, which was remarkably creamy and rich, with a hint of espresso and cocoa powder. The coffee was also excellent, with a smooth and rich flavor that complemented the dessert perfectly.Throughout the meal, the service was attentive and friendly, with our server happily answering any questions we had about the menu and making sure our glasses were always full.

I visited this city for business and arrived at my hotel around 7 p.m. for dinner. Since the hotel is very close to downtown, I decided to dine at "The Boathouse," a restaurant situated on the water. The food was exquisite, and the view was breathtaking. I ordered the seafood pasta, which was cooked to perfection. The staff was also very friendly and provided excellent service. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting the area.The next morning, I enjoyed a delicious breakfast at the hotel's buffet, which offered a wide variety of options. After breakfast, I explored the city by visiting the local art museum, which had an impressive collection of paintings. I also visited the farmer's market, where I purchased some fresh produce.In the afternoon, I met up with a friend who lives in the area. We had lunch at a charming little cafe and then went shopping, where I found some great deals on clothes and accessories. For dinner, I went to "The Grill," a cozy restaurant with an excellent menu.The following day, I checked out of the hotel and headed to the airport. I had a wonderful time in this city and look forward to visiting again in the future.

Those expectations kind of fell flat. Service here on a Saturday night was atrocious. We waited about 10 minutes before we were asked what we would like to drink and then another 20 min before we were asked what we would like to order. Not OK. On top of that, our interactions with our waiter were just awkward. Something seemed to be up, like there was some tension going on with him and maybe the staff/kitchen? As far as the sushi goes.. . it's pretty good. I got some maki rolls, which were very good, but nothing spectacular. Miso soup.. . OK. Salad was OK. The sashimi definitely seemed like a better option and something they took greater pride in. The people next to us who had ordered some sashimi options and seemed quite satisfied. If I come back again, I'll make sure to order sashimi. However, I was so annoyed by the lack of service that I doubt I'll be back anytime soon.

Pedro's is a place that I remember fondly from my childhood. It was a small, family-owned restaurant with a cozy atmosphere. The food was alwys delicious, and the service was impeccable. I have so many fond memories of eating there with my family. We would always start our meal with a basket of their warm, fluffy bread and their famous garlic butter. Then, we would order a assortment of dishes to share, like their spaghetti and meatballs, chicken cheddar, and eggplant parmesan. Everything was constantly cooked to perfection, and the flavors were amazing. Du staff at Pedro's was always so friendly and welcoming. They made us feel like we were part of their families. They consistently knew our names and our favorite dishes. We always had a great time eating at Pedro's. It was our go-to restaurant for special occasions, like birthdays and anniversaries. We also loved going there for a simple weeknight meal. No matter what the occasion, Pedro's never disappointed. The last time I ate at Pedro's was a few years beforehand. I was so happy to see that it was still the same great place that I remembered. The food was just as de licious as I remembered, and the service was still impeccable. I'm so glad that I gets to experience Pedro's again. It's a truly special place.

! ! ! ! ! ! ! ! ! ! ! Nathan Fish did an amazing job with my tattoo and I couldn't have been more pleased with it. I saw this picture online that I liked and printed it off as a basis for my tattooo. Nathan took the picture and made revisions for the specifics I wanted. The ending result was more than I expected, IT LOOKED BETTER THAN THE ORIGINAL! I think another great thing about this place is the people are awesome. It is really important for me to connect with my tattoo artist, and I didn't feel that when I got my first tattoo at a different shop. I went with my best friend Winnie and she got her tattoo with Travis Lakeman. Her tattoo turned out amazing as well. Both our artists made us feel comfortable and at ease, which is important if you are sitting there for hours getting tattooed. Not to mention all of these guys are artists and you can see their art work displayed at each of their stations and in the art gallery connected to their shop. It is a great way to see their artistic abilities and expression, which is what tattooing is all about. The overall experience was excellent and the price is extremely reasonable. They will not over charge you! I would definitely go back for another tattoo and recommend this place for anyone who wants a tat!

Oh boy. The ambiance is more like a Wendy's that tries to be upscale: cramped, busy, somewhat noisy. Of the two filet mignons we had (different sizes, medium rare) one was horribly overcooked, the other one a little on the rare side. The meat wasn't special. The deserts were OK but the Creme Brulee was bland in the extreme. Service was OK but occasionally inattentive. For two adults, one child, a check of $150 would have been reasonable for the quality provided. It ended up being $350 or so. Oh well - I rounded up the check to $400 and left with the intention of never coming back again. Imagine my shock when I found that my credit card had been charged with $600! I'm sure this will turn out to be an innocent mistake, but if this restaurant thinks it provides an experience worth $200 per head, they need to call Chef Ramsey.

They have perfected the Italian sub sandwiches nicely. This location in particular was very helpful and provided discounts. The young men working behind the counters were attentive, handled my order accurately, and promptly. Great job! I am a well balanced in my approach to food that entails me being a professional cook with many years experience in many types of cuisines from Latin America, Greek, Italian, American and many more. I take food as the ultimate pleasure in life along with many other things. I give my reviews based on my experiences eating out at least 2 times a day and 5-6 days a week. The store is a treasure trove for do-it-yourselfers and creative minds looking for inspiration. From paints to knitting needles, from model kits to scrapbooking supplies, they seem to have everything. As I walked through the aisles, I was amazed at the vast array of colors, textures, and mediums on display. What impressed me most was the knowledgeable and friendly staff. Whenever I had a question or needed help finding something, they were more than happy to help. They were clearly experts in their field and gave me valuable tips and recommendations to enhance my projects. In addition to the extensive selection and helpful staff, Michael's offers frequent workshops and classes for beginners and seasoned crafters alike. Attending one of these sessions was an enriching experience. I felt supported and encouraged to experiment and explore new horizons in my chosen hobbies. The instructors were skilled artisans who patiently guided us through each step of the process, fostering a sense of accomplishment and a passion for creativity. One aspect that pleasantly surprised me was the reasonable prices. Despite the vast selection available, I found the prices to be reasonable and accessible. The organization and layout of the store are also commendable. The aisles are clearly marked, making it easy to find what you're looking for. The store also frequently offers tempting promotions and sales, making it even more tempting to indulge in new projects without breaking the bank. The shelves are neatly stocked and everything is displayed in a visually appealing way, which makes it a joy to browse. Michael's commitment to sustainable practices is also worthy of mention.

The service is very good and the food is delicious. The menu has a variety of choices, and everything we order is cooked perfectly. The atmosphere is comfortable and seductive, and the staff is very friendly and careful. We spend a pleasant time and we will definitely come back again. Overall, this is a great experience. I strongly recommend that you recommend this restaurant to everyone who wants delicious food and good time. The price is reasonable and some are generous. We feel full and satisfied. This is definitely a hidden gem in the city. I can't wait to go back again.

I mean, seriously - I don't get it. Perhaps it has something to do with the relative age of each store? If that's the case, this particular location must have been "Plan C" for "chaotic. It's like someone made a list of all of the departments, threw them into a big top hat, shook the hat vigorously, and then dumped it onto a floor plan. Examples: you've just purchased a new faucet and would like to replace the faucet lines and fittings. One would reason to think these components would be located within a few aisles of one another.. . HA! Gotchya! They're nowhere near one another! Need a mirror to go with that new faucet? You'll be making a trip to the PAINT department for that, which seems entirely logical to me (insert eye roll). I could go on, but you get the idea. At least the checkout folks are friendly. The same can't really be said for the few department staff I've dealt with; on a recent visit, two department guys were standing in the middle of an aisle talking about how "f-ing dumb" a previous customer was. Nice. In general, I'm a fan of Menards - especially the west side store. This one? Not so much.

When I first told one of my friends about this dessert, he told me that the thought of it made him Krispy Kreme his pants. That's before I even went into the pornographic details about how it was swimming in Makers Mark Caramel Bourbon Sauce that was set ablaze. So naughty. I mean, I don't even like donuts all that much but it just felt wrong not to order an item that was just so blatantly taunting. I kept my expectations at bay before dining here. It's located inside of the City Center Marriott so I was very aware that the food may be uninspiring and generic. But what I found is that Savannah Red is actually a fabulous restaurant that stands on it's own two feet, with delicious food at tasty price pointsn nThings started off nicely with an amuse bouche of cauliflower soup, which was rich and delicious. I like to just nibble and taste so I ordered a few small dishes. The Jumbo Crab Cakes ($8) were pretty good, but keep in mind that the Cilantro Avocado Emulsion is little a small dollop on the plate. The Diver Scallop Ravioli w/ cream sauce, wilted greens, and Sriracha gastrique ($8) was my far my favorite dish ordered. You've got to try it. the greens are cooked perfectly and the two ravioli are large, fresh and meaty. I was given a bit of sorbet to cleanse the palate before being presented with my Pear and Endive salad, blue cheese brulee and pink apple vinaigrette. So good! Initially, I had no plans on ordering dessert. But the bread pudding was only $6 and sounded so novel that I had to give it a try. If you like donuts, you will love it. For my own personal taste (I'm not huge on donuts) it was a bit too sweet, but the preparation and plating were fabulous! Overall, an excellent restaurant with stellar service and an exciting menu.

I was expecting more, but left a bit disappointed. First of all, the directions from Google maps is a bit off.. . it takes you through an apartment complex to a dead end. It's located in a shopping center (with Food Lion). The atmosphere is small with humble interior design. There are approximately 4 booths with high backs and hard bottoms with worn out cushions. The greeting was all smiles. The service wasn't fast, but not too slow either. Our drinks were always full and the server was very friendly. The sushi list was limited, but priced well. The spicy tuna roll was very good. Do not order the teriyaki chicken unless you like two marinated chicken breasts with sauce on top served with a cup of rice and a side of lettuce with ginger dressing for $12. Very disappointing. The restaurant was fairly busy, so I'm sure they have better dishes. I'll have to go back and try some of the noodle items.

I took my boyfriend to Casbah at the end of September for his birthday, and we were both excited to try out this highly recommended restaurant. As we entered, the warm and inviting atmosphere immediately caught our attention. The dimly lit room was filled with soft music, creating a romantic ambiance that set the mood for the evening. We were promptly greeted by a friendly hostess who led us to our table near the large windows overlooking the bustling city. The menu at Casbah was diverse, offering a range of culinary delights from various cuisines. We started with the chef's special appetizer, a plate of perfectly seared scallops served with a tangy citrus sauce. The flavors were delicately balanced, and the scallops melted in our mouths. It was a promising start to the meal. For the main course, my boyfriend ordered the grilled ribeye steak, cooked to medium-rare perfection. The steak was accompanied by a delectable truffle mashed potato and sautéed asparagus. He couldn't stop praising the tenderness and flavor of the meat, declaring it one of the best steaks he has ever had.As for me, I opted for the vegetarian option, a roasted butternut squash risotto. The dish was a symphony of flavors with creamy risotto infused with the earthy sweetness of the squash. It was garnished with crispy sage leaves, adding a delightful crunch. I thoroughly enjoyed every spoonful.Despite the exceptional food, one aspect that slightly disappointed us was the service. While the staff was friendly, the wait time for our main courses was longer than expected. However, their sincere apologies and complimentary dessert made up for the delay. We indulged in the decadent chocolate lava cake, oozing with molten chocolate and paired with a scoop of homemade vanilla ice cream.Overall, our experience at Casbah was memorable. The cozy atmosphere, exceptional food, and delightful flavors made it a special evening for my boyfriend's birthday.

Went with my boyfriend after biking along the north shore trail, and didn't tell him about the negative reviews since I REALLY wanted to sit along the river. The view/environment is still very pretty, but we both found ourselves displeased with the food and the service. We both got the beer battered cod sandwhich (convinced him to go basic after reading bad things about the food) and although he enjoyed it, I thought the batter was very doughy and uncooked on the fish, and the tartar sauce tasted grainy (any giant eagle brand would have been better). It didn't seem like others were too crazy about the food as I heard the woman behind us complaining that her dish wasn't cooked and would like a refund. The beers were bottled and cold, so couldn't complain there, but the service was still poor as we were rushed to choose our drinks/dishes and given a second to pay. Would have thought after all the reviews that they would have changed employees. Overall, I would come here again only for some beers and nice seating, but would eat dinner beforehand.

So I tried this on my first visit to Elizabeth neighborhood on one rainy night on a Friday. It was worth it! I really liked the roti cani. The roti was cold but the perfect and spicy gravy compensated for that. I would highly recommend everyone to try roti canai, at least one time. This is a nice appetizer. I had a curry flavor from the Chef's Specialties. It was perfect. Very well cooked vegetables in the curry, made me happy. The meal was big for me after I had roti so go with the big appetite. I have to pack the left over but I know it would taste yummy next day. Any spicy food taste delicious next day. That's the fantastic fact about spices. As per my visit to this restaurant, it was favorable. The staff was friendly. Although I wanted to sit on a high tool or a high chair in the bar area but they made me sit at the short chair area in the bar area. That's fine. No harm done. The food made all the difference. The menu looked really great and it was hard for me to decide as everything on it seemed worth trying. I went for a simple (according my gut feeling) and predictable (as one can think) dish which was Curry Flavor. I have become very picky since I become pesceterian. Instead of trying sushi or seafood stuff, I went for pure vegetarian. I can confidently say that many vegetarian folks would like this place. They have few items on the menu for vegetarians. Overall, I like this place.

I believe I was the first Yelper to give this place a 5 star review. The food is amazing, the service is impeccable, and the atmosphere is inviting and cozy. The menu is creative and well-executed, with something to please everyone. The staff is friendly and attentive, and they make sure that you have a great experience. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal.The food is always fresh and delicious, and the portions are generous. I've never had a bad meal here. The service is also top-notch. The staff is friendly and attentive, and they make sure that you have everything you need.The atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the decor is stylish and modern. It's a great place to relax and enjoy a meal with friends or family.I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great dining experience. You won't be disappointed.In addition to the great food and service, this restaurant also has a great selection of wines and cocktails. The bartenders are knowledgeable and friendly, and they can help you find the perfect drink to pair with your meal.If you're looking for a special occasion restaurant, this is the place to go. The food, service, and atmosphere are all top-notch. You'll have a truly memorable experience.This restaurant is also great for large groups. They have a private dining room that can accommodate up to 20 people. The staff is happy to help you plan your event, and they'll make sure that everything goes smoothly.Whether you're looking for a romantic dinner or a fun night out with friends, this restaurant is sure to please. I highly recommend it.I've been to this restaurant many times, and I've never been disappointed. The food is always amazing, the service is impeccable, and the atmosphere is inviting and cozy.I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. You won't be disappointed.

really good, but i wasn't too impressed w/ my entree (the pasta trio - the broccoli one was kind of watery, tasted like it was seasoned only w/ salt, and then i didnt like the ravioli at all, the cheese was too smelly for me and then the linguini was alrite but also kind of watery)nni REALLY liked the butter that came w/ the bread - 3 kinds, crunchy sugar or something, apricot and strawberry; the appetizer table was really good too - caesar salad yummy, cured meats, soup was bleh, but it was a good variety and all you can eatnnthe desserts also were really good. had cookies, tangerine panna cotta, tiramisu (which everyone kept snatching up so if you see it, just grab it even if youre not ready for dessert), this brownie thing was REALLY good also. the almond cake wasn't as moist as i would have hoped.. . nnmy bf got the gnocchi w/ duck and that was really good. a LOT in terms of portion sizenn$24 1 entree and all you can eat appetizer and dessert. pretty good deal! but not your every-weekend brunch place

I was so disappointed when I heard that all Borders stores were closing. Borders was my favorite place to browse for hours and discover new authors. The atmosphere was always inviting and the selection was immense. I enjoyed perusing the shelves and coming across unexpected gems that I never would have found elsewhere. All of my favorite sections from mysteries to biographies were well organized. The staff was usually quite knowledgeable and willing to recommend similar books to ones I already enjoyed. Towards the end, it was sad to see the stores become more bare as the liquidation sales took their toll. I made multiple trips, hoping to find deals on series I had been meaning to start. While I'm glad I stocked up on reading material, I will really miss Borders and the experience of exploring their stores. It's such a loss to the book community.

Small patio even smaller bar. Appears to always be very crowded regardless of time of day. This place has a lot of neighborhood dive bar charm complete with tatt'ed hipsters both server and served. There is one dude with dreadlocks to his knees. The locals observation of this guy is he is usually in a bad mood and rude. I didn't interact with him so I cannot comment. However, I really don't like the idea of someone with hair that has been unwashed for more than 5 years handling my food or walking by food with 4 foot long dreadlocks - which is why we only drank there. The locals suggest that the reason he appears to be in a bad mood all the time is that he has not washed his hair in the past decade. : o)nnWe didn't eat, but the beer selection was awesome. There were several Belgium beers and our waitress was very good at suggesting some very good beers that I have not had before.

My 4 comrade and I were in Charlotte NC and our airplane was cancelled which then made us miss our connecting midair back to LAX. The airline rebooked us for the next day but that meant we would needed a place to repose for the night. After searching online, we indicated a extraordinarily rated hotel within walking distance of the airport that had rooms available for a reasonable price. When we come at the hotel around 10pm, they had us check in without any difficulty even though it was late. Our cinemas were basic but clean with comfortable beds. In the matinee, we had dine in the lobby area which had an adequate selection of continental options like pastries, yogurt and fruit. Our plane wasn't until the afternoon so we spent the morning relaxing at the hotel. When it was time for our flight, we recieve a ride to the airport and checked our bags. The burglaries to LAX was longer than expected as we hit some turbulence along the way. We landed in LA in the evening and made our connect to our hometown airports. A few extra hours in Charlotte wasn't ideal but overall our blitz hotel stay was pleasant and the airline become us home only a day later than planned. While missing flights is never humour, everything worked out okay given the circumstances.

The early spring and late summer when I'm using allergy medication like a fish uses water, I thought a little natural relief while I sleep would help alleviate the morning sneezing fits. I got one here for an Amazon price of relatively cheap. I also bought some healing stones and crystals. She also carries some impressive jewelry and stones that can be set in necklaces and brackets. The place is huge, and just when you think you've seen everything, you can walk down a hew hallway and find more things. Great little shop that reminds me of a shop in a Stephen King novel called Needful Things. Although that shop was owned by Satan and made his customers do unspeakable things to each other, this is far from that. But you do get the feeling here that we are not alone and there are other realms to our world. Books galore on the occult, spirit worlds, shadow people, how to rid your home of evil spirits and I just wish she wasn't closing the store when I was walking in. She was nice enough to stay open until I purchased my salt lamp. I'll return and get my fill of this place and look around for four or five hours.

It's locally owned. The owner takes great pride in serving the community and has been in business for over 30 years. You will usually find them at the shop greeting customers and ensuring every visit is a positive one. They work hard to maintain reasonable prices and give something back whenever possible through local sponsorships and donations. The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable about all the products and services offered. You will get excellent customer service and never feel like just another sale. The shop focuses on quality rather than quantity and forms lasting relationships with both customers and suppliers. They carry specialty items you cannot find everywhere as well as staples done exceptionally well. Everything is well organized and easy to find so you can get in and out quickly if needed. The locally sourced food options are always fresh and delicious whether grabbing something for breakfast or putting together components for dinner. Customer feedback is taken seriously and used to constantly evolve their selection and operations. Generations of families have grown up visiting this staple of the neighborhood. It is a welcoming place to spend time browsing, learning and connecting with the community. Special orders are rarely an issue and unexpected challenges are met with understanding and creativity. Overall it provides an exemplary small business experience and continues to be a shining example of how positive impact starts local. I always leave feeling good about supporting such a valuable small business.

Let me start by saying that I have incredibly challenging hair. It's the kind of hair that seems to have a mind of its own and refuses to cooperate, no matter what I do. I've tried countless hair products, followed numerous tutorials, and even sought professional help, but my hair always manages to defy all my efforts. The formula is lightweight yet incredibly nourishing, leaving my hair soft and easy to manage, without any greasy residue. Gone are the days of the dreaded midday slump when my hair would lose its style and turn into a puffy mess. With Silken Magic, my hair effortlessly stays in place, whether I wear it down, tie it up in a sleek ponytail, or experiment with intricate braids.Another aspect that has won me over is the captivating scent of Silken Magic. Instead, it boasts a delicate floral fragrance that lingers in my hair, leaving me feeling refreshed and confident throughout the day.The packaging of Silken Magic is sleek and elegant, perfectly reflecting the high-quality nature of the product. It dispenses just the right amount of product every time, ensuring that I never waste a single drop. The bottle is also travel-friendly, making it a must-have companion for all your adventures.In conclusion, I can confidently say that Silken Magic is a complete game-changer for those of us with difficult hair.

I am in love with it. Soft, warm and it looks like they brush it w/ a little butter and herbs/garlic. Do I sound obsessed? Hope not.. . Anyway, a few dishes I have tried include: nPenne Alla VodkanLasagnanBoth these pasta dishes are pretty good. I love them both but every once in a blue moon they can be a little off (dry, salty, etc)nCarrot Cake Cheesecake (for dessert I usually share and pick a bite or two and am over it, that's just me though. For my few bites, I liked it. It could have been a little more room temp, felt like it was pre sliced and taken out the fridge to our table but overall it was good. I liked the combo and it was huge--a must share dish. Love their sweet tea too! Oh and the last time I went I had the BEST server. His name sounded like Lavender but I know it wasn't Lavender. He was friendly, patient and attentive--to the point that he was already filling my glass of sweet tea as soon as I finished my last sip.

so after coming This place does exceed my expectations in various possible ways. From the moment I walked through the door, I received warm smiles and impeccable services. The atmosphere is breathtaking, perfectly integrating modern elegance and comfort. Let's talk about food. The menu provides a variety of options, which can satisfy all kinds of flavors and diet. Each dish is a piece of art, carefully made, and pay attention to details. The taste is bold and vibrant, and the speech is nothing more than extraordinary. Whether you are seafood, meat or vegetarian fans, there are things that can satisfy each taste. The waiters here are excellent. They are knowledgeable, concentrated, and eager to provide suggestions based on personal preferences. They do not work hard to make you feel like a valuable guest to ensure that your dining experience is perfect. The choice of wine is widely planned. Whether you are an appreciation or just enjoying a glass of wine, you can choose. The sommelier is not only knowledgeable, but also full of enthusiasm. Their suggestions perfectly supplement our meals. Pay attention to details beyond food and services. Interior design is impeccable, with elegant decoration and comfortable seats. The lighting set the mood perfectly, creating a private and attractive atmosphere. The restaurant also has a beautiful outdoor seat area, which is very suitable for gathering with friends. The dessert menu is a real temptation. One of their exquisite works must be obsessed. Each dessert is a small part of heaven, with a perfect flavor and texture balance. They are a pleasant ending of the excellent dining experience. In addition, the restaurant's commitment to sustainability is commendable.

The best thing about this place is that it's open until 4am on the weekends. Don't bother going there between 1: 30-3: 00, however, since it is generally filled with drunken club goers. If you happen to BE one of those drunken club goers, then you should fit right in. Just don't get too rowdy or the cops will drag you out of line and toss you outside. I don't bother with the slices or premade calzones anymore.. . they are ok, but if I want left-overs I'll make them myself. Get a whole pizza here or try the wings (not bad for a pizza place). The best time to go here is early evening on a weekend night when the weather is nice. They will usually open up the windows, letting the breeze and sounds of the city flow in. I like to sit by the open window with a friend, a large pizza, and some beers and watch the clubbers roll by on their way to the alley. It's no hot tub in the Rockies, but it beats eating hot pockets in front of the tube.

such is the case with this gap. nni don't even shop at gap. but the bestie and i were doing our usual shadyside rounds last weekend and he really wanted to check out the spring collection, so we dipped in. nnbestie found awesome pants suitable for both work and play but they didn't have the color in his size. the friendly (and super attractive) nate immediately asked if he could call another store for us. bestie and i agreed the pants would be a wise investment, so nate began calling stores nearby and, after several minutes, found them and placed them on hold. nnthough i didn't look at the women's collection (like i said, i'm not a gap-goer), i did roam around the men's collection while bestie was in the fitting room and was amazed at how mostly everything was in place and cleaned up. loads of natural light also make everything even more aesthetically appealing. the only thing that would've been better was a sale. oh wait! bought three pairs of boxers for a lucky gent for only $15. 95. no clothing tax in pgh = happy manda-panda.

I am a huge fan of their quick fast and efficient delivery service. I usually run the Sesame Chicken with fried rice. Because there is a delivery minimum, I usually get two smalls. I like that the Sesame Chicken comes with ample sauce and the chicken is usually cooked to my liking. Although you might be well served to ask for the chicken cooked crispy as my buddy usually does. The fried rice is always consistent and is the perfect complement to the sweet chicken. Though I've tasted the egg roll many times, I am not a fan, not because there's anything wrong with them, just because I don't like egg rolls in general. The delivery component is usually pretty straight as well. The delivery guy is usually there with my food pipping hot within 10 min of ordering. There have some serious Jimmy John's speed going on with their delivery. The delivery driver has always been friendly and polite. So why am I not giving fortune cookie 5 stars? The answer is simple, I can't award Fortune Cookie 5 stars, because I've been in the actual establishment within the past month and they had a sanitation rating of 87. Its low and it scares me. However, that should tell you how good I think there food is - I gladly continue to frequent this establishment despite this stomach quivering low sanitation rating.

Max's serves an awesome Sunday Brunch Buffet! The omelet station is standard (no egg whites for you health-nuts) and heavenly pastries will always await you along with potato pancakes. I'm not in love with their potato pancakes, but being that Max's specializes in German food, you've got to try at least one with their homemade applesauce. Some of my rotating favorites on the buffet include red cabbage, Eggs Benedict, and the Farmer's Breakfast. You can order off the menu during brunch if you aren't in mood to gorge yourself on the buffet. No drinks included with the buffet: ( but you can order them, of course. I love the decor at Max's - it's an old house, and much of the furniture looks like it was in this house and just remained when it converted to a restaurant. Max's location in Old Deutschtown on the North Side fits it perfectly. They even offer a shuttle to Heinz Field on Steeler game days (small fee applies).

Made a reservation and we were seated in a dark corner at a tiny table. Is the money from having that table worth the negative experience guests will receive? Methinks not. I had to ask to be moved to the patio, which was much better. The drinks we ordered from the bar were watery (the Manhattan and some drink with applejack in it). Later, they made a mistake and sent us the wrong cocktail, which turned out to be much better than the ones we wanted. Appetizers (meatballs with Brussels sprouts and beet salad) were very good, but the main courses left a lot to be desired in terms of seasoning. The texture of the short rib in the ravioli wasn't quite right, sort of dry, maybe overcooked. We had a bread pudding for dessert, which was probably the best part of the meal. I expect a better overall experience for the money.

My favorite tea is the China Rose tea, which not only has a beautiful look to it, but has a wonderful taste! The Apple Caramel Almond is also very good, complete with halved almonds! The milk oolong tea is a little more pricey, but tastes almost like buttery popcorn! It is so unique and exquisite. There are so many coffees and teas to choose from that you could get lost all day just smelling the coffees and choosing which ones you want to take home! You can buy tea pots and infusers here to accompany your new loose leaf teas if you need something new or want to try different ways to drink tea. The prices are absolutely phenomenal. Depending on the tea, for about 2 oz of loose leaf teas or coffee, you are looking at a minimum of $1 and some change! The space is small, so it can be overwhelming when it's busy, but once the crowd dies down, you can really take your time and enjoy the coffees and teas without feeling rushed. Definitely check out this place, you won't be disappointed!

Tom's Diner is a place that I really, really want to love. Its charming retro atmosphere and cozy booth seating immediately transport you to a nostalgic state. As I stepped through the door, the delightful scent of freshly brewed coffee and sizzling bacon filled the air, intensifying my anticipation. The menu offers a diverse range of breakfast options, catering to every palate, from classic pancakes to indulgent omelettes.Taking my seat in a booth, I eagerly awaited my order. Unfortunately, the service fell short of my expectations. The waitstaff appeared overwhelmed and disorganized, leading to delays in taking orders and delivering food. Despite their friendliness, it was evident that the restaurant was understaffed, which had a negative impact on the overall dining experience.When the food finally arrived, it was a mixed bag. The fluffy pancakes were a delight, perfectly cooked and drizzled with just the right amount of maple syrup. However, the omelette I ordered lacked the promised ingredients, leaving me disappointed. The bacon, although crisp and flavorful, could have used a touch more seasoning to enhance the flavor profile.The coffee, which is said to be their specialty, was a hit-or-miss affair. Sometimes it arrived piping hot and robust, but on other occasions, it was lukewarm and lacked depth. This inconsistency left me yearning for a consistently excellent cup of joe.Despite these setbacks, Tom's Diner has one redeeming quality-the ambiance. The vintage decor, accompanied by softly playing jukebox tunes, creates a warm and welcoming atmosphere. It's the kind of place that makes you want to linger, soaking in the old-world charm and engaging in conversations with fellow patrons.If Tom's Diner can address its service issues and focus on consistency in both their food and coffee, it has the potential to become a truly remarkable breakfast spot.

My boyfriend and I are in our 20s and have visited this D&B multiple times, and I must say that it never disappoints. From the moment we walk in, the energetic atmosphere captures our attention and sets the tone for a fun-filled evening. The staff members are always friendly and attentive, ensuring that we have everything we need to enjoy our time there.One of the things we love most about this D&B is the wide variety of games they offer. Whether you're into classic arcade games, exciting virtual reality experiences, or challenging redemption games, they have something for everyone. Their game selection is constantly updated, so there's always something new and exciting to try.The prices for the games and activities are reasonable, especially considering the quality of entertainment you receive. We usually purchase a game card with credits and find that it lasts us a good amount of time. It's a great value for the amount of enjoyment we get out of it.The food and drinks at the D&B are also quite impressive. The menu offers a diverse range of options, from tasty appetizers to satisfying main courses. We've tried everything from their delicious burgers to their mouthwatering pizzas, and we've never been disappointed. The drinks menu is also extensive, with a wide selection of beers, cocktails, and non-alcoholic beverages.Another aspect that sets this D&B apart is the cleanliness and upkeep of the facility. It's evident that the management takes pride in maintaining a clean and welcoming environment. The game areas are always tidy, and the restrooms are well-maintained.One thing that can get a bit crowded during peak hours is the wait time for popular games. However, the staff does an excellent job of managing the queues and keeping things organized. Additionally, there are often promotions and special offers that allow you to skip the lines or receive bonus credits, which is a nice perk.

This tiny little place at the edge of Brookline doesn't look like much, but it has a real family character, cheap eats and tasty food. I have dined in twice and got carry out twice as well. The first time I got a platter/dinner, but I found the deal is really to be had with the gyros. Getting two gyros and a huge amount of fries for only $10 is a steal. The gyro bread is toasted, but still soft and it is loaded with meat like your grandma would try to feed you. The veggies have always tasted fresh and it is served hot. If I could change on thing, I would prefer fresh herbs on the gyro instead of dried. This gyro is definitely more spiced up than your chain restaurant gyro. The fries are fresh cut and nothing is cooked until you order it. If you choose to dine in, you will be greeted by the proprietor and casually asked to take a seat any where you like. This isn't the type of place for formalities. She will offer you some delicious Greek Tea (you have to try it) and take your order, cook it and then serve it to you. Sometimes you can hear bickering in the kitchen between her and her old man- but that only adds to the family atmosphere. The store does take credit card, so that's a great modern convenience. At the end of the meal, we've always gotten a stick of gum: )nnIf you choose to carry out, it's a simple call and your food is ready by the time you drive down there. There is usually a place to park near by and you can be on your way quickly.

it's been at least two years since I've been to McNinch and I still remember the experience like it was yesterday. And I have to agree with Bill on this one, it's pretty amazing. Hubs and I decided to try this illustrious resto for Valentine's Day in 2008, we went through the whole reservation process, custom menu, custom wine pairings - the whole shebang. We actually followed all their directions to a t and arrive early, enjoyed some champagne while taking a tour of the sweet little home/restaurant on Church St. And then the incredible began.. . We were blown away (for the entire 3+ hours) by the spectacular pairings of food and wine, accompanied by fantastic service. I know we saved our menu for quite some time, but I'm not sure where it ran off to. Every single course was creatively prepared and tons of local ingredients were immersed into the dishes. Our server was also extremely knowledgable in each wine, explaining its heritage and vineyard to us. Since we choose the wine pairing option, we quite literally had a different (and interesting) glass of wine with every of the seven courses. Good thing we lived in the Fourth Ward at that time. Hey-oo! McNinch House is such a special place to experience an amazing meal. It's pricey and well worth every penny: I'm still talking about my meal 2. 5 years later. We probably spent about $400 all in, including the wine pairings for each of us, seven courses and tip. An expensive meal for sure, but it's wonderful for a anniversary or milestone celebration.

My partner took me to Alexander Michael's last night for dinner, and let me tell you, it was an incredible experience from start to finish. The ambiance was elegant and intimate, with soft lighting and comfortable seating. Our server, a friendly and knowledgeable young woman named Sarah, greeted us warmly and helped us navigate the menu.We started with a few appetizers, including the charcuterie board, which was filled with cured meats, cheeses, and accompaniments that perfectly complemented each other. The burrata was also a highlight, with its creamy center and flavorful accompaniments.For our main courses, my partner ordered the filet mignon, which was cooked to perfection and incredibly tender. I opted for the seafood risotto, which was out of this world. The seafood was fresh and expertly prepared, and the risotto was creamy and flavorful.We also ordered a few sides, including the truffle mac and cheese, which was decadent and delicious, and the sautéed spinach, which was cooked to perfection.For dessert, we shared a chocolate lava cake, which oozed warm chocolate sauce all over our plates. It was the perfect way to cap off a fantastic meal.The wine list was extensive and impressive, with options to suit every taste and budget. Your quaint French-inspired exterior and cozy interior promised a delightful dining experience. But alas, my hopes were quickly dashed. Our waitress, who seemed to be annoyed by our presence, barely acknowledged us during the meal. The menu, filled with confusing descriptions and overly complex dishes, made it difficult to choose something that sounded appetizing. I opted for the duck confit, which arrived lacking the rich, savory flavors I had anticipated. The meat was overcooked, and the potatoes were underseasoned. The sides were also disappointing. The roasted vegetables were bland and uninspired, and the spinach was drenched in a bitter sauce. My dining companion's salmon was similarly disappointing, with a strange, gelatinous texture and an overpowering sauce. The service, though friendly, was slow and inattentive. Even the desserts failed to impress. The crème brûlée was too sweet and had a strange, gelatinous texture. In short, despite the restaurant's charming atmosphere, the food and service fell short, leaving me feeling underwhelmed and disappointed. In conclusion, La Pomponnee failed to meet my expectations. I would not recommend this restaurant to my friends and family.

Mixed review. While some elements were tasty, others fell flat. The plot started off strong with an interesting premise, but it struggled to preserving momentum halfway through.
