Wow- similar experience as other reviewers. This place really exploded me away with how welcoming and friendly the staff was. From the moment we marched in, we felt right at home. Our server came over rightaway to greet us and let us know she would be taking great care of us. T he menu had a nice variety of options to choose from for anyone's tastes. I opted for the fish taos which were so fresh and delicious. My partner got the burger and said it was one of the be st they have ever had. The sides that came with our meals were also top notch. About halfway through our meal, our server jacked by to check on us and refill our drinks. The atmosphere in the restaurant was lively yet relaxed. As we finished up our food, we took our time lingered and enjoying our conversations. When it came time for the sheck, our server was super prompt to bring it. The price was very reasonable for the calibre of food and service. We left completely satisfied and looking forward to our next visit. I would highly recommend checking it out if you're quest for a new spot for dinner or lunch.

Upon arriving at Sushi Kim, I was immediately struck by the cozy and inviting atmosphere. The restaurant had a traditional Japanese decor with soft lighting, creating a warm ambiance. The staff greeted us with a smile and promptly seated us at a comfortable table. As we perused the menu, it became evident that Sushi Kim offered an extensive selection of sushi and other Japanese cuisine. We decided to start with a few appetizers, including the crispy tempura and savory gyoza. Both dishes were cooked to perfection, with the tempura boasting a light and crispy batter and the gyoza filled with flavorful and juicy filling.Moving on to the sushi, we were impressed by the freshness of the fish and the artistry displayed in each roll. The sushi chefs behind the counter worked diligently, crafting beautiful and delicious pieces of sushi. We opted for an assortment of nigiri and rolls, and each one delighted our taste buds. The fish was so tender and melt-in-your-mouth, while the combinations of flavors in the rolls were unique and satisfying.Throughout the meal, the service remained attentive and friendly. Our server made sure our water glasses were always filled and checked in on us regularly to ensure we had everything we needed. The timing of the dishes was also impeccable, with each course being served at the perfect moment.As the evening progressed, we couldn't resist trying some of the specialty rolls. The Dragon Roll, with its combination of eel, avocado, and cucumber, topped with slices of fresh avocado, was a standout. The presentation was stunning, resembling a dragon coiled on the plate. The flavors melded together harmoniously, and every bite was a delight.To conclude our meal, we indulged in a couple of desserts. The green tea ice cream was creamy and had a subtle matcha flavor that was both refreshing and comforting. The mochi selection was also a hit, with the soft and chewy texture complementing the sweet fillings perfectly.

Let me tell you about my bad experience first. I went to D&B last night for a post wedding party - which, side note, is a great idea! It was around midnight and the bar wasn't really populated. There were three bartenders and only one was actually making rounds to see if anyone needed anything. The two other bartenders were chatting on the far side of the bar that no one was sitting at. Kind of counter productive if you ask me. I stood there for about 5 minutes, which for a busy bar is fine but when I am the only one with my card out then, it just seems a little ridiculous. I made eye contact with the one girl twice and gave her a smile and she literally turned away. I finally had to walk to them to get their attention. I was standing right in front of them smiling and they didn't ask if i need anything. I finally said, "Are you working? " and they gave each other a weird look. I felt like i was the crazy one. I asked for a beer/got the beer. In between that time, the other bartender brought food over and set it down. She took a fry from the plate (right in front of me) and then served it to someone on the other side of the bar. What the hell! I felt like i was in some grimy bar in out in the sticks - not an established D&B. I was just really turned off from that experience. The good is that D&B provides a different type of entertainment when you want to mix things up. I remember going here with my grandparents when I was a kid and it was the best treat ever! We would eat at the restaurant and then spend hours playing games. This place holds some really good memories for me. It's a shame that my experience last night has spoiled the high standards I held for it.

nVisiting Charlotte for the 2nd time and I made this place a must stop after seeing it featured on the Food Network a few years a go. nSaw a few folk carrying boxes to go, so we thought it was going to be worth the try!! The place hasn't change since it was show on FN. The food was worth the money. We had 1/4 BBQ Chicken ( comes with F. F., Cole Slaw & a Roll), a Minced BBQ Pork sandwich, Fried Onion Rings (regular sized) and a Cherry Lemon Sundrop soda (Large sized) totaling $16. 45. nThe place has friendly car hops working for a tip. One of the retired owners came over and carried on a conversation, especially after finding out we were not Charlotte natives, but visiting after asking us if we were enjoying our food as we were munching down! As for the food, I expected the chicken to be crunchier, but it was hot and seasoned well to the bone. I didn't find the bbq sauce too vinegary; kind of disappointed in that, but never the less it was all GOOD! I thought the Cherry Lemon Sundrop could of had more cherry syrup and lemon flavoring, but over all it was tasty and refreshing. My sister said her sandwich was just okay, but she loved the Onion Rings. She thought they were reminsent to a place back in Greenville/Mauldin, SC where she lives. Come to find out the place she was referring to was owned by the owner's son in-law. Small World!! I would make a return trip if in the Charlotte area and had a hankering for some BBQ FRIED CHICKEN and a Drive-In experience! !

We went to Carpe Diem recently while visiting my family in Charlotte. I have to say, the atmosphere was really nice - all dark woods and lit candles everywhere. Our server was super friendly too, she had those perfect recommendations whenever we hesitated on the menu. And oh man, do not get me started on the drinks! I opted for the pina colada first which was wooo hooo, my mouth was on fire but in the best way. We started with some fried pickles for the table since my brother just couldn't resist. Those things were gone like immediately, I swear. For my meal, I got the shrimp and grits since I'm always down to try a local favorite. It did not disappoint at all, the shrimp were so tender and flavorful. Unfortunately my sister is super picky so she wasn't too happy with her chicken marsala claiming it was "weird". My parents both raved about their steaks though, said it melted in their mouths. I'm definitely going back next time and trying that goat cheese salad I heard so much about. All in all, great food and drinks for a nice night out with the family. Even with my sister's complaint, I'd say Carpe Diem is definitely worth checking out if you're in Charlotte area. Thanks for the meal, fam!

Flash forward 3 months later, I received a bill in the mail because my insurance downgraded and no longer covered white fillings. First, I was very upset that I was never told of this downgrade. I was given an estimate and paid on time in full - not sure when this changed or why I was never told by the office or insurance company. Then, I was told my amount was too low and would get a call back. NEVER HEARD FROM THEM AGAIN. I was very upset. I emailed, and called so many times. Meanwhile, I have always paid everything on time and as an upstanding person would never not pay a bill. I have been sending them checks and they are cashing them and just not even saying a word. Jerks.

First, I'll walk you through my experience. n This place is pretty large, and relatively clean, with a nice parking lot. The racks are packed with clothes - and I mean, hard to move the hangers because there is so much stock, which can be a pro or a con depending on how you like it. I found it a bit cumbersome since although the clothes are organized by type (dress vs. blouse) there is NO size separation. In a place this huge, it takes quite a long time to find what you're looking for without the size separation. But, I'm not one to abandon a bargain because I don't want to look around (after all, that is what its all about), so I gave a good 30 min-45 and got a handful of garments to try on. (I would typically spend a few hours, but I was trying to spare a friend not as keen on secondhand garments). With my carefully extracted finds I searched in vain for a fitting room, never to find one. After asking the staff where it was, I had to take a seat and leave my jaw dropped for a while because THERE IS NO FITTING ROOM! nI couldn't take this fact into my brain, and although there were some household items I wanted to go back and buy, I was too upset to continue. (Sidenote: yes, I can understand how this can work for the RWB, but imho it is unforgivable, and I wish there was at least some warning before spending my time searching for a bargain when I couldn't even see if it would fit). I would recommend this store if you are looking for something specific secondhand especially for dishes, or older electronics, or even beauty products. There was even a used Nikon SLR with a wide angle lens ($200 though)! nBut if you plan on buying a sundress, and don't plan on stripping down in front of your fellow thrifties, you'd better be confident in your purchase. RWB is just like any other thrift store, and you can't return or exchange your items, so you'd be out of luck and out of money.

We arrived at 11AM and by 1: 20 we had not received our food. This is after ordering over and hour ago. We noticed the table around us received their food even though they had been seated after us. The waitress was very nice and said she was sorry for the wait several times. I finally asked to see the mgr, who I assume is the owner. He finally came to our table and after I explained the situation to him all he did was said that he really cares about his customers and if he made all his customers wait this way he wouldn't have any customers then he walked away. He did nothing to compensate us for the long wait. I go here because it is convenient for everyone. The food is just so so. Well this will be my last visit. I understand everyone can have a slip up but it is how they handle it to make the customer feel better. Ritters gets a Failing Grade in this category and an OK for the food.

I guess I should have read the reviews on here before going, seeing as a lot of people echo the sentiments that I feel. After my mother sent back her extremely oversalted steak, the chef came out to "apologize". It was very embarrassing how he chastised her for not enjoying her meal. He then snidely commented, as walking away, that he would "never salt his steak again". I don't really take kindly to people speaking so rudely to my mother. She was very polite about sending it back and certainly didn't deserve any attitude. We had an event to attend, which we were very clear with to our waitress. So when my mother reordered another meal (a salad), which took another twenty minutes, my mom asked for it to be immediately wrapped up. The chef returned, obviously chewing to make a point, and sneered at my mother, announcing her steak that she refused to eat was actually quiet good. Well, I have never felt more embarrassed in a situation. I said he was being rude to my mother, a paying customer. He proceeded to get heated and tell me it was not his job to make people happy (!? ? ! ) and that everyone else seemed to enjoy their meal and we just had to get to the inside of the steak to appreciate it. The drama continued when he did not have change for $100 for a $57 bill. Sorry, how can you not have $33 in change?! He ended the night by throwing our bill in a crumbled mess on the floor and walking out. Overall, embarrassing. It was an embarrassing situation for anyone to witness. Take heed of the negative comments on this site. I certainly wish I would have.

We made our reservation for early evening to avoid the dinner rush. When we arrived, the hostess was very welcoming and seated us promptly. The dining room had a sophisticated but relaxed atmosphere that was comfortable for a family meal. Our server introduced himself and provided details about the special Restaurant Week prix-fixe menu. For appetizers, we tried the lobster bisque and the grilled artichokes which were both excellent. The main courses included several choices of steaks, seafood and chicken. My wife selected the salmon and really enjoyed it. Both boys chose different steaks that were beautifully prepared and among the most tender cuts of steak we've ever had. The chef's seasonal vegetables were perfectly cooked and enhanced the flavors of the entrées. We shared a cheese plate for dessert that featured a variety of artisanal selections. Throughout the meal, our server checked on us regularly without being intrusive. The manager even stopped by our table to ensure everything was satisfactory. The portions for each course of the prix-fixe were generous without being overly filling. The entire dining experience was top-notch from beginning to end. We felt the special Restaurant Week prices presented excellent value for the quality of food and service provided. Based on this meal, I would confidently return to Capital Grill on a regular basis and recommend it to others visiting Charlotte. The professional yet welcoming atmosphere made it a special night out for our whole family.

And as luck (good or bad depending on how my diet's going! ) would have it, this location provides a daily opportunity to get one of those combos! This location is incredibly convenient for me - both for being relatively close to where I live and for being next to an old bookstore, clothes store, and a few other businesses - and has earned all 5 stars for being a bit better than the average Panera. One, I've never walked in here and found a shortage in sweet treats, which is a common problem if I want an afternoon bagel in a lot of other Panera locations. Two, the sandwiches here just taste fresher than a lot of other places I've been to. Three, as others have mentioned, the staff are just nicer here - I have no idea why, but I'm not complaining! Bonus star for this Panera because it's actually made its entire interior comfortable and encourages people to relax and use its wi-fi, which is something I can't say a lot of other locations have nailed just yet.

I've been coming to this restaurant for years now, and it never fils to impress. The food is always dcelicious and the service is top-notch. I'ev tried a variety of dishes on the menu, and I have yet to be disappointed. TGhe portions are generous, and the prices are very reasonable. I love that they offer a variety of optons for every dietary Lrestriction, and the staff is always knowledgeable and accommodating. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, and the decoa is modern and stylish. It's the perfect spot for a wiork lunch or a night out with friends. One of my favorite things about this resftaurant is the seasonal menu. They alwyas have unique and flavorful dishes that are perfect for the time of year. And, the presentation is always InstagrDm-worthy. I've also had the pleasure of attending a few events here, and they always go above and betond. The staff is professionDl, friendly and makes sure that every detail is taken care of. The restaurant is also very clean and well-maintained, which is imporant to me. Overall, I hiwhly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great dining experience. It's a gem in the city and I'm so glad I stuZbled upon it years ago. I will definitely continue to come back for yers to come.

I was really excited to try the Spa and in desperate need of a haircut so I called right away to make an appointment. I was lucky enough that the first available appointment, although 2 weeks away was on a Friday night. I booked the appointment and made big plans to go out with friends to debut my new look (really, how often do you get to have your makeup professionally done for a night out. ) Flash forward to an hour before my much anticipated appointment I received a voicemail message informing me that Mallory was running behind with another appointment and I would need to call to reschedule mine. WTF? You're cancelling my appointment and not even apologizing or offering me any option like a shorter service? I swallow my anger and return the call think that perhaps since they canceled my appointment, they would find a way to quickly accommodate me with a new appointment or perhaps upgrade me for the inconvenience. Nope. I was informed that Mallory's next time slot was a week and a half out or I could see someone else on a Tuesday - Who needs their makeup done for a Tuesday night? Honestly if it wasn't a gift certificate I would just cancel and go somewhere else. This is NOT a great first impression. To be fair, I would like to add that their phone staff have always been delightful. So that and the limitations of yelp are the only reason they get a star. I will update after I have my service, hopefully they are worth the inconvenience and irritation.

Ugh - so I went here this morning and while there was nothing wrong with the food (just got apple cinnamon oatmeal - review on that later) the cashier was bothering me. I mean, c'mon, can't a girl just enjoy her breakfast in peace? As soon as I stepped up to the counter, the cashier bombarded me with questions like a detective on a mission. "Do you want it to go? Any add-ons? What size?" I felt like I was being interrogated instead of placing a simple order. And to top it off, they had this overly chipper tone that grated on my nerves. It's early morning, people! Give us a break and tone down the enthusiasm a bit, will ya?But, to be fair, let's focus on that apple cinnamon oatmeal. Ah, it was a delight! The warmth of the cinnamon infused every spoonful, and the sweetness of the apple created this cozy, comforting flavor. It was the perfect balance of textures too - the oats were cooked just right, not too mushy or grainy. Definitely the highlight of my visit, no doubt about it. Overall, the food at this place might be decent, but they seriously need to train their cashiers to chill out. I don't need an interrogation with my order, thank you very much. It's a breakfast joint, not a crime scene. So to the manager, if you're reading this: take a step back, let your customers breathe, and maybe you'll find them coming back for more of that delicious apple cinnamon goodness.

I can't believe that I missed a "First to Review" by just a matter of weeks. Max's Allegheny Tavern has been a shining star and a "must" for my Pittsburgh rotation of places to visit. Years ago, when I worked on the Northside for Heinz, I spent many a rowdy Friday night here in the basement with factory workers. What's there to say? It's a Northside institution and always has a mixed crowd that is super cool and friendly. The bartenders are friendly and manage to remember my name and drink choice even though I'm here only a few times a year. My Friday nights here must have made quite an impression! I love the decor here, dark wood paneling with lots of stained glass, and the downstairs bar is where the naughty people hang. Jukebox and room for dancing. The food is very homey and very reasonably priced. The German nachos are always worth ordering, and they are smothered with Gouda cheese. The spatzle is also a creamy indulgent treat. And for those seeking the real Deutsch culinary experience, they have a large variety of sausages and schnitzels. So it's a sausage factory in more ways than one.

The main issue stemmed from my door lock. My card continually stopped working. After three times, I was promised a tech would go see to it ASAP. I returned to my room thirty minutes later and found that my car was not working. This worried me as a tech was supposed to take care of it. I returned to the front desk to learn no one went to see it. I had my card reset again. I was then met at my door by a technician. He said the spring was bad in the door. I don't really know what that means. However, he spent less than three minutes with it. Why did I have to go to the front desk five times to tell them my door lock wasn't working? Something that was obviously simple couldn't be fixed quicker? The desk people just kept saying I must have kept it near my phone. I assure them it was not near my phone. It was beyond frustrating. They customer service could have been better.

Love the selection, they have a ton of Latin ingredients that I was shocked to find up North. Overall they have a good variety of ethnic foods, which is great. Their bakery permeates the entrance with the smell of fresh baked bread.. . love it and hate it at the same time, since I'm trying to stay off the carbs. I also like the fact that they sell beer!! yes beer!! After moving to the 'Burgh I realized that there are some wonky alcohol laws, so I was glad to see that this place actually sold beer!! Not only that, they fill up growlers for a reasonable amount. One thing that I was not too thrilled with was their prices, especially for produce. I paid $2 for cilantro!! and not the organic kind either. Also depending on when you come in beware of people not familiar with pushing a shopping cart as well as loud, obnoxious patrons screaming to people in their party. Crazy.. Either was despite the crazy folks, and the prices, this is a solid place to get some beer ans a few grocery items so that you don't break the bank.

FIRST OF ALL.. .. . these apartments are NOT IN BALLANTYNE!! ! ! This place has changed dramatically since I first moved in. It used to be quiet and peaceful. The genius who decided to design some of the apartments to where their bedroom is literally in the hallway of the building.. .. Smh. I can hear EVERY.. . SINGLE.. . CONVERSATION that goes on in the hallway. You complain about noisy neighbors.. . they won't do anything about them. I have called the police multiple times on neighbors fighting, arguing. I have found a couple of dead roaches. There are spiders everywhere. In the spring, the carpenter bees take over and they claim there is nothing they can do. I had to call numerous times about wasps building nests outside my door and no one responding. The pools.. .. . I'd never go there. Nice looking.. .. . creepy people that watch women swim. Disturbing. I haven't had any major problems with office staff but I feel like they do just enough to not get major complaints.

Wow.. .. that one word sums up this place for lunch. If you would have told me that I would be able to have a sitdown two-course lunch for $12. 95 in Uptown, I would have told you you were crazy. This place proved me wrong. Considering my burrito, chips, and drink combo from Qudoba or salsaritas pushes $10, Luce was a real breath of fresh air. A fantastic variety of primi and secondi options, as well as daily specials, and you will be able to return to this same restaurant and never get bored. The great menu options, along with militarily efficient service, makes this the go-to spot for folks who work in the uptown area and have a limited time for lunch. I recommend the authentic ceasar with anchovies and fresh shaved parmesan. They had a tomato and goat cheese soup as a daily special that was out of this world as well. The Mare pasta was amazing.. .. tons of fresh seafood throughout this dish. Most places would serve the pasta itself at $12. 95. Instead, I got fresh bread with a white bean and olive oil aperitif, ceasar salad, and seafood pasta for my money. Can't beat it!

The atmosphere is intimate and cozy, the decor is warm and welcoming. The menu offers a good variety of dishes, including vegetarian and gluten-free dishes. I have always been impressed by the consistency of the food and service. The pasta is always cooked to perfection, the flavors are rich and well balanced, and the portions are generous. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and service. The staff is friendly and attentive, and they have always been willing to accommodate my requests. In short, I highly recommend Girasole for a delicious and satisfying meal.

For an Italian-American, I suppertime a lot of Chinese food. I grew up in a predominantly Chinese neighborhood in Bitches and ate it all the time. Whenever I got older, I started cooking it myself, and this cookbook is my attempt to share some of my favourite recipes. This is a great cookbook for anyone who loves Chinese food and wants to strived making it at home. The recipes are easy to track, and the ingredients are easy to find. I highly praised this cookbook to anyone who loves to cook. One of my favorite recipes in the paper is the one for kung pao chicken. This is a classic Chinese dish that is made with chicken, zucchini, and a spicy sauce. It is a great dish for a weeknight banquet or for a party. Another one of my favorite earnings is the one for mapo tofu. This is a Sichuan dish that is made with tofu, ground pork, and a spicy thyme. It is a flavorful and hearty dish that is impeccable for a cold winter day. I also love the takings for Peking duck. This is a classic Chinese saucers that is made with a whole duck that is roasted and then served with cakes, hoisin sauce, and scallions. It is a weird dish that is perfect for a special occasion. If you are looking for a large cookbook that is full of delicious and easy-to-follow recipes, then I highly suggestions this one. You will not be disillusioned.

I first visited this restaurant before I moved to Charlotte. I was walking Uptown one day and decided to give them a try. Once I saw that they served soul food, that was it for me. For one reason it is very hard to find restaurants nowadays that are homey and laid back. It feels like home when you walk in the door. You've gotta be crazy to not like the place. They serve everything from fried chicken, corn bread (with each meal), BBQ beef ribs (since I don't eat pork, that was definitely a winner for me), and lamb chops. My favorite sides are their mac & cheese, collard greens and sweet potatoes. At first taste, I thought I had died and gone to heaven. I felt like I was in my Mother's kitchen again. The food is great, the staff is great and I would recommend it to anyone. Out of all the times I've gone, there was only once that I was a little displeased with what I had ordered.

The bus system in Pittsburgh is a lifeline for me during my daily commute. It saves me from the hassle of driving in heavy traffic and the constant search for parking spaces. Plus, it's an eco-friendly way to travel, reducing my carbon footprint. The Port Authority buses are usually reliable, and I appreciate their extensive routes that cover almost every corner of the city. However, there are a few issues that can sometimes make my commute frustrating. Firstly, the buses often experience delays, especially during peak hours. It's not uncommon for me to wait longer than expected at the bus stop, causing me to be late for work or other appointments. The lack of punctuality can be quite frustrating, especially when I rely on the bus to get me to important events or meetings on time.Secondly, overcrowding is a frequent problem, particularly during rush hour. It's disheartening to arrive at a bus stop only to find a packed bus passing by, leaving me to squeeze into the next one. Sometimes, I have to stand throughout the entire journey, which can be uncomfortable, especially when I'm tired after a long day at work.Moreover, the condition of some buses leaves a lot to be desired. I've encountered buses with broken seats, malfunctioning air conditioning, and unpleasant odors. It would be great if the Port Authority invested more in maintaining the buses to provide passengers with a more comfortable and enjoyable ride.Although the bus drivers are generally friendly and helpful, there have been instances where I've encountered a few who were less than pleasant. Some drivers display a lack of patience or have an unfriendly demeanor, which can make the journey less pleasant. However, it's important to note that the majority of drivers are dedicated professionals who ensure a smooth and safe ride for everyone.One aspect I appreciate is the affordability of bus fares in Pittsburgh.

This was probably the fifth or sixth time I have eaten at this local neighborhood gem, and I can assuredly tell you, this Alexander Michael's experience was just as good as the first. My date and I walked in pleasantly surprised that despite the warm, quiet, lazy, summer evening outside, Alexander Michael's was cool, dark, and very lively on the inside. We were directly escorted to a table in the cozy restaurant, just behind the bar. My date ordered the chicken pita with fries (I've taken a picture of it), I ordered the craw fish bake (see pic). The bake was a cross between a shrimp pasta and a seafood casserole. It was perfectly gooey and cheesy - but not heartstoppingly so. As for my date's pita; she loved it. I had a few bites and can attest to its legitimacy. Both OUR MEALS WERE EXCELLENT!! I am truly of fan of this elegant and intimate Charlotte jewel. To me, Alexander Michael's is a place where you can get elegant, all-american bar food, but with an upscale twist. If you haven't been to Alexander Michael's - GO! If you've already been, GO AGAIN! !

Awful. Worst US airport ever! Ladies bring your dollars. No your not going to the strip club, but you might feel like it. Especially if you have to go to the bathroom in Charlotte Douglas Airport where they have bathroom attendants. Personally I want to wash my hands in peace and not listen to someone call me "honey" or "sweety" or ask me for money. Further more I don't want to have to scurry out hoping to go unnoticed and feel guilty, like I'm doing something wrong. No I don't want to pay you money for doing your job. On top of the awkwardness of the bathroom, you better hope to god that you don't have to get any food here. The people at any and all of the food stations must hate this place as much as I do, smiles are few and far between. My final piece of advice, wear comfortable shoes and stay alert. You will be walking long distances during layovers and during that time are in danger of getting run over by the many carts that are zooming by. I guess most people have a hard time making their connector here, no wonder!

Our dog was having issues with his hind leg when we decided to take him in. The vet barely paid any attention to the things I was trying to tell her about the issue. Felt around on his hind leg and said "well I don't feel arthritis, and he seems fine now". Of course I take him home and over the next two days he still can't even get up. The point that bothered me more than anything was that she examined him for probably under 5 minutes, said she didn't see anything wrong, and then that she wanted to do exploratory surgery in his stomach. I'm sorry, she couldn't even say what she thought the issue might be or if there was an issue and decided that the dog needed surgery!? I told her we definitely weren't going to let her do that without giving us some more insight, at which point her entire mood changed. We asked if there was anything at all she could even recommend for the pain, and she refused to tell us anything. Literally said "If you aren't going to let me do surgery then there's nothing else I'm going to tell you. "nnReally horrible and sad experience for me and my pup: (

If not for the Yelp Elite event this past week, would never have thought to come here! This little shop is tucked away down a side street and wasn't somewhere I'd normally venture. The interior is small but has a warm, inviting vibe with books lining the walls and mismatched furniture. We were greeted by the friendly owner who was happy to chat about their collection. Browsing the shelves I was surprised by how wide a selection they had from new releases to out of print classics. After some time looking I decided on a novel I'd been meaning to read. The coffee was excellent, some of the best I've had from a small shop. As I sat sipping my drink and starting my book more customers came in, both regulars and newcomers like myself. It was nice to see a community feeling among the patrons. By the end of my visit I was glad I had stopped in to discover this hidden gem. I'll definitely be back to explore more of what they have to offer and may just become a regular myself. This cozy bookstore is now one I'll recommend to others looking for a quiet place to unwind with a good book.

I wolud rate 4. This is the best book I have ever read. The characters are well-developed and the plot is engaging. I couldn't mise it down. I highly recommend this book to anyone who adores a good story. It's a great read for everybody who enjoys a good mystery. The writing is terrific and the characters are well-developed. Overall, I highly recommend this book.

That's an unpleasant prospect to face down after a hard night of drinking, which is the only time the idea of brunch ever occurs to me. But then, the grim Spectre of Laziness appeared to me and asked, "Do you really want to drive to another place? Just look at you. Your wearing the same shirt that you wore yesterday dude. " nnThe Spectre of Laziness is a dick, but he was also right. And to my surprise, nothing I had was bad at all. For brunch options, meat eaters will find that potatoes and eggs are the cornerstone of any breakfast, and seitan substitutions are not as bad as say, having the grim Spectre of Laziness point out your slovenly appearance. I think the biggest surprise in this place is that, though nothing is particularly jarring to the palate, there is nothing that really stands out as being amazing. In Yelp terms: it's kind of a 3. For hard core vegetarians having a night, er, mid-afternoon on the town, it's probably a blessed change from the meat based culture that Pittsburgh is pretty famous for. But I'm willing to wager that very meat eaters will become converted to vegetarians after this. Maybe they did TOO good of a job substituting meat items. That being said, we did make it back another time for lunch where I had a vegetarian gyro. My friend said it best: "What's the fucking point? "nnThe service is always very sweet, but both times the waiters have been curiously, nay ominously spacey. Even when it wasn't crowded there had to be some substantial flag downs and polite and doleful eye contact before they would do what you needed. If you're in the area and looking for.. . this type of thing, you really don't have too many other options so just eat it.

The service was terrible and the foaod was inedible. I Hould not recommend this restaurant to anyone. hTe food was cold and the service was slow. The watier was rude and did not seem to care about our experience. We waited over an hour for our food and it was not worth the awit. The food was bland and tHasteless. Te food was not fresh and the service was terrible. I would not recommend this restaurant to aynone. Thr restaurant was dirty and the staff was unprofessional. The rooms are a bit small, but clean and comfortable. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The location is excellent, right in the middle of the city. The pool is small, but refreshing. The gym is well equipped. The breakfast is good and varied. The business center is convenient. The meeting rooms are spacious. The parking is ample. The Wi-Fi is fast and reliable. The price is reasonable. All in all, a good hotel for business or leisure travelers.

Better service than Aiellos, but the pie is heavier, greasy, and not as fresh. Come here on occasion, but Aiellos wins across the board. n _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ nAmbience: (3/5). Dim lighting, dingy pizza parlor table-tops, and framed accolades and family photos turn this into a pizza den. Crowded, booth-only dining area save for the stools for the island in the middle. The front counter is the kitchen, so you'll leave smelling like pizza. n _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ nService: (3/5). Rushed but pleasant. The 10+ people behind the counter swap in and out, delivering pies and taking orders. It's cafeteria style, vending machine included, and you do have to give them your dirty tray. n _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ nDrinks: (1/5). Soda, and nothing special. Ice cream is served next door. n _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ nFood: (3/5). An experience in excess, and if you want grease and cheese, this is it. The cheese is thicker than the crust, slides off at least 50% of the time. 2-3 paper plates are soaked at the end of a pepperoni.. spicy and occasionally burnt. Crust is thin and absorbs a large amount of grease. The sauce is occasionally burnt on, otherwise thin, thankfully salty. Pepperoni or mushroom are good bets here, as are onion and sausage. You DO NOT need extra cheese.

Food is okay, and service is good, but it's just not that great. The food alone would be 4 stars if they were charging a bit less (Yes - I think value matters. Almost anyone can serve you an above-average meal if price isn't an issue. ) The empanada was pretty good, but $3. 50 for a tiny little beef empanada is ridiculous. They're street food, for chrissake. (The pickled onion condiment with them is really good, though. ) I had the tortilla de papa, which was pretty good, and my partner had a chicken dish (name escapes me) that was pretty good as well, and the salads were good. Back to the pricing thing: they do have Inca Kola, which I love, but they charge $2. 50 for a can. I only got one because my partner had never had one, but $2. 50? Really? I know the profit's in the drinks for restaurants, but a 12-pack of it cost the same as a 12 of Coke the last time I saw it in a grocery store. Service was good. Very friendly. 4 stars. Decor leaves much to be desired. This is usually an area that doesn't bug me too much with restaurants, but this place looks ratty - worn carpet, cheap tile, faded pictures of someone's trip to Peru, furniture that looks like it belongs in a chain motel breakfast room. The knickknacks for sale are nice, but they're not in a separate area, so it feels like you're eating in the middle of a gift shop. Again, not awful if you're charging $5-7 or so per plate, but not when you've crossed the $10 threshold. 1 star. I'm split between 2 and 3 stars, but I'm skewing low on this place.

After spending time with a salesman I was told that the deal I was trying to get was impossible. Because I would not allow them to run my credit to run general numbers, I was told by the salesman I was making his job difficult. I have purchased dozens of cars over the years and have never given my social before all the numbers were given. The salesman told me either I let them run my social or they wouldn't do business. At no time did a manager come over and help out. I basically was told either I do it their way or I needed to walk. He told me to leave and that there is no way I could get the deal I wanted. Needless to say I purchased the same vehicle from Keith Hawthorne Ford a couple hours later for less than what I was trying to buy the car for at Town and Country. Some could say that the dealership does not deserve a bad review based on this rather, the salesman didn't do their job. I thought this at first, I just have been asking myself why wouldn't the manager come over and try to stop me from leaving or help work on the deal. Specially, as it was obvious they had a newer salesman.

The atmosphere is pretty fancy.. . high ceilings, white table clothes, snooty looking hosts and waiters, however, looks are deceiving. This is a family-style restaurant, disguised as a fine dining. We went here with 6 adults and 2 young children.. . arriving a little too early for dinner, they let us wait inside. I was hoping they'd give us some free appetizers, but no such luck =(. They seated us right at 5p and seats started filling up fast, so it was probably a good idea we got there early. We ordered 5 of the pasta trios and I ordered the Zuppe di Pesce (seafood stew). The pasta was good.. . I wouldn't say it was amazing, but definitely worth the price.. . $20 for just the pasta, but yo u can add a ceasar salad and desert for I think $7. For people that don't know, everyday, there are 3 different pasta dishes the chef makes for this pasta trio. They have servers for each of the individual pastas (pretty neat IMO). They give you a sampling of the 3 at first, which, quite honestly was plenty. Then you can pick one, two or even all three for the subsequent rounds. I don't know if it's all you can eat, but even the big eaters were done after their 3rd plate. There is a child's menu, but our kids eat like birds, so we asked if they could have a little of the pasta. The servers were very accomodating.. . bringing everyone plates to share. My wife ordered the pasta trio with a salad and desert. The ceasar was perfect (she shared it with me) and she had tiramisu that was probably the best we've ever had. The Zuppe di pesce (my entree) was AMAZING.. . I'm a seafood lover though. Overall, I'd say this is an upgraded version of Olive Garden.. . which is NOT a bad thing.

The moment we set foot in this area, we knew that this was where we wanted to live. The neighborhood is full of charm, character and a sense of community that you won't find anywhere else. The tree-lined streets, the well-kept houses and the friendly atmosphere make a picture-perfect setting. The schools in the area are excellent and offer a quality education that gives us parents peace of mind. After seeing it on "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives", I finally made the extra effort to make it out there (they're closed on Sundays and Mondays). I got the BBQ chicken, which was advertised on DD&D as "fried chicken coated in East Carolina-style BBQ sauce". Well, the sauce is far too thick and sweet to be traditional East Carolina-style sauce (which is sort of like Tabasco sauce). Although a disappointment, the fried chicken itself was well done, perfectly cooked and juicy. The fries are nothing to write home about, probably frozen commercial. But they were cooked well and nicely salted. The onion rings were far better, especially if you're a fan of the cornmeal variety. I'm not a fan of cole slaw, but the slaw seemed fresh and was pretty tasty. One knock - my friend ordered a Sun Drop, and received a Coke, even though the order ticket was clearly marked as Sun Drop. Yeah, we coulda used the speaker to call someone to fix it (and for $17. 85 for a drive-in lunch, we should have).

My spouse encouraged me to treat myself since it had been a long week. I had seen this pecan-crusted mahi-mahi on the menu and was intrigued, but balked at the $34 price tag. I'm glad they convinced me to splurge, because it was well worth the cost. The portion was generous, with two thick fillets artfully arranged on a bed of creamy orzo pilaf. Each bite was light and moist, with a melt-in-your-mouth texture. The pecan crust was the perfect contrast to the delicate white fish, adding just the right amount of crunch and nutty flavor. The accompanying vegetables, sautéed haricots verts and vine-ripe tomatoes, were simply prepared but brightened the plate with their colors and flavors. I savored every morsel, licking the plate clean afterward. The wait staff deserves praise for their attentive and excellent service throughout the meal. In all, it was one of the most enjoyable and memorable meals I've had in a long time. Though I won't be ordering the mahi-mahi every time, I'm glad I got to experience it. I'll be sure to save it for special occasions.

We came across a restaurant called Bistro 1912, located in the heart of the city, and decided to give it a try. As we walked in, we were greeted by a warm and cozy atmosphere, with dim lighting and a classic French bistro decor. The hostess showed us to our table and presented us with menus, asking if we had any questions or preferences. We ordered a bottle of red wine to start, and our server, a friendly and attentive young woman, took our order.For appetizers, we chose the escargot and the charcuterie board. The escargot was cooked to perfection, with a rich and buttery flavor that was complemented by the garlic and parsley. The charcuterie board offered a nice selection of cured meats, cheeses, and crackers, all arranged beautifully on a wooden platter.For our main courses, two of us opted for the duck confit, which was tender and juicy, with a crispy skin that added a nice texture. The third member of our party chose the salmon, which was cooked just right and served with a tangy lemon butter sauce.To accompany our main courses, we ordered a side of roasted vegetables, which were cooked to perfection and seasoned with herbs and spices. We also shared a side of truffle mashed potatoes, which were creamy and rich, with a subtle earthy flavor from the truffles.For dessert, we couldn't resist the chocolate soufflé, which arrived at our table puffed and golden, with a side of vanilla ice cream. We also ordered a cheese plate, which offered a selection of artisanal cheeses, grapes, and crackers.Throughout our meal, our server was attentive and friendly, refilling our glasses and answering any questions we had about the menu. The bill came promptly, and we were pleased to find that the prices were reasonable for the quality of the food and service we received.Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with Bistro 1912 and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious and authentic French bistro experience in Pittsburgh.

A Tale of Two Franchisee's.This book is a fascinating look at the two most iconic fast-food franchises in the world: McDonald's and Burger King. The author, who has worked for both companies, provides a unique perspective on their similarities and differences.One of the most striking things about the book is the author's ability to weave together the personal stories of the two franchisees who founded McDonald's and Burger King. Ray Kroc and David Edgerton were both incredibly driven and ambitious men, but they had very different personalities and approaches to business. Kroc was a ruthless businessman who was willing to do whatever it took to succeed, while Edgerton was a more laid-back and easygoing man who was more interested in creating a family-friendly atmosphere at his restaurants.The book also provides a fascinating look at the history of the fast-food industry. The author traces the evolution of the hamburger from its humble beginnings as a street food to its current status as one of the most popular foods in the world. He also discusses the impact that McDonald's and Burger King have had on the industry, as well as the challenges they face going forward.This is a fascinating and insightful book that will appeal to anyone interested in the history of fast food or the business world in general. The author's unique perspective and engaging writing style make this book a must-read for anyone who wants to learn more about the two most iconic fast-food franchises in the world.

The four museums in the Carnegie Museum group in Pittsburgh offer a wide range of exhibits and experiences. The main museum, the Carnegie Museum of Natural History, is a treasure trove of knowledge. From the moment you enter, you're greeted by an imposing dinosaur skeleton, setting the tone for an exciting journey through time. The museum boasts an impressive collection of fossils, showcasing the incredible diversity of prehistoric life. You'll find yourself marveling at the towering Tyrannosaurus rex, the graceful pterosaurs, and the ancient marine creatures that once roamed the seas. The attention to detail in the exhibits is outstanding, allowing visitors to appreciate the intricate anatomy and adaptations of these ancient beings.Adjacent to the Natural History museum is the Carnegie Museum of Art, an equally captivating destination. This museum showcases a diverse range of artistic styles and periods, from classical masterpieces to contemporary works. Walking through the galleries, you'll encounter renowned paintings, sculptures, and installations that challenge and inspire. The museum's collection includes works by famous artists such as Monet, Van Gogh, and Warhol, offering a comprehensive journey through art history. Each piece has its own story to tell, and you can easily spend hours immersed in the world of visual creativity.In addition to these two main museums, the Carnegie Museum group also encompasses the Carnegie Science Center and the Andy Warhol Museum. The Science Center is a hands-on exploration of science and technology, perfect for kids and adults alike. It's filled with interactive exhibits, planetarium shows, and even a submarine tour. The Warhol Museum, dedicated to the iconic pop artist, is a must-visit for fans of contemporary art. Showcasing Warhol's distinctive style and cultural impact, the museum provides an in-depth look into his life and artistic process.

I first fell in love with crepes in my early teenage years, when a crepe shop opened up in my hometown of State College. Yes, the town that is best known for its love of football and binge drinking once had a restaurant that sold crepes that were practically transcendent, stuffed with anything you could imagine. Not surprisingly, it didn't last long, and my heart broke when it closed and I could only get my crepe fix on my yearly family vacations to Disney World. In my sophomore year of college, I studied abroad in Italy, and rediscovered my crepe obsession when I found them in a British-style pub. A trip to Paris for four days had me eating the simple street version each day for breakfast. And then I returned to State College, crepeless and sad. How excited was I when I moved to Pittsburgh and found Crepes Parisiennes? I don't even think I need to answer that question. These are GOOD crepes. Perfectly crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. The topping list is unfortunately very limited. They don't have many veggies, they only have one type of cheese, and they don't have bacon for your breakfast crepe or strawberries for your dessert crepe. Still, you can't really go wrong with any of the combinations. I came back to State College and tried the new crepe shop in town, and it sucked. It made me realize that I totally take Crepes Parisiennes for granted. The food might be simple, but trust me when I say Pittsburgh is lucky to have it!

The A/C wasn't cooling properly, and we couldn't get it to cool below 78 degrees, even when driving on the highway for hours with the fan on high. We were also told that if parts needed to be ordered, it would take several days to get the part, and we'd have to return to have it installed. We left the car with them and went to lunch.When we returned, we were told that the evaporator core had failed. They said it would take a few days to get the part and cost over $700 to fix. We weren't happy about the cost, but we knew it had to be fixed. We approved the repair and left the car with them. We were told it would be ready in two to three days.We received a call the next day that the car was ready. We picked it up and were happy it was finally fixed. The A/C was working great, and we were able to drive home comfortably.Overall, we weren't happy with the experience. The cost was high, and it took longer than expected to get the car fixed. However, we were happy with the quality of the work and the fact that the problem was fixed.

I have been avoiding this place since the recent reviews have been very mixed. Today I was in the mood for BulGogi and my friend wanted sushi. So at Sushi Kim we arrived. I have never been here for dinner, only lunch and there is always enough tables and space. (Perhaps this is the best time to go) We both ordered from their lunch special menu; Sushi sampler & spicy pork BulGoGi & also an app of shrimp dumplings. Was not a fan of the dumplings but our pork was delicious, tender and spicy and the sushi was a nice mix and fresh. My friend ordered the green tea ice cream and my sample of it was quite tasty. We each had a glass of wine and with tip got out of there at around $50. 00. Not bad. nTheir menu is extensive and it may be hit or miss here depending on what you order. I have always had a hit with their BulGoGi, Korean Pancake, Hot Pots and sushi. Their service was attentive, but again, we were there for a late lunch and the place was not packed. All in all, the food was very tasty, service was good and price was respectable.

We were seated immediately and given menus to peruse. We started with several appetizers, including the truffle Parmesan fries, the brussels sprouts, and the seared scallops. There was an adventurous selection of small and large plates to share, as well as an extensive cocktail list. For our main course, we tried the steak frites, the branzino, and the mushroom risotto, which were all perfectly cooked. The food came out quickly and everything was delicious. The servers were attentive without being overbearing. They helped us choose food and drink pairings. We chatted and caught up over dinner, and the conversation flowed easily. About halfway through the meal, the energy in the restaurant picked up as more people arrived. Some of us ordered dessert, like the chocolate mousse and the berry crisp, while others sipped on a final cocktail, now that we were done with our business discussion. It was nice to catch up with colleagues in a relaxed setting away from the office. The bill came without any issues, and we debated whether to call it an early night or find another spot for drinks. We decided to head out into the warm Charlotte evening, full and satisfied from our meal. It had been the perfect place to host a group for both food and drinks. I would be remiss if I didn't mention the excellent service we received throughout the evening. Blue delivered on a relaxed yet impressive dining experience. While it was pricey, it was worth it for a special business dinner.

It's a mystery to me why I haven't reviewed Thai Cuisine before, especially since it's one of my favorite restaurants. I've been coming here for years and it never fails to impress. The food is always delicious and fresh, with generous portions that leave me feeling satisfied but not stuffed. I've tried a variety of dishes, from the classic Pad Thai to the spicy Basil Stir Fry, and everything in between. The flavors are bold and well-balanced, with just the right amount of sweetness, saltiness, and heat. The service is also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who always make me feel welcome. The restaurant itself is cozy and intimate, with beautiful decorations and a relaxed atmosphere. I've brought friends and family here alike, and everyone has left impressed. My only complaint is that I wish they were open for lunch on weekends, but that's a minor quibble. Overall, Thai Cuisine is a hidden gem that deserves more attention. If you haven't been, do yourself a favor and give it a try. You won't regret it!

From the dual head shower to the comfortable bed and pillows, everything was up to expectations. The real positive is that, although I got a room right across from the elevator (If I had been staying more than 1 night I would have requested a different room) it never became a noise issue. The two criticisms I do have are the breakfast menu in the restaurant, (NO BUFFET!! ) and the lack of concise instruction how the "Green Room" operates. For those of you who haven't experienced this as I hadn't, you put your key in a slot by the door so you can operate the thermostat and bathroom lights. Good idea, maybe more education at check in. One more small annoyance/observation, it seemed as though the AC turned off at about 3: 00 AM and the room became pretty uncomfortable. It was all 6 people in our party in six different rooms, not just me.

I enjoyed eating here well enough. I'm honestly not a die-hard fan of German food, although I guess that wouldn't have mattered: a peak at the menu beforehand revealed that this place's menu is mostly Americanized - proof of this is the fact that my salad was topped with French fries (only in Pittsburgh.. . ). Trust me, even if you don't really like German food, there'll at least be a sandwich you'll like here. Thinking about my usual "overall" summary, I have to say this place wasn't bad and served as a reasonable place to meet - the beer menu looked nice from what I saw and the atmosphere was pretty cozy and even nostalgic and homely - but man, the dining options really weren't that extraordinary. I'm still torn as to how to feel about its menu, because on the one hand obviously it being Americanized meant even I could find something to enjoy, but on the other I feel bad for the people who do like German food and may not be getting what they hope for. It wasn't bad enough that I'd say don't try it and see - just understand it may not be exactly what you expect.

Holly to attend a death in the family. Luckily I knew where the hotel was located or I would have driven right past the entrance. The parking situation is horrible. The parking layout is poorly designed and I spent far too much time waiting on other guests to park or drive past. The lady at reception did not greet us when we walked up to the front desk. I am an IHC Gold Elite member. The usual offer of bottled water was an after thought and she only offered a single bottle for two guests. There was no hair dryer in the room and when I called the front desk the lady responded as though I was lying. After a few minutes later a member of the housekeeping staff came to my room. She did not greet me as i opened the door. She came in and looked around the room as though I didn't think to look around for the hair dryer before calling the front desk. She did, however, return quickly with a hair dryer. Most of the staff were borderline rude or down right rude. The breakfast area was incredibly crowded. The morning of checkout my bill had not been placed under the door. I opened the door and it was lying in the hallway with my personal information there for anyone interested in reading my bill.

When it comes to eating I do not adhere to any particular mantra or dietary restriction like vegan, organic, vegetarian, ethical, etc. If it's edible and it's within my palate's liking range then I eat it. From that perspective this place just gets two stars. Some items were higher priced but the value added (from organic to vegan certified) would I guess justify it if you had to have it. But the items that do no fall under any of those premium-restriction value types are still just as highly priced. So it feels like 90% of their inventory is priced at a whole-store experience premium. Their prepared meals section was marvelous, and their cut fruit section was like I had died and gone to heaven. But that's about the only two sections I probably would have been willing to open up my wallet.

People's has better appetizers, and of course they have 1/2 off during certain hours, but Taste of India is better by far at entrees, and their masala tea is delicious. The nan is always hot, like hot hot, steaming hot, burn your hands hot, and perfectly done. Chicken Tikka Masala leftovers are sitting in the fridge right now, calling my name. Everything is good and the portions are beyond generous. What is particularly striking is the pricing. Indian food in Orlando and DC tends to be expensive, and those are my frames of reference, but Taste of India is completely reasonable. Even bizarrely inexpensive considering the quality of the food you get. The store front is odd, and the place never looks open, but don't be discouraged from going. Once you walk in you'll be seated quickly and served an onion and a mint chutney. Generally there is a young kid in the far back table playing on a computer or GameBoy. At the end of the meal, your tip tray comes covered in an anise and sugar mixture with little pink, yellow, and white pellet things. I'm an addict, but always end up eating one pinch more than I ought, where the flavor becomes unappealing. And as much as I know this, I cannot help myself.

Sooo . . . I went to the much ballyhooed new restaurant downtown last night with a few friends. Let me tell ya, it was packed! The hype machine must be in full effect because it was absolutely insane, even on a weeknight. We waited over an hour for a table, even though we had reservations. The hostess was really nice, but she seemed totally overwhelmed. Like, she couldn't even keep track of who was next on the list.Once we were finally seated, it took another 20 minutes for our server to acknowledge us. He seemed like he was running around like a chicken with its head cut off. I could see the poor guy sweating and looking totally stressed out.I asked for a beer and some water, but he must have forgotten my drink order because he never brought it. When he finally took our food order, he got it wrong. Like, not even close. I wanted the salmon, but he put in an order for the steak. By the time we got our food, it was like 2 hours later.And when it finally arrived, it was a total disappointment. The salmon was overcooked and dry. The vegetables were mushy and flavorless. The rice was undercooked and crunchy. It was like a bad joke.To make matters worse, my friend's steak was still mooing when it got to the table. We tried to flag down our server, but he was nowhere to be found. Finally, my friend just gave up and started eating it anyway.Needless to say, we didn't leave a tip. And we definitely won't be going back. This place was a total disaster. If you're thinking about going, my advice is to save your money and go somewhere else. You'll thank me later.The only upside was that the company was good. I was with my best friends, and we had a good time laughing and talking, even though the food was terrible. But that's not saying much.Overall, this place was a huge letdown. The food was terrible, the service was even worse, and the prices were outrageous. It's a shame because the location is great and the concept is interesting.

I had high expectations for this restaurant based on a friend's recommendation that it was a local favorite amongst the Japanese community in Charlotte. However, upon arriving I was disappointed by the lack of charm and personality. The plain interior decor featured generic artwork and basic furniture that resembled a hotel lobby more than a dining establishment. Upon being seated promptly, we had to wait an unusually long 20 minutes before a server even took our drink order. When she finally came to the table, the server seemed tired and rushed. The menu offered typical sushi and hibachi options but lacked creativity or standout dishes. I ordered salmon nigiri and chicken teriyaki which were mediocre - the fish lacked flavor and the chicken was overcooked. My dining companion chose shrimp tempura that had clearly seen better days, with soggy battered shrimp and vegetables. The noisy hibachi section provided little atmosphere for a relaxing meal. Both meals were overpriced given the underwhelming quality.Unfortunately, the experience did not live up to our expectations, and we will not return. The restaurant is in dire need of renovations to enhance the atmosphere. The servers also require more attentiveness and care towards customers. Based on this disappointing visit, I cannot recommend this restaurant. There are better Japanese establishments in the area offering higher quality food and ambiance worth exploring instead to satisfy your cravings. Unless significant improvements have been made, I suggest diners look elsewhere.

If this review was just for the food it would be an easy 3 or 3. 5 stars. The food was all delicious - we had the sauteed eggplant appetizer, the cucumber/tomato/onion salad, shishkabob dinner and burg dinner (not what I ordered but it was still good. ) The rest of the experience was kind of bizarre. We went here for lunch last week. The food was great and the service was excellent. The atmosphere was a bit too loud for my taste, but other than that, I had a great experience. I would definitely recommend this place to others.The menu had a wide variety of options to choose from, so there was something for everyone. I ended up getting the chicken parmesan, which was delicious. The chicken was cooked perfectly and the sauce was amazing. My friends got the steak and the seafood pasta, and they both raved about their dishes as well.The service was also top-notch. Our server was very attentive and made sure we had everything we needed. He also made some great recommendations for food and drinks.The only downside to the experience was the noise level. The restaurant was very crowded and it was hard to talk to my friends. However, this is a minor complaint and I would still highly recommend this place to others.Overall, I had a great experience at this restaurant. The food was great, the service was excellent, and the atmosphere was nice. I would definitely recommend this place to others.

SF and Boston have plenty of reviews to choose from but Pittsburgh didn't have many, let alone stellar reviews on salons. At the time I colored my hair so I didn't want to let just anyone put foils and scissors near my head. Finding a new hairstylist is like a game of russian roulette to me. I can either be safe or be really screwed for a few weeks. MCN was really the only salon ranked high in a search in my neighborhood so I gambled and scheduled an appointment with Sara. The salon is located near a Whole Foods, Starbucks, Walgreens and what use to be a Borders. It is clean, spacious and open with nice views overlooking the city. Sara did a great job and continues to do so (I'm loyal like that). She consults me first and doesn't deviate from what we agree upon. Her demeanor is professional and friendly. While I was waiting for my color to process, MCN has some outlets for you to plug in your computer to pass the time. Reasonably priced and another nice thing is that MCN occasionally will give free goodies as a thank you or for the holidays. While certainly the do is most important, the little things count as well. I will say though that they do seem a little pushy with product and the product may not even be the best one for your hair. I know salons can make a great profit off of product from the show Tabitha's Salon but this can ruin your experience at MCN after an awesome haircut/color treatment.

Well, I went here with my friends and my 3-year-old daughter for a dinner. We arrived around 6 pm, and the place was already bustling with activity. The hostess greeted us warmly and led us to our table. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a mix of modern and traditional decor. Our server, a friendly young woman, took our orders and brought usour drinks promptly.The menu offered a diverse selection of dishes, ranging from classic Vietnamese fare to more innovative creations. My friends and I were excited to try some of the chef's recommendations, while my daughter stuck to her favorite, chicken nuggets. We also ordered a few appetizers to share, including spring rolls and fried wontons.As we waited for our food, my daughter entertained us with her energetic dance moves, much to the amusement of the other diners. Our server brought out the appetizers, which were delicious and fresh. The spring rolls were crispy and flavorful, while the fried wontons had just the right amount of sweet and sour sauce.When our main courses arrived, we were impressed by the generous portions and vibrant colors. My friends and I tried a variety of dishes, including pho, pad thai, and bun cha. Each dish was expertly prepared and bursting with flavor. My daughter, on the other hand, was thrilled to see her chicken nuggets arrive, happily dipping them in ketchup and mustard.Overall, we had a wonderful experience at this restaurant. The food was exceptional, the service was top-notch, and the atmosphere was lively and engaging. We left feeling satisfied, but not overly full, and eager to return and try more of their delicious offerings. Well worth a visit!

I get a typical breakfast if eggs, ham, toast, and home fries. Delicious as usual. The ambience however is usually lacking. The walls are dark, with writing and signatures of semi famous people all over the place. Pictures of local people hang on the walls(i secretly want mine up there) along with posters galore. While its fun to look at the first 10 times, it gets a little boring after awhile. So today when I arrived I expected the same old experience. Wow was I wrong! As soon as I looked at the door I knew something was different. The place seemed lighter and brighter. To my pleasant surprise, they painted and got new counter tops!! They're not quite done yet but the place has a new Happy vibe to it. The awesome breakfast, the new decor and the 5 guys sitting at the counter making me laugh are why I will be back( maybe for lunch).

It's me again, back with another restaurant review. This time we're going to check out a little hole-in-the-wall place called The Greasy Spoon. Now I know what you're thinking: "A greasy spoon? That doesn't sound very appetizing." But trust me, this place is a hidden gem. The first thing you notice when you walk in is the friendly staff. They're always smiling and happy to make recommendations. The menu is full of classic diner food, but everything is made with a little twist. For example, the burgers are made with a special blend of ground beef and chuck, and they're topped with a secret sauce that's to die for. But my favorite thing on the menu is the chicken fried steak. It's a huge piece of beef that's been breaded and deep fried until it's golden brown and crispy. And the fries are hand cut and fried to perfection. The prices are also very reasonable. You can get a burger and fries for under ten bucks. And the chicken fried steak is only twelve. So if you're looking for a great place to get some comfort food, you should definitely check out The Greasy Spoon. The food is delicious, the staff is friendly, and the prices are reasonable. What more could you ask for? I give The Greasy Spoon a five out of five stars.

Rows and rows and rows of coffee, stretching out as far as the eye can see. The aroma of freshly brewed coffee fills the air, enticing all who enter the shop. Friendly baristas greet customers with a warm smile, ready to guide them through the vast array of coffee options. The menu board displaying the various blends and roasts is a thing of beauty, showcasing the passion and dedication that goes into each cup.From the classic Americano to the more adventurous cold brew, there's something for everyone's taste buds. The beans are sourced from the finest farms around the world, ensuring a rich and satisfying flavor in every cup. The hiss of the espresso machine signals the start of a new creation, as skilled baristas craft each drink with precision and care.For those looking for a sweet treat, a selection of mouth-watering pastries and cakes are available, perfectly complementing the coffee. The comfortable seating and relaxed atmosphere invite customers to linger and enjoy their coffee in peace. The sound of laughter and conversation fills the shop, creating a warm and welcoming ambiance.Whether you're in a rush or have time to savor your coffee, this coffee shop is a must-visit. The attention to detail and commitment to quality are evident in every aspect, making it a standout among its peers. Coffee lovers will feel like they've found their haven, and newcomers will quickly understand why this shop is so beloved.In short, this coffee shop is a gem, offering an unparalleled coffee experience that will leave you wanting more. From the expertly crafted drinks to the inviting atmosphere, it's a place that will keep you coming back for more. So, grab a cup of coffee, sit back, and savor the taste of excellence.

We were going to a concert and when we arrived many people were waiting to be seated. We were told to expect a half hour wait. We sat at the bar and had a drink and in what must have been only ten minutes we were asked if we would mind eating at a booth in the bar area rather than wait for the dinning room. We were thrilled, because we were considering eating at the bar. The booth worked out just fine. It wasn't too noisy and we got served quickly. Even though there were several specials that tempted us, we both ordered the best thing on the menu - their Ju00e4ger Schnitzel, with sides of hot German potato salad and sweet and sour cabbage. I had a German black lager and my wife a glass of wine. The basket of assorted rolls comes with delicious apple butter and sauerkraut relish, both very tasty. The schnitzel is quite large, and we only made it about halfway thru when we asked for a to-go box. We're looking forward to finishing it here at home. Maybe next time we'll try something different.. .. but probably not! nPros: inexpensive, very tasty schnitzelsnCons: no reservations for parties under 5

The menu offered a wide selection of their famous sandwiches, each one a generous portion that could satisfy the heartiest appetite. As soon as we arrived, the lively atmosphere greeted us with its vibrant energy. The aroma of sizzling grilled meats filled the air, making our mouths water in anticipation. I decided to try the classic Primanti's sandwich, piled high with juicy grilled steak, tangy coleslaw, and crisp French fries, all between two thick slices of Italian bread. One bite into this towering masterpiece, and I understood why it has become an icon of Pittsburgh cuisine. The tender steak complemented the crispness of the fries, and the tangy coleslaw added a delightful tanginess. The staff was friendly and efficient, and they were happy to recommend their favorite local attractions and even told us stories about the restaurant's history. It was clear that they took pride in their establishment and cared about their customers' satisfaction. We also enjoyed some of their famous fried appetizers, such as the crispy onion rings and the zesty fried pickles, which added another layer of deliciousness to our meal. The sandwich was so large that I couldn't finish it, but the staff happily packed up the leftovers for me to enjoy later. As we left Primanti's, I felt grateful for the chance to experience this iconic Pittsburgh restaurant. I would definitely return on my next visit to try more of their delicious menu. The combination of great food, warm hospitality, and lively atmosphere made for a memorable dining experience. Whether you're a local or just passing through, you must visit Primanti's.

Oh my, oh my.. . This book took me by completes surprise. I wasn't expecting such an emotional ride when I first picked it up. Within the first few pages, I was hooked on the characters and needed to find out what happened next. The author does an amazing job of drawing you into their world and making you feel what the characters believe. I read deep into the night because I couldn't bear to put it down. Each chapter left me on the edge of my seat, pondering the inevitable ups and downs that were sure to come. The triumphs felt so joyous and the trials absolutely gut-wren ching. I laughed and I screamed - this book took me through the whole range of emotions. Per characters are so fully developed and three-dimensional. It was effortless to relate to them and understand their motivations, even when I didn't agree with their choices. The plot kept me guessing with its many twists and turns. I didn't see some of the grands revelations coming at all. The writing and storytelling are absolutely top-notch. This is undoubtedly one of the best books I've read all year. li will definitely be recommending it to all my friends. Albeit the topics covered are complex, the author handles them deftly without allowing the material to feel heavy-handed. Even after finished it days ago, I find myself still thinking about the characters and their journey. It is a book that will stick with me for a long time to coming.

TWC needs to get their crap worked out with their IT infrastructure. First, ten minutes after I placed the order online I received an email that said I needed to call in to confirm some details. The operator said that everything looked fine but that he couldn't confirm the appointment time I had selected and the next available one was two weeks later. Uh, what? We certainly hope you'll reconsider Time Warner Cable. " Uh, WTF?
