The lackluster atmosphere, combines with the subpar service and underwhelming nourishing, tainted what could have been an enjoyable evening out. I departing the restaurant feeling thoroughly disappointed and regretful for choosing it in the first place. In conclusion, I cannot in alright conscience recommend this restaurant. Against the unwelcoming hostess to the lackluster service and subpar ate, the experience was far from what one would expect from a reputable establishment.

The staff is friendly and there is a fantastic restaurant located in the lobby. So, why only 2 stars you ask? I'm traveling on business, like many people who come to this town, and I cannot come close to expressing my frustration with the wireless internet.. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. Let me take a moment to calm myself. n It's horrible. Paying per device seems silly when it's not uncommon for people to have a few devices, but that's not my biggest issue. My complaint is that I'm having to refresh my wireless connection every 3 minutes on my iPad. It's absolutely maddening. I wouldn't be as concerned if I were here for pleasure. The ability to work from my room is pretty critical when traveling on business. I've never had connection issues on my device, so I'm confident it's not the problem. Over the past two nights, I have spent more time waiting on/refreshing my connection than actual productive time online.

The food is not only disappointing, but also the service is also bad. From the moment we arrived, it was clear that the staff was not interested in providing a happy dining experience. Our server does not concentrate, and seems to be annoyed by our existence. Our drinks spent forever. When they do this, they are wrong and must be returned. The menu has a variety of options, but the dishes we ordered are far from description. The steak is overly cooked and hard, the pasta is bland, and the flavor is insufficient. The vegetable li is cooked and cooked. Obviously, not in preparation of food. The atmosphere of the restaurant is also disappointing. The lighting is dim and dull, and the decoration is out of date and wear. Overall, this dinner is completely disappointing, and I will not recommend this restaurant to anyone.

I mean it's freaking 7: 45 AM in the morning - just let me pay for my damn oatmeal and get to work! There was NO ONE else in line, therefore no one in front of me and I'm standing in front of the cashier waiting to pay.. . now get this.. . I'm standing there, debit card in hand, while she's completing a text message. And it's not like she just needs to press "send" oh no - there's is content getting written before my eyes as I wait there, and I'm thinking to myself is this really happening, who the hell could she be texting this early, and why the hell is she making me wait while she completes the content of a text message. Now, I realize that ABP (Au Bon Pain) isn't some uber-professional establishment, but I'm thinking this should be in customer service 101 - stop texting while a customer is waiting to pay for item, you may resume texting after customer(s) are gone. The oatmeal was tasty - and I like that they have a self-serve topping area (containers filled with nuts, cranberries, raisins, brown sugar, granola). They had a choice between plain and apple cinnamon oatmeal - I went for the apps cinn mush - good stuff. If only they could train their employees better.

I had some time to kill this afternoon, and was looking for lunch in the city center. I decided to try a new sandwich store recommended by a friend, called the "sandwich board". When I walked in, a friendly staff greeted me and asked me how many people at the party. I told her that only me, she took me to the comfortable table next to the window. There are many sandwiches, salads and soups on the menu. I was torn between the classic Turkish clubs and vegetarian fun, but finally decided the latter. I ordered tea to drink and wait patiently for my food. The atmosphere is very happy, with clean and modern decoration. Unconsciously, my sandwich is ready, and it looks great. The bread is freshly baked and the vegetables are crispy. I took a bite and was impressed by the flavor immediately. The joy of vegetables is not disappointing. It is full of avocado, bean sprouts, tomatoes, cucumber and eagle -mouth bean. All ingredients are fresh and the effect is very good. I completed the sandwich and decided to try one of the desserts, a chocolate cookie. It is still warm from the oven, there is a very tightening outside, and the inside is soft. I let the sandwich board satisfied and satisfied with my lunch experience. This service is very careful, the food is delicious, and the atmosphere is very welcome. I will definitely recommend sandwiches to those who seeks delicious and healthy lunch in the city center. The price is reasonable and some are generous. In general, I provide 5 stars for the Director of Sandwich to provide delicious food, friendly services and comfortable atmosphere. I'll be back soon!

They make the perfect roast beef sandwich on this particular bagel and they may have just signed their own death warrant with me if they've discontinued making them. It tastes pretty damn close to a Beef on Weck. I went to this location the other day and they had a "pretzel" bagel in place of my beloved salt. I did ask for the salt but they told me that they had the pretzel instead. I though, what the heck, I'll give it a try. Dammit.. . it comes nowhere close to the original! The line got too crowded for me to go up there and air my grievance because I did have another complaint that must be addressed: SOUP! Brueggers used to have a wealth of soups that they would rotate on a daily basis. Now they only have 2! Chicken spaetzle or black bean! Every single time I go to this location, it's the same-old-same-old choices of soup! I realize it's Summer and maybe they don't move soup like they would during cooler weather, but if you're offering it.. . mix it up!! ! ! If you go on their site, they show they have about 8 different varieties but not this particular location. They used to have a delicious Velvet Veggie Cheese a few years ago, but discontinued it. I even complained about that online and just got a thank you/try our other soups bull$hit courtesy response. No salt bagel is a deal breaker with me with Brueggers. The lack of soup varieties I can live with but killing one of my favorite sandwiches cannot be forgiven. I will return just to see for myself the next time if my precious salt bagel has been permanently replaced. If it has, I will stage a walkout.. . but nobody else will follow. The WiFi sucks, too. The only plus here is the friendly staff. Your sad pal, nWalter

When a place is famous for something (ie having the best burgers in Pittsburgh), that's what you should order. It's like going to a pizza place and not getting a pizza, or visiting a sushi restaurant and not trying any sushi. If you're not going to try their signature dish, you're doing it wrong.I recently visited a burger joint in Pittsburgh that boasted about having the best burgers in the city. I was excited to put their claim to the test, so I ordered one of their famous burgers.The menu described it as a juicy beef patty topped with crispy bacon, melted cheddar cheese, and a tangy barbecue sauce, all sandwiched between a brioche bun. My mouth was watering just reading about it.When the burger arrived, I was immediately impressed by its appearance. The bun was perfectly toasted, and the toppings were generously piled high. I took a bite, and oh boy, it was love at first bite.The beef patty was cooked to perfection, with just the right amount of pinkness in the center. The bacon was crispy and added a satisfying crunch, while the cheddar cheese was melted to creamy perfection. And that barbecue sauce... wow, it was like a party in my mouth.I was expecting the burger to be good, but this was something else. It was like a symphony of flavors and textures, all working together in perfect harmony. I was in burger heaven.I finished the burger in record time, and I couldn't help but feel a sense of sadness that it was over. I wanted to savor every bite, but at the same time, I couldn't wait to take another bite. It was like a delicious paradox.I'm not sure what kind of magic they use in the kitchen, but this place truly has the best burgers in Pittsburgh. If you're ever in the city, do yourself a favor and stop by for a bite.Just remember, when a place is famous for something, that's what you should order. Trust me, you won't regret it.

I am a 'sorta regular' here. They have very good fish frys and equally tasty breakfasts [bacon is exceptional], along with generally friendly service.. . That changed Sunday.. Was here with companions. . Decided to play the "'cherry master video machine" during our visit.. Got to a $50 credit when we HAD to leave.. . Asked Julie to just clear the machine as she was very busy, and I would return later for the money.. . Please keep in mind clearing machine involves pressing a button and one second of time. Reply was "can't now". Waited ten minutes as she walked by me 3 times.. Finally told here again we needed to leave.. . She basically went into a public rant yelling to the bartender to "give this guy $50".. . We just can not justify returning after this experience.. Darn, cause it's generally a decent place.. .

The food and service were both excellent. The atmosphere of the restaurant is elegant and inviting. The food was delicious and well-presented. The service was impeccable. The staff was friendly and attentive. The prices were reasonable. The restaurant is located in a convenient location. The restaurant is perfect for a special occasion or a romantic dinner. The restaurant has a great selection of wines. The restaurant is decorated beautifully. The restaurant is very clean. The restaurant is quiet and relaxing. The restaurant is perfect for a business lunch or dinner. The restaurant is great for a family dinner. The restaurant is perfect for a group of friends. The restaurant is great for a date night.

The front desk was very friendly (Lindsay at the front desk has been particularly friendly and helpful) at check-in and the restaurant staff were also very nice. The room was clean and well kept with a ~24" flat TV and decent furniture. The breakfast has been improved since the last time. The potatoes were much better than before and the eggs were done on a per order basis when it wasn't busy. The bacon and was quite a bit better. The Not So Good: Dinner was decent but still left a bit to be desired as far as seasoning and interesting flavors to their dishes. They would do well to get a little more variety of beers on tap as well. Yes it is a hotel by the airport but I've stayed at several hotels this lose to airports and they generally have better windows to isolate some of the noise. Overall, this was a good hotel. I think the room is among the better quality ones in the area and, provided you're a sound sleeper when it comes to noise, it is pretty comfortable.

I remember the great crab legs I had years ago. I finally had the chance last week and was surprisingly disappointed. The service was great. We sat at the bar and in no time both bartenders greeted us with smiles and menus. I guess my main concern was the food quality. I ordered the beet salad with warm goat cheese (was not warm at all) and shrimp and scallop linguine. Both were not unique in flavor or presentation. It was as if I made it in my own kitchen. My boyfriend enjoyed his lobster bisque and his seafood jambalya that was perfectly spicy. I do applaud the venue for offering a diverse and affordable wine list. And, with all due respect to owners, I think the atmosphere needs a serious update in character and aesthetics. Especially since other key hotels are more pleasing to the eye. This should be vital to one of the BEST hotels in the city! I'd like to return someday to give it another go. We shall see. P. S. Invest in better wine glasses. Ugly. Ugly. Ugly.

The first impression was underwhelming, but I think there is room for improvement. The ambiance was pleasant, with dim lighting and soft music playing in the background. However, the seating arrangement was cramped and uncomfortable, with little room to move. The menu offered a decent variety of choices, but the prices seemed a bit steep for the portion sizes. The service was friendly, but the staff was not very attentive. It took quite a while for them to take our orders, and even longer for the food to arrive at our table. The food was beautifully presented, showcasing the chef's artistic flair. Unfortunately, the taste did not match the visual appeal. The flavors were mediocre at best, lacking depth and character. The drinks were the highlight of the evening, especially the cocktails. The mixologists were very creative and skilled, and the drinks were both visually stunning and deliciously refreshing. I would highly recommend trying their signature cocktail. The noise level was moderate, allowing for easy conversation. However, the acoustics in the restaurant were not up to par, amplifying the sound and creating a somewhat cacophonous environment. It was difficult to hear my dining companions without straining. The cleanliness of the restaurant could also use some improvement. The tables were sticky, and the floor looked neglected, with crumbs strewn about. The appetizers were rather small, leaving us wanting more. The main courses were quite generous in size, but unfortunately the quality did not match the quantity.

Busy, but not overly so, I have never waited longer than 20 minutes in the security checkpoint line. As others have said, there are 3 checkpoints, so if the one closest to you seems busy, try other ones, they may be faster. The TSA agents are usually pretty cheery here, which is always nice when you're toting a fussy (or talkative) toddler through the checkpoint. I only wish there were a few more food and drink options outside of security. Currently there's a Starbucks on the top level by the departure desks, and that's about it. Now, I understand the airport was built before the security restrictions were tightened (which is a shame, because I love going to the airport, and I'd probably go there to hang out if you didn't need a ticket to get in), but it would be nice if there were more things. Also, seriously? Quit it with the Cinnabon. You can smell it from a terminal away! I don't always want a $4 cinnamon bun, but that smell is just so damn enticing that I just can't resist sometimes! I guess it's better than the stale breath smell of an airplane, though: P

00. I highly suggest making a reservation- this place is packed to the gills. There's a huge bar in the main room, decent bartenders and reasonable priced drinks. We waited about 20 minutes past our reservation because there was a large party being served, but onced we had a drink in hand, the wait was tolerable. Seated, we were happily surprised to see how efficiently they run their fish fry- the tables were pre-set with a bowl of tartar sauce and a family-sized bowl of cole slaw, plus a basket with several slices of really tasty rye bread. Three of us enjoyed perch family-style, with fries and it was really good- a lightly breaded well-cooked platter of perch and fries was easy to share with friends. Looking around, it was a good mix of north and east-siders with an average age of well under 60, on the low side for a supper club. Can't wait to go back!

Ah, the Dor-Stop, a Pittsburgh gem that brings pure delight to anyone who steps foot inside. Situated in the heart of the city, this charming diner exudes a nostalgic ambiance, whisking you away to a bygone era. As you enter, warm smiles greet you along with the irresistible aroma of freshly brewed coffee. The vintage memorabilia and cozy booths envelop you in an atmosphere that feels like a second home.As you settle into your booth, you can't help but admire the extensive menu, a testament to the culinary excellence of the Dor-Stop. They offer a wide array of classic breakfast dishes, from fluffy pancakes to crispy bacon, as well as mouthwatering omelets brimming with flavorful fillings. Their commitment to quality is evident in the use of locally sourced ingredients, which highlights their support for local farmers.Among the impressive selection, one dish stands out-their signature Pittsburgh-style french toast. Thick slices of bread are lovingly soaked in a heavenly mixture of eggs, cinnamon, and a hint of vanilla, then cooked to perfection on the griddle. The result is a masterpiece with a golden-brown exterior that delicately balances pillowy softness and a tantalizing crunch. A dollop of creamy butter and a drizzle of maple syrup crown this creation, creating a symphony of flavors that will leave your taste buds singing.If savory is more to your liking, the Monte Cristo sandwich is an absolute must-try. Layers of savory ham, turkey, and Swiss cheese are nestled between two slices of golden French toast, blending the best of both sweet and savory worlds. Each bite harmoniously combines a delightful medley of textures and flavors that will leave you longing for more.The service at the Dor-Stop deserves commendation as well. The attentive and friendly staff members are genuinely passionate about ensuring that every guest has a truly memorable dining experience.

Their vegan options are extensive and amazingly delicious. The won-ton soup is vegan friendly too, at least that's what the server told me. Portion sizes are generous, the soy protein is to die for and the price is right. This place is a little piece of heaven for vegetarians and vegans, but omnis won't know the difference. I've visited this location a handful of times, and each experience has been nothing but pleasant. I have tried the fried mushrooms, the sesame soy protein, the orange soy protein, the sweet & sour soy protein, the wheat gluten veggie mix, the general tso soy protein and the hot and sour soup. My favorite is the sesame soy protein, but I plan to try all of the soy protein dishes at some point. The wheat gluten is tasty, but it's not the best I've ever had. I prefer the meaty and solid texture of the soy protein over tofu and wheat gluten. The spicy dishes are never spicy. You can always ask for extra chile paste like I do though. It's weird that they aren't spicy enough, but that could be because this area isn't as likely to have a preference for the spicy foods. My last visit here on April 1st was definitely the most memorable. The sweetest young male was our server. He forgot sesame on our sesame soy protein, and he apologized profusely and fixed it. He kept bringing us refills, especially on my diet coke. Restaurants can be a little stingy with soda refills, but he was generous. He also gave us free rice refills, and since we all love rice, we were immensely grateful. I can't say enough good things about this kid, but I hope the tip we left him conveyed our gratitude. China Palace is a win for sure!

That's not really a bad thing; it's just not typically a place I would seek out on my own. Trio certainly has a few things going for it. First, it's fairly large, and even with groups of five or six, I've never had to wait for a table. Second, even though the decor is decidedly dated, I kind of love it.. . the interior is decorated primarily in teal, which is great, and the whole dining room has a light, airy feeling about it. As for the food, I've had their pizzas and pastas and maybe a salad or two, and I've never had a bad meal. Granted, my mind has never been blown either, but I can at least appreciate a place that has more than one or two options that aren't loaded up with beef. Let's put it this way: I don't know that I would pay for this food myself, but it's a perfectly adequate place to be taken out to dinner.

review's premiere sentence: Not a big fan of Americana Chinese cuisine, but this makes the cut. The sweet and sour chicken here is probably the best I've had outside of Asia. The breading is light and crispy without being greasy, and the sauce has a ncie balance of sweet and tanginess. You can really taste the pineapple and bell peppers in the sauce instead of just corn syrup like many other places. The huose lo mein is also excellent. The noodles have just the rights tooth and don't clump together. They toss them frequenly so they don't get soggy. You get a good amount of chicken, shrimp, broccoli and carrots in the dsh too. The menu has several healthier options like kung pao cauliflower and mongolian beef and broccoli. Even the breaded subjects like orange chicken or general tsos don't feel overly fattening. For appetizers, the egg rolls and crab rangoon are crowd pleasers. The wontons in chili oil are a spice and tangy starter. On the few times I've dined in, the service has been attentive without being overbearing. They refresh hot tea or water frequently. The spot is convenience for quick takeout too since they have online ordering. Packaging stays intast well during the ride home. Overall, the food is far above average for Ameriacn Chinese. It strikes a great balance of familiar flavors but doesn't feel like stuff from a bag or can. The cost are also reasonable for the quality. While I wouldn't say it replaces actual Chinese food from Asia, it satisfies Chinese food cravings very well for an Americanized version. Fans of the cuisine should definitely give this place a try.

I initially spoke with an agent when I first arrived at Hertz. I specifically told her that I was going to add another driver. I received a slip of paper that said, in bold print, "TOTAL ESTIMATED CHARGE. " I then gave her the information about the second driver, after which I received several more pieces of paper. I later found out that one of those slips was a second contract that said, in small, faint print, that I had to pay $13 for each day with a second driver. If I had known that I wouldn't have added the second driver. This is clearly a rip off. Hertz should have printed a revised total that stated the updated price IN BOLD CAPITAL LETTERS, like they did with the original price. I found all this out when I dropped off the car. I talked to the manager, who was obnoxious and unhelpful - she basically asked if I could read. I called the 800 # twice and got even more discourteous service. (They never responded to an email I sent shortly after the incident. )nnHertz succeeded in ripping me off for an extra $100 or so. But they've lost my business for good. Don't get scammed like I did. Avoid Hertz and go with a reputable company instead.

Was sort of taken aback by 2 customers seated on the patio. Both guys had on sports jerseys, jean shorts, or jorts if you will, and were seriously blinged out. Just seemed so out of place with everyone around them. We sat at a table in the bar area and the bartender came over with some cocktail menus and got us all waters right away. I had the grapefruit buck and it was sooo delicious and refreshing. I believe it was gin, campari, ruby red grapefruit juice and maybe something else, served w/a grapefruit slice. I loved it. Tried someone else's drink and wasn't a fan so was def happy with my choice. Had to run to make our reservation so it was just the one round. Wasn't cheap for 3 cocktails and a beer it was $46 I believe. But it was a nice atmoshpere and we saw they are running for prix fixe in October so we might stop in for dinner before Chelsea Handler at TW.

I have purchased 4 Lexus vehicles over the last 15 yrs. The quality and reliability of these motorcar have been outstanding. The service I have attains from the dealership has also been excellent. I have always been addressing fairly and with respect. I hectares recommended Lexus to many of my buddies and family members, and they have all been happy with their experiences as well. I es purchased a variety of Lexus models, including the ES, GS, and GX. Each model has its own unique strengths and weaknesses, but they all portion a common obligation to quality and reliability. The ES is a grand choice for someone who wants a comfortable and fuel-efficient sedan. It is also very spacious, making it a good option for domicile. The GS is a sportier option that still offers plenty of comfort and flamboyant. It is a great options for someone who wants a car that is fun to drive but also practical for ordinary use. The GX is a great election for someone who needs a rugged and capable SUV. It is perfect for off-road adventures or for hauling vast loads. No matter which Lexus models you choose, you can be confident that you are getting a quality vehicle that will last for many yr. I highly recommend Lexus to anyone who is looking for a solid and luxurious car. In addition to the quality of the vehicles, I have also been completely impressed with the service I fi received from the Lexus dealership. The staff is always agreeable and helpful, and they go above and beyond to make sure that my needs are encounter. I have had my Lexus vehicles serviced at the dealership for everything from normal maintenance to major repairs. I have always been treated rightly and with respect, and I have forever been satisfied with the work that has been done. The Lexus dealership also offers a variety of amenities to make the service experience more convenient and nice. There is a comfortable expecting area with complimentary Wi-Fi, as well as a courtesy shuttle service.

The service was excellent. It was hard to choose from all the great-sounding items on the menu. For the first ten minutes of my visit, I was really happy with it. Then the food came. Ohmigod, it was GROSS! I ordered fettuchini with goat cheese, expecting a pile of noodles, some alfredo-ish sauce and cheese over the top, and maybe if I was lucky a few pine nuts or tomato bits or herbs. Nuh-uh. It was like somebody took a huge glob of cafeteria noodles, rolled them around in a cup of grated cheese, put a stick of butter on top and microwaved the whole mess on high for a minute. The garlic bread was the kind of roll you'd use to make a sub sandwich dipped in some garlic butter. My dog has deposited more appealing piles on the back lawn after gorging on leftovers. Checking out the other tables, I doubt anything else would have been a better choice. This is what they call comfort food--what Mom would give you to cheer you up after your Little League team lost or something. I suppose people like this stuff because of the emotional connotations, I don't know. My actual mom knew how to cook. She would have called this stuff "white food. " The servings are huge, except for the side salad which could have fit in a teacup. Many people love this diner. If you're a mac-and-cheese type person, you may very well love it too.

This store is in a convenient location but that is its only redeeming quality. The selection is paltry and the aisles are cramped, making shopping feel like a chore. Finding someone to help is nearly impossible as the few employees are always busy or hiding in the back. The quality of the items is questionable at best, with many products well past their expiration dates sitting on shelves. Cleanliness is also an issue, with spills and messes left untouched for days. Checkout is a nightmare, as long lines routinely snake through the tiny store. Prices are high for the low quality of goods offered. I avoid shopping here if possible but sometimes the location wins out of necessity. Overall, this store provides a terrible shopping experience and I would only recommend it as an absolute last resort for emergency items. Shoppers deserve much better options nearby.

Not to mention there was a guy singing and playing an accordion on the night we went for dinner. Would have been fine except for the fact that there are 10 people too many in the place to begin with and then he wanders around the dining floor going table to table. Wanted to pay the guy to stop for 30 min while I ate! Pasta dishes are way overpriced and honestly not that great. $20 for noodles and meat sauce.. . Dinner specials/entrees are your best bet and were very good. but also way over prices. Didn't have desert but multiple people in my dinner party raved about one of the cakes they had. nn Simply put - this place does not execute the level of food their price points represent. I'm all for paying for a good meal but when it falls short.. .. and this place does! Overall a very disapointing night out.

The hotel was immaculate, with spacious and well-appointed rooms. The bed was extremely comfortable, making it easy to relax after long days of meetings and presentations. The bathroom had plenty of room and high-quality amenities. The staff I interacted with during my stay were all very friendly and eager to help with any requests. For breakfast each morning, I enjoyed the many choices available in the on-site restaurant. The indoor pool was a great way to unwind after a day of work. The gym on one of the lower floors had all the equipment I needed to stay active on days when I didn't have meetings. The business center had excellent computers and printing services for any last-minute preparations. Every area of the hotel was clean and well-maintained. On my last night, I enjoyed drinks and appetizers with colleagues in the lobby lounge. I would definitely stay at the Westin again if I had business in Charlotte. This hotel offers excellent service and accommodations for both business and leisure travelers visiting Charlotte. The central location in uptown made it easy to explore the city between work commitments. The comfortable bed and high-quality amenities made it feel like a real home away from home during my trip. I would highly recommend the Westin as an excellent choice for anyone looking to book a stay in Charlotte.

My parents saw a recommendation to visit this place from Rick Sebak's "25 Things I Like About Pittsburgh" and he's usually pretty accurate. His recommendations were to try the Reuben, Fish Sandwich and Open-Faced Steak Sandwich. We went early afternoon for a late lunch today (a Saturday) and were seated right away. The staff is extremely friendly. My Mom & I each had the fish sandwich, while my Dad & Brother had a Reuben sandwich. The fish was very good, but the Reuben was to die for! Both dishes were massive, and could very easily be shared between two people. On top of being extremely large portions, it was incredibly affordable. The giant fish sandwich was $8 and the giant Reuben was $7. 50. Our drinks were always filled and we were checked on several times during the meal. We will definitely be back!! ! Oh and a bit of advice ahead of time - they take CASH ONLY. So come prepared, but I'm pretty sure I saw an ATM there as well. And I do believe they are closed on Sundays & Mondays.

Well it's been 3 years since I last examine this Walmart. The store is still in the same location, but it has been renovated and expecting much nicer. The staff is still friendly and operable, and the prices are still reasonable. One thing I noticed is that the store is drastically cleaner than it used to be. The floors are swept and mopped regularly, and the bookshelf are well-organized. The produce section is especially impressive, with a wide variety of fresh fruits and lettuce. The deli section is also very good, with a large selection of meats, cheeses, and allready foods. The bakery section is also worth a visit, with a variety of fresh-baked breads, pastries, and pudding. The only downside to this Walmart is that it can be entirely crowded, especially on weekends. The checkout lines can also be long, but the servants is ordinarily quick to open new registers when they see a line forming. Overall, this Walmart is a splendid place to shop. It has a wide varied of products, the prices are reasonable, and the staff is friendly and helpful. I would indubitably recommend it to anyone looking for a good place to shop. The store is open 24 hours a day, 7 hours a week, and offers a variety of services, including a pharmacy, a photographed center, and a money center. It is also posted near a number of other stores and restaurants, producing it a convenient place to stop for all of your shopping needs. If you are researching for a Walmart that is clean, well-organized, and maintains a friendly staff, then I would highly recommend this one. I have been shopping here for years and fi always had a positive experience. I recently purchased a ny TV from this Walmart and was very impressed with the selection and prices. The staff was also hugely helpful in helping me choose the right TV for my needs. I also recently used the pharmacy at this Walmart and was tremendously impressed with the service. The staff was considerably friendly and helpful, and they filled my prescription quickly and accurately.

Do you get your own personal Alan Greenspan? And yes, I have been a resident of Charlotte long enough to remember that was the name of the place before they changed it. Really I cannot say if Healthy Home Market is all that much better name-wise, but at least you do not expect some stiff coming over to invade your place. The store itself is not much to look at. Or be inside. And the parking lot is only decent if you compare it to the one outside the Asian Corners. As has been mentioned many times, the South Boulevard version is vastly superior in just about every respect, yet the new location near the Matthews Wal-Mart is strangely modeled after this store, being on the small side. So obviously they think there is something for it. As to the inside, it is actually a cool little space. It is strangely reminiscent of a grocery you might find in the downtown of a large city, with stuff crammed everywhere - though the product is decidedly funky, and you can get all sorts of things you might not find at most places. Many spices available by the ounce/pound/whatever weight you choose, and oils and honeys as well. I would also echo that they are excruciatingly slow, but it is definitely worth a peek if you want something out of the ordinary.

I've been to several USO's at airports, and this is a very impressive one. Although it doesn't have showers and beds like some of the other ones I've seen, this one has this feel like it's one of those red-carpet airport clubs because it has the big fancy leather recliners with a large flat-screen TV, and another room in case you don't like what's playing in the main room. It's got 3 computers for internet access, a couple of large round bar tables sitting just across a counter full of free food, sodas, hot dogs, baked goods, etc. There's a section of 2 small TVs for PS2/xbox, and a small room for young toddlers to keep busy. The USO is always a place I go when I have time in between flights, even if I'm not traveling on official Army duty. It's typically operated by volunteers, so I make it a habit to go sign in to show that it's being utilized. Even if you're not in the military, you can still go up to the 2nd floor where the USO entrance is at, and usually find some free seating even when the downstairs chairs are all taken. One funny thing about the Charlotte airport is how busy it was one moment, and then how deserted it was the next. Our flight must have arrived some time after 9pm. After a quick stop at the Tequileria restaurant, we went to the USO and milled around a bit. Then we came back downstairs right after 10pm, and most of the stores and the food court were closed. It must have only been about 10-15 minutes where before the airport was bustling with people, to what seemed like a twilight zone episode. This airport is pretty nice because most of the shopping/food places are centrally located. It was a fairly long walk to our gate for our connecting flight, but thanks to those jetson walkways, it didn't seem too far. I'd come back through Charlotte again just to sit in the rocking chairs for a minute.

I was instantly captivated by the tantalizing aromas and boisterous flavors that danced on my taste buds. From that first bite of bibimbap, I knew I possess felt a culinary gem that would accompany me on a lifelong gastronomic adventure. The intricately worded plaque, such as bulgogi and kimchi, quickly became regular fixtures in my dining repertoire, satisfying both my hunger and my craving for bold, unique flavors. Exploring Korean cuisine opened up a whole new world of ingredients and cooking manner. The cumbersome balance of sweet, savory, and spicy flavors, combined with the artistic presentation of the dishes, showcased the meticulous attention to detail in Korean culinary classics. Each bite felt like a harmonious symphony of flavours, leaving a lasting impression that glided long after the meal was over. One respect that struck me was the emphasis on the communal nature of Korean dining. Gathering around a shared grill for samgyeopsal or love a hot pot of broiling budae jjigae with friends created a sense of camaraderie and togetherness. These experiences not only satisfied my hunger but also strengthened my bonds with those around me, fostering unforgettable memories. As my appreciation for Korean food deepened, I delved farther into its rich history and cultural significance. Learning about the traditional fermentation process behind kimchi and the symbolic feel of concrete dishes deepened my respect for the cuisine. It had apparent that Korean food was not just about nourishment but also a reflection of the country's heritage and the resilience of its people. The availability of Korean cuisine in my college commune was a pleasant surprise. Korean restaurants barley up, offering an array of authentic plates that transported me back to the bustling streets of Seoul.

I told everyone that I wasn't feeling this, but in the end, I decided to give it a try. Who knows, maybe I would be pleasantly surprised? My friends had raved about this place, claiming it had the best food in town. So, with a hint of skepticism lingering in my mind, I stepped into the restaurant. The ambiance was nice, with soft lighting and cozy seating arrangements. I could hear a faint melody playing in the background, creating a soothing atmosphere. The restaurant was quite busy, bustling with customers eagerly chatting and waiting for their meals. After a brief wait, a server led me to my table, which happened to be in a corner near the window. I appreciated the cozy setup, as it offered some privacy. Glancing at the menu, I noticed an array of enticing dishes, each promising a burst of flavors. I decided to go with their famous pasta dish, which had been highly recommended. The server took my order and disappeared into the bustling kitchen. However, as time passed, my patience waned. The minutes turned into an eternity, and my hunger grew with each passing moment. Finally, after what felt like an eternity, my food arrived. The presentation was decent, but as soon as I took my first bite, disappointment washed over me. The pasta lacked seasoning, and the texture was too mushy. It simply didn't live up to the hype. I wondered if the kitchen had rushed the dish, sacrificing quality for efficiency. I tried to address my concerns with the server, but they seemed disinterested, barely acknowledging my complaints. Moreover, they failed to offer any substitutions or discounts for the underwhelming experience. As I left the restaurant, I couldn't help but feel let down. I had wanted to enjoy this dining experience, but it simply fell short of my expectations. In the end, I realized that sometimes the hype doesn't always match the reality.

I would call it a "finer diner" in terms of the definition of a Diner. The menu has your everyday American items; nothing too creative or imaginative. It's pretty basic. Salads, sandwiches, burgers and entrees we have all had before. nThe food is good though; however you're paying for the location and decor (which, in our opinion, was kind of out-dated). We started with the mushroom flatbread that was a bit on the sweet side; however it was loaded with mushrooms which is a huge plus. nI had the walnut crusted salmon sandwich and Jordan had the reuben. The salmon was very light and tasty and Jordan's corned beef was sliced real thick. French fries are pretty standard. nAll in all, I guess this is where the rich people of ShadySide get their diner food: same kind of food, just a fancier ambiance than Denny's. nWe will be back when we want something comforting but dont want to be surrounded by teenagers and want something better than Eat 'N Park.

Here is a continued 13 chastisement scrutiny:I have been to several Rock Bottoms including Denver, CO and this one was less than impressive. The atmosphere lacked energy and it was nearly empty on a Saturday nighttime. The bar area was dimly lit making it difficult to see drink elect clearly. When we tried to order drinks, the bartender hoped annoyed to be serving us. Our drunken arrived slowly and were weak poured. We decided to check out the dance floor but found it scattering with only a couple people migrated listlessly to the music. The DJ's singers selection did little to get people excited or in a dancing mood. Ago a few more drinks, we gave up on dancing and played a round of pool on one of the musty tables. Even the bathroom was disappointing with its stale smell and shortcoming of soap or paper towels. I'd come here wishes a fun night out but left feeling bored and underwhelmed. Unless this rentals radically improves its vibe and service, I don't see myself ever returning. There are much better ways to spend an evening than at this lackluster Pebbles Bottoms location. From the future I'll stick to locations like the one in Denver that know how to keep user entertained and satisfied.

DO NOT BUY T HE MEAL DEAL AT THE PARK OR ONLINE. The portions are tiny and not worth the price at all. I ordered the meal deal ideology it would be a good value but was sorely disappointed. The burger was the size of a cookie and the fries were just a handful. There was barely any drink in the bottle either. It did not fill me up at all despite costing over $15. I still left feeling hungry and ripped off. The caliber of the food was also very poor. The burger patty was thin and dried out while the fries tasted stale. Customer service was horrible as well when I tried to complain. The epmloyee did not seem to care at all that I got such a bad deal. I will not be ordering from this place again or recommending it to anyone. There are much better options that will actually leave you feeling total for the money. Learn from my mistake and do not waste your time or money on this so-called meal deal. Opting for a larger meal somewhere else instead to get your money's worth of food. This is easily the wost value I have ever received and want to warn others to avoid it.

The atmosphere was very nice and relaxed for a business dinner. We were seated promptly and the server was attentive to our needs throughout the meal. The menu offered a variety of tasty sounding options for appetizers, entrees and desserts. We started with an assortment of bruschetta, calamari and spinach artichoke dip which were all excellent. For our main courses we ordered the chicken piccata, salmon and New York strip steak. Everything was cooked perfectly and the flavors were vibrant. My clients especially loved the steak which they said was one of the best they've had. Towards the end of the meal we had some great conversations and everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves. I would definitely come back here for both personal and professional dining experiences. The rest of the night went smoothly and we closed an important deal. A few weeks later, one of my clients contacted me and said they wanted to meet at the same restaurant for another potential business partnership. We went back and had an equally pleasant time, sealing yet another deal over a relaxed and memorable meal. I've now made it a regular spot to take clients whenever I'm in town. The staff knows me by name now too which adds to the comfort level. Whether dining for pleasure or work purposes, this place reliably delivers quality food and a hospitable atmosphere. It's become one of my favorite local restaurants for both business and personal use any time I'm traveling through the area.

The first time I went, the service was excellent. The staff was friendly, attentive, and quick to take our orders. We were seated promptly, and our food arrived promptly. The food was delicious. I had their signature pizza, and it was delicious. The crust was thin and crispy, and the toppings were plentiful and flavorful. The second time I went, however, was a bit disappointing. The service was much slower, and it took a while for someone to even acknowledge our presence. Once we finally got menus, it took a long time before we were asked to order. The quality of the food was a far cry from my first visit. The crust was doughy this time, and the toppings were sparse. The wait for our food was excruciating, and when it finally arrived, it was lukewarm at best. I understand that every restaurant has its off days, but I was hoping for a more consistent experience. Despite the disappointment of my second visit, I'm willing to give Papa J's another chance. I'll just have to cross my fingers and hope for a better experience next time. Perhaps it was an anomaly, and I believe they have the potential to deliver excellent food and service.

Hubby and I have taken to driving up Carson street to get to the Wolverhampton in order to avoid that HORRENDOUS traffic in Squirrel Slopes. And let me tell you, it owns been a game-changer. Not only did we headed to avoid the bumper-to-bumper nightmare, but we also discovery a hidden gem along the way. As we drove up Carson, we dived upon a quaint little café called "Perky's Brew." Nestled between vibrant boutique and charming houses, this café exudes a cozy and welcoming atmosphere. The moment we walked in, the aroma of freshly brewed coffee enveloped us, and we think we were in for a curing. The menu offered a wide variety of artisanal coffee blends and crappy pastries, render it difficult to choose just one. We splurge in a creamy latte and a flaky almond croissant, and they were simply divine. The baristas were friendly and warmed, taking the time to explain each coffee's origin and flavor profiles. The cozy seating area earmarked the perfect spot to relax and sip our beverages while enjoying the soothing jazz music ballgame in the background. Perky's Brew has undoubtedly become our go-to café for a delightful start to our excursions across the city. Thanks to our detour from Squirrel Hill, we not only eluded the traffic nightmare but also stumbled upon a hidden caffeine haven that will stands a costly part of our routine.

As a matter of background, I am originally from Los Angeles and have experienced some EXCELLENT nail salons there for much cheaper prices. I don't know why manicures and pedicures are so expensive in Pittsburgh, but that's really a different path that I rather not venture into. Anyway, this place is really small and they hardly have any nail polish choices. It costs $15 for a manicure and $30 for a pedicure. If you decide to go here, take my advice and take your own nail polish. As for me, I picked out an OPI nail polish and they poured acetone in the nail polish to make it thinner!! I hate it when they do this, I guess its just their way of being cheap and not taking out a new nail polish. The end result is that there are bubbles now on my nails and less than 24 hours later I just noticed that one of my nails has already chipped. To make matters worse, their hot water was not working properly so they gave me my manicure and pedicure with pure COLD water. The only positive thing I found about this place is that they accept credit cards.

I'm not sure I'm sad about that either. I used a groupon to go here so I was able to taste appetizers, entrees, wine & desert. The prices were very reasonable but I wasn't super impressed with the food. Our waitress brought out some bread & breadsticks. I love my bread so I was sad when it wasn't fresh made, it was definitely bought. The breadsticks were more like bread crackers that came in little plastic bags just like crackers do. Nothing to come back for there. I got the lasagna that was described as "put back in the oven with more cheese", and though the lasagna part of the dish was fine - the gobs of cheese and grease weren't really up my alley. We had enough money leftover to get desert so we splurged for cheesecake - with pineapple. I had never had pineapple cheesecake and now I know why. It was very gelatin-y and we had to scrape the orange colored "pineapple" off the top. The decorations and the history of the place were neat, and I'm a bit sad I didn't try the famous pizza, but I don't think I'll be going back to try it either.

I got a plate with seisage, tofu scramble, and sundried tomato toast. My whole plate was entirely dry, chewy, and unpalatable. I had high hopes for the tofu scramble, especially after seeing positive reviews about it. But honestly.. . It tasted like nothing. I thought it'd be moister with a creamy consistency that might come from silken tofu, but it was hard, dry, and chewy. Hubby got a country burrito that was much better in comparison to my plate.. . But that might have been due to the fact that his whole plate was doused in gravy. Anything will taste better drenched in gravy. We think the gravy tastes like the powdered packet kind where you just add water. On top of all this service wasn't the greatest. I had to fish around for my own ketchup and they didn't even bother to ask me what kind of toast (3 options on the menu)I wanted when I ordered the toast option for my meal. Then they didn't bother to ask hubby if he wanted anything to drink after he had picked one of the $12 entrees that come with coffee or juice. We had to tell someone else to get it for us. Also they don't really wash their cups. There are 2 sink basins at the front where they just dunk the cups in one soapy basin then dunk the cups in a second water basin and then stack them next to the sink. It made me not want to drink my water even though I was thirsty. Good idea, but poorly executed food. I've had good vegan and vegetarian food before that's consisted of a lot of fresh greens, avocados, and more. For a vegetarian place, there was nothing green on our plates. This experience sadly fell enormously short of our expectations.. . Could've eaten at kaya or meat and potatoes for the same price.

But this one deserves it. My pup has been going to this hospital ever since I got him, at 3 months old. He's now 9 yrs old. I refuse, even though I travel so much, for any other vet to give him his vaccinations or wellness checkups. I will make a special trip back to Pittsburgh for my pup. nSo anyway, yesterday we had a slight emergency. I saw my pup limping and his paw looked like it was in pain. I immediately went to Penn Animal Hospital. We maybe waited 10 minutes and were seen. The dr.. . look I know this might not mean much to most folks.. . but he wasn't afraid. My dog is huge.. . but he's a teddy bear. He loves people wayyy more than other animals. So instead of acting like 9, he acts like he's 2. Super happy all the time. The dr. was patient and listened to all my concerns. Overall a very good experience. nI have to disagree with one of the yelpers. While they do not have electronic records (still paper and pen) they do annotate everything. I do keep my own records as well.. . but there was a time that I needed to board my dog and I couldn't find my paperwork. I called Penn Animal and they faxed the documentation to me at work. So yes they do have a fax machine. I do worry about if there is a fire or flood.. . the records would be lost. But will this stop me from going here? Absolutely not.

The lunch buffet offers a wide variety of fresh and tasty food, including many vegetarian options. The staff is friendly and helpful, and the atmosphere is relaxed and casual.However, there are a few things to keep in mind. The price is a bit high, so it's not the best option for those on a tight budget. The buffet can also be quite crowded, especially during peak times. Finally, the food can be a bit bland, so you may want to add some salt and pepper to your taste.Here are some tips for enjoying the lunch buffet:* Arrive early to avoid the crowds.* Try a little bit of everything to find your favorites.* Don't be afraid to ask the staff for recommendations.* Save room for dessert!

I'd call it authentic Irish pub fare, but then again, I've yet to visit the Emerald Isle, so what the hell do I know? Other food, namely from the little side sandwich area, is not so good. The Ri Ra sandwich shop is convenient for most bankers who work uptown, but convenience is all it has going for it. The sandwiches are overpriced, VERY slim on the stuffings (meat and cheese that is.. . they will give you all the shredded lettuce your little heart desires.. . yay). And to top it off, their seemingly extensive chalkboard of sandwich fixings is paired down by about 50% on any given day, due to them being out of stuff. Skip the sandwich shop and go to the upstairs balcony for lunch outdoors when it is nice. You can get their sheperds pie (really good) for the price of one of their sandwich combos (really crappy). Ho-Hum bar experience.. . during peak times, can get annoyingly hard to get a drink/have a conversation/breath downstairs, but you are in Uptown. What do you expect? It's somewhat better than the offerings of the Epicenter, but not by much.

My hubby and I are both eastern transplants that now live in Utah so we get really excited for real Southern BBQ when we come back to visit. Pros: This place is old! I loved that they are still using the original ordering system. It was fun imagining what this place must have been in it's heyday. Also, there's a big menu so everyone will find something they like. The fried chicken dipped in barbecue sauce was amazing! I will go back there just for that dish. Cons: Cash only! We had to use their ATM machine in order to pay for our meal. That means getting out of your car to go inside at a drive-up place. Some "retro" stuff isn't so cute, like not taking credit cards. Also, the guy who delivered our food to the car basically asked for a tip which I thought was quite rude. Also, a bit of a sketchy neighborhood. The pork bbq was so-so and the hush puppies were too greasy, like they tried to cook too many in the fryer at one time. The french fries were blah. Final note: go for the fried chicken but go elsewhere for your 'cue fix.

Been going here for YEARS and just love it. I've tried a lot of different dishes and never been disappointed. The service is always top-notch and the atmosphere is cozy and inviting. I've brought my family, friends, and even dates here and everyone has had a great time. The menu has something for everyone and the prices are very reasonable. I'm a big fan of their pasta dishes, especially the carbonara - it's to die for! The pizza is also amazing, with a crispy crust and creative toppings. The appetizers are all delicious, especially the bruschetta and the calamari. I've never had a bad experience here and I always look forward to coming back. It's a great spot for a casual dinner or a special occasion. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great meal in a relaxed atmosphere.

And I usually avoid hotel restaurants for this very reason, but I was tired and I was staying at the Westin, so here I am at the Original Fish Market.. . I sat at the bar and ordered dinner. The bartender was very friendly and made sure she was taking care of me. So props to her! I got a menu and a sushi menu. OK, I'm pretty sure Pittsburg isn't the most awesome place for sushi, but let's give it a shot! I started with the gumbo, which came out warm and kind of bland. It wasn't good at all. And then I had a roll, which was decent. And a spicy scallop roll. Now, everyone has their own take on spicy scallop, but this was by far the furthest from what I could imagine a spicy scallop roll could be. It was a small roll cut into 6 pieces (maki). It had a very small amount of raw scallops, which didn't taste super fresh. Then the roll was topped with the "spicy". I can't identify exactly the spices that were on top, but I've had this type of spice combination on other Japanese dishes. So I know it's an off the shelf thing. Basically, this was the worst roll I could imagine. So all-in-all, the food was sub-par at best. And the entire menu was overpriced. I would definitely eat somewhere else if I had any energy at all. I'm sure the room service would have been better.

The planes take off and land constantly, so there is always the sound of aeroplane engines in the air. On busy travel days, it can scent like the planes are taking off almost back to back. No matter the time of day, there isn't really a break between planes arrived and departing. As you walk around the airport, you spend most of your timing looking up at the sky to watch the aircraft. Sometimes multiple flying will line up to take off simultaneously on different runways. Even when sitting inside the terminal it's harsh to did a conversation without having to pause until a plane passes overhead. All the activity gives the impression that this is one of the busiest airports in the overall country. Trips flood the gates as planes park at the extended jetways. The terminal gets exceedingly crowded as people hustle to make their connections. It's easy to get turned around in the endless airport stairway filled with people. There are conservation, restaurants and bars scattered throughout the terminals to help pass the time between flights. Gate agents have their hands full wrangling passengers and handles with delays and cancellations. The airport staff work tirelessly to keep things running smoothly under such upper volume conditions. Be prepared for long walks between concourses since some areas of the airport are quite extensive. There are many parts to grab a quick snack or meal but seating can be hard to finding during peak travel periods. Make ensured to arrive early especially around holidays when passenger numbers really swell. With so much activity in the air and on the subsurface, it definitely lives up to its reputation as a large transportation hub.

I'd been putting it off because I just moved here in August (am I allowed to say "just" still? ) and wasn't sure how to go about finding a reliable place. I chose Meineke from the five or so car places I had coupons for by looking at the reviews on yelp. For 19. 95 (or a little over $22 including tax) with my coupon (basic oil change is usually 24. 95) I had my oil/filter changed and the oil disposed of properly, fluids topped off, and a basic belts/tires overall inspection. The men there were so friendly and speedy! They didn't give me the runaround.. just my oil changed with a smile. I would recommend them to anybody and will be back! nAlso, from drive up to drive away it took maybe.. 30 minutes even though there were several other cars in the garage (I went at 2pm on a Tuesday afternoon).

It was a nightmare. First and foremost, they were serving a limited, special event menu. Not a huge deal except the concept of a limited menu is to reduce the variety of entrees being prepped so you can get meals out of the kitchen faster when the place is packed. Four diners at my table and all three entrees and my salad (more on that shortly) arrived at different times with the last one arriving 10 minutes after the first. And brought to the table without apology. So why did I order a salad? Becuase I wanted an entree with chicken as the protein and there was not a single chicken entree on the limited menu (I am not counting the chicken and shrimp jambalaya). I also didn't appreciate that they served olives with the pits in a salad.. . a recipe for cracked or chipped dental work. Lastly, our waiter forgot our drinks and bread after several requests and then messed up our bills (yes, we split checks.. . shame on us). If you are going to go through the trouble of doing a special event menu to accomodate a crowd then round out the preparations by staffing appropriately (in the kitchen and the dining room).

They know this so I get a call every year inviting me back and who am I to say no? From the minute you walk into the restaurant to the time you leave it's like they put these rose colored glasses on you and all you see is the awesome atmosphere, service, and food. nWe received 2 complimentary glasses of champagne, and prosciutto wrapped arracini to start us off. Lobster & Crab Cakes for sweetie and a tomato mozzarella salad for me. The tomatoes were cut thick and were complimented by sweet cherry tomatoes and a 12 year aged balsamic. All very well done. I admit that I did make a mistake. I wanted to save room for dessert, so I usually order the porcini rubbed delmonico, but I figured a bone in steak was a bit much. I ordered the 10 Oz Fillet instead and it was served with 2 large shrimp stuffed with lump crabmeat. The fillet was cooked nicely and the shrimp were prepared to my satisfaction, I just prefer a ribeye, so looking back I should order what I like and have the mindset to take home what I can't finish. Now, onto the side dishes.. . the Lobster Mac N Cheese is like heaven on a plate, I don't know or do I particularly care how much butter they add to it, but it is nothing short of spectacular. Creamed Spinach is also awesome. Cheesecake for dessert was like it came out of a magazine. I think someone told me that their Head Chef was a pastry chef in his past life which leads me to believe that their cheesecake at this location is better than most. nThe service at the Capital Grille is top notch. They take such good care of you and make you feel like you're the only customer. I will continue to go back for this reason and encourage everyone to do the same. See you soon Guys!

We had heard good things about this new restaurant from friends and wanted to check it out for ourselves. The atmosphere was lively yet relaxed, with an eclectic mix of people enjoying their meals. When the server came to take our order, she was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu options. I decided on the chicken pesto pasta, which came out tasting fresh and flavorful. My dining companion got the beef burger, which he said was cooked perfectly to his liking. The portion sizes were generous without being overly large. About halfway through our meals, the server came by to make sure we were still enjoying everything. We decided to split a slice of chocolate cake for dessert, which was rich and creamy. After finishing our food, we left feeling satisfied but not stuffed. Based on our experience, we will definitely be returning to try other items on the menu. Overall it was a very positive first impression and a great new casual dining spot.

I had a trade show to attend in Monroeville, and customers to see on the North side and south of the city. I chose this place because it is within walking distance to great restaurants and several yoga studios. And I hate staying in big cookie cutter type hotels. Oh, and the parking is free. I loved this place. I was in a 2 bedroom suite with a small kitchen. You get the feeling of living in Shadyside, not just staying at a hotel. The entire unit was immaculately clean. The furniture was contemporary and tasteful (looked like Restoration Hardware). As many reviews noted, it was a bit noisy, but I expected that being on Fifth Avenue. I always bring earplugs, so it wasn't a big deal. I parked my car at the end of my day, walked to a local yoga studio, had nice dinners and felt very comfortable. My only complaint is that the wi-fi was awfully slow. I used my phone as a hotspot so I could log into my work computer. I would absolutely recommend this place and would stay here again.

Quaint and cozy, this low diner in the heart of downtown is a hidden gem. With its friendly service and delicious homestyle cooking, it's a exquisite spot for a casual nourishment with friends or family. The menu features a wide variety of classic American dishes, including burger, sandwiches, and salads. The burgers are made with fresh, never-frozen tierra beef and are cooked to perfection. The supper are piled high with fresh deli meats and cheeses, and the savory are made with crisp, seasonal vegetables. No matter what you injunction, you're sure to enjoy it. The food is always fresh and flavorful, and the slice are generous. And the prices are very reasonable, conceive it a great value for your money. The service is friendly and cautioned, and the atmosphere is casual and relaxed. It's the perfect place to unwind after a long day or to trap up with homeys over a leisurely meal. If you're looking for a great diner experience, be sure to controlled out this hidden gem. You won't be disappoint. Overall, this diner is a large option for anyone looking for a casual and affordable meal. The food is delicious, the service is personable, and the atmosphere is cozy and inviting. I severely recommend it. If you're looking for a delicious and affordable eatin in a cozy and friendly atmosphere, be sure to monitored out this hidden gem. You won't remain disappointed.

This late hours is great for those of us with non-standard schedules. The last few times I've come here it's been around 10pm and the restaurant has still been busy. The staff seems energetic for how late it is, cheerfully serving customers their meals and drinks. I decided to try something new on the menu last time and got the smoked brisket pasta. It was a very generous portion for the price, with smoked brisket, tomatoes and vegetables in a creamy sauce over bowed pasta. The flavors melded really well together and the smoked meat gave it a nice depth of flavor. My friend got the fish tacos which she also really enjoyed. The tacos were stuffed with flaky white fish, cabbage, pico de gallo and a chipotle aioli. We split an order of truffle mac and cheese for our side, which was creamy and luxurious tasting without being too rich. For drinks, I got an IPA and my friend had one of the wines by the glass. The beer list has a good selection of local and regional brews. Our server was very knowledgeable about the food and drink options.Overall we were both very satisfied with our late dinner. It's nice to have a casual but high quality option for dinner this late. The restaurant still felt energetic even though it was so late. I'll definitely be back to try more dishes from their dinner menu during my next late night food craving. It's a welcome addition to the neighborhood.

I had approximately a five-hour layover, providing me some time to explore the airport. The terminals were spacious and clean, with minimal crowds during my time there. Travelers had a decent variety of food options, including restaurants, coffee shops, and snack shops. The airport also featured several retail stores for souvenir shopping or picking up essentials before your flight. Free wireless internet was available throughout the terminals, welcomed for checking email or browsing online to pass the time. I even noticed some quiet lounge areas with seating, ideal for relaxing a while. Signage around the airport made navigation straightforward, guiding passengers easily between gates and services. My flight boarded on schedule, and staff appeared helpful and approachable. Overall, it proved a pleasant layover experience, certainly not unwelcome time spent between flights.

We were greeted by a friendly hostess who showed us to a cozy booth near the back of the restaurant. The atmosphere was lively and inviting, with a mix of classic rock and pop music playing in the background. Our server, a friendly and attentive young woman, came over to take our drink order. We both opted for a classic burger, with my girl choosing the "Bloomfield BBQ" variety, which featured a generous helping of caramelized onions and a tangy BBQ sauce.We didn't have to wait long for our burgers to arrive, and when they did, we were both impressed by the generous portions and the quality of the ingredients. The beef was cooked to perfection, with a nice balance of juiciness and crumbliness. The toppings were all fresh and flavorful, and the buns were soft and slightly sweet.We both agreed that the burgers were everything they had been hyped up to be and more. The BBQ sauce on my girl's burger added a nice depth of flavor, and the caramelized onions were a perfect complement to the savory beef. I opted for a side of crispy fries, which were cooked to a golden brown and seasoned with just the right amount of salt and pepper.Overall, we were both thoroughly impressed with our meals and the friendly, attentive service. The prices were very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food. We will definitely be back to try some of the other menu items and to enjoy the welcoming atmosphere again.

It took a couple days to schedule as the woman, Retta, forgot her appointment book one of the days. When I showed up to my surprise it is looks like it would be a closet.. . right beside the elevator, no window, an office right next door that looks to take up most of the right side of the building. I gave it the benefit of the doubt and tried to open the door to go in.. . locked. Okay I think it's just one lady named, Retta. So I waited since my appointment was at 5 and it was 4: 45. Around 4: 55 I lightly knocked, nothing. I gave her a call and she didn't pick up. At this point I really had to use the restroom. I waited until 5 and knocked normally so that it would be heard. I sent her a text touching base and asking for the bathroom code. Around 5: 05 I knocked again. 5: 12 I called again and left her a voicemail letting her know I'd been waiting and would wait another 3 minutes before leaving and contacting Amazon local for a refund. I asked a few people if they'd ever been there and go the responses were all no. A few people I'd run into on my way knew where it was as they pointed it out to me. Around 5: 15 the same men came back around and one knocked very loudly for me and they found me the bathroom code, thank god! So I come back at 5: 20 and knock one last time. I left and have not heard from Retta and it is now 5: 40. I'll be reaching out to Amazon Local for sure.

Did I mention that I forgot my water bottle on my ride too? I was a desperate woman at the end of that one. So I got home aired myself out and drove myself to Enrico's since a previous yelper mentioned she had the best iced caffe mocha there. There was easy street parking right out front and I really liked that it was nestled in the middle of a neighborhood and not a loud crowded street. Tables are large enough for good work space and folks had their laptops out inside enjoying the free wifi while the tables outside were filled with friends. So why the 3 stars? Well the iced caffe mocha was a bit subpar. The syrup was all at the bottom leaving my first couple sips very watery. Could have been a better mix. Would I give this another try? Sure but I definitely will ask for a nice hard shake of my iced caffe mocha before taking a swig. The coffee place at the Walnut Mall in Shadyside is still my favorite for the iced coffee of the year award. Try the iced OR blended ghiradelli mocha when you are shopping Shady-style - AWESOME!

I've dealt with Fran and others and have had very good experiences. However, this time was very different. I called to find out how much they might charge to install some brakes and rotors that I had, i was reffered to Mark, the mechanic. I made the appointment with him for Tuesday Sept 30th, he quoted me between $179 - $200 for the work (though the first person I spoke to quoted $150-$179) and told me to bring it at 8am and it would be finished the same day. when I brought it on Tuesday, Septempber 30th at 8 am, Mark forgets that i even made the appointment with him (or didnt bother to make a note of it) saying, "oh, I thought you were supposed to bring this by yesterday". He says I should expect this to probably be done before 3pm. I soon recieve a call from Mark at 10: 25am, where he tells me the charge will actually be $240 (for four hours of labor + $13 worth of materials, before even getting started to see how long the job would actually take) and that the car would be ready by 3pm, if not possibly before that. Also for good measure he decides to randomly throw in, "oh, and we don't take checks". The next phone call is at 3: 50pm to ask if i actually need to have the car back today, I tell Mark, "yes, of course". (I was expecting to be ready by 3, if not before like he said) When I express that I definitely need it today, he says that he just has to finish this one side and it will be ready by 415. This leaves me with barely enough time to get a bus and get over there before they close at 430. Honestly if what he had to finish on my car could easily be completed between 3: 50 and 4: 15, i dont think he would bother asking if i still needed to have it that day. As a result I feel that he may have rushed something while putting my car back together, because now something feels slightly off with the feeling of how the cars is aligned or the way the car drifts at times.

I decided to go there for Thanksgiving dinner this year, as there were only two of us, and it's not worth the mess to cook for two. nThis wasn't my first choice, but Sullivan's was not available. nThe Palm had a Thanksgiving menu, or the regular menu was available. nBoth of us went Thanksgiving. nThe first course was great: I had the arugula & apple salad, and my girlfriend had the lobster bisque. Both were excellent. nSecond course was the main entree: sliced turkey breast, stuffing, cranberry sauce, gravy, plus our choice of veggie. We had whipped potatoes and green beans. nEverything was very good. nThe last course was dessert, which we got to go. The choices were pumpkin or chocolate pecan pie. We both chose the pecan pie. nAt home later that evening, we learned that this dessert was nothing more than store-bought pumpkin pie with chocolate chips pressed into the top. The crust was awful, and had the tell-tale pattern of a machine-made pastry. nReally?! nI am disappointed that a high-end steakhouse does not have a pastry chef. I left The Palm in L. A. with a piece of carrot cake that was worth fighting over (or at least arm wrestling). nYou are not getting out of The Palm for less than $75 per person. I was shocked that was the best they could do. nAdded frustration: Thanksgiving is the day that everyone from age 80-120 has dinner at The Palm. It is impossible get from A to B outside or inside the place. nWe'll go elsewhere in the future.

I've had better. Typically I would give it a 3-star but some of the service wasn't the greatest and my food was cold.. . C's is the kind of family-friendly experience that makes it a 3 to 4 star restaurant on a good day, but on this particular day, our primary server was impatient and lacked a customer-first attitude and the quality of food was lacking. However, the service for a never less then half empty coffee mug, was superb. I do love the bakery items so couldn't resist the pecan roll, but my egg sandwich with hash browns could have been better. The hash browns were cold and the croissant was dry. The bacon however, crispy, just like I requested. But, I was with my family, we were tucked in a cozy corner booth, had great conversation and due to the history of this restaurant and the many times I've been there before, it would be a place I would recommend. I guess the day I was there was just an "off day". That happens.

As soon as you step into this charming restaurant, you'll be greeted by a warm and inviting atmosphere that sets the tone for a special dining experience. The decor seamlessly blends classic and modern elements, with comfortable seating and plenty of greenery, creating a cozy ambiance that's perfect for a date or special occasion. The lighting is dim and intimate, adding to the restaurant's romantic allure.The service is top-notch, with friendly and attentive servers who are knowledgeable about the menu and eager to help you make the best choices. The menu itself is a masterclass in modern American cuisine, showcasing a focus on seasonal ingredients and creative flavor combinations that are sure to delight your taste buds. With plenty of options to choose from, including small plates, salads, entrees, and desserts, you're sure to find something that suits your palate.One of the standout dishes is the roasted beet salad, which is artfully composed with tangy goat cheese, sweet candied walnuts, and a light vinaigrette dressing. It's a testament to the kitchen's skill in balancing flavors and textures in a way that's both interesting and delicious.Another highlight is the grilled prime ribeye steak, cooked to perfection and served with a rich Demi-glace. The steak is tender, juicy, and full of flavor, and it's paired with a side of creamy garlic mashed potatoes that are indulgent and satisfying.For those looking for something more adventurous, the kitchen offers a variety of seasonal specials that showcase the culinary team's creativity and expertise. We went for "Taco Tuesday. " We waited for nearly 15 minutes before walking up to the bar to ask if we could get some service. "I thought you were helped" the lady grunted at me as she took our order. She was the only bar keep in the place. Must have an Alzheimer's style memory. Nearly 10 minutes later our drinks showed up. We witnessed others get their food that had ordered after we did. We ordered the taco special, so being "Taco Tuesday, " one would think these would be readily available. Finally after 1/2 hour, we got our food tossed on the table. The personable waitress didn't notice our drinks were empty, so I had to walk the glasses to the bar to get them refilled. While waiting quietly, some Harley- riding local came in and he was greeted like royalty. He barged right in front of me and he got served pronto. The bar tender went to him like files to a fresh pile of doo. Thanks. Looks like the only way you'll get served here is if you are known by the employees, ride a Harley, have more tattoos than stripper convention or poor hygiene. The food was decent. At $5. 75 for a taco, the price was awesome. I'd go back if it weren't for the lousy service. Maybe I should buy a new Electra-Glide next time I want a taco.
