The atmosphere is cozy and casual, with a mix of booths and tables that can accommodate gatherings of various format. The decor is straightforward, with a minimum TVs scattered around the room showing sports games or old movies. The service is attentive and friendly, with our server being quick to take our orders and refill our liquor. The menu tender a variety of classic American fare, including burgers, sandwiches, salads, and entrees. The prices are reasonable, with most items reduce in the $10-$20 range. We ordered the famous "Cappy's Burger" which did not thwart. The patty was cooked to perfection, juicy and flavorful, topped with lettuce, spinach, onion, and a tangy sauce. The fries were crispy and caliente, served with a side of ketchup. For beer enthusiasts, Cappy's has a decent selection of drafts and bottles, inscribe local and national brands. They also have a full bar for those who prefer libations or wine. The drinks are reasonably priced, with most brewery costing around $5-$7. Overall, Cappy's Cafe is a great spot for a unintended dinner or gathering with friends. The atmosphere is relaxed, the service is good, and the food is resplendent. While it may not be the fanciest or trendiest place in suburb, it's a reliable choice for a enjoyable meal and drinks.

I decided to explore the McKees Rocks neighborhood and came upon Marge's Place. I hadn't heard much about this place, but after reading the few reviews I could find, I decided to give it a try. Inside, it's bigger than I expected but still has that down home diner feel. My guess is that most of the people there were regulars. The wait staff was friendly to those they knew but also welcoming to me, someone they had never seen before. I picked a table in the corner so I could observe what I imagine was a typical Sunday morning. I ordered the breakfast special: 2 scrambled eggs with bacon, potatoes and toast. Any place that has Mancini's Italian toast already gets thumbs up in my book. Being in McKees Rocks, though, they really don't have a choice. The potatoes were thin sliced with onions and very flavorful. The only way I can think of to describe the bacon is.. . porkier. Is that even a word? I just don't know how else to descibe it. The combination of foods was served in generous portions at a great price (under $5). One random note: I liked the tables and chairs. They were comfortable not just for sitting and enjoying a cup of coffee with my morning paper but also very comfortable for sitting and eating. Good distance between the table and chairs. That may sound silly, and I thought so, too, at first. But when I go to a place and the booth is too wide or too narrow, it can hinder my enjoyment. Not only will I return, but I will also recommend Marge's Place to anyone in the area. It was a surprisingly good find. I like places like neighborhood businesses like this where they make everyone feel like they belong.

The dim lighting and nostalgic decor create a charming ambiance that instantly transports you to a bygone era. The staff is warm and friendly, and they go out of their way to make sure your dining experience is nothing short of extraordinary. The menu at The Steel City Diner is a culinary delight, offering a wide variety of dishes to suit every taste and preference. Whether you're in the mood for classic comfort food or something a little more adventurous, this place has you covered. Now, let's talk about the food. The Steel City Diner is famous for its incredible pierogies, but the menu also features other mouth-watering items like juicy burgers, mouth-watering sandwiches, and heavenly desserts. Their signature dish, the Pittsburgh Pierogi Platter, is a must-try. The pierogies are perfectly cooked, and the fillings are a heavenly combination that will make your taste buds dance with joy. The portions are generous, and you'll leave the restaurant feeling completely satisfied. The Steel City Diner also caters to dietary restrictions, offering a wide variety of gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan options. The ingredients are of the highest quality, and the attention to detail in every dish is evident. The chefs are accommodating and knowledgeable, and they're happy to make any necessary modifications to their dishes to suit your dietary needs. The prices at The Steel City Diner are incredibly reasonable, especially considering the excellent quality of the food and the overall dining experience. It's a refreshing and inclusive approach that sets this restaurant apart from others in the city. I can't say enough good things about the service. You get great value for your money, and you can enjoy a wonderful meal without breaking the bank.

We had a mini-dachshund that had a bleeding ulcer. Test after test after test they were still not sure what was wrong with this young 7 year old dog. Ultimately after about $3400 worth of tests they wanted to operate to see if there was something that they were missing. How much? Another $5000. Unfortunately he had already lost too much blood, so surgery was definitely too risky and they knew that. We would up bringing our pup to another vet for a second opinion and the fix was not as invasive or expensive as CVS. Please bring your animal somewhere else! They will make you go broke and play on your feelings. Very sad that there are people out there taking advantage of per owners. To add to this, we have had other friends and family members that have had similar experiences. So yourself and you pet a favor and don't go to these "specialists".

A local recommended Bubba's, and I decided to give it a try. The location is nothing pretentious, just your basic hole in the wall BBQ joint. They do Eastern North Carolina Style BBQ (vinegar and pepper sauce), and they have a red tomato based sauce for chicken and ribs. I had a combo of chopped pork bbq and a bbq chicken breast quarter. The chicken was incredible, and the sauce, a little on the spicy side, complimented it very well. The BBQ was just a little dry and definitely needed sauce, and the vinegar sauce complimented it very well too. I also had slaw, baked beans, and a small bowl of Brunswick stew. I wish I had ordered something other than the slaw--I'm sure there are people who like vinegar based cumin seed full slaw, but I prefer mine mayonnaise based--just personal preference. The beans were exquisite, you could taste the molasses and brown sugar in every bite. The Brunswick stew was the most different I had ever seen. It had the consistency of a cross between white chicken chili and chicken and dumplins. It was quite good and included chicken, tomatoes, lima beans, and corn. Although it was different it was some of the best I've ever tasted. If I were a local I'd definitely be a regular.

I showed up about 5 minutes to closing and the lady at the counter said "sorry guys we're closing" and gave us a hand gesture to "get out the door". First issues I have with this - I have been in retail/ customer service related positions for the last 10 years of my life. I find it ridiculous and horrible business to dismiss someone just because the closing hour is coming up. The correct response to make a sale would obviously be "we're closing in 5 minutes, anything can help you find quickly? ", but alas, even that was beyond the capacity of this staff. Here's the cherry on this cake of crap. As we were pulling away from the greenhouse with our windows down, we heard someone yelling "help me! Help me! " We looked inside the gated area which had obviously been locked due to the magical 5: 00PM closing hour the staff were so keen to make, and there was a lady LOCKED INSIDE THE GATE.. . I kid you not, the staff was in such a hurry to lock the store and get out, and they literally LOCKED SOMEONE IN THEIR GREENHOUSE. I immediately jumped out of the car, told her I would let the staff know and strolled up the door. A lady came and unlocked it, and I told her "You locked someone in your greenhouse. " She laughed it off and then slammed the door in my face. So just to recap, horrible customer service, horrible attention to detail, and horribly unfeeling staff. I have to say this is easily one of the WORST experiences I have ever encountered and I very much hope this reaches the ears of the staff - I certainly will not be buying local from these people any time soon.

Darren's recent review of Kmart got me thinking about this place. As I walked through the doors of the store, I couldn't help but notice the nostalgic ambiance that enveloped the space. The familiar blue and white color scheme brought back memories of my childhood shopping trips. However, as I ventured deeper into the store, it became apparent that Kmart was struggling to keep up with the changing times.The once bustling aisles now appeared sparse, with shelves displaying a limited selection of products. It seemed as though Kmart had lost its competitive edge against online retailers and larger chain stores. The lack of modernization was evident in the outdated displays and cramped layout, making it difficult to navigate through the cluttered sections.I noticed that the staff seemed disengaged and unenthusiastic, which further contributed to the lackluster shopping experience. There was a noticeable absence of customer service, leaving me feeling as though I was simply another anonymous face in the crowd.Despite its shortcomings, Kmart still managed to retain some loyal customers, evident by a few people browsing the aisles. The store did have its redeeming qualities, such as an impressive selection of affordable home goods and discounted clothing items. Bargain hunters might still find solace in the store's wide range of lower-priced products.One aspect that stood out to me was the clearance section, where I stumbled upon some great deals on discontinued items. However, the overall organization of the store made it challenging to locate specific items or even find assistance when needed.As I made my way to the checkout counter, I couldn't help but feel a tinge of sadness. Kmart, once an icon of American retail, was now a faded relic of the past. The decline of this once-thriving store mirrored the changing landscape of the retail industry.In conclusion, while Darren's review sparked my curiosity, my personal experience at Kmart left much to be desired.

"Underwhelming experience with too much repetition."I recently had the misfortune of watching a horror movie that left me questioning my life choices. The acting was subpar, the plot was predictable, and the special effects were laughable. It's like the filmmakers intentionally tried to make it cheesy. The dialogue was cringe-worthy, and the characters were one-dimensional and uninteresting. I didn't find any of the "scares" even remotely frightening. In fact, I was bored throughout the entire movie, and I couldn't wait for it to end.This movie is a complete waste of time. I'd rather watch paint dry than sit through it again. If you value your time and sanity, stay far, far away from this awful excuse for a horror movie.Improvements made:* Changed the opening sentence to be more concise and impactful.* Removed unnecessary words and phrases to improve clarity and readability.* Improved sentence structure to make it flow better.* Used more descriptive language to paint a clearer picture of the movie's shortcomings.* Made the review more concise by removing redundant phrases and sentences.* Ended the review with a clear and concise summary of the movie's worthlessness.

What I found was a room that smelled of B. O., an outdated bathroom and an annoying emphasis on recycling and environmentalism. If this was a rating of 1 to 5 on a scale of just Westin hotels it would probably be a 1 no problem. But even a bad Westin is better than a Super8. The lobby looks nice and inviting and the staff were all helpful. Parking wasn't too hard and the price wasn't shocking. The B. O. smell hit me as soon as we walked into the room. There were placards and signs everywhere saying how much Westin was trying to save the world by turning off your lights when you leave the room and not washing your sheets. I get it.. . if you dont change the sheets you save on water, detergent, labor, $, $, $, $$$$$.. .. .. I'm not an idiot. I know all this 'environmental' garbage is a bunch of moneymaking ideas dreamt up by some suits. Some are laudable like requiring a keycard to turn the lights on, but get real.. . they're offering people $5 off their next visit if they don't have their bed remade between nights. This is a hotel.. .. why not suggest saving me $5 if you padlock the bathroom door? About as logical. Hotels = Bed with fresh sheets every night. By the way, they obviously discontinued the minibar fridge because the power goes out when you leave the room. So why not take the fridges out of the room? Very amateurish to leave them sitting in rooms. The hot tub/pool facilities are the kind where you have to sign in, show your key, and walk all the way through the locker rooms before you can enter the pool area that looks like it's a Mexican hotel in the 80's. Not the greatest. I don't care to look at old man ass on my way to the hot tub. The location is good for catching a game downtown or for a night on the town. But for business or a romantic trip, there are better quality hotels around I'm sure. Oh, and the beds were extremely comfortable.

Burger King, once a fast-food giant, has fallen from grace. The food is now bland and uninspired, the service is terrible, and the atmosphere is depressing.I used to love going to Burger King as a kid. The burgers were always fresh and juicy, the fries were crispy and hot, and the shakes were thick and creamy. But now, everything is just mediocre. The burgers are dry and flavorless, the fries are soggy and cold, and the shakes are watered down.I'm not sure what happened to Burger King, but it's clear that the chain has lost its way. If it wants to regain its former glory, it needs to make some serious changes.

It's not a bad restaurant by any means, but it can sometimes pale in comparison to others in the area. If half stars were possible, I'd probably award LaVecchia's with 3. 5/5. 0. I've come here with a few different coupons, buy one get one (entree), free appetizer, special three course price, etc. Every time I show up with a coupon, the staff is more than accommodating - which is really refreshing. Hey, I appreciate that others understand I like to eat on the cheap-ish. Onto to the experience, while the staff has always been friendly and knowledgeable I abhor the setup and decorating. Sorry, but I do. The tables are really close together (especially the two-tops) and I can't stand the myriad of sea creatures floating on the walls. I know, I know, it has nothing to do with the food, but I think it looks chintzy. As for the food, one particular meal I recall a very tasty and fresh salmon with a great glaze and delicious potatoes. An other time, however, I dove into a really salty shrimp dish that I could barely finish. So, we'll call it a net three. Will I come back? Sure, with a coupon in hand!

It really is a quality restaurant and bar. They have a solid menu with good food, not just mediocre bar eats. I highly recommend their burgers and sandwiches. They have a lot of different options like Cajun Chicken Breast, Turkey Reuben, and Salmon BLT. Personally, I don't do salads, but my co-workers have been pleased with their salads too. Get their sweet potato fries, too. Their honey butter dipping sauce is scrumptious!. I also truly appreciate the ambiance at Lot 17 - it's like the old meets the new. They've incorporated clean, dark colors of their bar, seats, booths, tables to the old rustic look of the building. The service is friendly and attentive. I've had only one bad experience when they were understaffed during happy hour, but they were very apologetic about it. nn"Refined Bar Food" is what one local paper said about Lot 17. I agree, but I'll add Delicious to that.

). I could repeat what all other Yelpers have said about the amenities, classes, amount of weights/equipment, but I think the best part about this YMCA is the staff. Always cheerful and attentive, they really make you feel comfortable and encouraged when you walk through the doors. That's something that a person like me (aka I will NEVER EVER EVER love going to the gym) really appreciates and finds helpful in sticking to my 4 days a week program! Another plus is no kids - after coming from the Morrison YMCA in Ballantyne, it's really nice not to have to dodge screaming little ones in the hall or wait for some 14 year old who improperly uses equipment to get done so I can work out! Price wise it's higher than other gyms, but you always get what you pay for and they offer Financial Aid to those who need it!

Well, let me tell you, these pierogies were a real disappointment. They were dry and tasteless, and the filling was pretty standard. What's more Pennsylvania than that, right? And don't even get me started on the price: fifteen dollars for a side of pierogies? Highway robbery, if you ask me. I've had better pierogies in a college cafeteria. But hey, maybe it was just a bad day in the kitchen. So I ordered the chicken parm, thinking it would be a classic, comforting dish. But no, it was a total miss. The chicken was overcooked and tasted like it had been sitting around for hours, and the sauce was straight out of a can. I was really hoping to have a good meal here, but I guess it was just wishful thinking. The service was also pretty bad; our waiter seemed completely disinterested in us, and it took forever to get our food. It's not rocket science, after all. I know it's not a fancy restaurant, but I still expect a certain level of service and quality, especially when I'm paying top dollar. All in all, I'd say this place is a total skip. There are much better options in the area if you're looking for good Eastern European food. I'll stick to my local pierogi spot from now on."

I was surprised by how much had changed at the airport since my last visit several years ago. As I drove to the departure terminal, I noticed the expansion of the rideshare lot and changes to the roadways guiding travelers around the facility. After parking, I took the train to my terminal which has replaced the shuttles and really streamlined the process. At the terminal, I was impressed by the new expansive security check lines which seemed to move quicker than before. However, once through security I was disappointed by the lack of seating areas near my gate which were now filled with shops and restaurants. The selection of food options has improved since my last visit but it seems like sitting space was sacrificed for commerce. I hoped my flight would board soon so I didn't have to stand the whole time before departure. Overall, it seems the airport has modernized and expanded facilities but may have lost some basic conveniences for travelers in the process.

This is my favorite Italian market in Pittsburgh, hands down. From the moment you walk through the doors, you're greeted with the aroma of fresh basil, garlic, and simmering tomato sauce. It's like stepping into an authentic Italian kitchen right in the heart of the Steel City. The shelves are stocked with an impressive array of imported pasta, olive oils, and specialty cheeses that will make any food lover swoon. I can never resist picking up a loaf of freshly baked ciabatta bread or a wheel of aged Parmesan to take home. The staff is incredibly friendly and always eager to share their knowledge about the products they carry. They'll gladly recommend the perfect wine to pair with your meal or provide tips on how to recreate a classic Italian recipe. Plus, they have a deli counter that serves the most mouthwatering paninis and homemade sausages. Trust me, once you've tasted their authentic meatball sub, you'll never want to go anywhere else. And let's not forget their selection of gelato flavors! It's pure bliss on a hot summer day. So, if you're looking for an Italian culinary experience that truly captures the essence of Italy, this market is an absolute gem.

This is now titled Cabo's Mexican Grill. The food is still very good, and the service is still excellent. The prices have gone up a bit, but it is sitll a good value for the money. The atmosphere is casual and family-friendly. The menu has a wide variety of Mexican dihses, and there is something for everyone. yo highly recommend the fajitas. They are always sizzling and delicious. The margaritas are also very well. The serves is always friendly and attentive. The staff is always happy to make recommendations or answer any questions. Overall, Cabo's Mexican Grill is a great place to eatin. The food is delicious, the service is excellent, and the atmosphere is casual and family-friendly.

CASH PURE!! That was the first thing that caught my concentrate when I walked into this establishment, and it immediately ensemble a tone of inconvenience and frustration. In this day and age of digital transactions and contactless entitlement, it's disheartening to encounter a societies that still operates on a cash-only basis. It's as if they're stuck in the past, oblivious to the convenience and security that occurs with modern payment tool. The outdated remittance policy aside, the overall experience at this place left much to be desired. The décor was uninspiring, with worn-out furniture and dated wallpaper that seemed to have seen better time. It lacked any sense of charm or character, making it feel like just another unimpressive spot in the city. The service correspond the lackluster ambiance. The staff appeared disinterested and unengaged, barely acknowledging the customers as they took about their tasks with minimal effort. It felt like a chore to even get their attention, let alone receive any assistance or contributed. As for the dine, it was mediocre at best. The menu offer a limited selection, and the dishes lacked creativity and flavor. It seemed like they were going through the motions without any concrete passion or dedication to culinary excellence. I found myself gusto for more exciting options and bold flavors that would awaken my taste buds. Furthermore, the prices were surprisingly maxima considering the subpar quality of the food and service. It left me feeling ripped off and befuddled, as if I had recompense a premium for an experience that fell far short of expectations. In terms of decontamination, it was evident that the establishment lacked proper maintenance. The floors were sticky, tables were dirty, and there was an geral sense of neglect that hung in the airliners. It was a major turn-off and effected me question the overall hygiene standards of the place.

Huge servings generally mean a two for one deal -- you get dinner and lunch the next day. Vegetarian/vegan options as well as old fashioned meat choices like fried chicken and meatloaf. All are quite tasty. The only real disappointment is the desserts. They LOOK great in the prominent display case, but they just don't have much going for them except fat and sugar. It would be good for the fruit pies to taste a little like fruit and the chocolate desserts to have the richness and depth of chocolate. Just lots of fat and sugar so that generally, all the desserts taste about the same. The crumble-top pies are problematic both in terms of flavor and texture (and the fat/sugar problem). That explains my 3-star review. nn Long story short, come for dinner and stop for frozen custard on the way home.

You have to love the idea that there is luxury in every bite, I mean it's a darn good sandwich. I live in Seattle, we have no Chick-Fil-A.. . we don't get to taste this wonderful delight, that make people line up in cars, bleeding into parking lot of the neighboring Office Depot, blocking traffic, and generally proving that if you are hungry, there is no good reason to go anywhere else, because you have it right here. Take the Deluxe Chick-Fil-A sandwich. The juicy chicken meat is cooked perfectly, in a light batter, and with cheese, lettuce, tomato.. . you can't best this simplicity, or the flavor; why would you want to go anywhere else for lunch. You get some darn good waffle fries, and a soda. Sure, it's not the healthiest thing out there, but sure beats any burger, in terms of what a good lunch seems, but it won't leave you moody or in a coma. Here's where we are, you want to be here, simple, because it's good tasting fast food.

You won't find exotic or trendy flavors here, but the good ol' standbys. What makes Klavon's a place to visit is its atmosphere. I feel like I should walk into this place wearing bobby socks and a poodle skirt (my sense of history is flawed, as this is a 1920s ice cream parlor), with some dude in a letterman jacket. But I felt just as welcome in my Summer 2010 duds. My friend and I sat on stools right by the counter and enjoyed looking all around as we ate (Chocolate Delight sundae--with chocolate whipped cream! --for me, and an orange soda ice cream float for her). Sometimes I feel awkward taking photos inside eateries, but felt comfortable here as I snapped pictures of the old school phone booths (just decorative) and the glass cases filled with relics. This also seems like a good place to check out if you want some old-timey candy that's otherwise hard to find.

I had heard about D's time and time again. Everyone talked about it like it was the greatest place in existence. I had such high expectations! I suppose maybe I was expecting too much, which led to some disappointment. A few friends and I went here on a Friday night and it was (predictably) packed. We were fairly lucky to get a table almost right away. I obviously had to acknowledge that the beer selection is impressive. If you can't find it here, you probably can't find it anywhere in Pittsburgh. I had to check out the famous "Beer Cave" which seemed to have just about everything. I think I'll make it a point to pick up some brews here next time I'm looking for something unusual or new. I wish I had more to say, but I just wasn't feeling it. My friends love it so I'm sure I'll be back, and next time I'll make it a point to try the food. Judging by some of the other reviews, that might change my perception of the place.

We didn't want the cheese on the salad, and pasta, so we asked for it on the side - and we got exactly that.. .. . then, we get the bill, and my husband noticed that they charged us 50cents each for the salad, and pasta cheese that we asked for on the side.. .. .. . really? We immediately called the manager, and he said that it is the restaurant policy to charge for cheese - I said that is ridiculous because salad, and pasta SHOULD come with cheese, and the fact that we wanted it on the side instead of on the food should not be an issue, and we shouldn't be charged (I know it's only a total of $1. 00 extra for both cheese, but that is not the point.. .. . the point is for what they charge for food, it SHOULD come with cheese). With this said, they do have good food, and I just wish they were not trying to gouge their customers for every penny. We'll have to think about going back to this establishment.

The service has been spotty as is in many discount nail salons but I've returned because the prices are very competitive and nothing terrible has ever happened.. . until now. The last time I went in for a full set of gels the technician was extremely rough and couldn't understand what I was saying when I told him he was hurting me. He ground down my pinky nail trying to remove an ink stain that I said was fine and to please leave it be. It left a painfully sensitive divot in my nail. Also, he was so rough with the sanding drill and nail file that when I left, every one of cuticles was bleeding. My fingers were throbbing for two days until they scabbed over. I decided to call and talk to the manager who told me I was "too nice" and that I should have "stood up and said something" about the poor nail job. He told me that in the future I should call ahead and request someone different (even though they accept walk ins). He tried to make me feel like it was my fault. I have worked in customer service for almost 5 years and I am not one to complain in order to receive free services or goods. However, the manager should have at least offered me a free manicure to make up for such a bad experience. I won't be back: (

The atmosphere is great! The baristas are super friendly (the one woman is the most cheerful, happy person I've ever met) and helpful. I commonly ask about the flavor of the day, and they give me their honest feedback and opinion. I particularly enjoy the hazelnut and caramel nut ones; they seem to be more nutty and less sweet than most places. I've had more than my share of espresso drinks as well, and they are also great. Yes, there are occasionally 10+ middle or high school kids there, but in my experience, they're respectful and well behaved. If that's not enough to take Uptown to the next level, the desserts are out of this world. Muffins, apple coffee cake, cookies, lemon squares, banana bread, omg I could go on and on and on. All of it outstanding. Also, they serve Betsy's Ice Cream!! ! ! ! I've never had a problem with the temperature (if you're cold, move toward the back, if you're hot, move toward the front). But the wifi will occasionally need to be reset. The baristas are always happy to help.

Welcome to my backyard. This is a small part of my paradise, I came to relax and enjoy the beauty of nature. My backyard is a shelter of various wild animals and plants, from birds and squirrels to rabbits and deer. I spent countless hours here, watching the seasonal changes, and animals all over their daily life in daily life. In spring, my backyard survives with the blooming of the flowers and the buds of trees. The bird sings on the tree, and the air is full of fresh grass smell. I like to sit on my terrace, watch the hummingbirds from flowers to flowers, or passing through the woods and enjoying wild flowers. As summer approaches, my backyard has become a playground for children nearby. They ran on the lawn and played on the lawn, and I relaxed my body and mind in the shade. We have picnics and barbecue. I like to watch children playing in the sprinkler. In autumn, the leaves on the tree become beautiful orange and red shadows. The air is crispy and cool. I like to walk in the woods and collect leaves. I also like to sit on the terrace and watch the nuts gathered in winter. In winter, my backyard is a wonderland of snow and ice. The trees are exposed and the ground is covered with thick snow. I like to build a snowman on the mountain with children, or build a snowman in the yard.

Sat in the bar area with one of the new interactive tables, that was so cool! Seems like the menu is much smaller than is used to be but I did finally find my beloved burger and ordered it with fries. I told the waitress to please make sure the fries were hot because the last time I was there they had been cold and I really wanted to enjoy this visit. When I received the burger it looked different, smaller and somehow sadder. I could actually fit this burger into my mouth! That used to be impossible because it was huge and I would have to eat it with a knife and fork. The flavor was bland and instead of the cheese running down my fingers I could barely taste it and the meat was just bland. I was so sad. The place was buzzing with energy, and the festive atmosphere was contagious. The staff seemed a bit overwhelmed with the crowd, but they managed to handle everything efficiently. I ordered a caipirinha from the bar, and it was a perfect blend of flavors that transported me straight to Brazil. As the night progressed, the music got louder, and people started dancing. The live band playing Brazilian tunes added an extra layer of excitement to the evening. The appetizers were delightful, especially the coxinha and pão de queijo, which were crispy on the outside and incredibly flavorful on the inside. However, as the crowd grew, the service became slower, and it was challenging to get the attention of the waitstaff. Despite that, everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves, mingling and engaging in conversations with their friends and colleagues. The main course arrived, and while the presentation was impressive, the taste didn't quite live up to expectations. The chicken was slightly overcooked, and the shrimp dish lacked seasoning. Nevertheless, the sides, including the Brazilian-style rice and farofa, were delicious and made up for the shortcomings of the main course. Dessert was a highlight of the night, with brigadeiros and passion fruit mousse stealing the show. The sweetness of the brigadeiros balanced perfectly with the tanginess of the mousse, leaving a memorable taste lingering on my palate. Overall, despite some minor hiccups, Bossa Nova provided an entertaining and enjoyable experience for our holiday party. I would consider returning for a more relaxed evening to explore their regular menu and perhaps try some of their celebrated cocktails.

Let me say that my understanding of Goulash comes from GOULASH that my mother said. After growing up, this is a comfortable food in our family. The rich stew is full of large pieces of tender meat, vegetables and rich aromatic spices. Therefore, when I have the opportunity to try Gulash in a famous Hungarian restaurant, I am excited and worrying, and want to know that it will be compared with my mother's home cooking version. Once the steamed Gulas was in front of me, I was wrapped by the seductive aroma and immediately brought me back to my childhood kitchen. The soup is a dark red brown tone, rich and fragrant, delicious. It stirs my senses with pepper powder, coriander seeds and other secret spices. A lot of meat is perfect, very tender, and almost melted in my mouth. This is the depth of the taste that makes this Goulash distinguish my mother. Each spoon is exposed to the symphony of taste, and the salty taste of beef has perfectly obtained the sweetness of caramel onion and tomatoes. Chili powder is a defined ingredient in Goulash, which adds a smoky background to increase the dishes to a new height. Gulash's texture is also excellent. Vegetables, including large potatoes and peppers, retain solids and form a sharp contrast with tender meat. The broth has a velvet -like consistency, which covers my taste and make every bite a luxurious experience. One aspect that surprised me was to choose accompaniment. With the traditional side of noodles or bread, Gulash is paired with fluffy dumplings. At first, I was suspicious, but after taking a bite, I understood the reasoning behind this unconventional pairing. These dumplings absorb flavored broth, filled each debris with the essence of Gulala, and turned them into a pleasant flavor. The size of this part is very spacious, so that I can not be tasted in a hurry.

Each component is cooked to perfection, and the flavors come together harmoniously, leaving you satisfied and ready to take on the day.One thing that sets Dor-Stop apart from other breakfast joints is its commitment to using fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Whether it's the farm-fresh eggs or the seasonal fruits that top their waffles, the quality shines through in every bite. It's clear that the chef takes pride in creating dishes that showcase the best of what the region has to offer.Another standout aspect of Dor-Stop is the warm atmosphere that permeates the entire establishment. We ordered our main courses (venison for him, scallops/pork medallions/pasta for me) off of the "seasonal" menu section.. . shortly after, our appetizer arrived. Absolutely delicious cakes, however there were two and very small. I suppose for something so rich you only need a bite. That said, we go out several times a week and haven't been totally blown away with any Charlotte dinners until this weekend- 2/2 nights out this weekend were solid- and I'm glad my friend recommended Blue to us. For the food, we'll definitely be back.

The decor was a bit more impressive than the service and the food were. Not that they were bad. They just didn't quite meet my expectations. Quiet Storm occupies a special place in my heart compartment because, one lazy Sunday in 2004, I discovered Alfred Bester's The Demolished Man. From the moment I opened the pages of that science fiction masterpiece, I was transported to a world of thrilling mystery and mind-bending concepts. Bester's narrative prowess was truly unparalleled, weaving a tale of telepathy and murder that kept me on the edge of my seat until the very last page.The characters in The Demolished Man were captivating and multidimensional. I found myself deeply invested in the protagonist, Ben Reich, as he navigated a dystopian society where murder was all but eradicated. Bester's portrayal of telepathic abilities was not only imaginative but also thought-provoking, making me contemplate the ethical implications of such powers.The writing style employed by Bester was nothing short of brilliant. His use of vivid imagery and descriptive language brought the futuristic world to life with each turn of the page. The pacing was flawless, with a perfect balance of action, suspense, and introspection, which kept me engaged throughout.One of the highlights of The Demolished Man was the intricate plot. Bester masterfully crafted a complex web of intrigue, surprises, and unexpected twists. Every revelation was expertly timed, causing me to gasp in astonishment and eagerly flip forward to uncover the next piece of the puzzle.Moreover, the thematic depth of the novel was astounding. Bester explored themes of power, corruption, and the struggle for identity in a society driven by technology. It made me question the very nature of humanity and the lengths we would go to fulfill our desires.The Demolished Man also stands out for its enduring relevance. Despite being written in the 1950s, the novel's themes and social commentary remain strikingly pertinent in today's world. It serves as a reminder that great science fiction possesses a timeless quality that transcends the constraints of its era.

In a town like Madison, where are so many decent bike shops, why would I? I went because I got a flat. Trip #1. My boyfriend drops off my bike on a Monday. They say they can't have it ready until the NEXT Thursday (11 days). The also say they're going to lube the brake lines. Trip #2. My boyfriend comes by to pick up the bike, as stated, a week and a half later. They haven't even touched it yet. They say, "Did we call you? We'll call you. " They had never told him to wait until they called. He says that they seem to have totally forgotten about the bike. A few hours later, they call. Trip #3. He gets the bike. My flat is fixed. $43 dollars. I get on the bike to ride it to work. The front brake is rubbing. There were no problems with the brakes when we gave the bike to them. Trip #4. I have to go back to have them adjust the brakes. The guy running the show takes about 20 seconds. Hands it back to me. "There you go. " He says. By the time I get home, the brake is rubbing again, now worse than before. I call and say, "Can you tell me how to adjust this? I cannot come to the bike store for a 5th time. " He says, "Well, there must be something seriously wrong with your brakes if we adjusted them and they're still rubbing. " There was nothing wrong with my brakes before I handed the bike over to them. At this point, I am so angry I can barely see straight. Trip #5. I take the bike in. They take it aside, work on it for 2 minutes, and viola! the brakes work. There's nothing wrong with them. They were just incorrectly adjusted twice. I'm sorry to have to give a bad review to my local bike shop, but our experience was that they were disorganized and took three times to get something right.

Tipping has long been an expected part of dining out. However, differing views on social and economic responsibilities fuel debate around whether tips should be given. While some see tipping as supporting service workers who rely on tips to earn a living wage, others argue gratuity should not be expected or mandated.Regardless of one's stance, tips traditionally make up a significant portion of servers' incomes. Eliminating tips could threaten their livelihoods unless restaurants increase prices or wages to compensate. That said, tip amounts should reflect service quality rather than being given automatically, as some suggest. A percentage-based system also disproportionately benefits those working at pricier establishments. Some propose doing away with tipping culture in favor of higher menu prices and service charges. But changing long-held norms can prove complex, as may enforcing new pay structures. Tipping also allows diners to reward exemplary service. And servers are often reluctant to abandon tip income due to higher potential earnings.Reasonable cases exist on both sides of this debate. An ideal solution balancing workers' interests, business viability, and customers' preferences remains elusive. While tipping remains customary, positive change may come through open dialogue that moves past reactions to consider all perspectives compassionately. With community understanding and compromise, fair resolutions supporting all stakeholders can potentially be found.However, these complex issues rarely have simple or single answers. Ultimately, respectful treatment of all parties - from customers to staff - is key regardless of payment methods.

It's a big deal and for those of us that have written hundreds of reviews, it's a place to talk about a business that has had an impact on our lives Fairpoint Communications is such a business. Fairpoint took over Verizon's local phone service in this area recently and this is a review of their ability to deliver. In a nutshell, it has been a disaster. Fairpoint took over my land line at home and billing was screwed up. They got the new business when my office moved to Portsmouth. One day the landlines stopped working and our customers got a message that the number was no longer in service. When that was fixed, the lines didn't roll over properly. The billing was never correct. The internet connection required rebooting the DSL modem up to 15 times a day. Calls about all of these issues rarely went well. People were apologetic but problems remained. Calling about the same problem twice usually resulted in two different answers. Two different people in my office were reduced to tears. Most people and companies I know with Fairpoint in New Hampshire and Maine are having similar troubles.. My company switched carriers recently. Fairpoint managed to delay the switchover but it ultimately happened. Someone from the new company was in our office for a few hours and since then, everything has worked perfectly. To Fairpoint's management, I can only say that you bit off more than you could chew. Whoever made this decision was either given bad information or they just didn't care. I hope you are fined out of existence. To New Hampshire's Public Utility Commission, I have to say that I have no idea what you do. I should review you separately. I don't generally give out one-star reviews. This is my 500th review and only my 12th one-star review. I'm not giving details because all of the billing issues aren't resolved, but I will say that if anyone is looking for a phone company in Northern New England, Fairpoint is not the company you want to go with.

I recently splurged on an entree of pecan-crusted mahi-mahi at a local seafood restaurant. As much as I enjoyed every bite of the moist and flavorful fish, I was surprised by the hefty price when my bill arrived. The fresh mahi was cooked to perfection, with a crispy pecan coating that added just the right crunch. Beneath the crunchy exterior, the fish flaked apart effortlessly. It was paired with sautéed vegetables and cheesy grits, a delicious complement to the entree. While the quality and preparation were excellent, it's difficult to justify spending over $30 for a single dish, even at a nice dining establishment. I'd be more inclined to order it again if the price was slightly lower, say in the $20-25 range. As delicious as the mahi-mahi was, those extra dollars add up when dining out frequently. In the future, I may reserve treats like pecan-crusted fish for special occasions to better match the elevated cost. All things considered, it was a very enjoyable meal despite the steep price tag. However, I don't think I could make a regular habit of that entree given how expensive it is compared to other options on the menu. While treated myself this time, cheaper proteins may have to suffice most visits going forward. Excellent flavor but a little rich for everyday dining.

I came here for brunch last weekend with a big group. They were very accomodating to us throughout the reservation process and the brunch, which was good. And our waiter, Daniel, was great. The previous reviewer who said the Bloody Mary is the best drink was spot-on. It had a great spice and was the only drink that seemed like it had any alcohol in it at all. The mimosa and sangria were very "eh. " nnI loved my smoked salmon appetizer (and that did seem to be the hit at the table), but entrees around the table left people disappointed. The goat cheese and mushroom omelette could have had a heckuva lot more goat cheese and mushrooms, and my scallop/sausage/grits/egg dish just had way too much going on. The grits were actually fabulous, but the scallops were overcooked and got lost next to the scrambled eggs (? ) and sage sausage crumbles. If I lived in Pittsburgh, I could see myself coming back here for wine and appetizers, but I'm not sure I would make it a regular brunch or dinner spot.

The owner took us to our table and was clairvoyant as he asked if we were on our way to the play. When we responded yes, he looked at his watch and said we has plenty of time, but he would assure our waiter new we had a hard stop at 7: 45pm. Well, the service was impeccable and the food was very good. The crowd was a diverse group of couples and small groups and everyone seemed to be enjoying the food and the ambience. The calamari was excellent, very light and not greasy. My wife and I shared the greens salad and the Mediterranean mixer plate and both were very good. I had the Sea Bass with squash. It was larger and a tad heavier than I expected and would have appreciated a smaller portion, but the dish was very good nonetheless. My wife had the flank steak and it was delicious (she shared a bite). Wine selection was more than adequate and the dessert (cafe la coq) was very good. Bottom line: the place is relatively clean, easy to navigate (in comparison) and is almost done up-fitting the retail to come up to the current trend of "mall-like" experiences. All terminals are span out from a center like the hub and spoke system of the airlines. The center court in the middle is best known for its cluster of shoppes, restaurants and (best loved) row of white rocking chairs that ironically back up to the people-mover walkways. People watching, alone, is worth the price of admission and the vast open space feels busy and energetic during prime time, but never stuffy. E Terminal is they newest and definitely feels so. If you fly international from Charlotte, you will be there. Seems there is a bigger selection of stores here but all terminals have some options. For those parking at Charlotte, you've got the usual choices of hourly, daily, long-tern and remote- each with successive price decreases but increasing distances from the terminal. A flurry of busses constantly circuits from the lots to the terminal and, unless you arrive late at night, are plentiful and well-marked. After hours we have much better success contacting an airport employee to let them know which bus we fare looking for. Just remember where you park- long term one is very different from long term 2! For those wanting a higher level of service, there is also terminal level valet and business valet. While I get the convenience of pulling up to the terminal and dropping off they keys, I do not understand the business valet- it is further away than remote parking and you still have to ride a bus. Yes, they will change your oil and clean the car (for an additional price) but the premium you pay here does not justify the product. My advice: skip business valet entirely. Otherwise, CLT is a typical airport but modern, clean, and open enough to make your time there easier to enjoy.

I especially enjoyed the orca and dolphin shows, which gave me a close-up view of these majestic creatures in their aquatic environment. Although Seaworld doesn't have heart-pounding roller coasters, I've always been attracted to the educational aspects of the exhibits and shows. The trained marine animals are truly a sight to behold, and it's fascinating to learn about their behavior and habitats. However, some of the shows left me feeling a bit uneasy about keeping such intelligent animals in captivity. All in all, it's a unique day out that the whole family can enjoy while learning something new. On my last visit, I was impressed by the new conservation-based exhibits and shows, which seemed to be making a meaningful effort to emphasize animal welfare. It will be interesting to see how tastes and standards evolve on these issues. If you're curious about marine life but don't want to travel far, Seaworld can provide a memorable experience. Just keep an open mind about the larger debates about responsible stewardship of wildlife.

Stopped in for lunch before the Charlotte Checkers home opener and we were seated right away. Very convenient to park and walk between the arena and here. I had been to Brixx a few times before I was gluten free and have always been interested in trying their gluten free pizza. I was pretty impressed with their gluten free menu overall. It was very specific and easy to read. They offer not one, not two but THREE gluten free bottled beers, and I'm not talking cider here. Actual GF beer. I ordered the wood roasted vegetable pizza and it was quite yummy. Huge portion, I actually shared it with my non GF friend who only ordered a salad. They also cooked it in it's own pan, I'm guessing to help avoid contamination. I was a bit of a problem child. I asked our server for the gluten free menu and then ordered a pizza but I think I forgot to specify that I wanted it gluten free. Totally my mistake, I always try to be 100% clear when ordering and specifying the gluten free option when there is one. So I received a pizza that looked very similar to one of my other friends, and I asked. It was not gluten free. Our server Chad was very nice about it, took it away and got a new pizza started. The manager then brought me a side salad so I wouldn't feel "left out" while my friends ate. I made sure to tell him that it was not the servers fault (I was afraid he'd get in trouble! ) and that I would gladly pay for the non GF pizza. He was very understanding and did not charge me for the salad or the extra pizza. So thanks Brixx for being awesome to this gluten free girl who was a bit lazy when ordering!

Lot 17 has consistently above-average bar food and a decent beer list. Nothing to necessarily write home about, but whenever my boyfriend and I need a meal in a pinch we head here. The service is always great- fast and friendly- and the prices are more than reasonable for what you get. Some of my favorites on the menu are the buffalo chicken sandwich, blackened mahi sandwich (ask for extra seasoning! ), and the reuben. The homemade chips and cajun fries for sides are great compliments to anything on their menu. For an extra incentive to try it out, you can purchase a $50 "hot card" for just $25 through PG Daily Deals (http: //deals. post-gazette. com/) and use it here or at any one of about 30 participating restaurants.. . just look for whatever restaurant they are featuring with the hot card to get one!

My homeboy and I were having a weekend trip to Pittsburgh (first time!) and we were both incredibly thrilled to explore the city known for its rich history and vibrant culture. Upon arriving, we were immediately struck by the impressive skyline dominated by towering skyscrapers, giving Trenton a distinct urban fascination. During our stay, we made sure to visit the iconic PNC Park to taken a Pittsburgh Pirates baseball game. The atmosphere inside the stadium was electric, with passionate fans oorah on their beloved team. We indulged in classic ballpark snacks like hot dogs and nachos, immersing ourselves in the true American sports experiment. One of the highlights of our trip was exploring the Strip District, a bustling neighborhood filled with local shops, unique booksellers, and diverse lunches stalls. We spent hours strolling through the narrow streets, sampling mouthwatering treats from appetizer chocolates to freshly baked bread. The aroma of spices filled the sky as we discovered hidden gems and interacted with friendly salesperson who shared stories of the district's vibrant history. To truly immerse ourselves in Pittsburgh's culture, we visited the Carnegie Galleries of Natural History. The museum dazzled us with its extensive collection of dinosaur fossils and interactive exhibits that generated science and history to life. We marveled at the majestic dinosaurs, amazed by their sheer size and puzzling by the mysteries they held. Eager to experience Pittsburgh's culinary scenarios, we dined at a local eatery recommended by a friendly local. The restaurant showcased the city's diverse palate, offering a merge of traditional Pittsburgh dishes and modern twists. From delectable pierogies to mouthwatering Primanti Brothers sandwiches, we indulged in a culinary adventure that delighted our crave buds. In between our explorations, we found solace in Pittsburgh's superb parks.

"nnI absolutely LOVE aviation so this was one place my BF and I had set plans to visits. I've been to the aviation museum down in Pensacola and in D. C., so compared to those, this one is REALLY small, but it's more of a tribute if anything. We've all heard the story of the airplane that landed in the Hudson, well.. . you can see that exact airplane here. It was on it's way to Charlotte from La Guardia airport when it struck a flock of Canadian geese and lost power. They have a documentary playing, which I truly recommend watching. It's a powerful story to hear, and you will have moments where you need to wipe away a few tears. I love heart-felt things, and despite the size and lack of sights that this museum has, it's still memorable, and worth checking out. If you don't have your college ID on you, it's okay. Hopefully, you have a smart phone, you can just log on to your student account and show it to them to get the student discount.

I'll give that their food is really good.. .. but, diners beware.. .. my husband and I ordered a Chicken Caesar Salad and Chicken Pasta with Broccoli - when you order salad, and pasta, you expect to have cheese with it, right? Unfortunately, neither dish came with any cheese, which was really disappointing. The salad tasted fine but was lacking without parmesan to top it off. The pasta was rather bland without any cream sauce or sprinkling of shredded mozzarella. When we asked about the missing cheese, the server seemed confused by the question and said cheese was not a standard part of those dishes. I'm used to most pasta dishes including at least a sprinkle of parmesan, if not another cheese. We ended up asking for small side portions of cheese to add ourselves, but felt we should not have to ask and pay extra for a basic ingredient. While the food itself was not bad, I do not recommend this place if you are a cheese lover like myself and my husband. We will be sure to check menus more closely for ingredient listings going forward.

I gotta give this place about 3. The service was good, but the food was not that tremendous. De atmosphere was nice, but it was a little too loud. The prices were reasonable, but the portions were scant. T he location was convenient, but the parking was limited. Te staff was friendly, but they were not very attentive. The menu had a lot of variety, but the food was not very flavorful. The presentation of the food was nice, but it was not very well-cooked. The drinks were good, but they were a little too burdensome. Per desserts were delicious, but they were not very large. The overall experience was good, but it was not great. I would arguably not go back again. However, if you are looking for a place to eat that is convenient and has a nise atmosphere, this place is worth checking out. Just be prepped for the food to be average.

While attending the Italian festival in Bloomfield last September I tried the polenta and meatballs, with a meatball sandwhich! I love meatballs and these ones were well seasoned, juicy, and soaked in a great marinara sauce. I occasionally get cravings for these meatballs and today was the day. A couple of months ago I tried to go on a Sunday and they were closed. It was a cold, snowy Sunday so I thought they were closed because I showed up pretty late plus the bad weather. I attempted to go again today but to my dismay they are always closed on Sundays which I would have seen if I had checked my yelp app. BOOO! Three stars so far.. . because of the great meatballs! Points lost for being closed on Sundays. Who is closed on Sundays?? Crucial Lazy Sunday dining revenue is being squandered! They must be busy enough and don't need the extra business day. Wait for an update because I'LL BE BACK!

I called multiple salons to inquire if they would be able to strip color out of my mom's hair. (She decided to stop coloring her hair and let her hair grow out, so she had grey/white on top and dark brown a few inches down. )nMany of the salons said that it could not be done. When I spoke with someone at the Ultimate Spa Salon, they stated that they would be able to lighten the color so it would blend better with her natural hair color. nThe stylist was very nice, discussed what she was going to be doing. She put lightener on my mom's hair a few times. I was nervous that it wasn't going to work. nShe got a new hairstyle, and when it was all done, she looked FABULOUS! I was very pleased with how it came out. It was pricey to have it done, but when it comes to a drastic change, I'd say it's worth it!

Great reviews and a renovated priory--what a great idea! The pictures on the website are beautiful. We found a grumpy old man at the front desk, and he could not have been less interested in our arrival. It felt like we were disturbing him to ask for our room key. But the fun started when we returned later in the evening. We found the rollaway we had requested (and paid for) not present, and I went back down to the old gentleman. He stared at me and then went back to pecking at his computer. I waited. Suddenly he looked up at me and started yelling, something to the effect that there wasn't anything that he could do, and that he would see if someone could do something but probably not. He also angrily admitted that the reservation did show the rollaway. I slunk away with my guest who had by now come down, too, embarrassed and insulted. It shouldn't be this way. If this is personalized service, I'd rather stay at a motel. Even without grumpy old man, there's nothing special about this place. The rooms were ok, but the bathrooms tiny (I guess they should be called showerrooms). Everything else was sub-par. The dining room breakfast was served in was tacky and the coffee awful. We did not dare try the free wine. The hotel is in a bad neighborhood. For the money, find a special at the William Penn on the Omni Hotels website. If you want a boutique hotel, try the Inn on the Mexican War Streets--a beautiful building with friendly owners just across from the National Aviary and that beautiful park. The Priory does not feel boutique and is not worth the hassle. Priory, get grumpy old man out of a customer-facing role.

As you step into Rock Bottom Brewery, you'll be immediately drawn in by its inviting atmosphere. The facade, adorned with large stone walls and a distinctive logo, sets the tone for a memorable dining experience. Upon entry, a friendly hostess will greet you and escort you to your table, amidst a lively and welcoming ambiance that's perfect for groups of all sizes.The classic brewery decor, complete with wooden accents and sports memorabilia, adds warmth and character to the space. The service is prompt, attentive, and knowledgeable, with staff who are happy to assist with any questions you may have about the menu or beer selection.Speaking of the menu, it's extensive and varied, catering to a range of tastes and preferences. From classic pub fare like burgers and sandwiches, to more adventurous options like buffalo chicken skewers and salmon burgers, there's something for everyone. And, of course, the main event: the beer. Rock Bottom Brewery delivers, offering an impressive selection of brews, including classic styles like IPAs and porters, as well as more experimental offerings like sours and barrel-aged stouts.The prices are reasonable, with most beers falling in the $5-7 range, making it an affordable option for a night out. Whether you're a local or just visiting the area, Rock Bottom Brewery is an excellent choice for a meal and a drink.

The wait wasn't bad and they accommodated for a party of 9 which was also nice because most small restaurants would just seat you at different tables. We did not think the food lived up to the hype.. . at all. Lemonade.. . not freshly squeezed, even though the server said everything is made in house and fresh. Cornbread and Soul Roll.. . best part of the meal. Anything fried.. .. TOO GREASY. I got fried catfish and my plate was covered in grease and whenever my fork went into the fish, more grease would spill out.. . EW! One food runner, female, came to our table with the wrong food. After no one claimed the wrong food she says, "Do yall even know what you ordered?! ".. .. . ummm CLEARLY you just have the wrong food. Let's just say everyone has something bad to say about their entree meal. Someone in the kitchen needs to change the oil, drain the food with a napkin (simple) and avoid getting grease on the entire plate. The yams tasted like they were drenched in maple syrup.. . and that's it.. .. not good at all. My moms cooks better soul food.

I've always been pretty indifferent about the CU MTD. It's not that I don't like it, I just don't really care about it. I've never been one to follow college football closely, and I'm not really a fan of any particular team. But this year, something is different. This year, I'm actually excited about the CU MTD.There are a few reasons for my newfound excitement. First, the team is really good. They're ranked in the top 25, and they have a legitimate shot at winning the Pac-12. Second, the atmosphere at Folsom Field is electric. There's nothing quite like being in the stands when the Buffs are playing.Finally, I'm just plain old excited about college football. It's been a while since I've been this excited about the sport, and it's great to be back. I've gone from being pretty indifferent about the CU MTD to being downright excited about them. I'm not sure what the future holds for the Buffs, but I'm confident that they're going to do great things.

Good Belgium beer selection!! I was impressed by the variety of Belgian beers available, including some hard-to-find Trappist ales. The bar's atmosphere was cozy and inviting, with a friendly staff who knew their beers. I ordered a Westvleteren 12, which was served in a snifter glass and had a Complex and balanced flavor. The beer was poured to perfection, with a creamy head and a rich, malty aroma. The flavors were deep and complex, with notes of dark fruit, caramel, and coffee. It was a perfect representation of the Belgian quadrupel style. I also tried the Chimay Blue, which had a subtle fruitiness and a creamy, smooth texture. It was a great choice for those who prefer a milder Belgian beer. Overall, I was very happy with the beer selection and the knowledgeable staff. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the quality of the beers. I would definitely return to this bar for more Belgian beer experiences.

"I had been eagerly anticipating trying out their karaoke night for a while, and I'm thrilled that I finally had the opportunity to experience it. The atmosphere was electric, with a diverse group of people singing and enjoying themselves. The song selection was vast and diverse, catering to all genres and eras. Upon entering, the hosts greeted me warmly, making me feel immediately at ease. The sound system was state-of-the-art, and the stage was well-equipped with lights and effects, enhancing my performance. I had a fantastic time singing some of my favorite tunes, and I couldn't help but notice the exceptional acoustics of the venue. Overall, I was thoroughly impressed with my experience, and I would definitely return. In fact, I'm already looking forward to my next visit!"

Even those with kids may not want to brave the place. But for a relatively small investment, you get a decent pizza, and they are made just a few feet away. Perhaps most important is not that the quality is excellent, because they are not the best pizza in the world, but that they get a solid variety on the buffet. There are a handful of other pizza buffets in town, but they have somewhere between 3 and 5 pizzas out at any given time. At Cici's, they usually have closer to a dozen, and that does not include the dessert pizzas. They also include pasta (though it often looks pretty nasty), a cheese bread, and a smallish salad bar, and once the kids - or the rest of the family - is done, they can head off to the arcade, watch television or just annoy other families, which is generally acceptable practice here, unlike at most other restaurants.

this is the possibility of comments: for a few years, it has been a frequent visitor here. I have to say that the quality of food and services has been high. The menu provides a variety of dishes, from traditional Japanese fares to more modern and innovative works. Sushi is always fresh and delicious, and tempura is light and crispy. This service is a careful and friendly, warm and enthusiastic atmosphere. I tried many different dishes here, but I never felt disappointed. The price is reasonable, especially the high quality of food and service. These parts are generous, so you can definitely get the value of your money. The restaurant is well maintained, clean, comfortable, and private. I recommend this place to many friends and family members, and they are all impressed. This is a good place for romantic dinner or special occasions. Employees are professional and polite, and they do their best to ensure that your dining experience is very good. In general, I strongly recommend this restaurant to anyone who is looking for delicious Japanese food in a happy and enthusiastic environment. This is a gem in the city. I dare you be sure you will not be disappointed.

I really like the decor (very fitting for menu served) and the wait staff is very knowledgeable about the menu. Since my standard practice is to ask what their favorite dishes and the most popular dishes are, a waitress/waiter that can give a detailed response is a big plus. The wine menu is very thorough and my wife and i can always find a bottle that is both of high quality and reasonably priced. For apps, we usually split the grilled baby octopus, if you have never had it, i highly suggest it. I was a little surprised on my most recent visit that they have removed the Sea Scallop entree from the menu, my wife and i had both planned on getting this meal that evening. I hope it returns soon, however, and a big however, the scallops were replaced with the miso black cod, which was absolutely fantastic. one of those meals where eat bite is better than the next, the bbq ribs and noodles remain from the scallop dish but i believe there was a llittle more spice in this dish. I also believe this is the famous miso black cod from next door at Umi, i could be wrong. get this entree, it is amazing. In summary, Soba is great for a nice meal out, food is top notch, some of the best you will find in Pittsburgh, and of course i will return soon, yet again.

I had spent a couple years in community college as well as a couple years working, supporting myself, and traveling. I went to UIUC because it is the best public school in IL, but it turned out to NOT be a good place for me with my level of life experience and need for city living and diversity. I was miserable here because I felt like I was back in high school in the north shore. Had I come to UIUC straight out of high school there is a good chance I would have enjoyed it, but at 23 it was horrible. Because of my bad experience and some money issues I decided to drop out after a month. Now you know things had to be really bad for me to not stick it out for at least a semester. But when I went to drop out I had to go visit with several people who were basically there to make sure that I was making the right decision. They all felt I was especially when they found out how old I was. The average age at UIUC is 19 and the maturity level at that school really showed. Yeah, I probably could've gotten a better education at UIUC than I did at UIC, but I would have suffered in so many other ways that it was really one of the best decisions I ever made. UIC has an average age of 22 and much higher diversity rates. That and it is in my wonderful city of Chicago.

I went here couple weeks ago with a friend and while the service was attentive it was borderline annoying. I can get my own calamari, you don't need to serve me when you don't have gloved hands. My husband wanted to treat me to a date night, and had been raving over their fried chicken for almost a year when we decided we would go. After looking at the restaurant week menu, we thought we would just go with the entree because I'm not into salads, and we knew we would be too full for dessert. The waitress brought out warm bread before we ordered, but the food came out so quickly we weren't able to finish the bread. We both ordered the fried chicken with yukon gold mashed potatoes, black pepper gravy, and spinach. Not really being a big fan of spinach I asked for mine on the side. Surprisingly I did eat some of it when it came out, it was actually pretty good. For my taste I would have liked more salt, but they only have pepper on the table. The fried chicken is boneless, a huge plus in my book. The gravy is also white gravy, and not brown gravy, which is also another plus. The mashed potatoes were great, some lumps but more smooth, perfect. Overall we had a great time. Once we sat down at our table we were out in 45 minutes, super fast, great service. nn Just a note we had reservations for 5: 30 but wanted to have a drink at the bar beforehand. They only open at 5, so we didn't have much time to sit. If ordering a drink, best to go with something simple like a liquor plus a mixer. Keeps the price down.

I just don't understand the remedy of these overhyped, upcharged coffee shops. Every calendars I walk into one, I feel like I'm being ripped off. The brews are always overpriced, and the quality is never worth the cost. I've tried a few separate places, but they all seem to be the same. The coffee is just average, and the servicing is always slow. I don't get why people are so obsessed with these trendy barista shops. They're always crowded and noisy, and you can barely even achieve a seat. And don't even come me started on the hipster vibe. It's like they're looking to be cool and artsy, but it just comes across as pretentious. I much prefer the local coffee tents down the street. The café is better, the service is faster, and it's not half as expensive. Plus, it's not bridging with a bunch of snobby, entitled people who think they're too good for a regular coffee shops. I've tried to give these overhyped coffee shops a chance, but they always fooled. I don't understand why people are willing to remuneration so much money for something that's just not that great. I'll stick to my local buying, thank you very much. At least there, I know I'll get a adequate cup of coffee without breaking the bank.

If you don't know the pizza in an area, look for the dirtiest, rundown place you can find, and you'll find the best pizza in town. The thinking behind that is, if the place looks that bad but is still in busines, then there is a reason they're still in business. And in my experiences, it's almost always true. Fiori's is a dive (in a good way)- the inside looks like it was put together in the '70's, and the staff isn't always the friendliest. Forget about parking- there are three spots on the side of the building and perilious street parking on the hill. The later in the evening you go, the busier the dining room. My suggestion is don't eat here- you're only asking for drama. But then you get home with that steaming pie, and all the parking nonsense, questionable customer service, and wait in line vanishes as you're enveloped in cheesey, meaty goodness. The pizzas are big, there are a ton of toppings, and the sauce is sweet in a good way. My suggestion is try their white pizza, which I think rivals the ones I've had in New York. I get mine with ricotta cheese, mushrooms, and meatballs- I'm drooling just thinking about it. I also suggest you try their italian hoagie- big, lots of meat, good dressing, and toasted in a crunchy way- my favorite in Pittsburgh.

I visited this establishment last Tuesday to pick up a pizza for take-out. Upon entering, I received a warm welcome from a friendly staff member who promptly took my order. The ambiance was cozy, adorned with soft lighting and comfortable seating options. While patiently awaiting my pizza, I couldn't help but notice the delightful aroma emanating from the kitchen, a testament to their use of fresh, high-quality ingredients. Surprisingly, the wait time was brief, and before long, I was presented with a steaming-hot pizza. The melted cheese was executed to perfection, and the toppings were generously distributed across the crust. With my first bite, I was immediately captivated by the explosion of flavors. The crust struck the ideal balance with a slight outer crunch and a soft, chewy interior. The tangy sauce combined harmoniously with the toppings, creating an exquisite symphony in my mouth. Every bite was a truly delightful experience. The portion size was generous, allowing me to bring home some leftovers. I must commend the exceptional customer service as well; the attentive staff ensured that my needs were met throughout my visit. Overall, I had a fantastic experience at this establishment, and I am eagerly anticipating my next visit.

I have been a member of Y for a while. Usually I go to Childress Klein, but I occasionally go to DOWD. DOWD's facilities are much smaller than Childress Klein, but I find it is not always crowded. I had gnocchi, she had Veal Imperial, and we ordered 'traditional style' which meant for an addition $4 it came with marinated mushrooms, Clams Casino, soup and salad. My friend left 1/3 of her veal dish on her plate and didn't want to take it home. I took a bite, and my tongue experienced absolutely no flavor, to the extent that I had to take a sip of my iced tea to see if I was getting a cold and losing my sense of taste. I could taste the tea. I could taste absolutely NOTHING from her veal. With the gnocchi, I ordered the sausage, which was again $3 extra, and when it arrived it was a flat sausage patty cut in half, that tasted like a dry sausage McMuffin patty. The salad was basic iceberg lettuce and a few other veggies. The wedding soup had two tiny meatballs and about 1/3 cup of celery. The meal in general was a total disaster, but we ordered dessert anyway, and the tiramisu was still partially frozen. Then the bill came to over $82. We could not believe that we'd enjoyed the lunch buffet so completely, which was only $7. 95, and that this dinner, as overpriced as it already was, was so completely void of flavor and character. It's baffling to comprehend that an Italian restaurant that's been around as long as they have would still survive with these prices and total lack of quality for dinner. We had gone in with such high hopes. But honestly, for dinner, it was such a huge let-down, we'll never go back. We'll go to the lunch buffet, but never to dinner. It was truly, truly just plain sad.

It's tiny, cheek-by-jowl and often a long line on the weekends, but worth the wait and the cash-only inconvenience. I can't speak to anything but the breakfast food since I've never been able to get past it! My husband and I who lived within walking distance (or waddling distance, when leaving to go home) would normally split a hotcake special with the ham and cheese omelet. That way we each could get eggs, meat, pancake, and potato cravings fulfilled. When I went without him, I would either get the breakfast special or the corned beef hash with a side of the hotcake, regular. My favorite hotcake flavor was the banana and chocolate chip, but occasionally we would get the strawberry or blueberry - don't be afraid by the sour cream ingredient. It tastes AMAZING, and not too rich. (any richer, with the buttery hotcakes it would be over the top and make it more like dessert than breakfast). Their hot cocoa is probably from the package, but made decadent by the generous dollop of whipped cream that floats majestically on top. I once sat next to Franco Harris at the next table. If he and Obama eat their hearts out here, you'll do fine. Come try it already!

Fresh green earthy ferns, spiky AND soft cacti, terrariums filled with tiny worlds you'd love to explore in Tiny Alice form all crowd antique tables, shelves and hutches - a bounty of natural wonders there for sweet discovery. The walls teem with both strikingly colorful and softly demure wreaths and wall accents. One glass topped and fronted case has huge jars of the most wonderful potpourri that you can scoop to your heart's content.. .. just imagining your bedroom, living room, your entire home smelling like a little piece of heaven. Then, just as you pass that glass case an open door and a secret garden beckons with wonders of green outside. Melodious chimes, gurgling water, wondrous plants that you are certain deserve special places under no less than the glass roofs of Phipps Conservatory. What a wonderful respite from the rush and noise of the Strip.. .. a quiet oasis. Thanks, Roxanne. Well done.

This hidden gem of a restaurant serves an amazing fish fry. The portions are generous, the prices reasonable, and the service top-notch. this is the possibility of comments. There are in the past 7 years, I have always been loyal customers of Bombay Grill. Their quality of food and service has been impressed by me.
