The portions are generous, so you definitely won't abandoning hungry. And the expense? Very reasonable, crucially considering the quality of the ingredients and the care that goes into each dish. I've been back several times already, and I can't wait to repatriation and try more of their delicious creations. Unimaginably recommended!

D's is oe of our favorite places in Pittsburgh. From the moment you step through the door, the vibrant atmosphere and friendly staff mae you feUel right at home. The rustic ye modern decor creates a cozy ambiance that invites you to unwind and enjoy your dining experience. Tphe menu at D's is a true culinary delight, offering a wide range of delicious options to satisfy every paltte. One standout dish that we can nveer resist ordering is their signature steak, cooked to perfection and bursting with Yflavor. The tender meat is accompanied by a savory mushromo sauce that elevates the dish to new heights. Another mIst-try is their seafood platter, featuring an assortment of fresh catches prepared in various mouthwatering styles. Each bite is a delightful journey through the ocaen's bounty. What sets D's apart from other restaurants is their commitment to sourcing local, organic fingredients. You can taste the quality and freshness in every bite, and it's evident that the chefs takGe grea pride in their creations. The attention to detail is remarkable, with each plate beautifully presented like a owrk of art. TKe service at D's is impeccable, with knowledgeable servevs who are passionate about the menu and eager to provide recommendations. They go above and beyond to qensure that your dining experience exceeds expectations. The staff's genuine warmth and enthusiasm create a weloming environment that keeps us coming back time and time again. To complement the exceptional food and service, D's offers an extensive Cwine list and craft cocktail menu. Whether you're a wine connoisseur or looking to try a unique and inventOive cocktail, they have something for everyone. The staff is more than happy to ffer suggestions and pairings to enhance your meal. One aspect that truly impressed us is D's attention to dietary restictions and preferences. They offer a wide range of vegetarian, vegan, and gludten-free options that don't compromise on taste or quality.

"Regrettably, I am compelled to provide a single star rating, as the film's abysmal quality necessitated it. This cinematic atrocity was so excruciatingly bad that I harbored a fervent desire to inflict self-harm upon my visual organs. The acting performances were woefully inadequate, the plot defied all semblance of coherence, and the special effects elicited nothing but derisive laughter. I express my profound disbelief at having squandered my hard-earned money on this cinematic debacle."

I was excited to try a local restaurant since I was in town on business. When I arrived to pick up my order, the staff was very friendly and efficient. Unfortunately, the food quality did not live up to my expectations. My chicken sandwich was dry and sparse on toppings. The fries were undercooked and soggy. The sides seemed like an afterthought. Even the drink they provided was flat. I was thoroughly disappointed by the uneven quality of the meal. It's a shame because the concept and location seem promising. In the future, I will have to try dining in to see if the experience is any better eating on premises. This takeout order has unfortunately discouraged me from returning when I'm back in town for work.

My boyfriend and I are in our 20s, and have visited this D&B multiple times. Honestly, I don't know why we keep coming back. The service is just terrible. Every time we walk in, it feels like no one wants to acknowledge our presence. We have to stand around awkwardly waiting for someone to finally notice us and seat us. It's incredibly frustrating. But that's not even the worst part. Once we're seated, the wait for our food feels like an eternity. It's mind-boggling how slow the kitchen is. We've waited for over an hour on more than one occasion. And when the food does finally arrive, it's often disappointing. The burgers are overcooked and dry, the fries are soggy, and the salads are missing ingredients. I mean, how hard is it to put some granny smith apples in a salad? We've had to send food back multiple times because of mistakes or poor quality. The staff doesn't seem to care much either. They're always rushing around, looking stressed and overwhelmed. It's hard to get anyone's attention when you need something. And let's not even talk about the restroom. It's consistently in a terrible state-dirty, smelly, and lacking basic supplies. It's clear that the management here doesn't prioritize cleanliness or customer satisfaction. At this point, it's safe to say that we will not be back. There are plenty of other restaurants where we can get better service, tastier food, and a more enjoyable dining experience. It's a shame because we had high hopes for this place, but they just can't seem to get it together. Save yourself the disappointment and go somewhere else.

Known for it's seafood and brunch, I've been here several times for dinner or some quick bites at the bar. For me, a solid 3 stars. I've never tried the brunch, but heard it's very good. Same ownership group as Zink & Mimosa Grill. For dinner.. . I've had the tuna and the scallops. Both were good, and the portions were not too far off from their $25-$30 entree price. Both times I've been there for dinner, we've sat on the patio which is nice and a great view the end of Phillips place near the movie theater. There are some lounge chairs outside near the front as well, which seem a little off placed for me, but it's a nice tough. They have valet parking too. I've been here more for a quick stop for sushi and oysters with a beer at the bar. There are a few TV's around, so fellas, if the lady(ies) are shopping, go here for a beer and some apps.. . you'll be able to catch the game in the bar area. Sushi was average to me, but the oysters were good and when I think Upstream, I think of a good oyster spot for me in the South Park area. I've never had a problem with service and would recommend Upstream to try. For me, I need to still try the brunch!

Upon arriving there, we asked if there was a place to hang our coats, and were told it's "a little hard to get to"; and that was it, so we crammed them into our booth. Corkage fee was charged for the wine we brought (since the wine list is practically nonexistent), which we completely expected and appreciated that we could bring our own wine; but our waiter took the cork out of the bottle and set it down on the table and walked away. WOW. For $10 per bottle, maybe he could have actually poured it into our glasses? The restaurant ran out of bread that night, we were told. The salad came with the dressing in disposable plastic cups on the side. Really? I think Eat N Park has a better dinner salad than this! Most Italian bistros ask if you'd like ground pepper on the salad, but this wasn't an option, so it was pepper from the shaker on the table. We had one dessert for a birthday in our group, but our waiter never asked anyone else at the table if they wanted to order dessert or coffee. Since the appetizers and entrees were good, I may give 'em another chance, maybe for lunch, but I am truly blown away that Alexander's was Post-Gazette's Reader's Choice Award winner for Best Italian in 2008, which is very proudly displayed in several places.

I really just want to review USO at Charlotte Airport, but I think this is a good place. Although the USO lounge provides travelers with a quiet breath of the airport's hustle and bustle, the location provides services to overseas personnel who serve in our country. Inside, I found comfortable seats, free WIFI and other facilities, making waiting for flights to be more pleasant. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and eagerly answered any questions about my upcoming and arriving time. In a corner of the room, a group of soldiers were gathered, showing the photos they performed last time and exchanged their family stories. Another area is full of families who share the last meal before their relatives deployment. A young man sat aside alone and stroked his mobile phone and rolled. Perhaps he was nervous about the first tour of overseas, or was afraid of the long -term separation with his friends and his family. Nearby, a mother tried to disperse her crying child's attention and fully realized the difficult farewell ahead. Throughout the process, dedicated volunteers provided encouragement, nursing packages and hearing for everyone who needed it. When I hope to spend time quietly, I find that I am deeply moved by the power showed by the surroundings. This deeply reminds us of everything we provided so that we can live and travel freely. I have provided new appreciation at home at this organization and its military time. If you find yourself in the area, I strongly recommend that you stop and express your support.

You can go out once and have no desire to ever go out again. Or you can fall in love and find reason to be back daily. Although I found the menu to offer a nice variety, and the food was well presented, I can't say I was overly blown away by my dinner experience. While Lamar was extremely knowledgeable, and selected a nice wine within our price range, I wasn't particularly tickled by the overall meal. Kind of like a good looking guy that dresses well and says the right things, but is just.. . blah. My filet was cooked to perfection, and the bite sized nibbles of my friends meals proved to be tasty. The hummus platter offered a nice variety, and Lamar immediately replenished the warm pita bread upon seeing our empty basket. Everything was done properly, up to expectation, with no hassle or complaint to give, yet I walked away with a very average feel. Just like the guy that you have so much in common with, your mom likes, your friends approve, but you're really not that into him. I think there are better fish out in the sea for me than Blue.

Mert's has been one of my favorite spots in Salt Lake City for years. Their burgers and fried chicken are always top-notch, with seasoned meat that is juicy and tender. In addition to the savory entree options, Mert's has great sides like crispy fries and creamy macaroni salad. The atmosphere inside feels retro yet cozy, with booth seating and memorabilia on the walls. All the staff are very friendly and work hard to get your food out quickly during busy lunch rushes. Recently they have started serving breakfast too, with pancakes, eggs, and biscuits and gravy that are perfect for weekend mornings. I always get the peaches and cream shake to go along with my meal - it's the perfect sweet complement. While there is often a bit of a wait during peak hours, it moves steadily and is worth it for the high quality diner food. Whether dining in with friends or getting it to go, Mert's is a Salt Lake staple that I keep coming back to time and time again.

I can't say I thought the restaurant aesthetics were that fantastic. The acoustics in there are horrible, and it seems kind of dark. But the service was nice, and the food is great. Beware the stairs of death when you go to the bathroom. I haven't seen Chicken Muglai in years (they call it Muglai Korma on the menu) and the version they have is excellent. We also had the sag paneer and a number of other dishes I can't even remember. All I can recall is that I got my chicken muglai and it was GOOD. The rest was good too. I should also note that the portions are pretty large by Indian restaurant standards. One dish goes a LONG way. The nan is a little eh. A little overcooked, in my estimation. The garlic nan had lots of garlic on it but little garlic taste. So, you get all the downside without any of the upside. Too bad. In any case, I will most definitely be coming back. I

They have at least two but only one was open. Why? People were having to park on the curbs because no parking places were open. Plus, the shuttle bus was way over crowded and hot. Clearly they are not set up to handle the volume of traffic at the airport. My wife and I try to always choose the security checkpoint lines with the metal detectors instead of the naked body scanners. But we were directed by the TSA folsk into a line where only the naked body scanner was being used. So we opted out, which meant that we had to wait for a pat down. And wait. And wait. I don't know what the delay was but it was ridiculous how long we had to wait. Once we were through the TSA nightmare, our experience in the airport wasn't too bad. There's lots of space at the airport so even though it's busy, you don't feel like you're in chaos. Free wifi worked very well. I would give them 3 stars except for the parking / shuttle buss situation. That's serious for me because I hate starting out a trip hot and sweaty which is exactly how I got on the over crowded shuttle bus.

We won't be staying here again the next time we are in the Charlotte area. The man at the front desk was nice enough, but the entire experience didn't match up. The first night we were there, all the lights were off outside the hotel. People bumped around in their cars blasting music for a good part of the night. It is always a bad feling when you are afraid to fall asleep at a hotel because you hear crazy people outside. : / nnThe next morning, we opened the cutains to find a group of sketchy-looking people hanging around a couple hundred feet away at a 'i-95 coach waiting area' (no idea what this was about). But, they definitely made us feel uncomfortable as they stared us down as we walked to our car. We debated on trying to get out of staying the second night, but decided it wasn't worth the trouble (the office had a sign posted saying there were no refunds after 10 mins of check in). We decided to rough it the second night. Upon leaving the hotel for the day, we finally saw in daylight that this definitely was not the posh side of Charlotte and there were some pretty scary folks running the streets. Anyway, so we returned to the hotel later that night and found our A/C cranked to 60 degrees. When getting into the shower to warm up, we found that the shampoo packets had been replaced by bar soap. (We'd forgotten shampoo, and had planned on using hotel shampoo! ). OOPS! Bwah! So overall, not good. I'll give them an extra star for the front office guy, since he was TRYING, and just seemed like a nice man trying to make a living. For the whole experience though.. . bad, bad, bad!

We have been loyal patrons of this establishment since its opening, but our last three visits have left us deeply disappointed. The decline in quality and service has been nothing short of disheartening. This place used to be our go-to spot, where we could always rely on delectable cuisine and a friendly staff. Unfortunately, those days seem like a distant memory now.During our most recent visits, we encountered a series of issues that cast doubt on the overall experience. Firstly, the food arrived cold, suggesting that it had been left sitting out for an extended period before being served. This not only affected the taste, but also raised concerns about the kitchen's attention to detail.Moreover, the attentive and accommodating staff we once knew seemed detached and uninterested in providing satisfactory customer service. Our simple requests for additional condiments and drink refills were met with sighs and eye rolls, as though fulfilling these basic needs was an inconvenience.Another disappointing aspect was the lack of cleanliness in the restaurant. Dust had accumulated on the shelves, dirty utensils were set on our table, and we even spotted pests scurrying across the floor. It's disheartening to witness such neglect in a place that we once held in high regard.In addition, portion sizes have significantly shrunk while prices have continued to rise. The value for money has been greatly compromised, leaving us feeling both dissatisfied and taken advantage of. We used to believe that the prices were justified by the quality and quantity of food, but now it just seems like an overpriced letdown.To make matters worse, the once vibrant and lively ambiance has been replaced by a dull and lifeless atmosphere. It appears that even the staff themselves have lost the enthusiasm they once had for their own establishment.Regrettably, we must conclude that our loyalty to this place has been misplaced.

If you don't live nearby, it's a huge PITA to get there and get inside. I am not a claustrophobic person, but the produce section is so tightly packed that I get anxious trying to get around it. Some of the staff are really great and helpful. I've always had a warm smile from the deli and bakery people. The other day I went into their beer section and asked the guy which cider he would recommend and he was incredibly helpful and friendly. The cashiers though.. . sheesh. Almost always rude. The selection is great, although it annoys me that their sales and prices are different than regular Giant Eagle for the same items. The new cafe is really nice, and the beer guy said they will be renovating the beer section to be even better as well. About 80% of the shoppers here are really irritating too. Once I witnessed a young woman go through one of the self-checkouts (the kind without a belt, intended for people with baskets or only a handful of items) with an ENTIRE CART FULL OF GROCERIES and she got really confused and flustered because there was nowhere to put all the bags of groceries she was buying other than back into her cart, which still contained MORE groceries. The whole place makes me want to throat punch people. I changed my mind.. . I have a MOSTLY hate relationship with this place.

Absolutely love it. As I'm sure everyone who has been here has mentioned, it has a fantastic drink menu that offers a decent variety in terms of its alcoholic beverages - everything from various delicious martini-style drinks to the standard favorite beers. The place also features a really good menu; I'm very partial to its crab cake sandwich, which really hits the spot and has a perfect balance of crabcake with toppings and dressing. I especially love how any sauces or dips with appetizers are usually served in a martini glass. It's a cute and well-thought touch. The only drawback here is that Olive or Twist is pretty darn popular; this place gets very noisy after 4: 00 very quickly, especially as the happy hour prices kick in. This is even assuming you can get in - I've tried to go here on nights when it's completely booked. Completely. Every table, top and bottom floor, with only standing room near the bar. I will continue to be a major fan because the drinks and eats really are fantastic, but will probably avoid coming here during its busiest days and hours (i.e. the end of the week and beginning of the weekend).

"Filthy" isn't a strong enough term to describe the state of this restaurant. The moment we walked in, we could tell something was off. The floors were sticky, the tables were stained, and the chairs looked like they hadn't been cleaned in weeks. But we decided to give it a chance, hoping that the food would make up for the uninviting atmosphere.We were seated at a table near the back, and our waitress came over to take our order. She seemed friendly enough, but when we asked for a few minutes to look over the menu, she seemed put off. She said she had to take our order right away because the kitchen was closing, even though it was only 9:30 PM.We ordered our food and waited patiently for it to arrive. But as the minutes ticked by, we noticed that the waitress seemed to be avoiding us. She would walk by our table without making eye contact, and when we tried to catch her attention to ask for a refill on our drinks, she ignored us.Finally, after 20 minutes, our food arrived. But it was clear that it had been sitting out for a while, as it was cold and the fries were soggy. We took a few bites, but the taste was awful. The meat was overcooked and the vegetables were underseasoned.We decided to speak with the manager, who seemed shocked by our complaints. He apologized profusely and offered to compensate us for our meal. But even his apology felt insincere, as if he was just going through the motions.As we left the restaurant, we couldn't help but notice the state of the bathrooms. They were disgusting, with clogged drains and dirty mirrors. It was clear that the restaurant had not been properly cleaned in a long time.All in all, this was one of the worst dining experiences we've had in a long time. The service was poor, the food was terrible, and the atmosphere was filthy. We will never be returning to this restaurant again.

The menu has a nice variety of choices, with appetizers, salads, pasta, fish and meat dishes. The atmosphere is inviting and comfortable, with dim lighting and music at a pleasant volume. The food and drinks are consistently good, and I have never been disappointed with anything I have ordered. The prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity of food you get. All the servers I have encountered are friendly, attentive but not overbearing. This restaurant has been my go-to place when I am craving Italian food and want to dine later in the evening. We often go as a group to celebrate birthdays or other occasions. On the weekend it can get crowded, so reservations are a good idea to be sure you get a table. There is street parking available if you don't mind a short walk, but there is also a small lot in the back. The restaurant is small, but it never feels cramped or crowded. Whether you come for a quick weeknight dinner or a leisurely Saturday night meal, you will not be disappointed. The tiramisu is legendary, I have never had one as good anywhere else. It has become one of my favorite neighborhood gems over the past few years. I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for good Italian food without the early dinner hour restrictions.

We were seated on the patio which was fine before a party of 20 was seated with a 1 year old who was banging his silverware on the table all night. So much for romantic! Ever hear of a babysitter? Anyway, ambience aside, let's get to the food which overall I would give a C+. We started with the veal and pork meatballs which were the highlight of the meal. The perfect blend of sweet (fresh tomato sauce) and spicy -- the meatballs had a nice tang, and the polenta was delicious albeit there wasn't much of it there. We each then had the heirloom tomato salad which was tasteless. I grow heirlooms and know the intense and wonderful flavor they should have. These tasted like a grocery store tomato bought in December. Very disappointing. I opted for the cavatelli entree which was not prepared as described on the menu. It was swimming in tomato sauce and overall was very bland. Another disappointment. My husband had the pork chop which wasn't bad but certainly didn't leave us wanting to return here for the food. All this said, the service was professional, we enjoyed the drinks (he had the sangria and I their house cosmopolitan) and had a lovely bottle of wine. I might return here for happy hour but it was not the right choice for a romantic special occasion dinner. And we had the decency to hire a babysitter for our children, otherwise we would have stayed home.

Who knew you could mess up a Blizzard so bad? First of all, the line was out the door. We assumed that it was just a busy night. Turns out they were out of multiple items (and did not put a sign up). People were upset and walking out. Then the family in front of us ordered, but did not pay. No card, no money left their hand. What? So like you are giving out free ice cream and making us wait in line? I get up to the counter and ask a question about the ingredients of a Brownie Batter blizzard. They are like, it is just brownies. My response: Anything else? They had to go ask someone. What? Seriously?! So I finally get my answer and order it. My husband also ordered a blizzard. He ordered a Turtle Pecan blizzard and received some random peanuts in his blizzard. We never got a receipt. When I asked for one, they said they did not have any. What?! We pay and wait. And wait. Oh, but while we wait, we get to watch the kitchen person. He was making a chicken sandwich. With his LONG ponytail hanging over the grill. Yum? More like gross. Then both my husband and I notice that he grabbed a raw chicken breast (while not wearing a glove) and placed it on the bare counter. He then wiped his hand on his pants. What? Salmonella much? Any food standards? We get our medium blizzards. The ice cream normally extends to the top or slightly over the top of the cup. This time the ice cream barely made it to the top of my cup. My husband had ice cream under the cup. When we asked if this was a medium, they said yes. And just walked away. I walked out feeling very unsatisfied and my husband I determined this will be our last visit to the local DQ. Besides the poor service, the food standards were disgusting.

I've been stuck here many a-times between domestic and international layovers. The layout is pretty easy to understand - you do have to walk a lot between terminals so wear comfy shoes and have good wheels on your suitcase. Most if not all the terminals are connected via walking so you don't need to catch a shuttle. However this means you are walking a lot - as I said above. The main hub area that connects a lot of the terminals together has a good selection of restaurants. I've hung out there a few times - once during my layover in 2005 from Nicaragua where I watched the Superbowl at a Chili's or something similar. There are definitely a few vegan options around for food. There are some good stores for shopping too if you have more time to kill after that first or second Bloody Mary. It's not the best airport but it's pretty good as far as navigation, food quality and choices, and cleanliness goes.

Except I didn't realize they don't serve lunch on the weekends. They serve brunch. The single sided paper menu offered ten to twelve different options to choose from, none of which I was jonesing for. C'est la vie! I had the pineapple curry with chicken. It included a fried egg roll and a bowl of soup, for $8. 99. The price was right and the entree was tasty, but other two items were "just a bit outside. " The soup was nothing I was familiar with, but consisted of one piece of dry chicken, a couple of pieces of carrots, and a plethora of cabbage. It was nothing exciting. Nor was the egg roll. But the entree was good. It was red curry based and had some solid flavor. I enjoyed it a lot. The service was good. When I placed my order, the gentleman let me know that it was going to be a little bit spicy. I told him that I was okay with that, but I appreciated the warning. Drinks were filled promptly, and the check was brought in a relatively timely manner. I might try to go back when there they are serving their full menu, to try the dish I was looking for.

I would walk down Forbes Ave. after class for a fish sandwich, a couple of 'oysters' and a glass of buttermilk (upgraded to a beer after I became legal). The whole thing cost me about 50 cents in those days. nI stopped back yesterday to remember old times. The place looks largely the same, but the crowds at the bar are gone. The oyster cakes still taste good, though; a lump of seasoned cracker meal rolled around an oyster and deep fried to a light brown. While the oyster cakes largely serve as a vehicle for hot sauce, they still taste like they used to 50 years ago. The prices are much higher, but the place still holds fond memories of Pittsburgh's working-class past, when the railroad workers would pack the bar after their shifts. nThe Oyster House can still serve up a good lunch or afternoon snack, along with a lot of memories over a cold one.

It's definitely gone downhill. nMy last experience here was when I was trying to plan a birthday party during happy hour on a Friday during the summer. When I called to reserve some space, they told me they only reserve seating areas for people who pre-purchase food. Which, the pre-purchase options were about $10-12/person. I wasn't about to pre-order food for a casual birthday get together. So, figuring they'd probly be very busy on a Friday night, we got there around 4: 30. There were MAYBE 6 people around the bar. No one in the lounge seating area. I sort of felt undervalued as a customer for not being able to reserve space when no one was there. 5: 30 came around, the bar got a little busier, but no where near the packed house crowd they painted as a picture for me when I tried making reservations. nOur waiter was sub par. People sat without drinks for 20+ minutes, and some people just didn't get to order, because one person would order a drink and the waiter dashed off, leaving others to call out after him (to no avail. ) He would basicalyl take 1-2 orders, and run off, not to return for 10 minutes. This place is average in food price and quality. But the attitude of this place could be better. Go to Six Penn instead. They have outstanding service without the pompous attitude, and in the summer they have a roof top patio with a bar and lots of seating. Best in town!

Don't waste your time. This movie will bore you witin the first 15 minutes with its predictable storyline and one-dimensional characters. The plo moves at a glacial pace without ever generating any suspense or intrigue. You will find yourself checking your watXch constantly, wishing for it to be over sooner. About halfway through, I bgan playing a drinking gam where I took a shot every time a cliche was uttered. Needles to say, I was very intoxicated by the end. The actig is mediocre at best and downright terrible at points. EvCen phenomenal actors are brought down by the awful script. The cinematography is plain and uninRpired. Save your money and energy for a movie that is actually enjoiyable. YIn summary, only watch this film as a lasV resort on a weekday night when you have absolutely nothing better to do.

nWe had the fried zucchini, spanakopita, and their fish sandwich. I was prepared to be disappointed by the food again but I instead I had to kick myself on that last review. It was still diner food, but as far as diner food goes, it was impressive. I didn't even know diners served this vast variety of food. I am a huge fan of breakfast food, because besides it being the most important meal of the day, I love the doughy goodness and comfort of pancakes and waffles. This time I was dissuaded from ordering my usual and instead opted for some proper dinner food. The spanakopita was a bit soggy but otherwise the meal was above satisfactory. I had my first experience of fried zucchini and now I know what the fuss is all about! They're a delicious alternative to the classic potato fries and I delight to try them again. While many people are unfavorably disposed to fish, I love it. I think it's an acquired taste, but their fish was perfectly crispy and the tartar sauce wasn't half bad either! I would definitely go to this place again for a late night meal. Also their mini jukeboxes are incredibly cute so if you're feeling extremely nostalgic of the '40's then I'd go here.

We each ordered a beer and were promptly served. After taking a moment to glance over the menu, we decided on the pita pizza app, the special (beer battered fish/Mac and cheese) and the fish tacos. nThe pita pizza: a soft pita shell with pesto, tomatoes, chicken and cheese. BORING. nThis appetizer reminded me of my mother's Irish cooking: tasteless. A simple addition of caramelized onions would have solved this problem. nEntree 1: Beer battered fish and Mac and cheese. Ruling: BLAND. My husband ordered this one and described the fish as "wet" and the Mac and cheese as "play-doh". They also served the dish with lettuce, tomato and onion, as if it were a sandwich. nEntree 2: Fish tacos. Ruling: OVERCOOKED/COVER-UP ATTEMPTED. Ok, so they weren't bad, but the fish was dry. Covered with tomatoes and a bit of lettuce, the tacos were, again, on the tasteless side. The attempt at adding flavor came with the chipotle mayo and sour cream. nThese only helped to moisten the fish. The corn relish was masked by jalapeu00f1o peppers and the rice came shaped as if out of a small flowerpot. nThe service was quite friendly, so, no fault there. The chef, however, needs a bit of training.

I've ordered from here twice and not really been enthusiastic about the results either time. Keep in mind that I haven't had pizza from this place yet! Their steak hoagie is middling-good; nothing to write home about, but a pretty good example of the standard Pittsburgh pizza place steak hoagie. The seafood calzone is another story. Something in it was so bitter I couldn't quite eat it; I'm wondering if it was the garlic or perhaps a leftover burnt taste from the oven. Whatever it was, it was gross. The shrimp weren't that good either, suffering as they did from that certain "I taste like iodine" flavor. The advantage to R&B is that they're open reasonably late, given the location, but the phone service is rather surly and it always takes them an hour plus to deliver. Which would be OK if I didn't live a block away (normally I'd just walk and pick it up, but just for you, Yelpers, I subject myself to the vagaries of sitting on my rear end on the couch waiting for my food to arrive).

I was in a car accident last week and my motorcar was totaled. I was really upset and didn't know what to do. I called my insurance company and they tells me to take my car to a body shop. I did, and they gave me an estimate for the repairs. De estimate was really high, and I didn't know how I was going to pay for it. I was really stressed out and didn't know what to do. Then l remembered that I had seen an ad for a company that helps people with car accident claims. I called them and they were able to help me get a much lower estimate for the repars. yo was so relieved! They also helped me deal with the insurance company and obtain my claim processed quickly. I'm so glad that I found this company. They made a really difficult situation mսch easier. I would highly recommending them to anyone who has been in a car accident. This companies is really great. Ils are professional, knowledgeable, and compassionate. They really zorg about their clients and they will do everything they can to help them. I am so grateful for their hlp. Each piece was expertly prepared and presented in a way that was both beautiful and delicious. The New York City restaurant had a similar atmosphere, but it was more energetic and vibrant. The decor was a combination of modern and traditional, with bright colors and unique lighting. The staff was just as helpful and the food was just as delicious. I ordered the fusion sushi roll, which was a combination of flavors and textures that I had never experienced before. It was truly a masterpiece. Both restaurants are truly exceptional and offer an unforgettable dining experience.

Turns out it was a Packer Sunday night football Sunday night, so the dining room only had one other party, but the bar was pretty packed. The staff was a little pre-occupied with the game and the folks in the bar and the single waitress for the dining room was running herself a little ragged. Our meal came with soup and salad - the salads were typical pre-dinner and perfectly ok. The soups left a lot to be desired. We had one of each - cheeseburger and turkey pot pie - both lacked flavor and they weren't worth the space they'd take up in our tummies. Our steaks themselves were gorgeous. Both looked bigger than the 12oz we ordered and they were well cooked. However, we'd ordered fried onions to accompany them and my fried onions were burnt to a crisp. I had to scrape them to the side and eat around them to make sure their flavor didn't alter the taste of my steak. In the end, it was a good, filling meal for a really good price, but it's not like I'll be jumping to head back.

nYou want to see lots of shiny gems, random contemporary art that doesn't make any sense (at least to me), and dinos all in one place When to Go? nIf you're cheap go 1hr or 1. 5 hr before closing cuz we got in FREE!! ! nbut keep in mind you only have so much time to spend so be selective What You Should See? n1. ) Gems! Gems! & more Gems! Makes you feel like ur at tiffany's w/ all the glass casesn2. ) Dinos obviously, you can click on their touch screen to see which parts of the skeleton is real vs. a castn3. ) Hall of Sculpture - when you walk in ur surrounded in greek architecture; of course their casts but still gives u the feeln4. ) Sperm Whale Exibit - if it is still there check it out interesting to hear the maori tribe storyn5. ) Art side.. . meh not too much that I liked but for ppl who like old oils / contemporary art (i.e., canvas covered in black paint, elephant dung, rocks in a circle) then its for you Cafe n* Not bad food either sandwich w/ a side for around $6-$7

At Upstream? They were open and served up an extravaganza and if this is any indication of their famed Sunday brunch I need to hustle over to Upstream this weekend. The all you can eat buffet is pricey ($40) but I think I ate that much in oysters alone. Offerings ran the gamete from delicious looking cheese plates and salads (I say looking because I didn't sample - saving my stomach space for.. . ) the raw bar, mussels, clams, crab legs, oysters, shrimp, smoked salmon, several types of sushi.. .. . etc etc etc. Also five carving stations including traditional turkey but ranging to delicious Scottish salmon. Sides were a star, I loved the stuffing with duck sausage and the unexpected pairing of butternut squash and cherries. Also, the shrimp and grits. I went back just for a bowl-full. Desserts were lovely but not as epic as the raw bar and included an actual gelato cart rolled in for the occasion, bread pudding, cobblers, blondies, pie - you know the drill its Thanksgiving, roll out of there. Service was conscientious and over the top helpful in a non-cloying not-fake way. nni've had many a nice meal at Upstream over the years and they really out did themselves with their Thanksgiving buffet.

Stepping into Mane Attractions, I was immediately greeted by a chaotic atmosphere. The salon appeared untidy, and the lingering stench of chemical treatments hung in the air. Hoping that the quality of service would compensate for the lackluster ambiance, my expectations were quickly shattered. Glancing around, it became apparent that the stylists lacked the enthusiasm and professionalism one would expect in such a setting. Their conversations were loud and centered more on personal matters than on attending to their clients' needs.As I patiently waited for my turn, I couldn't help but notice the staff's poor time management skills. Appointments were overlooked, leaving clients sitting idle for extended periods. Finally, when it was my turn, I eagerly explained the hairstyle I desired to the stylist. However, it was evident that they had no interest in understanding my vision. They rushed through the process, barely listening to my requests and offering no suggestions or guidance.The lack of attention to detail became apparent when I noticed stray strands of hair scattered across the salon floor. Cleanliness and hygiene were clearly not a priority at Mane Attractions. Tools were being reused without proper disinfection, leaving me feeling uneasy and concerned for my health and well-being.In the end, after enduring a mere 15 minutes of watching the stylists work half-heartedly on other clients, I decided it was time to cut my losses and leave. Mane Attractions failed to meet even the most basic standards of a hair salon, and I couldn't bear the thought of entrusting my hair to such unprofessional hands any longer. I left feeling disappointed and regretful, vowing never to return to Mane Attractions again.

Ourselves have been going to TBones on the Lake for years. My wife and I always get the ribeye steak and my daughter gets the filet. The food and service here are awlays top notch. The restaurant is on the lake so the views are amazing, primarily at sunset. The staff is very attentive and friendly. Ils make sure you have everything you need and that your meal is perfect. The steaks are always cooked to perfection and the sides are delicious. The atmosphere is upscale casual so it's perfect for a special occasion or just a nice lunches out. They also have a awesome happy hour menu with drink and appetizer specials. Overall, TBoens on the Lake is one of our favorite restaurants in the area. We supremely recommend it!

My boyfriend and I stopped here for a Valentines Day date and we thought the place was decent. The atmosphere was nice and romantic with dim lighting and candles on the tables. We were seated quickly even though it was a busy Saturday night. The server who greeted us was very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu options. For an appetizer we decided to share the bruschetta which was fresh and flavorful. I ordered the chicken piccata which was cooked perfectly with a light lemon caper sauce. My boyfriend had the steak which he said was tender and cooked to his liking. The sides were average but the entrees were good quality. Overall we both enjoyed our meals and thought the prices were reasonable for a special occasion date night. I would recommend this restaurant for couples looking for a nice yet casual dinner on Valentines Day or any night.

The flights I end up taking into Charlotte (e.g., STL to PHF) invariably seem to have me jumping across a few terminals to make my connection. You'd think the situation would be improved by the huge number of moving walkways connecting the different gates, but there is NOTHING more infuriating than being stuck behind a family of four blocking the entire walkway, or someone slowly trudging along on the left. For god's sake, people: Just like on the road, pass on the left, walk on the right. There are people in this airport, obviously not you, that are in a HURRY. Can't speak much to the food and drink options here. The selections seem plentiful. US Airways was friendly to me here, too, when a flight was canceled back home. They shuttled me to a nearby hotel -- I forget where -- and covered both my transportation and lodging for the night. Good work, guys.

This place definitely has everything you need for home wine and beer making but for the most part I feel a store like this should have friendly people working here that are ready and willing to answer your questions or at least when you are the only person in the store.. .. .. . acknowledge you. I have been into this store numerous times and have the impression that everyone in here is sort of pissed off to be here. I'm fairly new to home brewing (within the last year and half) and I have questions. This hobby has a lot of questions to be asked, don't act like such a pretentious elite home brewer that I am reluctant to ask my questions. On my last visit the young dude checking me out was literally prying a thank you from his lips. I don't want my ass to be kissed but come on, say hello, can I help you, or thank you have a nice day. I feel that they think that I have to buy products from them although I can easily buy anything that I buy from these guys, on-line. I'm all about keeping it local but if I wanted impersonal service I could order this stuff on-line.

Overall, I had a great experience at this cat groomer, and I would defin itely recommend it to anyone who is looking for a place to take their cat for a bath or nail trim. I will definitely be taking my cat backseat to this groomer in the future. yo highly recommend this cat groomer to anyone who is looking for a mise to take their cat for a bath or nail trim. The staff is very friendly and helpful, and they pick great care of the cats. The prices are also very reasonable. I will definitely be taking my cat back to this groomer in the futսre.

This place is old. I believe it used to be a hub for trains and buses. The outside looks nice but the hallways to the rooms look a little dingy. There was mildew on the floors of my bathroom and bathtub. The washer and dryer was old. There was rust on some of the door hinges. The dresser, fixtures, coffee table, dining table, and dining chairs looked new and modern. The carpet for the most part was clean. The sofa looked old and was not comfortable. The bedsheets had yellow stains on them. I did not use the comforter and one of the layers. The Pennsylvanian has a maid service option with 1 week or 2 week intervals. I am not sure if they even changed or washed my bedsheets because they all had the same yellow stains? wtf? The views from the apartment is nice, but the windows are hard to see through since the window screens are dirty. The kitchen is ok. The corporate apartment comes with a fullsized fridge, dishwasher, coffee maker, silverware, platewear, pots and pans. There is also an iron and ironing board. There is also a 22 inch? CRT-TV with about 100 cable channels. I had a router for internet but it was taken away from me 2 weeks into my stay. The Pennsylvanian claimed Comcast took it away without even telling me. They did not offer me a chance to pay for it. The fitness room was nice. There are treadmills, elliptical machines, pullup bars, and other various machines. There are even a few sets of dumbells. I never used the sauna, so I cannot comment on that. There is a 24 hour concierge that is always helpful and friendly. There is also an option to sign up for a dry-cleaning service, which is outsourced to another company. You drop your dirty clothes into a room and pick it up a few days later after it has been cleaned. This is rather expensive as well. Everyone who has a dry-cleaning Key has access to this room. Thieves could come in and steal your clothes. If I had an option, I would not stay at the Pennsylvanian again.

The restaurant had an amazing selection of local ingredients on the menu. We started with a beet salad topped with goat cheese and pistachios that was the perfect balance of flavors. The scallops were seared to perfection, with just a light char on the outside and still tender inside. They were plated artfully alongside Brussels sprouts that had been roasted until caramelized and sweet. The sauce elevating both was a light lemon butter that tied the dish together beautifully. The flavors were bright and fresh yet rich and indulgent at the same time. I was incredibly impressed by the Executive Chef's skills and creativity. The staff provided excellent and attentive service throughout the meal. It was the best dining experience I've had in quite some time. I will definitely be returning to enjoy more of the restaurant's superb cuisine.

This becomes most apparent when you look at the bathrooms, which have fixtures and mildew growth both from the seventies. I've stayed in motels that were cleaner and better appointed. I could have done without the Sleep Number bed, but that's probably more of a personal preference than anything. However, it appeared to me that the money would have been better spent on updating the rooms themselves. Apparently it used to be a Marriott some time ago - I'm guessing they decided to drop the brand rather than update to Marriott's standards. The continental breakfast was a crime. $12 for buffet style eggs (from a bag no less), sausage, french toast, and oily potato cubes they were trying to say were home fries is unconscionable. Passing on this gastronomic atrocity, I decided to invest my money in an english muffin and two 4 oz. yogurts (only option is Strawberry Banana? Really? ). At least there was a pretty nice pool where we could.. . oh, closed for private party. Just as well. Thankfully this was a business trip and the client is paying expenses, otherwise I might have actually felt upset.

Are you for real?! So my friend and I are scoping out all the Chinese restaurants in Madison, and this one was not impressive. Although it looked promising when we arrived because of how many people were here, we quickly learned the truth. This place. .. is whack. I ordered my go to - cashew chicken - and my friend ordered one of her go to's - fried rice with beef - and we were both NOT impressed. Second bite into my chicken, and it's HARD. Like BONE hard. Eew. And my friend's fried rice had so much egg in it, it took up a quarter of her plate after picking the egg out of a third of her dish. Like, we know protein is important, but there are other food groups too, ya know? The best parts of my cashew chicken were the cashews and the white rice - which if you don't know - are impossible to mess up. So we wait for our bill, like forever, and when we finally get it, there are our fortune cookies! I open mine, and it has the fortune sticking out, and she opens hers, and BOOM. No fortune. That's like the whole reason we're doing this. We love those fortunes. Disappointment. Wah. Anyway. The chicken was bad quality, I've had much better. The pieces that weren't hard were dark meat - very spongy. But they fill up that soy sauce bottle real good, because we used over half of it, so that's a plus. Prices weren't bad either. Overall, we decided not to come back.

"Had brunch there yesterday and was thoroughly impressed! The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, with a modern twist on traditional brunch dishes. The service was top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who made sure our glasses were always full and our plates were never empty.The food was exceptional, with creative combinations of flavors and textures that really made each dish stand out. I particularly enjoyed the eggs benedict, which was cooked to perfection and had a delightful tanginess from the hollandaise sauce. My companion's avocado toast was also delicious, with a generous serving of fresh avocado and a perfectly poached egg on top.The portion sizes were generous, and we left feeling satisfied but not overly full. The prices were reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food and service. Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a tasty and satisfying brunch experience."

Pepperidge Farm remembers.. . I have dined with the King many a time across this fine land. I have watched their slow decline with sadness over the last thirty years. At one point, they actually challenged the Clown for burger superiority, but now, they're a weak shadow on the market, barely a player.. . nn.. . and the BK at this location is a perfect example of why. EVERYTHING at this BK takes ten minutes. Doesn't matter what you order, be prepared to wait. It's always dirty. When I was a kid and worked at the Clown, we were always cleaning. There was usually one or two people on any shift whose sole job was to keep the lobby clean. This place is a hole. Why does the food taste weird? If I want BK, I actually make the drive to Deforest, rather than eat at this location, which is actually a stone's throw from my house. The food here tastes bad, bleachy, and wrong. What are they doing to the food? Fix thyself, King, and maybe I'll return. Until then, I will take my cheap, poorly constructed eats elsewhere.

I'm happy to share my experience with Primanti Bros in Pittsburgh! As soon as we stepped inside the famous restaurant, a lively atmosphere enveloped us. The aroma of sizzling meats and fresh bread wafted through the air, instantly whetting our appetites. The place was bustling with locals and tourists, which further emphasized its popularity.With great anticipation, we scanned the menu, filled with an array of sandwich options. Eventually, I settled on their classic Primanti sandwich, while my dining companion opted for a Turkey and Cheese version. The sandwiches arrived promptly, and let me tell you, they were massive! Stacked high with meat, cheese, coleslaw, and hand-cut fries, the unique presentation was a sight to behold.As I took my first bite, the flavors exploded in my mouth. The warm, tender meat was complemented perfectly by the crispy coleslaw and the tangy pickles. The hand-cut fries added a delightful crunch, giving the sandwich a satisfying texture. The combination of all the ingredients was truly a testament to Primanti Bros' culinary expertise.Despite their generous portion sizes, the sandwiches didn't feel heavy or greasy. The bread, although substantial, was soft and pillowy, providing a reliable base for all the delicious fillings. As I savored each bite, it became apparent why this iconic sandwich has garnered such a loyal following.The service at Primanti Bros was top-notch. The staff members were friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about their menu. They were quick to offer recommendations and answer any questions we had, ensuring a memorable dining experience.The restaurant's ambiance added to the overall enjoyment of the meal. The walls were adorned with Pittsburgh sports memorabilia, creating a sense of nostalgia and hometown pride. Conversations buzzed around us, and we couldn't help but feel a part of the vibrant Pittsburgh community.To accompany our sandwiches, we indulged in some local craft beers.

My fiance, a friend and I were trying pizza from three different places and Luigi's was one of them. I have driven by Luigi's many times before and for some reason had never stopped in but that did allow it to come to mind whenever I was looking for a pizza place I had not yet tried in the Bellevue area. Whenever I called to place my order I was told that my pizza would be ready in about 15 minutes. I arrived closer to 30 minutes later and was immediately confused whenever I walked into the restaurant. You see there was a large dining room on the left that was full of people and I didn't immediately see the are where I would get my pizza from. Finally after a few steps into the restaurant I noticed that the whole back area of the restaurant was where I needed to be and I made my way back there. My pizza was ready for me and I quickly paid and was leaving whenever the cashier told me "Stay out of trouble". I really hope that was a friendly sentiment and not one that was based upon my appearance or anything else. The pizza itself had a medium thick crust with a bland sauce which is weird since I could see a ton of green herbs in it. The cheese was just ok and nothing special while the pizza itself had a slightly sour taste to it which I did not enjoy. Out of the three different pizzas we ate that night this one was overwhelmingly our least favorite which was evidenced by the fact that 3/4 of it was left after the evening. The bottom line for me is that I will probably not head back to Luigi's in the future. I just don't see myself making a trip to Luigi's between the weird experience (although not bad) that I had in the restaurant and the fact that there are much better pizza places nearby.

The menu is marginally more updated than the decor. Some dishes remind me of food fads from the 90's (e.g., the chef seems to have a penchant for meat and fruit pairing). Overall, the menu is too long and rambling without a theme, covering everything from the Baja to the Mediterranean. The food was unremarkable. The bread tasted like a generic supermarket baguette; it was served with olive oil and powdery parm (i.e., from the green can). For appetizers, we ordered the prosciutto and figs as well as the trout and peaches. They were probably the highlight of the meal, but the portions were tiny, and the ingredients were not the best. For the main course, I tried their fish taco, which was on the bland and dry side. Summary: if you are ever nostalgic for "fine dining in a small American town during the 80's, " this place is for you.

But this place takes the cake, or should I say, the fish sandwich. I've tried many different variations, but this one takes the prize. The cod was fresh and flavorful, cooked to perfection, and the slaw was a perfect accompaniment. The bun was lightly toasted, just enough to give it a slight crunch. I added a side of fries, which were crispy and seasoned just right. Overall, this fish sandwich was a home run. Highly recommend!

The food, which was once a highlight, has become bland and uninspired. The service, which was once attentive and friendly, has become sluggish and uninterested. The atmosphere, which was once vibrant and lively, has become dull and uninviting. The prices, which were once reasonable, have skyrocketed, making it difficult to justify the cost. The menu, which was once full of creative and exciting dishes, has been reduced to a selection of unimaginative and unappetizing options. The location, which was once a major draw, has become a liability, with its lack of parking and its lack of accessibility. The drinks, which were once delicious and carefully crafted, have become watered down and unremarkable. The staff, which was once knowledgeable and passionate about the food and drinks, has become disinterested and detached. The restaurant's attempts to revamp and rejuvenate its image have fallen flat, with too much repetition and not enough innovation. The restaurant's reputation, which was once sterling, has taken a major hit, with negative reviews and word of mouth spreading quickly. The once-loyal customer base has dwindled, with many former regulars seeking better options elsewhere. Management and staff need to take a hard look at their offerings and make major changes if they want to compete in the crowded and competitive culinary landscape. Despite the decline, there are still some glimmers of hope, with some dishes and drinks showing promise. But the overall experience is disappointing and not worth the high prices. The poor service and high prices make it difficult to recommend, despite some glimmers of hope. In summary, the restaurant is a shadow of its former self, with subpar food, unremarkable drinks, and an uninviting atmosphere.

Nice to be able to pick your fish and style of cooking. I had a trio of Jamaican jerk tilapia, salmon, and scallops. All good but too much sauce on scallops. Husband had surf n turf special. Snow crab legs tasty but smaller portion than I expected. Glad they had raw oysters, but no idea where they were from. For $2. 50 each you'd think they'd say. Waitstaff friendly but inexperienced when it came to wine. We taught two of them how to open a champagne bottle. Nice time out, but two gripes.. . #1 Used my phones flashlight to see if there was an outlet on the floor. Felt like an archaeologist finding old remains of dinners gone by. Crumbs, napkins wedged between booth and wall, gum, dirt. For the price I would expect a cleaner place. #2 our waiter kept saying Thank you. After every single sentence, even when it wasn't appropriate. Silly gripe, right? But it was way over the top and felt more like, Can I have a tip? Can I have a tip?

The ambiance of Enrico's was cozy and welcoming, with dim lighting and soothing background music. As we entered, the smell of freshly baked bread wafted through the air, instantly stimulating our appetites. The attentive server promptly seated us at a cozy booth and handed us the menus with a smile. The menu offered a tempting array of Italian dishes, making it difficult to decide what to order. After much contemplation, my friend and I settled on sharing a plate of cheesy garlic bread as an appetizer. The bread arrived warm and oozing with melted cheese, and each bite was a delightful burst of flavor. For the main course, I chose the lasagna, while my friend opted for the penne alla vodka. The portions were generous, and the presentation was aesthetically pleasing. The lasagna was perfectly layered with tender pasta, rich meat sauce, and creamy cheese, creating a harmonious blend of textures and flavors. The penne alla vodka was divine, with its velvety tomato sauce infused with a hint of vodka and topped with grated Parmesan cheese. As we savored our meals, the ambiance was enlivened by the conversations and laughter of other diners, creating a convivial atmosphere. To accompany our meal, we ordered a bottle of a full-bodied red wine recommended by our knowledgeable server, which complemented our dishes beautifully. The attentive staff ensured our glasses were never empty and promptly checked on us throughout the evening to ensure our satisfaction. Though pleasantly full, we couldn't resist indulging in dessert, and we were not disappointed. We shared a slice of tiramisu, which was an exquisite blend of creamy mascarpone, espresso-soaked ladyfingers, and a dusting of cocoa powder. Every bite transported us to the streets of Italy. Overall, our experience at Enrico's was exceptional. The quality of the food, the attentiveness of the staff, and the inviting atmosphere combined to create a memorable dining experience.

However, today was different. I had a hankering for some delicious pad thai, and I knew just the place to get it. I suggested to my coworkers that we order from there for lunch, and to my surprise, they all agreed.I took charge and placed the order, specifying that we wanted it to be delivered to our office. The restaurant staff was friendly and accommodating, answering all my questions about their menu and making sure that our order was correct.The delivery arrived right on time, and the aroma of freshly cooked noodles filled the room. My coworkers and I eagerly opened the boxes and dug in. The verdict? Absolutely delicious!The pad thai was cooked to perfection, with a nice balance of sweet and savory flavors. The texture was just right, too - not too mushy, not too crunchy. And the shrimp were plump and juicy.We all raved about the food, and my coworkers thanked me for suggesting it. It was a great way to break up the monotony of our workday and enjoy a tasty meal together.I'm so glad that I stepped out of my comfort zone and suggested ordering out with my coworkers. It was a great experience, and I can't wait to do it again.If you're looking for a great pad thai and a satisfying lunch, I highly recommend giving this restaurant a try. You won't be disappointed!

I walked into the restaurant with high hopes, excited to try their unique sushi creations. The interior design was sleek and modern, with a chic ambiance that set the tone for a promising dining experience. However, as I looked around, I noticed that the tables were packed tightly together, making for a less than intimate setting.The menu offered a variety of sushi options, but the descriptions were uninspired and lacked detail. I ordered the spicy tuna roll, which arrived lacking the kick of heat that I had been expecting. The fish was fresh, but the roll itself was overwhelmed by a sea of mayonnaise.I also tried the California roll, which was unremarkable and forgettable. The avocado was overripe, and the crab meat was scarce. The sushi rice was flavorful, but it couldn't save the dish from the lackluster filling.As I waited for my food, I couldn't help but notice the dim lighting, which made it difficult to read the menu and even harder to see the food on my plate. The music was a bit too loud, and the chatter of the other patrons only added to the cacophony of sounds.The service was friendly, but not overly attentive. Our server seemed to be juggling multiple tables, and it took her a while to check in on us. When she did, she was quick to refill our drinks and take away our plates.Despite my initial disappointment, I was happy to see that the restaurant offered a full bar with a creative cocktail menu. I ordered a sake-based drink, which was expertly crafted and a welcome reprieve from the mediocre food.Overall, I was underwhelmed by my experience at this sushi spot. While the ambiance was pleasant, the food and service fell short of my expectations. I would recommend this restaurant to those looking for a casual, no-frills sushi experience, but for those seeking a high-quality meal, there are better options in the area.

I travel to quite a few conventions, have been here twice. The first time was about 5 years ago for a gaming conference. It was a Friday afternoon and the traffic getting there was a nightmare. Seemed like every road around the airport was backed up. Took us over 2 hours just to go 10 miles. Never again will I try to drive that route on a weekend! The second time I came was last year for a comic book convention. Flew in on a Tuesday so didn't have to deal with weekend traffic thank goodness. Got an Uber from the airport to the hotel which went much smoother. Checked into my room and rested for a bit before heading to the convention center. Didn't realize how massive the place was until I was actually inside it. Spent the whole afternoon checking out all the exhibitor booths. Had dinner plans that night with some friends also in town for the con. We ended up at some food hall place in the airport, can't remember the name. Service was pretty slow but the food was decent. Talking and people watching made the time pass. Wed morning woke up and did it all again at the con. So many cool panels and events to choose from, it was hard to pick! Took a lunch break in the airport atrium area, was really nice sitting outside. Late afternoon my flight got delayed of course. They said 3 hours but ended up being over 5 thanks to a storm. I was ready to pull my hair out by then from boredom! Finally boarded and took off just before sunset. Touchdown in Charlotte only to sit on the runway for another hour. Not the smoothest trip home but the convention itself was a blast as always. Next time though I'll try to avoid traveling on a weekend if possible. Too much hassle!

The salon was untidy, and the air reeked of chemical treatments. As I looked around, I noticed that the hairdressers seemed disinterested and lacked the enthusiasm one would expect in a professional setting. I hoped that the quality of the service would compensate for the lack of a pleasant ambiance, but unfortunately my high expectations were shattered. As I patiently waited for my turn, I noticed the poor time management skills of the staff. Appointments were being missed, and clients were left waiting for long periods of time. I'm a pretty big fan of airports, though not to the point of ecstasy or anything too bonkers. There's something undeniably thrilling about the organized chaos of countless travelers crisscrossing the globe. Of course, the prices one pays these days can easily induce heart palpitations - a bottle of water shouldn't cost more than a small country's GDP. But I'll gladly shell out cash for the strange comfort of staring out the window at planes taking off and landing with laser-like precision, their maneuvers still seeming miraculous despite all these years. The sheer scale of the bustling terminals is awe-inspiring too, a microcosm of our interconnected modern world under one gigantic roof. It's always fascinating people-watching as well, observing the harried business folks rushing to their gates alongside excited families beginning their vacations. Though the security lines can test even a zen master's patience, I still get a kick out of the ephemeral community formed among weary travelers just trying to reach their destination. Perhaps it's the romantic in me, but I'll always feel a tinge of wanderlust waiting at the gate for that magical boarding announcement.
